text: M10 Chapter 1: Legal System and Regulatory Bodies in Hong Kong — Phase 1 速查表 + Phase 2 閃卡 Phase 1 速查表 Learning Objectives 1. Describe the constitutional framework of the HKSAR and the role of the Basic Law and the HK National Security Law (HKNSL). 2. Identify and explain the sources of Hong Kong law: common law, rules of equity, ordinances, subordinate legislation and Chinese customary law. 3. Apply the jurisdictional limits of Hong Kong courts and tribunals to select the correct forum for a given dispute. 4. Explain the doctrine of precedent (stare decisis) and analyse when a court may depart from a precedent. 5. Distinguish the literal, golden and mischief rules of statutory interpretation and apply them to a scenario. 6. Describe the roles, duties and powers of the HKMA, SFC, HKEX, AFRC and IA in relation to the work of an accountant. 必背考點 A. Relevant Ordinances（Cap. + section，以 LP 所引為準） 主題 法例 / 條文 核心內容 香港法律來源 Basic Law Art. 8 & Art. 18 Art. 8：1997 前已生效的 common law、rules of equity、ordinances、subordinate legislation、customary law 繼續有效（除抵觸 Basic Law 者）；Art. 18：現行法律 = Basic Law + Art. 8 法律 + 特區立法機關制定的法律 Basic Law 高於本地法律 Basic Law Art. 11 Basic Law 如其他國家的成文憲法，凌駕香港本地立法 法官任命 / 司法獨立 Basic Law Art. 2, 19, 85, 88 法院享有獨立司法權及終審權；法官由 Judicial Officers Recommendation Commission 推薦，行政長官不能直接任命 參照其他普通法地區判例 Basic Law Art. 84 香港法院可參考其他 common law jurisdictions 的判例 Basic Law 解釋權 Basic Law Art. 158 涉及中央人民政府事務或中港關係的條文，法院須經 CFA 提請 SCNPC 解釋 行政長官發回法案 Basic Law Art. 49 法案不符合香港整體利益可發回重議；立法會以不少於全體議員 2/3 多數 再次通過，行政長官必須簽署或解散立法會 三讀投票門檻 Basic Law Annex II Government bill：出席議員 simple majority；Members' bill：功能界別 + 分區直選兩組議員各自 simple majority HKNSL 與本地法律衝突 HKNSL Art. 62, 65 （列入 Basic Law Annex III，依 Basic Law Art. 18） 本地法律（含 common law）與 HKNSL 不一致時 HKNSL 優先；解釋權屬 SCNPC 法定釋義總原則 Interpretation and General Clauses Ordinance (Cap. 1) s.19 所有條例視為 remedial，須以最能達致條例目的、符合其 true intent, meaning and spirit 的方式詮釋（即採 mischief rule）；Cap. 1 s.7 ：男性詞彙含女性、單數含眾數 附屬法例授權（例子） MPF Schemes Ordinance (Cap. 485) s.47 ；Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112) s.85 Parent/enabling ordinance 授權特定機構（MPFA / Board of Inland Revenue）制定 rules 中國習慣法認可 New Territories Ordinance (Cap. 97) s.13 ；Legitimacy Ordinance (Cap. 184) s.14 法院可承認及執行影響新界土地的中國習慣；按中國法律習俗締結的婚姻所生子女屬婚生子女 專門審裁處 Lands Tribunal Ordinance (Cap. 17)；Labour Tribunal (Cap. 25)；Small Claims Tribunal (Cap. 338)；Competition Ordinance (Cap. 619)；IRO (Cap. 112) s.65 （Board of Review） 各審裁處的成立法例；Board of Review 處理稅務上訴 調解 Mediation Ordinance (Cap. 620) s.8(2)(a),(b),(g) 調解通訊保密；例外：雙方及調解員同意、資料已公開、法律規定披露 律師較高出庭權 Legal Practitioners Ordinance (Cap. 159) 設立 Higher Rights Assessment Board（HRAB），批核事務律師的 higher rights of audience 監管機構法例 Banking Ordinance (Cap. 155)；Securities and Futures Ordinance (Cap. 571)；Financial Reporting Council Ordinance (Cap. 588) + FRC (Amendment) Ordinance 2021；Insurance Ordinance (Cap. 41) HKMA 認可及監管三類認可機構；SFC 發牌 10 類受規管活動（Type 4/5/6/9 若 wholly incidental to CPA practice 豁免領牌）；FRC 2022 10 01 起改名 AFRC 成為會計專業全面獨立監管者；保險公司核數師須為 HKICPA 會員或 IA 認可資格 AML 申報 Cap. 615 / Cap. 405 / Cap. 455 / Cap. 575 核數師就打擊洗錢及恐怖份子籌資須向有關當局申報 B. Leading Cases（full citation，全部出自 LP） 案件 確立原則 Tong Ying Kit v HKSAR [2020] HKCFI 2133 首宗 HKNSL 案件；CFI 確認香港法院應以 common law approach （而非 civil law approach）詮釋 HKNSL，與詮釋 Basic Law 的方法一致 Re Wong Choi Ho & Another (1969) HKLR 391 香港適用的 Chinese customary law = 1843 年起在香港沿用的 Qing Law 及習俗 Grant v Australian Knitting Mills Ltd (1936) AC 85 製造商對消費者負 duty of care（縱無合約關係）；內衣殘留化學品致皮炎 Griffiths v Peter Conway (1939) 1 All ER 685 Distinguishing 示範：原告皮膚異常敏感屬 material fact 差異，法院拒跟隨 Grant 案；duty 不及於正常範圍以外的人 London and North Eastern Railway v Berriman (1946) AC 278 Literal rule ：死者當時在 oiling 路軌（routine maintenance），不屬 "relaying or repairing"，遺孀不獲賠償 — 即使結果不公亦照字面解釋 Adler v George (1964) 2 QB 7 Golden rule ：被告在禁區「內」阻礙執勤人員；字面 "in the vicinity of" 會令區內犯案反而無罪，屬荒謬，故讀作 "in or in the vicinity of" Heydon's Case (1584) 76 ER 637 Mischief rule 四問：立法前法律為何？舊法未涵蓋的 mischief/defect 為何？立法提供何種 remedy？remedy 的真正原因為何？ Smith v Hughes (1960) 2 All ER 859 Mischief rule 應用：妓女在屋內敲窗招徠街上行人，仍屬 "solicit in a street" — 法案目的係令行人免受滋擾 C. IRAC Application Points（考試套用框架） 1. Court jurisdiction 選擇題（Ch.1 最常考應用點） Issue : 案件應由哪個法院/審裁處審理？ Rule : Small Claims Tribunal ≤ HK$75,000 （不可律師代表，可放棄超額部分遷就）；District Court 合約申索 ≤ HK$3 million （收回土地 ≤ HK$7m；年租/應課差餉租值 ≤ HK$320,000；刑事最高監禁 7 年，無陪審團）；CFI civil HK$3 million（unlimited jurisdiction）；Labour Tribunal：至少一名申索人申索額 HK$8,000 或申索人 10 人；所有刑事案件首訊必經 Magistrates' Courts（一般最高判監 2 年 + 罰款 HK$100,000）。 Application : 將 scenario 金額/案件性質對照門檻。 Conclusion : 指明 forum + 理由（金額、可否聘律師、是否刑事）。 2. 法院何時可偏離 precedent Rule : 只有 ratio decidendi 具約束力；obiter dicta 僅 persuasive。可偏離的情況：(1) distinguished （material facts 不同）；(2) overruled （上級法院在 另一案件 推翻下級法院確立的先例）；(3) reversed （上級法院在 同一案件 上訴中推翻下級判決）；(4) 先前陳述屬 obiter dicta；(5) reasoning divergent and unclear；(6) per incuriam （法官漏考慮相關案例/法例）。Vertical：CFI 受 CA/CFA 約束；DC/Magistrates 受 CFI 約束。Horizontal：同級法院互不約束（CFI 不約束另一 CFI）。 Trap : overruling 與 reversing 的分別在於「不同案件」定「同一案件上訴」；下級法院 不能 overrule 上級法院先例，只能 distinguish。 3. Statutory interpretation 三步判斷 Rule : Literal rule → 字面清楚即照用，即使不公；Golden rule → 字面導致 absurd result 時採最少荒謬的解釋；Mischief rule → 探究立法意圖壓制 mischief（Cap. 1 s.19 要求香港法院採用）。 Application : 先問字面是否清楚 → 再問字面結果是否荒謬 → 最後問立法要杜絕的 mischief 是甚麼。 Trap : ejusdem generis（具體詞 + 概括詞 → 概括詞限於同類）與 contextual rule（整條條例一齊讀）係 輔助規則 ，唔係三大規則之一。 4. Subordinate legislation 控制 Rule : 由 parent/enabling ordinance 授權制定； Negative vetting （毋須明文）：刊憲後於立法會下次會議席上提交，立法會可在 28 日 內以決議修訂或延長審議期，一般刊憲日生效； Positive vetting ：parent ordinance 規定須立法會批准，議員動議，立法會可 approve / reject / amend。 Trap : subordinate legislation 超越 parent ordinance 權限 = ultra vires ，可經 judicial review 推翻；立法會對毋須審議的附屬法例無權廢除或修訂。 5. Equity 補救 Rule : Common law 補救只有 monetary damages；equity 補救係 court orders（injunction、specific performance），屬 酌情 授予，原告 not entitled as of right；common law 與 equity 衝突時 equity prevails ；equity 承認新權利（如 trust 受益人權利），common law 不承認。 Application : 標的物獨一無二（unique property）→ damages 不足 → 可求 specific performance，但由法院酌情決定。 6. Judicial review Rule : 針對政府/法定機構決定，理由限於 illegality, unreasonableness, procedural impropriety ；申請人須有 sufficient interest；法院 不會 判斷決定本身對錯；敗訴須付對方訟費；Basic Law Art. 64 政府須守法。 易混淆概念對比 對比一：Common Law vs Rules of Equity Common Law Rules of Equity 來源 法官在案件判決中創造（case law），嚴格跟 precedent 為紓緩 common law 嚴苛而發展，追求 fairness and natural justice，法官酌情 補救 只有 monetary damages （金錢賠償） Decrees / court orders ：injunction、specific performance 權利 不承認新權利（如 trust 受益人權利） 承認新權利（trust 受益人可向 trustee 主張權利） 取得補救 權利確立即可獲 damages 酌情 授予，not as of right；damages 足夠時不授予 衝突時 — Equity prevails 📌 點樣分辨 ：題目問「賠償金」→ common law；問「強制履行/禁制令」→ equity。 考試伏位 ：買家想強制賣家完成獨特物業交易，答案唔係「一定獲批 specific performance」，而係「法院酌情，damages 不足先會考慮」。 對比二：Arbitration vs Mediation（vs Conciliation） Arbitration Mediation Conciliation 性質 Adjudicative ：仲裁員作出裁決 Non adjudicative ：調解員協助雙方自行達成和解 Conciliator 角色比 mediator 更被動，可作 evaluator/intervener 提建議 結果約束力 Award final and binding ；極少情況可上訴（除 obvious error of law） 無裁決； settlement 由雙方自願達成 建議無約束力，雙方可不跟隨 程序 毋須正式聆訊、證據規則較寬鬆、閉門進行 受 Mediation Ordinance (Cap. 620) 規管；通訊 保密 （s.8(2) 例外） 多用於勞資/歧視爭議，預防糾紛擴大 費用/場地 雙方須付仲裁員酬金及場地費 較訴訟便宜快捷 較訴訟便宜快捷 📌 點樣分辨 ：關鍵字 "final and binding decision by a third party" = arbitration；"assist parties to reach settlement themselves, no decision imposed" = mediation。 考試伏位 ：題目若講「上訴仲裁裁決」→ 一般唔得（除非 obvious error of law）；若講「調解保密可隨便向法庭披露」→ 錯，要符合 Cap. 620 s.8(2) 例外。 Phase 2 閃卡 Card 1 Front: Which articles of the Basic Law preserve the pre 1997 sources of Hong Kong law, and what are those sources? Back: Article 8: laws previously in force — common law, rules of equity, ordinances, subordinate legislation and customary law — are maintained, except those contravening the Basic Law and subject to amendment by the HKSAR legislature. Article 18: laws in force = the Basic Law + Article 8 laws + laws enacted by the HKSAR legislature. Article 11: the Basic Law is above local laws enacted by Hong Kong. 💬 白話：97 前嘅法律（普通法、衡平法、條例、附屬法例、習慣法）過渡照用，前提係唔好同 Basic Law 有衝突；Art. 8 講保留、Art. 18 講而家嘅法律體系組成。 Card 2 Front: In Tong Ying Kit v HKSAR [2020] HKCFI 2133, which interpretive approach did the Court of First Instance confirm for the HKNSL, and why? Back: HK courts should apply the common law approach (not civil law approach) to interpret the HKNSL. Reasoning: the Basic Law, also a national law enacted by the SCNPC, is construed using the common law approach; no valid basis to adopt a second approach for the HKNSL. Under HKNSL Art. 62 local laws (incl. common law) apply unless inconsistent with the HKNSL; Art. 65 vests interpretation power in the SCNPC. 💬 白話：HKNSL 雖然係全國性法律，但香港法官照用普通法方法去詮釋，因為 Basic Law 都係咁做，保持一貫。 Card 3 Front: State the civil monetary jurisdictional limits of the Small Claims Tribunal, the District Court and the Court of First Instance. Back: Small Claims Tribunal (Cap. 338): claims not exceeding HK$75,000 ; informal; no legal representation . District Court: contract claims up to HK$3 million ; recovery of land up to HK$7 million ; annual rent/ratable value not exceeding HK$320,000 . Court of First Instance: unlimited civil jurisdiction; hears claims over HK$3 million . 💬 白話：記住三條數：7.5 萬（小額錢債）、300 萬（區院合約）、超過 300 萬去原訟庭。考試好鍾意畀個金額叫你揀法院。 Card 4 Front: What is the difference between overruling and reversing a decision under the doctrine of precedent? Back: Overruling : a higher court, in a different (later) case , declares that a precedent set by a lower court in a previous case is no longer binding and substitutes a different rule. Reversing : a higher court, on appeal in the same case , reaches a decision opposite to that of the lower court. Only the ratio decidendi binds; obiter dicta are persuasive only. 💬 白話：Overrule = 上級法院喺 另一單案 度推翻舊先例；Reverse = 同一單案 上訴時改判。考試最常伏位就係混淆呢兩個，記住「同一案定另一案」。 Card 5 Front: List six grounds on which a court may depart from a precedent. Back: 1. The case is distinguished (material facts differ — e.g. Griffiths v Peter Conway (1939) 1 All ER 685). 2. The precedent has been overruled by a higher court. 3. The decision has been reversed on appeal. 4. The statements relied on were only obiter dicta . 5. The reasoning of the previous case was divergent and unclear . 6. The decision was given per incuriam (failure to consider relevant case law/legislation). 💬 白話：口訣「D O R O D P」：Distinguish、Overrule、Reverse、Obiter、Divergent、Per incuriam。Horizontal stare decisis：同級法院（如 CFI vs CFI）互不約束。 Card 6 Front: Match each rule of statutory interpretation to its leading case: literal rule, golden rule, mischief rule. Back: Literal rule — London and North Eastern Railway v Berriman (1946) AC 278: "oiling" tracks ≠ "relaying or repairing"; widow denied compensation despite harsh result. Golden rule — Adler v George (1964) 2 QB 7: "in the vicinity of" read as "in or in the vicinity of" to avoid absurdity. Mischief rule — Heydon's Case (1584) 76 ER 637 (four questions); applied in Smith v Hughes (1960) 2 All ER 859; adopted for HK ordinances by s.19, Interpretation and General Clauses Ordinance (Cap. 1). 💬 白話：Literal = 照字面，唔公平都照；Golden = 字面荒謬就修正；Mischief = 問立法原意想杜絕咩弊端。香港考試記住 Cap. 1 s.19 指定用 mischief rule。 Card 7 Front: Distinguish the negative vetting procedure from the positive vetting procedure for subsidiary legislation. Back: Negative vetting : no express provision needed in the enabling ordinance; subsidiary legislation is laid on the table at the next LegCo sitting after gazettal; LegCo may amend it by resolution within 28 days or extend the scrutiny period; effective on gazette date unless otherwise provided. Positive vetting : the parent ordinance requires LegCo approval ; a public officer moves a motion; LegCo may approve, reject or amend ; amended legislation deemed effective on gazette date. 💬 白話：Negative = 刊憲先生效，立法會「唔出聲就過關」、28 日內可改；Positive = 要立法會主動批准先生效。名字「negative/positive」指立法會參與程度。 Card 8 Front: Which five external regulatory bodies should an accountant know, and what is the key statute/role of each? Back: HKMA — Banking Ordinance (Cap. 155): authorisation/supervision of the three types of authorised institutions; currency and banking stability. SFC — Securities and Futures Ordinance (Cap. 571): licenses 10 types of regulated activities; CPAs exempt from Type 4/5/6/9 licences if services are wholly incidental to CPA practice. HKEX — frontline regulator of listing matters; administers and enforces the Listing Rules. AFRC (formerly FRC, from 1 Oct 2022) — Financial Reporting Council Ordinance (Cap. 588) as amended by FRC (Amendment) Ordinance 2021: registers PIE auditors/practice units, issues practising certificates, inspects, investigates, disciplines; oversees HKICPA. IA — Insurance Ordinance (Cap. 41): regulates insurers and intermediaries; protects policyholders. 💬 白話：銀行搵 HKMA、證券期貨搵 SFC、上市搵 HKEX、會計師搵 AFRC、保險搵 IA。記住 2022 年 10 月起 FRC 改名 AFRC 並接管 HKICPA 大部分監管權。 本章急救詞彙 EN Term 繁中白話 English Model Sentence stare decisis 「跟住舊判決行」— 下級法院要跟上級法院先例 Under stare decisis, the District Court is bound by the decisions of the Court of First Instance. ratio decidendi 判決理由 — 判案所依據的法律原則，先有約束力 Only the ratio decidendi of a case becomes a binding precedent for later cases. obiter dicta 「順便講嘅話」— 法官非必要的法律意見，只具說服力 Statements made by the way are obiter dicta and are persuasive but not binding. per incuriam 「搞錯咗」— 法官漏咗考慮相關法例或案例而作嘅判決，可不跟隨 A decision given per incuriam need not be followed because the judge failed to consider the relevant legislation. subordinate legislation 附屬法例 — 立法會經 parent ordinance 授權其他機構訂立嘅規則 The Board of Inland Revenue may make rules as subordinate legislation under s.85 of the Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112). ultra vires 越權 — 附屬法例超越母條例授權範圍 Subordinate legislation made beyond the limits of the parent ordinance is ultra vires and may be challenged by judicial review. specific performance 強制履行令 — equity 補救，法院命令違約方履行合約，酌情授予 The buyer may seek an order of specific performance where damages are inadequate because the property is unique. judicial review 司法覆核 — 法院審查政府/公共機構決定嘅合法性，唔審對錯 The court will grant leave for judicial review only if the application has a realistic prospect of success.

excerpt: M10 Chapter 1: Legal System and Regulatory Bodies in Hong Kong — Phase 3 Answers Q1 — Answer: A Model Answer (EN): Mandy should commence her claim in the Small …
text: M10 Chapter 1: Legal System and Regulatory Bodies in Hong Kong — Phase 3 Answers Q1 — Answer: A Model Answer (EN): Mandy should commence her claim in the Small Claims Tribunal . The Small Claims Tribunal, set up under the Small Claims Tribunal Ordinance (Cap. 338), hears monetary claims involving amounts not exceeding HK$75,000 , and its main types of claims include debts and service charges. Mandy's claim of HK$68,000 is within this limit. The hearing is informal and no legal representation is allowed , which matches Mandy's wish to avoid instructing a lawyer. 解題思路（繁中）: Issue : HK$68,000 債務申索應去邊個 forum？ Rule + Application : Small Claims Tribunal 上限係 HK$75,000，HK$68,000 喺範圍內，而且唔准律師代表，完全配合 Mandy 嘅需要。 Distractor 分析 ：B (District Court) — 區院合約申索上限 HK$3 million，HK$68,000 技術上可以入稟，但題目明確講 Mandy 想平、快、唔請律師，所以 District Court 唔係 best answer（MCQ 揀最貼題嗰個）；C (CFI) — 處理超過 HK$3 million 嘅民事申索，完全唔啱；D (Labour Tribunal) — 只處理僱傭合約申索（工資、遣散費等），呢單係商業債務。 考試伏位 ：唔好見到「contract/service agreement」就直覺揀 District Court — 題目畀咗金額同「唔想請律師」兩個線索，係指住 Small Claims Tribunal。 Rule Check: Small Claims Tribunal Ordinance (Cap. 338); LP §1.3.2.3 Common Trap（繁中）: 混淆各法院金額門檻：SCT ≤ HK$75,000；District Court 合約申索 ≤ HK$3 million（收地 ≤ HK$7 million）；CFI HK$3 million 且無上限。另外記住：勝訴後被告唔找數，申索人仍要自行採取行動強制執行判決。 Q2 — Answer: B Model Answer (EN): The court has most likely applied the golden rule . Under the literal rule, Oscar was "in" the station and not "in the vicinity of" it, so no offence would be committed. However, the court applies the golden rule where the literal rule would produce an absurd result the legislature cannot have intended: it would be absurd if obstructing staff just outside a station were an offence but the same conduct inside the station itself were not. The court therefore reads "in the vicinity of" as "in or in the vicinity of" and adopts the interpretation producing the least absurd result. This mirrors Adler v George (1964) 2 QB 7 , where "in the vicinity of" a prohibited place was read to include "in" the prohibited place. 解題思路（繁中）: Issue : 被告喺車站「入面」犯事，條文寫 "in the vicinity of"，點樣解釋？ Rule + Application : 字面解釋會令「站外阻礙有罪、站內阻礙無罪」，荒謬 → golden rule 修正字面意思。同 Adler v George 嘅邏輯一模一樣。 Distractor 分析 ：A — literal rule 會導致 Oscar 無罪 （佢唔係 "in the vicinity"），同題目「法院定罪」矛盾；C — ejusdem generis 係處理「具體詞 + 概括詞」嘅同類限制，同 "in the vicinity" 嘅荒謬性無關；D — mischief rule 雖然都係探究立法意圖，但佢唔係「must always be applied before any other rule」，而且呢類「字面造成荒謬」嘅經典情況係 golden rule 嘅地盤。 考試伏位 ：golden rule vs mischief rule 最易混：「字面意思荒謬」→ golden；「條文含糊/有漏洞，要問立法想杜絕咩 mischief」→ mischief（香港法院依 Cap. 1 s.19 常用 mischief rule，但本題 scenario 係典型 golden rule 事實）。 Rule Check: Adler v George (1964) 2 QB 7; cf. s.19, Interpretation and General Clauses Ordinance (Cap. 1) Common Trap（繁中）: 見到「legislative intent / purpose」就自動揀 mischief rule。本題嘅關鍵字係 absurd result （站內無罪、站外有罪），呢個係 golden rule 嘅 trigger。 Q3 — Answer: C Model Answer (EN): The Court of Appeal has overruled the principle in Chan v Lee . A precedent is overruled when a higher court , in a different (later) case , declares that the precedent established by a lower court in a previous case is no longer binding authority and puts forward a different rule. Here the Court of Appeal (higher court), in the appeal arising from Wong v Cheung , declared the District Court's principle in Chan v Lee (a previous, different case) wrong and no longer binding. This matches the LP's Illustrative Example: the CA/CFA has the power to overrule the decision of a lower court made in a different case. 解題思路（繁中）: Issue : CA 喺另一單案嘅上訴中推翻 DC 舊先例嘅法律原則，術語係咩？ Rule + Application : Overrule 三要素：(1) 上級法院 (CA vs DC)；(2) 另一案件 （唔係 Chan v Lee 本身嘅上訴）；(3) 宣佈舊原則不再是 binding authority。三項齊全。 Distractor 分析 ：A (reversed) — reversing 係 同一案件 上訴改判下級判決；CA 推翻嘅係 Chan v Lee 嘅原則，而 Chan v Lee 本身無上訴，所以唔係 reverse（CA 可以 reverse Wong v Cheung 嘅判決，但題目問嘅係佢對 Chan v Lee 原則做咗咩）；B (distinguished) — distinguishing 係法官認為兩案 material facts 唔同而拒絕跟隨，呢度係 CA 直接宣佈舊原則錯，唔係話事實唔同；D (per incuriam) — 指法官漏考慮相關法例/案例而犯錯，係偏離先例嘅 理由 之一，但題目描述嘅 動作 係上級法院推翻下級先例，即 overrule。 考試伏位 ：overrule vs reverse 係經典伏位 — 記住「overrule 係另一案、reverse 係同一案」。 Rule Check: LP §1.4.3 (grounds for departing from precedent); cf. Grant v Australian Knitting Mills Ltd (1936) AC 85 and Griffiths v Peter Conway (1939) 1 All ER 685 (distinguishing) Common Trap（繁中）: 見到「CA 話 DC 錯」就揀 reverse。問自己：CA 處理緊嗰單案（Wong v Cheung）同被推翻嘅先例（Chan v Lee）係咪同一單案？唔係 → overrule。 Q4 — Answer: C Model Answer (EN): The Regulation was subject to the negative vetting procedure . Where subsidiary legislation is intended to be subject to negative vetting, the enabling provision does not need to provide for it expressly — the absence of any approval requirement in the parent ordinance points to negative vetting. The Regulation is published in the Government Gazette and laid on the table at the next sitting of the Legislative Council. Not later than 28 days after that sitting, the Legislative Council may amend the subsidiary legislation by resolution at a Council meeting, or extend the scrutiny period. Unless another date is provided, the Regulation took effect on its gazettal date (1 June); the amendment on 20 June was within the 28 day window and was valid. 解題思路（繁中）: Issue : Parent ordinance 無講要立法會批准，立法會 28 日內修訂附屬法例 — 屬邊種 vetting？有無效？ Rule + Application : 無明文規定 = negative vetting（預設機制）；刊憲後下次會議席上提交，28 日內可以決議修訂。20 June 喺期限內，修訂有效。 Distractor 分析 ：A — 錯，negative vetting 唔需要 enabling provision 明文規定；B — positive vetting 需要 parent ordinance 明文 規定須立法會批准，呢度無，所以唔係 positive vetting（而且 positive vetting 下立法會都可以 amend，所以「只能 approve or reject」本身都錯）；D — 附屬法例喺 刊憲日（1 June）已生效 ，唔係等立法會決議先生效（除非另有訂明日期）。 考試伏位 ：兩大混淆位：(1) 「無明文 = 無審議」係錯，無明文 = negative vetting；(2) 生效日期 = 刊憲日，唔係審議完結日。 Rule Check: LP §1.5.2.2 (negative and positive vetting procedures; 28 day scrutiny period) Common Trap（繁中）: 以為立法會修訂附屬法例一定要經 positive vetting。記住：negative vetting 下立法會都可以 amend（或延長審議期），分別在於 positive vetting 要主動批准（approve/reject/amend by motion），negative vetting 係「唔出聲就自動過關」。 Q5 — Answer: Kelvin may seek an order of specific performance, but he is NOT entitled to it as of right; the remedy is discretionary and likely to be granted because the building is unique. Model Answer (EN): Issue : Whether Kelvin is automatically entitled to a court order compelling Doris to complete the sale. Rule : At common law, the only remedy for breach of contract is monetary damages . Equity, developed to relieve the harshness and rigidity of the common law, provides remedies in the form of decrees (court orders) , such as specific performance — an order requiring a party to a contract to perform his/her part. Equitable remedies are discretionary : the court awards them where common law damages would be inadequate (e.g. where the subject matter is unique); if damages are sufficient, the remedy will not be granted. Equity recognises new rights and, where there is conflict between common law and equity, equity prevails . Rules of equity are a source of Hong Kong law under Articles 8 and 18 of the Basic Law. Application : The tong lau is one of only a handful left in Hong Kong with unique architectural features, so damages would not adequately compensate Kelvin — no equivalent substitute can be bought with money. This is precisely the situation (unique subject matter) where equity intervenes, as in the LP's example of a unique property. Conclusion : Kelvin is not entitled to the remedy as of right . He may apply for specific performance, and the court is likely to exercise its discretion in his favour because damages are inadequate; but the award remains at the court's discretion. 解題思路（繁中）: 呢題考你兩層：(1) 認到 remedy 係 equity 嘅 specific performance（而唔係 common law damages）；(2) 識講「 not as of right，法院酌情 」— 呢個係 LP 明確強調嘅位，都係考生最常漏嘅位。 IRAC 寫法：先點出 issue（可否自動獲得強制履行令）→ rule（common law 只有 damages；equity 有 specific performance，酌情授予，damages 不足先用）→ application（唐樓獨一無二，damages 唔夠補償）→ conclusion（可申請、好大機會批，但唔係自動有）。 Distractor 式錯誤答案 ：答「Kelvin 一定贏，Doris 必須交樓」= 忽略 discretion；答「Kelvin 只能收 HK$5 million 差價」= 忽略咗 equity 喺 damages 不足時嘅角色；答「equity 一定跟 common law」= 調轉咗，衝突時 equity prevails。 Rule Check: LP §1.2.1.3–1.2.1.4 and Illustrative Example 1 (specific performance is discretionary; equity prevails over common law); Basic Law Arts 8 & 18 (rules of equity as a source of law). (Note: the LP cites no specific case for specific performance in this chapter — no case citation is invented here.) Common Trap（繁中）: 最大陷阱係「unique property = 一定有 specific performance」。正確講法係「damages inadequate → 法院 酌情 授予；法院認為 damages 足夠就唔會批」。答題時一定要寫 "not as of right / at the discretion of the court"。

title: M10 Chapter 1: Legal System and Regulatory Bodies in Hong Kong — Phase 3 Quiz
headings: M10 Chapter 1: Legal System and Regulatory Bodies in Hong Kong — Phase 3 Quiz
excerpt: M10 Chapter 1: Legal System and Regulatory Bodies in Hong Kong — Phase 3 Quiz Rules: Closed book · 15 minutes · 5 questions · Submit as 1. … 2. … 3. … 4. … 5. ……
text: M10 Chapter 1: Legal System and Regulatory Bodies in Hong Kong — Phase 3 Quiz Rules: Closed book · 15 minutes · 5 questions · Submit as 1. … 2. … 3. … 4. … 5. … — 超時如實申報 Question 1 (MCQ) Mandy runs a small florist shop. A corporate customer owes her HK$68,000 for flower arrangements delivered under a service agreement. The customer refuses to pay. Mandy wants to recover the debt quickly and cheaply, and she does not wish to instruct a lawyer to represent her at the hearing. Before which forum should Mandy commence her claim? A. The Small Claims Tribunal B. The District Court C. The Court of First Instance of the High Court D. The Labour Tribunal Question 2 (MCQ) A hypothetical Public Transport (Conduct) Ordinance provides in s.5: "No person in the vicinity of any railway station shall obstruct any member of the station staff engaged in crowd control duty." Oscar was inside the concourse of a railway station (i.e. within the station premises, not merely near it) when he deliberately blocked a station supervisor who was directing passengers during an evacuation drill. Oscar is charged under s.5. His counsel argues that Oscar committed no offence because he was in the station, not "in the vicinity of" it. If the court rejects counsel's argument and convicts Oscar, which rule of statutory interpretation has the court most likely applied? A. The literal rule, because "in the vicinity of" clearly covers persons inside the station B. The golden rule, because a literal reading would produce the absurd result that obstructing staff outside the station is an offence but doing so inside the station is not C. The ejusdem generis rule, because "station" must be read in the same class as "vicinity" D. The mischief rule, because the court must always consider the four questions in Heydon's Case before applying any other rule Question 3 (MCQ) In 2019, the District Court decided Chan v Lee (a hypothetical case), holding that a particular contractual clause was enforceable. In 2023, the District Court decided Wong v Cheung , a different dispute raising the same point of law, and followed Chan v Lee . The losing party in Wong v Cheung appealed, and the Court of Appeal has now declared that the legal principle laid down in Chan v Lee was wrong and is no longer a binding authority. In relation to the doctrine of precedent, what has the Court of Appeal done to the principle in Chan v Lee ? A. It has reversed the principle in Chan v Lee B. It has distinguished the principle in Chan v Lee C. It has overruled the principle in Chan v Lee D. It has treated the principle in Chan v Lee as decided per incuriam Question 4 (MCQ) The Food and Health Bureau has made the Fruit Juice (Labelling) Regulation under powers conferred by a parent ordinance. The parent ordinance says nothing about whether the Regulation requires the Legislative Council's approval. The Regulation was published in the Government Gazette on 1 June and laid on the table of the Legislative Council at its next sitting. On 20 June (within 28 days of that sitting), the Legislative Council passed a resolution amending one schedule to the Regulation. Which of the following statements is correct? A. The Regulation is invalid because the parent ordinance did not expressly provide for Legislative Council scrutiny B. The Regulation was subject to the positive vetting procedure, and the Legislative Council could only approve or reject it, not amend it C. The Regulation was subject to the negative vetting procedure, and the Legislative Council was entitled to amend it by resolution within 28 days of the sitting D. The Regulation could only take effect after the Legislative Council had passed the resolution on 20 June Question 5 (Short answer — apply IRAC) Kelvin signed a contract to purchase a pre war tong lau (tenement building) in Sheung Wan from Doris for HK$40 million. The building is one of only a handful of its kind left in Hong Kong and has unique architectural features. A week before completion, Doris tells Kelvin she will not complete the sale because a third party has offered her HK$45 million. Kelvin does not want monetary compensation; he wants the building itself, and claims he is automatically entitled to a court order forcing Doris to complete the sale. Advise Kelvin on the nature of the remedy he seeks and whether he is entitled to it as of right. Your answer should identify the relevant source(s) of law and apply the principle(s) to the facts. End of quiz. No answers are provided in this file.

title: M10 Chapter 2: Principles of Contract and Consumer Law in Hong Kong (Part 1) — Phase 1 速查表 + Phase 2 閃卡
headings: M10 Chapter 2: Principles of Contract and Consumer Law in Hong Kong (Part 1) — Phase 1 速查表 + Phase 2 閃卡
A. Relevant Ordinances（Cap. number + section numbers，以 LP 所引為準）
B. Leading cases（full citations，按主題分組）
C. IRAC application points（落 scenario 嘅分析框架）
excerpt: M10 Chapter 2: Principles of Contract and Consumer Law in Hong Kong (Part 1) — Phase 1 速查表 + Phase 2 閃卡 Phase 1 速查表 Learning Objectives 1. Analyse the essential…
text: M10 Chapter 2: Principles of Contract and Consumer Law in Hong Kong (Part 1) — Phase 1 速查表 + Phase 2 閃卡 Phase 1 速查表 Learning Objectives 1. Analyse the essential elements in the formation of a contract (offer, acceptance, capacity, intention to create legal relations, consideration) and apply them to practical business scenarios. 2. Distinguish offers from invitations to treat, and apply the communication rules of acceptance (including the postal rule and its exceptions). 3. Evaluate the enforceability of promises through the doctrine of consideration and promissory estoppel. 4. Apply the rules on express and implied terms, and assess the validity of exemption clauses under the Control of Exemption Clauses Ordinance (Cap.71) and related statutes. 5. Advise on third party rights under the Contracts (Rights of Third Parties) Ordinance (Cap.623) and on unconscionable consumer contracts under the Unconscionable Contracts Ordinance (Cap.458). 必背考點 A. Relevant Ordinances（Cap. number + section numbers，以 LP 所引為準） Ordinance Key provisions Core rule Age of Majority (Related Provisions) Ordinance (Cap.410) s.2(1) A person under 18 lacks capacity to contract; contracts with minors are generally void, subject to exceptions (necessaries / beneficial employment / voidable contracts). Sale of Goods Ordinance (Cap.26) ('SOGO') s.4(2) Definition of 'necessaries' for minors — goods suitable to the minor's condition in life and actual requirements at the time of sale. SOGO (Cap.26) ss.14–17 Implied conditions in sale of goods: right to sell (s.14(1)(a)); correspondence with description (s.15(1)); merchantable quality (s.16(2)); bulk corresponding with sample (s.17(2)(a)). SOGO (Cap.26) s.60(b) At auction, each bid is an offer; acceptance occurs with the fall of the auctioneer's hammer. SOGO (Cap.26) ss.23(1), 24(1), 25 Nemo dat rule (s.23(1)); market overt exception for goods openly sold in a HK shop/market (s.24(1)); buyer acquires good title from a seller with voidable title not yet avoided, if in good faith without notice (s.25). (Detailed treatment in Ch.3.) Conveyancing and Property Ordinance (Cap.219) s.3(1) An agreement (or memorandum) for the disposition of land must be in writing and signed to be actionable. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties) Ordinance (Cap.623) ('CRTPO') s.3, s.4(1)(a), s.4(1)(b), s.4(2), s.4(3), s.4(6), s.5, s.6, s.8(2)–(4) Statutory exception to privity (in force 1 Jan 2016). Two enforceability tests: express provision (s.4(1)(a)) or term purporting to confer a benefit (s.4(1)(b), rebuttable under s.4(3)). Third party must be expressly identified (s.4(2)) and need not exist at formation (s.4(6)). Same remedies as contracting parties (s.5); restrictions on rescission/variation where third party has assented or relied (s.6); defences/set offs available against third party (s.8). Control of Exemption Clauses Ordinance (Cap.71) ('CECO') s.2(2)(a), s.4(1), s.5(1)(a)–(b) Applies to business liability; covers clauses excluding/limiting liability, rights or remedies. 'Dealing as a consumer' = party not contracting in the course of a business while the other party is (s.4(1)). CECO (Cap.71) s.7(1), s.7(2) Negligence liability: can NEVER exclude liability for death or personal injury caused by negligence (s.7(1)); other loss/damage from negligence can be excluded only if the term passes the reasonableness test (s.7(2)). CECO (Cap.71) s.8(1), (2)(a)–(b) Against a party dealing as consumer or on the other's written standard terms: breach of contract liability, or rendering substantially different/no performance, cannot be excluded unless reasonable. CECO (Cap.71) s.3(1), s.3(4), Sch.2 Reasonableness test: the term must be fair and reasonable to include, judged at the time the contract was MADE (not breach); burden of proof on the party relying on the clause; Sch.2 guidelines (bargaining strength, inducement, knowledge of the term, practicability of conditions, special order goods); s.3(4) — whether the language was understood (HK bilingual contracts). CECO (Cap.71) s.9(1), s.10, s.11(1)–(3), s.14 Indemnity clauses against consumers must be reasonable (s.9(1)); manufacturers' guarantees of consumer goods cannot exclude liability for defective goods/negligent manufacture (s.10); SOGO title undertakings (s.14 SOGO) cannot be excluded at all (s.11(1) CECO); SOGO ss.15–17 liabilities excludable in B2B only if reasonable (ss.11(3), 3(2)), never against a consumer (s.11(2)); no evasion via secondary contract (s.14). Supply of Services (Implied Terms) Ordinance (Cap.457) ('SSITO') ss.5, 6(1), 7(1), 8(1) Implied terms: reasonable care and skill (s.5); performance within a reasonable time if time not agreed (s.6(1)); reasonable charge if price not agreed (s.7(1)); cannot exempt liability to a consumer by contract term (s.8(1)). Misrepresentation Ordinance (Cap.284) ('MO') s.4 Any term excluding/restricting liability or remedies for misrepresentation (incl. non reliance clauses) is of no effect unless it satisfies the CECO s.3(1) reasonableness test. Unconscionable Contracts Ordinance (Cap.458) ('UCO') s.5(1), s.5(2), s.6(1), s.6(2)(a) Only covers consumer contracts for sale of goods/supply of services — NOT land, NOT B2B. Court may refuse to enforce, enforce the remainder, or revise the unconscionable part (s.5(1)); burden on the claimant (s.5(2)); non exhaustive factors e.g. bargaining strength (s.6(1)); disregard unconscionability from circumstances not reasonably foreseeable at formation (s.6(2)(a)). B. Leading cases（full citations，按主題分組） Offer vs invitation to treat / unilateral contracts Harvey v Facey (1893) AC 552 — a statement of the lowest price is a mere indication of price, not an offer. Clifton v Palumbo (1944) 2 All ER 497 — vague statement 'I am prepared to offer you my estate…' not sufficiently definite, especially for land. Partridge v Crittenden (1968) 1 WLR 1204 — advertisements are generally invitations to treat ('limited stock' rationale). Carlill v Carbolic Smoke Ball Co (1893) 1 QB 256 — reward advertisement = unilateral offer to the world; performing the stipulated act = acceptance; £1,000 bank deposit showed intention to be bound; inconvenience of use = consideration. Pharmaceutical Society of Great Britain v Boots Cash Chemists (Southern) Ltd (1953) 1 QB 401 — goods on self service shelves are invitations to treat; contract forms at the check out. Fisher v Bell (1961) 1 QB 394 — shop window display with price tag is an invitation to treat. Thornton v Shoe Lane Parking Ltd (1971) 2 QB 163 — automatic/vending machines are standing offers (no negotiation possible); contract forms when money is inserted, before the ticket issues. Harvela Investments Ltd v Royal Trust Co of Canada (CI) Ltd (1986) AC 207 — an invitation to tender promising to accept the most competitive bid is binding; referential bids impliedly forbidden. Termination of offers Byrne & Co v Van Tienhoven (1880) 5 CPD 344 — revocation is effective only when communicated to the offeree before acceptance. Shuey v US (1875) 92 US 73 — a reward offer to the public can be revoked via the same medium. Routledge v Grant (1828) 4 Bing 653 — an offer can be revoked before acceptance unless an option contract (supported by consideration) keeps it open. Ramsgate Victoria Hotel Co Ltd v Montefiore (1866) LR 1 Ex 109 — an offer lapses after a reasonable time. Acceptance Hyde v Wrench (1840) 3 Beav 334 — a counter offer destroys the original offer (mirror image rule). Stevenson, Jacques & Co v McLean (1880) 5 QBD 346 — a mere request for information does not destroy the offer. Butler Machine Tool Co Ltd v Ex Cell O Corp (England) Ltd (1979) 1 WLR 401 — battle of forms: the 'last shot' wins; sellers accepted the buyers' counter offer by returning the signed acknowledgment slip. Adams v Lindsell (1818) 1 B & Ald 681 — postal rule: posted acceptance is effective on posting. Holwell Securities Ltd v Hughes (1974) 1 WLR 155 — general rule: acceptance must be communicated; postal rule excluded where receipt is expressly/impliedly required. Household Fire and Carriage Accident Insurance Co Ltd v Grant (1879) 4 Ex D 216 — postal acceptance effective even if the letter is lost. R v Clarke (1927) 40 CLR 227 — a person cannot accept an offer in ignorance of it. Capacity / intention Proform Sports Management Ltd v Proactive Sports Management Ltd (2006) EWHC 2903 — a minor's contract (Wayne Rooney's agency contract) was voidable, not a contract for necessaries/apprenticeship. Hart v O'Connor (1985) AC 1000 — mental incapacity makes a contract voidable only if the other party knew of it; otherwise the incapacity is ignored. Balfour v Balfour (1919) 2 KB 571 — domestic agreements presumed not legally binding. Jones v Padavatton (1969) 1 WLR 328 — mother–daughter agreement: presumption not rebutted. Wu Chiu Kuen v Chu Shui Ching (1992) HKCU 29 — HK example where the domestic/social presumption WAS rebutted. World Food Fair Ltd v Hong Kong Island Development Ltd (2007) 1 HKLRD 498 — 'subject to contract' rebuts (though not conclusively) the commercial presumption. Consideration Currie v Misa (1875) LR 10 Ex 153 — classic definition: some right/interest/profit/benefit to one party, or forbearance/detriment/loss/responsibility of the other. Tweddle v Atkinson (1861) 1 B & S 393 — consideration must move from the promisee; also an authority for privity. Chappell & Co Ltd v Nestle Co Ltd (1960) AC 87 — consideration must be sufficient (some value, even chocolate wrappers) but need not be adequate. Roscorla v Thomas (1842) 3 QB 234 — past consideration is no consideration. Pao On v Lau Yiu Long (1980) AC 614 — three requirements for the 'implied assumpsit' exception (act at promisor's request; understanding of remuneration; enforceability if promised in advance); also: performance of a duty owed to a third party is good consideration. Lampleigh v Brathwait (1615) Hob 105 — request exception to past consideration. Collins v Godefroy (1831) 1 B & Ad 950 — performance of an existing duty imposed by law is no consideration. Glasbrook Brothers Ltd v Glamorgan County Council (1925) AC 270 — doing MORE than a legal duty is good consideration. Scotson v Pegg (1861) 6 Hurl & N 295 — performance of an existing duty owed to a third party is good consideration. Stilk v Myrick (1809) 2 Camp 317 — performance of an existing duty owed to the promisor is no consideration (deserting sailors). Hartley v Ponsonby (1857) 7 E & B 872 — contrast: voyage became so dangerous that remaining crew did more than their existing duty. Williams v Roffey Bros & Nicholls (Contractors) Ltd (1991) 1 QB 1 — 'practical benefit' exception for promises to pay more (six strict criteria; no economic duress/fraud). UBC (Construction) Ltd v Sung Foo Kee Ltd (1993) 2 HKLR 207 — HK application of Williams v Roffey. Pinnel's Case (1602) 5 Co Rep 117a — part payment of a debt is no consideration for discharging the whole debt; needs fresh consideration (e.g. horse, hawk, robe, or earlier payment). Foakes v Beer (1884) 9 App Cas 605 — House of Lords confirmed Pinnel's Case; Re Selectmove Ltd (1995) 1 WLR 474 — practical benefit analysis does NOT apply to promises to accept less (stare decisis). Promissory estoppel Central London Property Ltd v High Trees House Ltd (1947) KB 130 — the foundational case; estoppel suspended (not extinguished) the landlord's right to full rent for 1940–1945. Combe v Combe (1951) 2 KB 215 — estoppel is a shield, not a sword; consideration remains 'a cardinal necessity'. Tool Metal Manufacturing Co Ltd v Tungsten Electric Co Ltd (1955) 1 WLR 761 — promisor may withdraw the promise on reasonable notice (suspensory effect). Collier v P & MJ Wright (Holdings) Ltd (2008) 1 WLR 643 — estoppel may extinguish the balance where creditor voluntarily accepted part payment and debtor relied; NOT yet followed in HK. Luo Xing Juan v Estate of Hui Shui See (2009) 12 HKCFAR 1 — HK CFA on the inequitability element. Mistake / privity Smith v Hughes (1871) LR 6 QB 597 — objective approach; mistake as to quality/collateral matter ≠ mistake as to terms; caveat emptor. Hartog v Colin and Shields (1939) 3 All ER 566 — if one party knows the other is mistaken as to a term, the contract cannot be enforced against the mistaken party. Cundy v Lindsay (1878) 3 App Cas 459 — written contract with a rogue impersonating a KNOWN, identifiable firm: void ab initio for mistake as to identity. King's Norton Metal Co v Edridge Merrett & Co Ltd (1897) 14 TLR 98 — no known existing entity impersonated: mistake only as to attributes (creditworthiness); contract not void. Ingram v Little (1961) 1 QB 31 — face to face presumption rebutted where identity was essential to the contract (not just payment); of questionable authority. Lewis v Avery (1972) 1 QB 198 — face to face presumption NOT rebutted; mistake as to attribute only. Shogun Finance Ltd v Hudson (2004) 1 AC 919 — the face to face presumption is strong; rebutted only in rare cases (e.g. impersonating a family member/personal acquaintance). Saunders v Anglia Building Society (sub nom Gallie v Lee) (1971) AC 1004 — non est factum: document must be essentially different in substance or kind; signer must also have exercised reasonable care. Lewis v Clay (1897) 67 LJ QB 224 — non est factum succeeded: signer mistaken as to the CAPACITY in which he signed (thought he was witnessing). L'Estrange v E Graucob Ltd (1934) 2 KB 394 — a signature binds the signer to unread terms. Dunlop Pneumatic Tyre Co Ltd v Selfridge & Co Ltd (1915) AC 847 — privity: only a party to the contract can sue on it. Beswick v Beswick (1968) AC 58 — widow could not sue personally (no privity) but succeeded as administratrix of the estate. Shanklin Pier Ltd v Detel Products Ltd (1951) 2 KB 854 — collateral contract as a common law circumvention of privity. Terms / exemption clauses Chan Yeuk Yu v Church Body of the Hong Kong Sheng Kung Hui (2001) 1 HKC 621 — 'regal surroundings for the select few' = mere puff (HK). Heilbut Symons & Co v Buckleton (1913) AC 30 — term vs representation determined objectively by intention; guiding principles are rebuttable. Dick Bentley Productions Ltd v Harold Smith (Motors) Ltd (1965) 1 WLR 623 — statement by a party with specialist knowledge (car dealer on mileage) = term. Oscar Chess v Williams (1957) 1 WLR 370 — contrast: private seller without specialist knowledge = representation. Bannerman v White (1861) 10 CB NS 844 — statement of crucial importance to the buyer (sulphur free hops) = term. Curtis v Chemical Cleaning and Dyeing Co (1951) 1 KB 805 — misrepresentation of the extent of an exemption clause defeats reliance on it, despite signature. Parker v South Eastern Railway Co (1876–1877) LR 2 CPD 416 — reasonable notice test for unsigned documents. Chapelton v Barry Urban District Council (1940) 1 KB 532 — a mere receipt/voucher has no contractual status. Olley v Marlborough Court Ltd (1949) 1 KB 532 — notice after formation (hotel bedroom notice) is too late. Interfoto Picture Library Ltd v Stiletto Visual Programmes Ltd (1989) QB 433 — particularly onerous/unusual terms need a HIGHER degree of notice. McCutcheon v David MacBrayne Ltd (1964) 1 WLR 125 — course of dealings requires CONSISTENT past dealings on the same terms. The Moorcock (1889) 14 PD 64 — business efficacy test (implied in fact). Shirlaw v Southern Foundries (1926) Ltd (1939) 2 KB 206 — officious bystander test ('Oh, of course!'). Marks & Spencer Plc v BNP Paribas Securities Services Trust Co (Jersey) Ltd (2015) UKSC 72 — implied terms: reasonableness alone is not sufficient. Kensland Realty Ltd v Whale View Investment Ltd (2001) 4 HKCFAR 381 — HK CFA: a party cannot take advantage of its own breach of an implied term. Liverpool City Council v Irwin (1977) AC 239 — term implied in law as essential to landlord–tenant relations. R & B Customs Brokers Co Ltd v United Dominions Trust Ltd (1988) 1 WLR 321 — a company can 'deal as a consumer' if the transaction is not integral to its business and not regularly entered into. George Mitchell (Chesterhall) Ltd v Finney Lock Seeds Ltd (1983) 2 AC 803 — reasonableness is fact dependent; appellate courts interfere only if plainly and obviously wrong. Shum Kit Ching v Caesar Beauty Centre Ltd (2003) 3 HKLRD 422 — HK case on the UCO: 'no refund' clause unenforceable; pre payment not a forfeitable deposit. C. IRAC application points（落 scenario 嘅分析框架） 1. Offer vs invitation to treat — Issue: is the communication an offer or an ITT? Rule: definitions + established categories (advertisements/shop displays/websites/tenders/auctions). Application: check the exact wording ('will go to the first 500 replies' → unilateral offer; 'for sale' price tag → ITT); objective intention from the language. Conclusion: state who makes the offer and when the contract forms (e.g. at check out — Boots). 2. Counter offer vs request for information — Rule: mirror image rule (Hyde v Wrench); even a slight variation destroys the offer; asking about flexibility is not a counter offer (Stevenson v McLean). Application: compare the reply word by word with the offer; in battle of forms scenarios, identify the 'last shot' and any acceptance by conduct (Butler Machine Tool). 3. Revocation — Rule: effective only when communicated before acceptance (Byrne v Van Tienhoven); for unilateral offers to the world, revocation via the same medium suffices (Shuey v US). Application: timeline analysis — date of offer, posting of acceptance, receipt, revocation; check whether the postal rule is excluded ('replies received'). 4. Capacity — Rule: minors void subject to necessaries (s.4(2) SOGO) / beneficial employment / voidable contracts (Cap.410 s.2(1)); mental incapacity voidable only if the other party knew (Hart v O'Connor). Application: classify the contract first (necessaries? employment? interest in land/shares/partnership?). 5. Intention to create legal relations — Rule: domestic/social → presumed not binding (Balfour v Balfour); commercial → strong presumption of binding, rebuttable e.g. by 'subject to contract'. Application: identify context, then look for rebutting evidence (detrimental reliance, bank deposit as in Carlill). 6. Consideration — Rule checklist: moved from promisee? sufficient (not adequate)? past (Roscorla v Thomas; Pao On exception)? existing duty (which type — by law / owed to third party / owed to promisor)? part payment (Pinnel/Foakes; exceptions: composition agreements, third party payment)? Application: map the promise to one of the categories before concluding enforceability; do not confuse with privity or promissory estoppel. 7. Promissory estoppel — Rule: (1) clear promise not to insist on strict rights; (2) reliance; (3) inequitable to renege; suspensory only; shield not sword (High Trees; Combe v Combe). Application: estoppel can only DEFEND; if the promisee is the plaintiff claiming extra payment, estoppel fails — look to Williams v Roffey consideration instead. 8. Exemption clauses — Three step analysis: (1) incorporation (signature — L'Estrange, subject to misrepresentation — Curtis; reasonable notice before/at formation — Parker, Olley, Thornton; higher notice for onerous terms — Interfoto; consistent course of dealings — McCutcheon); (2) construction — does the wording cover the liability (contra proferentem)?; (3) statutory validity — CECO: death/PI negligence can never be excluded (s.7(1)); other negligence loss needs reasonableness (s.7(2)); consumer/standard terms breach liability needs reasonableness (s.8); SOGO implied undertakings in consumer contracts cannot be excluded (s.11(2)); reasonableness judged at formation, burden on the party relying (s.3(1), Sch.2). 9. Third party rights — Rule: privity burden/benefit rules (Dunlop v Selfridge); CRTPO s.4 two tests + s.4(2) identification + s.4(3) rebuttal. Application: check first whether the contract expressly excludes CRTPO ('A person who is not a party… shall have no right…'), then whether the third party is identified by name/class/description. 10. UCO (Cap.458) — Rule: consumer goods/services only; unconscionability is a HIGH threshold (higher than 'unfairness'); court's three powers under s.5(1). Application: raise UCO only after CECO/MO/SSITO fail; expect rare success (LRC: 'extreme cases, very rare'). 易混淆概念對比 Table 1: Counter offer vs Request for Information vs Mere Puff vs Invitation to Treat Counter offer Request for information Invitation to treat / puff Effect on original offer DESTROYS the original offer (Hyde v Wrench (1840) 3 Beav 334) Offer survives (Stevenson, Jacques & Co v McLean (1880) 5 QBD 346) No offer exists yet — the other party's response IS the offer (Partridge v Crittenden) Language test 'I will give you HK$90,000' (a definite varied proposal) 'Would you accept HK$90,000?' (an enquiry about flexibility) Advertisement / display / marketing rhetoric 點樣分辨 睇語氣：係咪一個確定性、可即時被接受嘅新提議？係 → counter offer。只係查詢、留有空間 → request for information。ITT 就係連 offer 都未出現，對方先係 offeror。 考試伏位 Mirror image rule 極嚴：微小改動（例如現金代替支票）都係 counter offer。考生常誤以為「合理嘅小修改」唔會 destroy offer——會！（Jones v Daniel） Table 2: Promissory Estoppel vs Consideration (Williams v Roffey practical benefit) vs Part payment (Foakes v Beer) Promissory estoppel Practical benefit (pay MORE) Promise to accept LESS Leading authority Central London Property Ltd v High Trees House Ltd (1947) KB 130 Williams v Roffey Bros & Nicholls (Contractors) Ltd (1991) 1 QB 1 Pinnel's Case (1602) 5 Co Rep 117a; Foakes v Beer (1884) 9 App Cas 605 Consideration needed? No — relies on promise + reliance + inequitability No fresh detriment needed if promisor obtains a practical benefit (strict 6 criteria) Yes — part payment alone is never consideration; needs fresh consideration (e.g. early payment, chattel) Effect Suspensory, not extinctive; shield not sword (Combe v Combe (1951) 2 KB 215) Makes the promise to pay more enforceable Promise unenforceable; practical benefit analysis does NOT apply (Re Selectmove (1995) 1 WLR 474); exceptions: composition agreements; third party part payment 點樣分辨 邊個係原告？promisee 用 estoppel 告人 → 死（shield not sword）。Promisor 追返權利、promisee 防守 → estoppel。承諾「俾多啲」搵 Williams v Roffey；承諾「收少啲」搵 Foakes v Beer，千祈唔好將 practical benefit 套用落去收少啲嗰邊。 考試伏位 考生常犯：promisee 做 plaintiff 仲用 estoppel；或者將 Williams v Roffey 用落 part payment of debt。留意 Collier v P & MJ Wright (2008) 未獲香港跟隨。 Phase 2 閃卡 Card 1 Front: What distinguishes an offer from an invitation to treat, and how are (a) newspaper advertisements, (b) shop shelf displays and (c) reward advertisements classified? Back: Offer = an expression of willingness to contract on specified terms without further negotiation; ITT = a statement indicating a willingness to receive offers. (a) Newspaper advertisements: generally ITTs (Partridge v Crittenden (1968) 1 WLR 1204) — the 'limited stock' rationale. (b) Shop shelf displays: ITTs; the contract forms at check out (Pharmaceutical Society of Great Britain v Boots Cash Chemists (Southern) Ltd (1953) 1 QB 401; Fisher v Bell (1961) 1 QB 394 for window displays). (c) Reward advertisements: offers in unilateral contracts — performance of the stipulated act is acceptance (Carlill v Carbolic Smoke Ball Co (1893) 1 QB 256). 💬 白話解釋：記住大原則——廣告、貨架陳列、網站基本上都係「請你出價」(ITT)，即係話客人才係 offeror。唯一大例外係懸賞廣告：因為做咗個動作已經係 acceptance，如果當佢 ITT，登廣告嘅人就可以免費享受成果，唔公平，所以 Carlill 案訂明呢類係 unilateral offer。 Card 2 Front: State the mirror image rule and its consequences, and distinguish a counter offer from a request for information, with authority. Back: Acceptance must be an unconditional assent to ALL terms of the offer — any variation, however minor, is a counter offer (mirror image rule; Jones v Daniel (1984) 2 Ch 332). A counter offer destroys the original offer, which can no longer be accepted (Hyde v Wrench (1840) 3 Beav 334). A mere request for information (e.g. asking about flexibility on terms) does NOT destroy the offer (Stevenson, Jacques & Co v McLean (1880) 5 QBD 346). Battle of forms: the party whose correspondence was the 'last shot' wins; acceptance can occur by conduct, e.g. taking delivery (Butler Machine Tool Co Ltd v Ex Cell O Corp (England) Ltd (1979) 1 WLR 401). 💬 白話解釋：Acceptance 要一模一樣，改少少都當你開咗個新 offer，原本嗰個即刻冧咗。但「問吓價」唔算還價——關鍵係個回覆係咪一個可以即時被接受嘅確定提議。商業上雙方用自己 standard terms 你來我往，邊個「最後一槍」就用邊個嘅條款。 Card 3 Front: When is a revocation of an offer effective, and how can an offer made to the public be revoked? What is the postal rule and its limits? Back: Revocation is effective only when communicated to the offeree BEFORE acceptance (Byrne & Co v Van Tienhoven (1880) 5 CPD 344); an option contract (consideration given to keep the offer open) prevents revocation (Routledge v Grant (1828) 4 Bing 653). A public/unilateral offer can be revoked through the same medium, e.g. the same newspaper (Shuey v US (1875) 92 US 73). Postal rule: a posted acceptance is effective on posting, even if lost or delayed (Adams v Lindsell (1818) 1 B & Ald 681; Household Fire and Carriage Accident Insurance Co Ltd v Grant (1879) 4 Ex D 216). Limits: applies only to acceptances (not offers/revocations); only where post is a reasonable mode; excluded where the offeror requires receipt, expressly or impliedly (Holwell Securities Ltd v Hughes (1974) 1 WLR 155); not applicable if the letter was wrongly addressed by the offeree. 💬 白話解釋：撤銷 offer 要對方收到先算數，而且必須喺 acceptance 之前。郵寄規則係特例：acceptance 一放入郵筒就生效——但只限 acceptance，offer 同 revocation 唔適用；如果 offer 話明「收到為準」，郵寄規則就被排除。 Card 4 Front: What are the rules on minors' capacity to contract in Hong Kong, and how does mental incapacity affect a contract? Back: Under s.2(1) of the Age of Majority (Related Provisions) Ordinance (Cap.410), a person under 18 generally lacks capacity; contracts with minors are void, subject to exceptions. Binding: contracts for necessaries (s.4(2) SOGO — goods suitable to condition in life and actual requirements) and beneficial employment/apprenticeship contracts. Voidable: contracts acquiring interests in land, shares, or partnerships — the minor may repudiate before 18 or within a reasonable time after; money paid is recoverable only on total failure of consideration (Steinberg v Scala (Leeds) Ltd (1923) 2 Ch 452; Proform Sports Management Ltd v Proactive Sports Management Ltd (2006) EWHC 2903). Mental incapacity: contract voidable only if, at formation, the person could not understand the nature of the transaction AND the other party knew of the incapacity (Hart v O'Connor (1985) AC 1000); bound by necessaries (s.4 SOGO). 💬 白話解釋：未成年合約三大類——必需品同有益僱傭有效；土地、股份、合夥係「可撤銷」，未成年一方可以話唔玩；其他一概無效。精神無行為能力就睇兩樣嘢：當時係咪真係唔明白，同埋對方知唔知——對方唔知就當你正常。 Card 5 Front: State the rules on past consideration and its exception, with authority. Back: Past consideration is no consideration: an act performed before the promise was not given in exchange for it (Roscorla v Thomas (1842) 3 QB 234; Re McArdle (1951) Ch 669). Exception ('implied assumpsit'): per Pao On v Lau Yiu Long (1980) AC 614 — (1) the act was done at the promisor's request; (2) the parties understood the act would be remunerated; (3) the promise would have been legally enforceable if made before the act. Classic illustration: Lampleigh v Brathwait (1615) Hob 105. Also: consideration must move from the promisee but need not move to the promisor; sufficient but need not be adequate (Chappell & Co Ltd v Nestle Co Ltd (1960) AC 87). 💬 白話解釋：「做完先講」唔計數——個動作唔係為咗換個承諾而做，就唔係 consideration。例外係：你按對方要求做、大家心知肚明有報酬、而報酬承諾本身合法——咁即使承諾喺行動之後先講，都可以強制執行。 Card 6 Front: To what extent can performance of an existing obligation be good consideration? Back: Duty imposed by law: NO consideration (Collins v Godefroy (1831) 1 B & Ad 950); but doing MORE than the legal duty is good consideration (Glasbrook Brothers Ltd v Glamorgan County Council (1925) AC 270; Ward v Byham (1956) 1 WLR 496). Duty owed to a third party: YES, good consideration (Scotson v Pegg (1861) 6 Hurl & N 295; New Zealand Shipping Co Ltd v AM Satterthwaite & Co Ltd (The Eurymedon) (1975) AC 154; Pao On v Lau Yiu Long (1980) AC 614). Duty owed to the promisor: NO consideration (Stilk v Myrick (1809) 2 Camp 317); exceptions — doing more than obliged (Hartley v Ponsonby (1857) 7 E & B 872) or promisor obtains a practical benefit under the six strict criteria, absent duress/fraud (Williams v Roffey Bros & Nicholls (Contractors) Ltd (1991) 1 QB 1; UBC (Construction) Ltd v Sung Foo Kee Ltd (1993) 2 HKLR 207). Part payment of a debt: never consideration for discharging the whole debt (Pinnel's Case (1602) 5 Co Rep 117a; Foakes v Beer (1884) 9 App Cas 605); practical benefit does not apply (Re Selectmove Ltd (1995) 1 WLR 474). 💬 白話解釋：三步分類法——法定義務：唔得，超額先得；欠第三方嘅約定義務：得；欠承諾人自己嘅：唔得，除非做超咗或者對方有實際利益。借錢還少咗永遠唔算 consideration，呢條線千祈唔好用 Williams v Roffey 兜過去。 Card 7 Front: What is promissory estoppel, what are its criteria, and what are its two key limitations? Back: Definition: where a promisor promises not to enforce strict contractual rights and the promisee relies on it, the promisor may be prevented from reneging (Central London Property Ltd v High Trees House Ltd (1947) KB 130). Criteria: (1) a clear promise not to insist on existing rights; (2) reliance by the promisee (detriment not strictly necessary); (3) it would be inequitable to go back on the promise (Luo Xing Juan v Estate of Hui Shui See (2009) 12 HKCFAR 1). Limitation 1 — suspensory, not extinctive: rights are suspended, not extinguished; the promisor may resume them on reasonable notice (Tool Metal Manufacturing Co Ltd v Tungsten Electric Co Ltd (1955) 1 WLR 761). For instalment debts, rights accruing during the suspensory period may be extinguished. Limitation 2 — a shield, not a sword: it is a defence only, never a cause of action (Combe v Combe (1951) 2 KB 215). 💬 白話解釋：Estoppel 係平衡法上嘅「反口唔得」原則——你應承咗唔追，對方信咗你，你就要守信用。但記住兩點：佢只係暫停你嘅權利（可以合理通知後恢復），而且只可以做擋箭牌，唔可以拎嚟告人。 Card 8 Front: Under the Control of Exemption Clauses Ordinance (Cap.71), which liabilities can never be excluded, which require reasonableness, and how is reasonableness assessed? Back: Never excludable: liability for death or personal injury resulting from negligence (s.7(1) CECO); seller's implied undertakings as to title under s.14 SOGO (s.11(1) CECO); SOGO ss.15–17 liabilities as against a person dealing as a consumer (s.11(2) CECO); liability to a consumer under the SSITO (s.8(1) SSITO). Reasonableness required: other loss/damage from negligence (s.7(2) CECO); breach of contract liability against a consumer or on written standard terms (s.8 CECO); indemnity clauses against consumers (s.9(1)); SOGO ss.15–17 liabilities in B2B contracts (ss.11(3), 3(2)); misrepresentation exemption/non reliance clauses (s.4 MO (Cap.284) + s.3(1) CECO). Reasonableness test (s.3(1) CECO): fair and reasonable to include, judged at the time the contract was MADE; burden on the party relying on the clause; Sch.2 guidelines (bargaining strength, inducement, knowledge of the term, practicability of compliance, special order goods); appellate deference unless plainly and obviously wrong (George Mitchell (Chesterhall) Ltd v Finney Lock Seeds Ltd (1983) 2 AC 803). 💬 白話解釋：記住金字塔——頂層係「永遠唔可以豁免」：疏忽致死傷、賣方業權、消費者嘅 SOGO 貨品質素責任。中層係「過到 reasonableness test 先得」：其他疏忽損失、消費者/標準條款違約責任、misrepresentation 免責條款。合理性以簽約當刻衡量，舉證責任喺靠條款嗰方。 本章急救詞彙 EN Term 繁中白話 English Model Sentence Invitation to treat 邀請出價——唔係 offer，對方回應先係 offer A shop window display of goods with a price tag is merely an invitation to treat (Fisher v Bell (1961) 1 QB 394). Unilateral contract 單方合約——一方出承諾，另一方以行動接受 A reward advertisement constitutes a unilateral offer which is accepted by performance of the stipulated act (Carlill v Carbolic Smoke Ball Co (1893) 1 QB 256). Mirror image rule 照鏡規則——acceptance 必須同 offer 完全一樣 Any variation of the offer's terms constitutes a counter offer which destroys the original offer (Hyde v Wrench (1840) 3 Beav 334). Consideration 約因——用嚟換對方承諾嘅代價，必須有價值但唔需要等值 Consideration must be sufficient but need not be adequate (Chappell & Co Ltd v Nestle Co Ltd (1960) AC 87). Past consideration 過去約因——承諾之前已做嘅行為，原則上唔算數 A promise made after the act has been performed is supported only by past consideration and is unenforceable (Roscorla v Thomas (1842) 3 QB 234). Promissory estoppel 承諾性禁止反言——只可防守、只暫停權利 Promissory estoppel operates as a shield, not a sword, and is suspensory rather than extinctive (Combe v Combe (1951) 2 KB 215). Privity of contract 合約相對性——非合約方無權利無義務 Under the benefit rule, a third party cannot enforce a term of a contract to which he is not privy, subject to the CRTPO (Cap.623). Reasonableness test 合理性測試——以簽約當刻衡量，舉證責任喺依賴條款一方 Under s.3(1) of the CECO (Cap.71), the clause must be fair and reasonable to include having regard to circumstances known or contemplated when the contract was made.
