text: M10 Chapter 2: Principles of Contract and Consumer Law in Hong Kong (Part 1) — Phase 3 Model Answers Q1 — Answer: B Model Answer (EN): Issue: whether the window display constituted an offer capable of acceptance by Marcus. Rule: a shop window display of goods with a price tag is an invitation to treat, not an offer (Fisher v Bell (1961) 1 QB 394; Pharmaceutical Society of Great Britain v Boots Cash Chemists (Southern) Ltd (1953) 1 QB 401). The customer makes the offer when presenting the goods (or the price) to the shop, which the shop is free to accept or reject. Application: the display of the Rolex with the HK$88,000 tag was an invitation to treat; Marcus's tender of HK$88,000 was his offer. Golden Hour Jewellery Ltd never accepted it. Conclusion: no contract was formed and the shop is not bound to sell at the displayed price. 解題思路（繁中）: 呢題係經典「櫥窗陳列 = invitation to treat」考點。Option A 係最常見錯誤：Carlill 嘅例外只適用於懸賞式 unilateral contract（承諾任何人完成指定行動即有獎賞），一個標價牌唔係向全世界出嘅懸賞。Option C 將 Thornton v Shoe Lane Parking 嘅「standing offer」亂套——嗰個係針對自動售票機（無法議價嘅機器），櫥窗展示背後有店主可以議價，所以唔係 standing offer。Option D 係混淆視聽：unilateral mistake as to terms 嘅前提係已經有合約（Hartog v Colin and Shields），呢度根本連 offer 都未成立，唔使講 mistake。記住答呢類題要先問「邊個先出 offer」——喺舖頭情境永遠係客人出 offer。 Rule Check: Fisher v Bell (1961) 1 QB 394; Pharmaceutical Society of Great Britain v Boots Cash Chemists (Southern) Ltd (1953) 1 QB 401 Common Trap（繁中）: 見到「標錯價」就急住答 mistake——其實第一層 issue 係 offer vs invitation to treat；陳列品從來唔係 offer，後面所有 mistake 分析都係多餘。另外唔好一見「advertisement/display」就諗 Carlill；Carlill 只限 reward/unilateral contract。 Q2 — Answer: C Model Answer (EN): Under s.7(1) of the Control of Exemption Clauses Ordinance (Cap.71), a person cannot, by reference to any contract term, exclude or restrict his/her business liability for death or personal injury resulting from negligence. The prohibition is absolute — the reasonableness test does not apply. By contrast, s.7(2) permits exclusion of liability for OTHER loss or damage caused by negligence (e.g. property damage, financial loss) only if the term satisfies the reasonableness test in s.3(1). Section 8 deals with liability arising in contract against a consumer or a party on the other's written standard terms (reasonableness required), and s.5(1) of the UCO (Cap.458) deals with unconscionable consumer contracts generally, not negligence liability. 解題思路（繁中）: 呢題考 pinpoint section knowledge。CECO 嘅結構要背熟：s.7 管疏忽責任，(1) 死傷 = 絕對唔可以豁免；(2) 其他損失 = 過 reasonableness test 先得。Option A (s.7(2)) 係「可以豁免但要合理」——掉轉咗。Option B (s.8(1)) 係違約責任（consumer/standard terms），唔係疏忽致死傷。Option D 係 UCO，佢管 unconscionable terms 整體，而且舉證門檻高、唔係「絕對禁止」。考試伏位：題目關鍵字係 "IMPOSSIBLE, in any circumstances"——CECO 入面絕對禁止嘅就只有 s.7(1) 同 s.11(1)（SOGO s.14 業權承諾）呢兩類。 Rule Check: Control of Exemption Clauses Ordinance (Cap.71) s.7(1), s.7(2), s.8(1); Unconscionable Contracts Ordinance (Cap.458) s.5(1) Common Trap（繁中）: s.7(1) 同 s.7(2) 掉亂——死傷永遠唔得豁免，財物損失可以先要過合理性測試。背誦口訣：「死傷絕對，財損合理」。 Q3 — Answer: B Model Answer (EN): Issue: whether Daniel's day 3 email destroyed Karen's offer. Rule: acceptance must mirror the offer exactly; a counter offer destroys the original offer (Hyde v Wrench (1840) 3 Beav 334), but a mere request for information — an enquiry about the flexibility of the terms — leaves the offer intact (Stevenson, Jacques & Co v McLean (1880) 5 QBD 346). Application: Daniel's day 3 email ("would you consider HK$320,000…?") was framed as an enquiry, not a definite varied proposal capable of immediate acceptance; it is therefore a request for information and Karen's offer of HK$350,000 remained open. Karen had stipulated the offer would remain open for 14 days, so it had not lapsed by day 9. Daniel's day 9 email was an unconditional, mirror image acceptance, communicated to Karen. Conclusion: a binding contract was formed on day 9 at HK$350,000; Karen must sell. 解題思路（繁中）: 呢題係 mirror image rule 嘅 classic twist。分辨 counter offer 同 request for information 要睇措辭：「Would you consider…?」係探問彈性，唔係一個可以即時 accept 嘅確定提議——如果 Daniel 寫「I will pay HK$320,000 in six instalments」，咁先係 counter offer（Hyde v Wrench）。Option C 唔得：Karen 自己講明 offer 開放 14 日，day 9 遠未過期，冇 lapse of time 問題（Ramsgate 係講冇指明期限先按合理時間計）。Option D 錯：silence 唔係 acceptance，acceptance 必須 communicated（雖然可以有 acceptance by conduct，但 Karen 完全冇任何行為）。 Rule Check: Stevenson, Jacques & Co v McLean (1880) 5 QBD 346; Hyde v Wrench (1840) 3 Beav 334 Common Trap（繁中）: 見到個回覆提咗另一個價錢就即刻答「counter offer destroyed the offer」——呢個正正係考官預設嘅錯誤。一定要逐字分析個回覆：係確定性建議定係查詢？考試伏位第二層：就算係 counter offer，原本 offer 只係 destroyed，唔係話 offeror 之後可以默認接受。 Q4 — Answer: B Model Answer (EN): Issue: whether Sparky's completion of work it was already contractually obliged to perform is good consideration for BrightBuild's promise of an extra HK$150,000. Rule: performance of an existing contractual duty owed to the promisor is generally no consideration (Stilk v Myrick (1809) 2 Camp 317), but under Williams v Roffey Bros & Nicholls (Contractors) Ltd (1991) 1 QB 1 (applied in Hong Kong in UBC (Construction) Ltd v Sung Foo Kee Ltd (1993) 2 HKLR 207), the promise is enforceable where: (1) A has contracted to do work for B; (2) before completion, B has reason to doubt A will complete; (3) B promises extra payment for on time performance; (4) B thereby obtains a practical benefit or obviates a disbenefit; (5) there is no economic duress or fraud by A; and (6) the benefit is capable of being consideration. Application: all criteria are met — BrightBuild doubted timely completion, promised the extra HK$150,000, and obtained practical benefits: avoiding the HK$500,000 late completion penalty under the main contract and avoiding the trouble and expense of engaging a replacement subcontractor; there was no duress or fraud. Conclusion: the promise is supported by consideration and Sparky can enforce the HK$150,000. 解題思路（繁中）: 呢題係「promises to pay more」嘅 standard scenario。Option A 係半對：Stilk v Myrick 係 general rule，但 Williams v Roffey 係公認嘅 refined exception，答 A 即係忽略咗 practical benefit。Option C 係張冠李戴：Pinnel's Case 係「promises to accept LESS」（還少咗債）嘅 rule，唔適用於「俾多啲」，而且 Sparky 係完全履行唔係 partial payment。Option D 係 Exam Lens 特別警告嘅陷阱：promissory estoppel 係 shield not a sword（Combe v Combe (1951) 2 KB 215）——Sparky 係原告拎嚟告人，estoppel 即刻死。六項 criteria 要逐條對落事實，特別係 (4) practical benefit（避咗 penalty clause + 避咗搵替工嘅麻煩）同 (5) 無 duress/fraud。 Rule Check: Williams v Roffey Bros & Nicholls (Contractors) Ltd (1991) 1 QB 1; Stilk v Myrick (1809) 2 Camp 317; Combe v Combe (1951) 2 KB 215 Common Trap（繁中）: 兩大陷阱：(1) 將 Williams v Roffey 嘅 practical benefit 套用落「收少啲」嘅債務減免——唔得，Re Selectmove Ltd (1995) 1 WLR 474 話明 Foakes v Beer 繼續管住 part payment；(2) 原告身份用 estoppel。答題口訣：「俾多用 Roffey，收少用 Foakes，告人唔好用 estoppel」。 Q5 — Answer: C Model Answer (EN): Issue: whether Clause 12 validly excludes FitZone's liability for (a) Ms. Wong's personal injury and (b) her damaged smartphone. Rule: assuming incorporation (the clause was in a signed document — L'Estrange v E Graucob Ltd (1934) 2 KB 394) and clear wording, statutory control applies. Under s.7(1) of the Control of Exemption Clauses Ordinance (Cap.71), business liability for death or personal injury resulting from negligence can NEVER be excluded or restricted. Under s.7(2), liability for other loss or damage (e.g. property damage) resulting from negligence may be excluded only if the term satisfies the reasonableness test in s.3(1) — the term must be fair and reasonable to include having regard to circumstances known or contemplated when the contract was made, and the burden of proving reasonableness rests on FitZone, with reference to the Schedule 2 guidelines (relative bargaining strength, inducement, knowledge of the term, etc.). Application: FitZone's negligent failure to maintain the treadmill caused the fractured wrist — Clause 12 is wholly ineffective as to that claim regardless of reasonableness. As to the smartphone (property damage), the clause is effective only if FitZone discharges its burden of proving reasonableness; against a consumer signing non negotiable standard terms, this may be difficult. Conclusion: Ms. Wong can recover for her injury in full; recovery for the smartphone depends on the reasonableness test. 解題思路（繁中）: 呢題係 exemption clause 三步曲嘅全面應用：(1) incorporation——簽咗名表面上有约束，(2) construction——「howsoever caused, including negligence」字眼夠闊，(3) statutory validity——先至係勝負關鍵。Option A 係典型「簽咗就係咁」陷阱：L'Estrange 只係解決 incorporation，完全唔過問 CECO 嘅 statutory control。Option B 矯枉過正：CECO 唔係一刀切禁止所有 negligence 免責——財物損失過到 reasonableness test 就得（s.7(2)）。Option D 係錯嘅法律工具：UCO (Cap.458) 管嘅係 exemption clause 以外嘅 unconscionable terms；exemption clause 嘅主戰場係 CECO，而且 UCO 嘅「revise or alter」權力從未用過、門檻極高。答題次序好重要：personal injury 先答 s.7(1)（絕對無效），財物先答 s.7(2) + s.3(1)（要過合理性測試，舉證責任喺 FitZone）。 Rule Check: Control of Exemption Clauses Ordinance (Cap.71) s.7(1), s.7(2), s.3(1), Sch.2; L'Estrange v E Graucob Ltd (1934) 2 KB 394 Common Trap（繁中）: 三大伏位：(1) 以為簽名就大晒，忽略 CECO 嘅 statutory override；(2) 以為 negligence 免責條款一律無效——只有死傷係絕對無效；(3) 記住 reasonableness 係以簽約當刻衡量（唔係 breach 當刻），而且舉證責任喺依賴條款嘅一方。涉及 misrepresentation 嘅免責條款就要用 s.4 of the Misrepresentation Ordinance (Cap.284) + CECO s.3(1)，唔好用錯條文。

title: M10 Chapter 2: Principles of Contract and Consumer Law in Hong Kong (Part 1) — Phase 3 Quiz
headings: M10 Chapter 2: Principles of Contract and Consumer Law in Hong Kong (Part 1) — Phase 3 Quiz
excerpt: M10 Chapter 2: Principles of Contract and Consumer Law in Hong Kong (Part 1) — Phase 3 Quiz Rules: Closed book · 15 minutes · 5 questions · Submit as 1. … 2. … …
text: M10 Chapter 2: Principles of Contract and Consumer Law in Hong Kong (Part 1) — Phase 3 Quiz Rules: Closed book · 15 minutes · 5 questions · Submit as 1. … 2. … 3. … 4. … 5. … — 超時如實申報 Q1. Golden Hour Jewellery Ltd displays a vintage Rolex watch in its shop window in Tsim Sha Tsui with a price tag of HK$88,000. Marcus sees the display, walks in, and tells the shop assistant: "I accept your offer — here is HK$88,000 in cash." The shop manager refuses to sell, saying the price tag was printed with the wrong price. Marcus insists the shop is contractually bound to sell him the watch at HK$88,000. Which statement BEST describes the legal position? A. The shop is bound: the window display constituted a unilateral offer to the world, which Marcus accepted by tendering the price (Carlill v Carbolic Smoke Ball Co (1893) 1 QB 256). B. The shop is not bound: the window display is an invitation to treat, so Marcus's tender of HK$88,000 is merely an offer which the shop is free to reject (Fisher v Bell (1961) 1 QB 394). C. The shop is bound: the window display is a standing offer because it cannot be negotiated with, like an automatic machine (Thornton v Shoe Lane Parking Ltd (1971) 2 QB 163). D. The shop is not bound, but only because the marked price was a mistake, rendering any contract void for unilateral mistake as to terms. Q2. Which statutory provision makes it IMPOSSIBLE, in any circumstances, for a person to exclude or restrict his/her business liability for death or personal injury resulting from negligence? A. Section 7(2) of the Control of Exemption Clauses Ordinance (Cap.71) B. Section 8(1) of the Control of Exemption Clauses Ordinance (Cap.71) C. Section 7(1) of the Control of Exemption Clauses Ordinance (Cap.71) D. Section 5(1) of the Unconscionable Contracts Ordinance (Cap.458) Q3. Karen offers to sell her ceramic studio equipment to Daniel for HK$350,000, the offer to remain open for 14 days. On day 3, Daniel replies by email: "Thanks — would you consider HK$320,000, payable in six monthly instalments?" Karen does not respond. On day 9, Daniel emails again: "I accept your original offer of HK$350,000 in full." Karen now refuses to sell, arguing that Daniel destroyed her offer with his day 3 email and that she is free to sell to another buyer at a higher price. Which statement BEST describes the legal position? A. No contract exists: Daniel's day 3 email was a counter offer which destroyed Karen's original offer, so it could no longer be accepted (Hyde v Wrench (1840) 3 Beav 334). B. A contract exists: Daniel's day 3 email was a mere request for information which did not destroy the offer, and his day 9 email was a valid acceptance within the 14 day period (Stevenson, Jacques & Co v McLean (1880) 5 QBD 346). C. No contract exists: Karen's offer had lapsed after a reasonable time given the volatile market price of ceramic equipment (Ramsgate Victoria Hotel Co Ltd v Montefiore (1866) LR 1 Ex 109). D. A contract exists: even if Daniel's day 3 email was a counter offer, Karen's silence amounted to acceptance by conduct of that counter offer. Q4. BrightBuild Ltd is the main contractor for the renovation of a shopping arcade in Mong Kok under a contract that imposes a HK$500,000 penalty for late completion. BrightBuild subcontracts the electrical work to Sparky Ltd for HK$1,200,000, due in 10 weeks. In week 7, Sparky falls seriously behind schedule because of financial difficulties and an under resourced workforce. Fearing the penalty, BrightBuild promises Sparky an additional HK$150,000 if it completes the electrical work on time as originally agreed. Sparky completes on time. BrightBuild refuses to pay the HK$150,000, arguing that Sparky provided no consideration because it merely did what it was already contractually bound to do. There is no evidence of fraud or economic duress by Sparky. Which statement BEST describes whether Sparky can enforce the promise of the extra HK$150,000? A. Sparky cannot enforce the promise: performance of an existing contractual duty owed to the promisor can never constitute consideration (Stilk v Myrick (1809) 2 Camp 317). B. Sparky can enforce the promise: BrightBuild obtained a practical benefit — avoiding the HK$500,000 late completion penalty and the trouble of engaging a replacement subcontractor — and the strict criteria are satisfied (Williams v Roffey Bros & Nicholls (Contractors) Ltd (1991) 1 QB 1). C. Sparky cannot enforce the promise: a promise to pay more in return for part performance is unenforceable unless supported by fresh consideration such as early payment or a chattel (Pinnel's Case (1602) 5 Co Rep 117a). D. Sparky can enforce the promise by relying on promissory estoppel as a cause of action, since it relied on BrightBuild's promise by completing the work (Central London Property Ltd v High Trees House Ltd (1947) KB 130). Q5. Ms. Wong signs up for a one year membership at FitZone Gym in Causeway Bay. The membership is on FitZone's standard printed terms, which she signs without reading. Clause 12 states: "FitZone Gym Ltd, its employees and agents accept no liability whatsoever for any injury, loss or damage to members or their property, howsoever caused, including the negligence of FitZone Gym Ltd, its employees or agents." Three months later, a treadmill belt snaps because FitZone's staff negligently failed to maintain the equipment. Ms. Wong suffers a fractured wrist, and her smartphone (worth HK$9,000), stored in a gym locker, is smashed in the fall. FitZone relies on Clause 12 to refuse all compensation. Which statement BEST describes the validity of Clause 12? A. Clause 12 is fully effective for both claims: Ms. Wong signed the contract and is therefore bound by all its terms, whether or not she read them (L'Estrange v E Graucob Ltd (1934) 2 KB 394). B. Clause 12 is entirely ineffective: no exemption clause can ever exclude liability for negligence of any kind under the Control of Exemption Clauses Ordinance (Cap.71). C. Clause 12 cannot exclude FitZone's liability for Ms. Wong's fractured wrist because liability for personal injury resulting from negligence can never be excluded (s.7(1) of the CECO (Cap.71)); however, it may exclude liability for the damaged smartphone if FitZone proves the clause satisfies the reasonableness test in s.3(1) of the CECO (s.7(2) of the CECO). D. Clause 12 is governed exclusively by the Unconscionable Contracts Ordinance (Cap.458), under which the court may revise the clause so as to avoid an unconscionable result (s.5(1) of the UCO). End of quiz. Do not look at the answers file until you have submitted.

title: M10 Chapter 3: Principles of Contract and Consumer Law in Hong Kong (Part 2) — Phase 1 速查表 + Phase 2 閃卡
headings: M10 Chapter 3: Principles of Contract and Consumer Law in Hong Kong (Part 2) — Phase 1 速查表 + Phase 2 閃卡
A. Vitiating Factors（令合約 void 或 voidable 嘅因素）
excerpt: M10 Chapter 3: Principles of Contract and Consumer Law in Hong Kong (Part 2) — Phase 1 速查表 + Phase 2 閃卡 Phase 1 速查表 Learning Objectives 1. Analyse the different…
text: M10 Chapter 3: Principles of Contract and Consumer Law in Hong Kong (Part 2) — Phase 1 速查表 + Phase 2 閃卡 Phase 1 速查表 Learning Objectives 1. Analyse the different vitiating factors (common mistake, misrepresentation, duress, undue influence, unconscionability, illegality) and their legal effects on a contract (void vs voidable). 2. Analyse how a contract can be discharged by performance, agreement, breach and frustration, and apply the rules on loss apportionment under the Law Amendment and Reform (Consolidation) Ordinance (Cap. 23). 3. Apply the rules relating to the award of damages (remoteness, mitigation, liquidated damages) and evaluate the range of remedies (action for an agreed sum, deposits, specific performance, injunctions). 4. Apply the key provisions of the Sale of Goods Ordinance (Cap. 26), the Supply of Services (Implied Terms) Ordinance (Cap. 457) and the Trade Descriptions Ordinance (Cap. 362) to business to consumer scenarios. 必背考點 A. Vitiating Factors（令合約 void 或 voidable 嘅因素） 1. Common Mistake（雙方共同錯誤）— 效果：void ab initio Rule: 雙方犯同一錯誤，訂約後先發現 → contract void from the beginning。 Necessary elements（ Great Peace Shipping Ltd v Tsavliris Salvage (International) Ltd (2002) EWCA Civ 1407）：(1) common assumption as to a state of affairs; (2) no promise by either party that it exists; (3) non existence not attributable to either party's fault; (4) non existence renders performance impossible; (5) the state of affairs is the existence/vital attribute of the consideration。 Limitations：(a) contractual allocation of risk（ Jan Albert (HK) Ltd v Shu Kong Garment Factory Ltd (1990) 1 HKLR 317 — 被告 expressly undertook to procure export quota → 承擔風險，no common mistake）; (b) fault of one party。 Three categories: mistake as to subject matter（ Couturier v Hastie (1856) 5 HL Cas 673 — 粟米已被賣咗，買方唔使畀錢）; mistake as to ability to perform（physical/legal impossibility， Cooper v Phibbs (1867) LR 2 HL 149）; mistake as to quality — test of essential difference （ Bell v Lever Bros Ltd (1932) AC 161 — 極窄；買錯畫唔夠， Leaf v International Galleries (1950) 2 KB 86）。事件喺訂約 前 已發生 → common mistake（ Griffith v Brymer (1903) 19 TLR 434）；訂約 後 先發生 → frustration。 2. Misrepresentation — 效果：voidable（可以 rescind） Actionable misrepresentation = false statement of fact that induces the representee to enter into the contract。 Silence 一般唔算（caveat emptor, Keates v The Earl of Cadogan (1851) 10 CB 591），但 exceptions：(1) active steps to conceal（ Horsfall v Thomas (1862) 1 H & C 90 — 但必須 known to representee 先算 induced）; (2) half truths（ Dimmock v Hallett (1866) LR 2 Ch App 21）; (3) change of circumstances（ With v O'Flanagan (1936) Ch 575）; (4) fiduciary relationships; (5) contracts uberrimae fidei（e.g. insurance）。 Fact vs opinion：opinion 一般唔算（ Bisset v Wilkinson (1927) AC 177），但 maker in a better position to know → implied assertion of fact（ Smith v Land & House Property Corp (1884) 28 Ch D 7）；future intention 一般唔算，除非無該真實意圖（ Edgington v Fitzmaurice (1885) 24 Ch D 459）。 Inducement 四要件：material / known to representee / intended to be acted upon / actually acted upon（ Attwood v Small (1838) 6 Cl & F 232 — 自行查證 → 無 reliance；但 Redgrave v Hurd (1881) 20 Ch D 1 — 有機會查但無查，仍可有 actionable misrep）。 Types: fraudulent （knowingly / without belief / recklessly — Derry v Peek (1889) 14 App Cas 337）; negligent （honest but no reasonable care）; innocent （honest + reasonable grounds）。 Rescission ：equitable, all or nothing，voidable contract 被 set aside。 Bars to rescission : (1) affirmation; (2) lapse of time（fraud → time runs from discovery; negligent/innocent → from contract formation — Leaf v International Galleries ）; (3) restitution impossible（ Clarke v Dickson (1858) EB & E 148）; (4) third party rights（ Car and Universal Finance Co Ltd v Caldwell (1961) 1 QB 525；s.25 SOGO (Cap. 26) sale under voidable title）。 Damages ： Fraudulent (tort of deceit): 所有直接 flowing from the transaction 嘅損失，唔使 foreseeable（ Doyle v Olby Ironmongers Ltd (1969) 2 QB 158； Smith New Court Securities Ltd v Scrimgeour Vickers (Asset Management) Ltd (1997) AC 254 — 可計及成交後跌價）；contributory negligence 不相干。 Negligent at common law (negligent misstatement): 要 special relationship + duty of care（ Hedley Byrne & Co Ltd v Heller & Partners Ltd (1964) AC 465； Caparo Industries Plc v Dickman (1990) 2 AC 605）；burden on representee；remoteness = reasonably foreseeable。 Innocent at common law: no damages （ Redgrave v Hurd ）。 Misrepresentation Ordinance (Cap. 284)（MO）s.3(1) ：statutory negligent misrep — (i) 唔使 special relationship; (ii) burden reversed（representor 要證明有 reasonable grounds believe 屬真）; (iii) remoteness = fiction of fraud（all direct losses — Royscot Trust Ltd v Rogerson (1991) 2 QB 297）。 前提 ：representee 被誘導同 representor 本人 訂約（誘導去同第三者訂約 → 只可以 common law 追討）。 MO s.3(2) ：non fraudulent misrep → court discretion 判 damages in lieu of rescission（若 rescission 已 barred 就用唔到）；s.3(3)：s.3(1) award 要扣減 s.3(2) award。 Contributory negligence 可減 damages（s.21(1) Law Amendment and Reform (Consolidation) Ordinance (Cap. 23)），但 fraud 除外。 3. Duress（尤指 economic duress）— 效果：voidable 三類：duress to the person（ Barton v Armstrong (1976) AC 104）/ to goods（ Astley v Reynolds (1731) 2 Str 915）/ economic duress （最常考）。 Economic duress 三要件：(1) illegitimate pressure （多為威脅 breach of contract；區分正常商業討價還價 — Pao On v Lau Yiu Long (1980) AC 614； Tung Wing Steel Co Ltd v George Wimpey International Ltd HCA No. 3285/1984 — 買方可以轉去第二個供應商 → 無 illegitimate pressure）; (2) causal link （but for / significant cause — Dimskal Shipping Co SA v ITF (The Evia Luck) (No. 2) (1992) 2 AC 152）; (3) no practicable alternative （ Estinah v Golden Hand Indonesian Employment Agency (2001) 4 HKC 607）。 Remedy: rescission（若只是 variation 受脅迫，只撤銷 variation 部分）；若構成 tort of intimidation 可索償。 Trap ：delay/affirmation 會失權 — North Ocean Shipping Co Ltd v Hyundai Construction Co Ltd (The Atlantic Baron) (1979) QB 705（17 個月後先 protest → 已 affirm，收唔返 extra 10%）。 4. Undue Influence — 效果：voidable（equitable doctrine，闊過 duress） Class 1 actual undue influence（overt improper pressure，唔使有 threat）。 Class 2 presumed undue influence = (1) relationship of trust and confidence + (2) transaction calling for explanation（ Royal Bank of Scotland Plc v Etridge (No. 2) (2002) 2 AC 773； Li Sau Ying v Bank of China (Hong Kong) Ltd (2005) 1 HKLRD 106）。 Class 2A（irrebuttable presumption of influence）：parent–child、religious leader–disciple、doctor–patient、solicitor–client、fiancé–fiancée。 Husband–wife 唔屬 2A （考試伏位！）。 Class 2B：要受害人提出 trust and confidence 嘅證據（包括 husband–wife、employer–employee）。 Rebuttable presumption 成立後，burden shifts to the influencer。 Spouse surety：wife 要 set aside guarantee，須證明 bank (1) put on inquiry （非商業 surety 關係）+ (2) failed to take reasonable steps （最穩陣做法：取得獨立律師 confirmation letter — Etridge）。 Remedy: rescission（同樣受 bars 限制）；barred 時或可獲 damages in lieu。 5. Unconscionability — 效果：voidable Two stage test（ Commercial Bank of Australia Ltd v Amadio (1982–1983) 151 CLR 447；HK 承認 — Ming Shiu Chung v Ming Shiu Sum (2006) 2 HKLRD 831）：(1) victim has a special disadvantage （seriously affecting ability to judge own best interests）; (2) 另一方 unconscientiously took advantage （knowledge 包括 constructive knowledge / wilful ignorance — Kakavas v Crown Melbourne Ltd (2013) HCA 25）。對方除非證明交易 fair, just and reasonable，否則 set aside。 HK cases： Evelyn Semana Bachicha v Poon Shiu Man Henry (2000) 3 HKC 452（settlement HK$50,000 → HK$975 set aside）； Lo Wo & Ors v Cheung Chan Ka Joseph & Anor (2001) 3 HKC 70（老婦人三分之一市價賣樓 set aside）。 同 undue influence 嘅分別：unconscionability 睇 強者嘅行為 （弱者意志仍可 independent）；undue influence 睇 弱者意志被壓倒 （consent 唔 independent）。 Statutory consumer protection: Unconscionable Contracts Ordinance (Cap. 458)（詳見 Ch.2）。 6. Illegality Sources: common law rule / statutory rule / public interest（ Pearce v Brooks (1866) LR 1 Ex 213）。 Illegal at formation → void ab initio（ Re Mahmoud and Ispahani (1921) 2 KB 716 — 無 licence）；illegal mode of performance → 唔一定 unenforceable，視乎立法目的（ St John Shipping Corp v Joseph Rank Ltd (1957) 1 QB 267 — 超載唔影響運費申索）；illegal purpose remote from contract → not tainted。 General rule: money/benefits under illegal contract 唔可以 recover（ Holman v Johnson (1775) 1 Cowp 341）。 Gambling: Gambling Ordinance (Cap. 148) ss.3, 4（unauthorised gambling unlawful）; s.14（明知借錢俾人非法賭博 → offence；loan irrecoverable）。 Restraint of trade: void unless reasonable（ Nordenfelt v Maxim Nordenfelt Guns & Ammunition Co Ltd (1894) AC 535）— reasonable as between parties + public interest, protecting a legitimate interest, scope/area/time balanced。 B. Discharge of the Contract 1. Performance — must be complete and precise （ Arcos Ltd v EA Ronaasen & Son (1933) AC 470 — 1/16 吋偏差都係 breach； Re Moore & Co and Landauer & Co (1921) 2 KB 519 — 24 罐裝 vs 30 罐裝，buyer 可以 reject 全部）；de minimis rule 只係 possible exception。 Entire obligations ：incomplete performance → 一分錢都收唔到（ Cutter v Powell (1795) 6 Term Rep 320 — 船員中途死亡，widow 收唔到人工）。 分開 entire contracts ：substantial performance doctrine 適用於 entire contracts 但 唔適用於 entire obligations （ Hoenig v Isaacs (1952) 2 All ER 176）。 SOGO 語境：sale of goods 數量屬 entire obligation（ Oxendale v Wetherell (1829) 9 B & C 386），qualifications：相反約定 / trivial discrepancies / instalments（s.33(2) SOGO）；接受咗錯誤數量 → pro rata 付款（s.32(1) SOGO）。 Severable obligations：分階段付款（月薪、進度款）。 Unjust enrichment：自願接受 partial performance → 要畀合理價錢；wrongful prevention of performance → damages 或 quantum meruit （ Planché v Colburn (1831) 8 Bing 14）。 2. Agreement — 需要 consideration：雙方都有未完成義務 → mutual release 即 consideration；一方已全做晒 → 對方要畀新 consideration。例外：deed / force majeure clause / termination clause。 3. Breach Actual breach（fail to perform / defective performance；liability 多屬 strict ，如 s.16 SOGO merchantable quality；但 s.5 SSITO (Cap. 457) 只係 duty of reasonable care and skill — qualified obligation）vs anticipatory breach （refuses / makes known unable to perform — 非真正 breach 但 law 容許 treat as breach）。 Types of promissory terms（後果關鍵）： Condition ：goes to the root → repudiatory → terminate + damages。Express label 唔係 conclusive；custom/precedent/statute 自動屬 condition（e.g. 'time is of the essence' — Union Eagle Ltd v Golden Achievement Ltd (1997) UKPC 5，遲 10 分鐘都可以 terminate；s.16(2) SOGO）。 Warranty ：lesser term → damages only， 唔可以 terminate 。 Innominate term ：睇 breach 後果嚴重性 — deprive substantially the whole benefit → 當 condition 處理（ Hong Kong Fir Shipping Co Ltd v Kawasaki Kisen Kaisha Ltd (1962) 2 QB 26 — seaworthiness clause 唔係 condition，charterers wrongful repudiation 反而自己 breach）。 Terminate or affirm：affirm after anticipatory breach → 要等到 performance due date 先有 damages；affirm 後若自己 breach 或 contract frustrated，可能乜都冇（ Avery v Bowden (1855) E & B 714）。 4. Frustration — supervening event（outside parties' control）令 performance (1) impossible / (2) illegal / (3) radically different → automatic discharge ，唔理雙方意願。 Grounds: destruction of subject matter（ Taylor v Caldwell (1863) 3 B & S 826 — music hall 燒毀）；death in personal service contract；method stipulated 變成 impossible；supervening illegality（ Fibrosa Spolka Akcynja v Fairbairn Lawson Combe Barbour Ltd (1943) AC 32 — trading with enemy）； frustration of purpose （ Krell v Henry (1903) 2 KB 740 — 租樓睇加冕巡遊，巡遊取消 → frustrated；但 Herne Bay Steam Boat Co v Hutton (1903) 2 KB 683 — 海軍檢閱取消但仲可以環島遊 → not frustrated；common foundation 係關鍵）。 Limitations：(1) express provisions（ force majeure clause 三大特徵：trigger events / reporting obligations / consequences — 可 suspend/vary/extend，闊過 frustration）; (2) foreseen or foreseeable event（ Davis Contractors Ltd v Fareham UDC (1956) AC 696； Walton Harvey Ltd v Walker & Homfrays Ltd (1931) 1 Ch 274 — 明知有 compulsory purchase 風險 → 唔係 frustration，要賠）; (3) self induced （ J Lauritzen AS v Wijsmuller BV (The Super Servant Two) (1990) 1 Lloyd's Rep 1 — 自己分配 SS1 去其他合約 → 唔算 frustration； Maritime National Fish Ltd v Ocean Trawlers Ltd (1935) AC 524）。 Consequences — LARCO (Cap. 23)： s.16(2) ：frustration 前已付嘅錢 prima facie recoverable（突破 common law 嘅 total failure of consideration 要求 — Fibrosa ）；payee 可 retain/recover just sum ，上限 = min（advance paid/payable, actual expenses incurred）。 s.16(3) ：一方 performance 令對方獲得 valuable benefit → 可追 just sum（唔超過 benefit 價值）；two stage：先 identify + value the benefit（end product），再 assess just sum（ BP Exploration Co (Libya) Ltd v Hunt (No. 2) (1979) 1 WLR 783）。 C. Remedies 1. Damages — primary remedy, available as of right；compensate 唔係 punish（ no punitive damages — Addis v Gramophone Co Ltd (1909) AC 488）。 Types of loss: expectation loss / reliance loss / restitution（total failure of consideration）/ incidental loss；可以組合但 no double recovery （ Millar's Machinery Co Ltd v David Way & Son (1935) 40 Com Cas 204）。 Date of assessment：一般 as at date of breach（ Johnson v Agnew (1980) AC 367）；SOGO s.53(3) non delivery → contract price vs market price at delivery time；非絕對 — Golden Straight Corp v Nippon Yusen Kubishika Kaisha (The Golden Victory) (2007) 2 WLR 691（計及 breach 後已知事件）。 Limitations： Causation （ C&P Haulage Co Ltd v Middleton (1983) EWCA Civ 5）。 Remoteness — Hadley v Baxendale (1854) 9 Ex 341 two limb test：(1) normal loss（usual course of things）; (2) special loss（breaching party 訂約時 actually knew of special circumstances — Victoria Laundry (Windsor) Ltd v Newman Industries Ltd (1949) 2 KB 528 — 一般 laundry profit 賠得，特別政府合約唔賠）。Foreseeability = 'not unlikely'（ Koufos v C Czarnikow Ltd (The Heron II) (1969) 1 AC 350）；知識評估時點 = time of contracting （ Jackson v Royal Bank of Scotland (2005) 1 WLR 377）。 Assumption of responsibility ：即使 foreseeable，若雙方無意令違約方承擔該類 loss → 唔賠（ Transfield Shipping Inc v Mercator Shipping Inc (The Achilleas) (2008) 2 Lloyd's Rep 275）。 Mitigation ：無法律義務但可避免嘅 loss 唔賠；只需 reasonable steps；burden on breaching party；reasonable 嘅 mitigation 措施造成嘅進一步 loss 都可以追（ Banco de Portugal v Waterlow (1932) AC 452）；mitigation 成功晒 → 只得 nominal damages。Anticipatory breach：accept breach 後即要 mitigate；affirm 的話到 actual breach 先要 mitigate。 Non money losses ：一般唔賠 distress/disappointment；exceptions：(1) loss of amenity（ Ruxley Electronics and Construction Ltd v Forsyth (1996) 1 AC 344 — 泳池深度，cost of cure 唔成比例 → 判 loss of amenity）; (2) physical inconvenience causing distress（ Farley v Skinner (No. 2) (2002) 2 AC 732）; (3) contract purpose 係 pleasure/relaxation（ Jarvis v Swan Tours Ltd (1973) QB 233 — holiday）。 Liquidated damages ：genuine pre estimate of loss → enforceable；disproportionately high / unconscionable → penalty , unenforceable（ Dunlop Pneumatic Tyre Ltd v New Garage and Motor Co Ltd (1915) AC 79； Philips Hong Kong Ltd v A G of Hong Kong (1993) 61 BLR 41； Cavendish Square Holding BV v Talal El Makdessi; ParkingEye Ltd v Beavis (2015) UKSC 67）。 Equitable damages ：s.17 High Court Ordinance (Cap. 4) — in lieu of / in addition to specific performance or injunction；可涵蓋 anticipated cause of action。 2. Action for an Agreed Sum (the Price) — claim in debt （唔係 damages）：唔使 quantify loss；remoteness/mitigation 唔適用；可 summary judgment（Order 14, Rules of the High Court (Cap. 4A) / Rules of the District Court (Cap. 336H)）。前提：plaintiff 已 fully perform。Anticipatory breach 後 affirm + 繼續履行 → 可追 price（ White & Carter (Councils) Ltd v McGregor (1962) AC 413），但若 plaintiff no legitimate interest in continuing → 唔得（ Ocean Marine Navigation Ltd v Koch Carbon Inc (The Dynamic) (2003) 2 Lloyd's Rep 693）。 3. Deposits and Part Payments （ Polyset Ltd v Panhandat Ltd (2002) 5 HKCFAR 234 — CFA） 定性取決於 parties' intention（ Mayson v Clouet (1924) AC 980）。 Part payment ：impliedly conditional on completion → payor breach 都可收回，但 innocent party 有 right of set off for damages（ Dies v British and International Mining and Finance Corp Ltd (1939) 1 KB 724）；若 intended unconditional（e.g. shipbuilding instalments）→ 唔可以收返（ Hyundai Heavy Industries Co Ltd v Papadopoulos (1980) 1 WLR 1129）。 Deposit ：an earnest / guarantee of performance → buyer default → forfeited regardless of whether seller suffered any loss （ Howe v Smith (1884) 27 Ch D 89）；seller 仲可以 sue for damages（超過 deposit 嘅部分，credit for deposit — Shuttleworth v Clews (1910) 1 Ch 176）。 注意 ：deposit forfeiture 唔受 penalty rule 規管。 4. Specific Performance — equitable, discretionary ，唔係 as of right；damages inadequate 先考慮（unique goods / land）。 Limitations：claimant 要 ready, willing and able to perform（ Lau Suk Ching Peggy v Ma Hing Lam (2010) 3 HKLRD 247）；damages adequate → 唔批（貨物有市場替代品）；equitable maxims — clean hands （ Quadrant Visual Communications Ltd v Hutchison Telephone (UK) Ltd (1993) 1 BCLC 442）+ delay defeats equity / laches （Limitation Ordinance (Cap. 347) s.4 六年時效唔適用於 SP，但要 act promptly）；hardship to defendant（ Patel v Ali (1984) Ch 283）；lack of mutuality；contract too vague；需要 mutual co operation。 永唔批：contracts for personal service ；contracts requiring constant supervision （ Co operative Insurance Society Ltd v Argyll Stores (Holdings) Ltd (1998) AC 1 — 唔會強迫超市繼續營業）。正面例子： Beswick v Beswick (1968) AC 58（批咗）。 5. Injunctions — equitable, discretionary；final/perpetual vs interim/interlocutory。 Prohibitory injunction ：enforce negative promise；可能構成 indirect specific performance — 若 SP 會被拒，同效果嘅 injunction 亦應被拒；但 Lumley v Wagner (1852) 21 LJ Ch 898 — 可以禁佢去對手戲院唱歌（唔等於逼佢唱）； Warner Bros Pictures Inc v Nelson (1937) 1 KB 209；HK: Beacon College Ltd v Yiu Man Hau Alfred & Ors (2001) 4 HKC 433 — 有 realistic alternative employment 就可以批（補習老師可轉去官立學校）；越長期越難批（ Warren v Mendy (1989) 1 WLR 853）。 Mandatory injunction ：更難攞；triviality / disproportion / public interest 可拒（ Wrotham Park Estate Co Ltd v Parkside Homes Ltd (1974) 1 WLR 798 — 拒拆樓，改判 damages in lieu = 5% anticipated profit）。 D. Consumer Law Legislation 1. Sale of Goods Ordinance (Cap. 26)（SOGO） Contract of sale of goods：seller transfers/agrees to transfer property in goods to buyer for a money consideration (the price) （s.3(1)）；無特定形式（s.5）；goods = personal chattels（s.2(1)），唔包 land / fixtures / money；existing vs future goods（s.7(1)）；無定價 → reasonable price（ss.10(1), (2)）；retention of title / Romalpa clause （ Aluminium Industrie Vaassen BV v Romalpa Aluminium Ltd (1976) 1 WLR 676）。 Implied terms： s.12(1)：time of payment not of the essence（除非另有意思）。 s.13(1)–(3)：buyer 可 waive condition 或當 warranty 處理；accept 咗貨之後，breach of condition 只當 warranty。 s.14(1) ：implied condition seller has right to sell（title）；implied warranty free from encumbrance + quiet possession。CECO s.11(1)： 任何情況下都唔可以豁免 。 s.15(1) ：sale by description → goods must correspond with description（condition）。 s.16(2) ：in the course of a business → merchantable (satisfactory) quality （condition）；exceptions：defects drawn to attention / buyer examined / sale by sample defects apparent。s.2(5) 定義 merchantable quality（fit for common purposes; appearance and finish; free from minor defects — 以 reasonableness 為準）。 s.16(3) ：buyer made known particular purpose → reasonably fit for that purpose（condition），除非無合理 reliance on seller's skill/judgement。 s.17(2) ：sale by sample — bulk corresponds with sample 等（condition）。 CECO (Cap. 71)：buyer 係 consumer → s.15/16/17 責任 完全唔可以豁免 （s.11(2)）；non consumer → 受 reasonableness test 規管（CECO s.3 + s.11(3)）；CECO s.5(1)(a) 防止用 onerous conditions 變相豁免。 Dealing as a consumer （s.2A(1)）：(1) 唔係以 business capacity 訂約; (2) 對方係 business; (3) 貨品屬 ordinarily supplied for personal use or consumption 嘅類型。拍賣/competitive tender 買家永遠唔算 consumer（s.2A(2)）；主張對方 唔係 consumer 嘅一方負舉證責任（s.2A(3)）。（ Artech Printing Ltd v Yee Fat Printing Equipment Ltd CACV92/2000 — printing press 唔係 consumer goods。） Passing of property ：unascertained goods 未 ascertain 前唔會過戶（s.18）；specific goods → 按 parties' intention（s.19(1), (2)）；無意圖 → s.20 五條 default Rules（Rule 1: specific goods deliverable state → 訂約時過戶，唔理付款/交貨時間；Rule 4: sale or return；Rule 5: unascertained goods by description — unconditional appropriation / delivery without reserving right of disposal, s.21）。 Passing of risk （s.22）：risk follows property（除非另有協議）， 唔理交付咗未 ；一方 fault 延誤交付 → 該方承擔風險。 Nemo dat quod non habet （s.23(1)）：非物主出售 → buyer 拎唔到 title（即使 good faith）。 Statutory exceptions ：s.23(1) estoppel；s.23(2)(a) mercantile agent；s.23(2)(b) power of sale； s.24(1) market overt （公開商店/市場正常營業中出售，buyer good faith + without notice → 攞到好 title； R v Tai Shing Jewellery Co (1983) 2 HKC 441 — 只保護向商店買嘢嘅公眾，唔保護商店收購）； s.25 sale under voidable title ；s.27(1) seller in possession after sale；s.27(2) buyer in possession after sale。 Performance：seller 交貨 + buyer 收貨付款（s.29）；交付與付款 concurrent（s.30）；交貨地點/時間（s.31(1), (2)）；wrong quantity（s.32(1)–(3)：少咗可全拒；多咗可收啱嗰部分或全拒；接受咗就 contract rate 找數）；instalment delivery 可拒（s.33(1)）；交 carrier 當交付（s.34(1)）。 Acceptance （s.37）：intimates acceptance / acts inconsistent with seller's ownership / reasonable time 後 retain 唔 reject；未檢查過嘅貨 → 有 reasonable opportunity to examine 先當 accept（s.37(2)）；consumer buyer — 絕對（s.37(3)）。（ Master Weaving Ltd v Hanbo Enterprises Ltd HCA 676/2012 — 出 cargo receipt + 繼續用貨 = accepted。）Buyer 合法拒收後無義務退貨，seller 自己攞返（s.38）。 Unpaid seller's remedies against goods ：withhold delivery（s.42，title 未過戶）； lien （s.43(1)，即使 title 過咗 — 但 s.45(1) 交付 carrier 等情況會失去）； stoppage in transit （s.46，buyer insolvent）； re sale （s.50(2) 新買家攞好 title；s.50(3) perishable 或通知後 buyer 唔找數可轉售 + 追 damages；s.50(4) 保留轉售權）。 Actions for breach：seller — action for the price（s.51）/ damages for non acceptance（s.52）；buyer — damages / specific performance for non delivery（ss.53, 54）/ damages for breach of warranty（s.55）。 2. Supply of Services (Implied Terms) Ordinance (Cap. 457)（SSITO） 適用於 contract for the supply of a service（one off work），唔包 contract of service（continuous, e.g. employment）（ss.3(1), (2)）。 Implied terms： s.5 reasonable care and skill； s.6(1) reasonable time（無指定時）； s.7(1) reasonable price（無指定時）。 Exemption：consumer → s.8(1) 完全唔可以豁免 ；non consumer → s.8(2) 可以，但要過 CECO reasonableness test。 Thomsen & Anor v Johnson Burglar Alarms Co Ltd (2001) 3 HKLRD 571 — common law 同 s.5 SSITO 嘅 duty 相同。 3. 485)、SFO (Cap. 571)）除外。 s.13E misleading omissions — omit/hide material information / unclear, unintelligible, ambiguous or untimely / fail to identify commercial intent → 導致 average consumer breach Payor breaches → recoverable? No — forfeited regardless of whether payee suffered any loss （ Howe v Smith (1884) 27 Ch D 89； Polyset Ltd v Panhandat Ltd (2002) 5 HKCFAR 234） Yes — impliedly conditional on completion; payee 只可以 set off damages（ Dies v British and International Mining and Finance Corp Ltd (1939) 1 KB 724） Enforceable if genuine pre estimate of loss ；否則係 penalty, unenforceable（ Dunlop Pneumatic Tyre Ltd v New Garage and Motor Co Ltd (1915) AC 79） Penalty rule applies? No — forfeiture of deposit 唔受 penalty rule 規管 N/A Yes — disproportionate/unconscionable sum struck down（ Cavendish v Makdessi; ParkingEye v Beavis (2015) UKSC 67） 點樣分辨 睇 parties' intention（ Mayson v Clouet (1924) AC 980）；常見 "as deposit and in part payment" 字眼 = 雙重性質 純粹預付貨款一部分，無擔保功能 合約訂明違約賠償機制 考試伏位 Seller 無損失都可以沒收 deposit — 考生常誤用 penalty rule 反駁；仲可以追 damages（超過 deposit 部分，要 credit for deposit） 若 instalments intended to finance payee's performance（如造船）→ unconditional，收唔返（ Hyundai Heavy Industries Co Ltd v Papadopoulos (1980) 1 WLR 1129） 唔好同 deposit forfeiture 混淆 — 兩者規則完全唔同 Phase 2 閃卡 Card 1 Front: What are the four elements of an actionable misrepresentation, and what are the five exceptions to the rule that silence is not a misrepresentation? Back: A false statement of fact which induces the representee to enter into the contract. Inducement requires: material / known to the representee / intended to be acted upon / actually acted upon. Silence is not a misrepresentation (caveat emptor), EXCEPT: (1) active steps to conceal; (2) half truths ( Dimmock v Hallett ); (3) change of circumstances ( With v O'Flanagan ); (4) fiduciary relationships; (5) contracts uberrimae fidei. 💬 記住口訣：「假嘅事實陳述 + 誘導訂約」。純粹沉默唔算（buyer beware），但五個例外情況要背熟——尤其 half truth（講一半呃人）同 change of circumstances（之前講嘅嘢變咗唔啱要更正），呢兩個最常用嚟出 scenario 題。 Card 2 Front: Why is it usually better for a representee to claim damages for negligent misrepresentation under s.3(1) of the Misrepresentation Ordinance (Cap. 284) than at common law? Back: (1) No need to establish a special relationship / duty of care (unlike Hedley Byrne at common law). (2) Burden of proof reversed : representor must prove he had reasonable grounds to believe, and did believe, the statement was true. (3) Fiction of fraud : remoteness test = same as the tort of deceit — all losses directly flowing from the transaction, regardless of foreseeability ( Royscot Trust Ltd v Rogerson (1991) 2 QB 297). BUT: only available where the representee was induced to contract with the representor himself (not a third party). 💬 s.3(1) MO 三大優勢：唔使證 special relationship、舉證責任掉轉、賠償範圍當佢欺诈咁計（fiction of fraud）。伏位：如果 misrep 誘導你同 第三者 訂約（如 Hedley Byrne 嘅 facts），s.3(1) 就用唔到，只可以行 common law。 Card 3 Front: List the four bars to rescission for misrepresentation and state when time begins to run for lapse of time. Back: (1) Affirmation of the contract (with knowledge of the misrep and right to rescind). (2) Lapse of time — fraud: time runs from discovery (or when reasonably discoverable); negligent/innocent: from contract formation ( Leaf v International Galleries (1950) 2 KB 86 — 5 年後先發現，barred). (3) Restitution impossible (e.g. goods consumed/irreversibly changed — Clarke v Dickson ). (4) Third party rights (bona fide purchaser without notice — Car and Universal Finance Co Ltd v Caldwell (1961) 1 QB 525; s.25 SOGO). Rescission is all or nothing — no partial rescission. 💬 四個 bars：affirm、拖得太耐、還唔返原狀、第三者權利。時間起算係大伏位： fraud 由發現日起計 ，negligent/innocent 由 訂約日 起計 — 所以 fraud 受害人隔好多年都可能仲 rescind 得，innocent misrep 就很快就 bar 咗。 Card 4 Front: What must a party show to establish economic duress, and what is the remedy? Back: (1) Illegitimate pressure (usually a threat to breach the contract; distinguish from normal commercial bargaining — Pao On v Lau Yiu Long (1980) AC 614); relevant factors: good/bad faith, protest at the time, subsequent affirmation. (2) Causal link : would not have agreed but for the pressure / pressure was a significant cause. (3) No practicable alternative but to submit ( Estinah v Golden Hand Indonesian Employment Agency (2001) 4 HKC 607). Remedy: contract/variation is voidable → rescission (variation only rescinded as to the varied part); damages if pressure amounts to the tort of intimidation. Right to rescind can be lost by affirmation/delay ( The Atlantic Baron (1979) QB 705). 💬 三件套：illegitimate pressure → caused the agreement → 無實際選擇。考試最常見係威脅 breach 去逼對方同意加價/改條款。記住 Atlantic Baron 嘅伏位：就算真係有 duress，拖十幾個月先出聲 = affirmed， rescind 唔到。 Card 5 Front: When is a contract discharged by frustration, and what are the three limitations on the doctrine? Back: A supervening event (outside the parties' control, no fault) makes performance (1) impossible ( Taylor v Caldwell ), (2) illegal ( Fibrosa ), or (3) radically different / common purpose destroyed ( Krell v Henry (1903) 2 KB 740; contrast Herne Bay Steam Boat Co v Hutton ). Effect: automatic discharge , regardless of the parties' intentions. Limitations: (1) express provision (e.g. force majeure clause — trigger events / reporting / consequences); (2) event foreseen or foreseeable ( Davis Contractors v Fareham UDC ); (3) self induced frustration is not frustration ( The Super Servant Two (1990) 1 Lloyd's Rep 1). Loss apportionment: LARCO (Cap. 23) s.16(2) (money paid/payable) and s.16(3) (valuable benefit → just sum). 💬 Frustration = 訂約後發生嘅意外令合約做唔落/犯法/完全變質， 自動 終止。三大限制：合約自己有寫（force majeure）、預見到、自己造成。同 common mistake 分清楚： 訂約前已存在 嘅事實錯誤 → mistake； 訂約後先發生 嘅事件 → frustration（睇 Griffith v Brymer vs Krell v Henry 嘅加冕巡遊對比）。 Card 6 Front: State the two limb test for remoteness of damage in Hadley v Baxendale and the effect of the 'assumption of responsibility' analysis. Back: Limb 1 (normal loss): loss arising naturally , i.e. according to the usual course of things — recoverable if within the breaching party's reasonable contemplation as a likely result of breach. Limb 2 (special loss): loss from special circumstances — recoverable only if the breaching party actually knew of those circumstances at the time of contracting ( Victoria Laundry — general laundry profits recoverable; lucrative government contract not, because unknown). Foreseeability = loss 'not unlikely' to result ( The Heron II (1969) 1 AC 350). Even if foreseeable, no liability if the parties did not (objectively) intend the breaching party to assume responsibility for that type of loss ( The Achilleas (2008) 2 Lloyd's Rep 275). 💬 兩肢測試：正常損失（自然發生 → 賠）vs 特殊損失（訂約時對方 實際知道 特殊情況先賠）。The Achilleas 加多一層：就算 foreseen 到，如果客觀上雙方無諗過違約方會孭呢類 loss，都唔使賠。時間點係 訂約時 ，唔係違約時！ Card 7 Front: What are the implied conditions under ss.14–17 of the Sale of Goods Ordinance (Cap. 26), and to what extent can they be excluded under the Control of Exemption Clauses Ordinance (Cap. 71)? Back: s.14(1) : seller has the right to sell (condition); goods free from undisclosed encumbrances + quiet possession (warranties). s.15(1) : sale by description — goods correspond with description (condition). s.16(2) : goods of merchantable (satisfactory) quality (condition); s.16(3) : reasonably fit for a particular purpose made known (condition). s.17(2) : sale by sample — bulk corresponds with sample, reasonable opportunity to compare, free from hidden unmerchantable defects (condition). CECO: s.14 liability — never excludable (s.11(1)); ss.15–17 — not excludable against a consumer (s.11(2)); against a non consumer, excludable only if reasonable (s.11(3) + s.3). Dealing as a consumer: s.2A(1) SOGO; auction/tender buyers never consumers (s.2A(2)); burden on the party alleging non consumer (s.2A(3)). 💬 一條龍記法：14 = 有權賣、15 = 貨對辦、16 = 品質好+啱用途、17 = 大貨同板。豁免規則：s.14 永遠唔豁免得；15–17 對 consumer 永遠唔豁免得，對 business 就要過 reasonableness test。邊個係 consumer 睇 s.2A(1) 三要件 — 貨品要係「通常私人使用」嘅類型（printing press 唔係 — Artech 案）。 Card 8 Front: List the six offences against consumers under the Trade Descriptions Ordinance (Cap. 362), with section numbers, and state the maximum penalty. Back: (1) s.7(1) : false trade description of goods; s.7A(1) : false trade description of services. (2) s.13E : misleading omissions. (3) s.13F : aggressive commercial practices (harassment / coercion / undue influence). (4) s.13G : bait advertising. (5) s.13H : bait and switch. (6) s.13I : wrongly accepting payment. Maximum penalty: HK$500,000 fine + 5 years' imprisonment (s.18(1)); court may order compensation to the consumer (s.18A(1)). Enforcement: Customs and Excise Department; exempt persons (Sch. 3) and excluded products (Sch. 4). 💬 六宗罪口訣：「假描述（貨7/服務7A）、漏料13E、硬銷13F、誘餌廣告13G、誘餌轉移13H、收錢唔出貨13I」。Bait advertising vs bait and switch 嘅分別：前者係 根本無合理理由相信有貨賣 ；後者係 有 invitation 之後拒絕展示/接單/俾缺陷樣本 ，意圖轉推另一產品。最高罰 50 萬 + 坐 5 年，呢個數字成日考。 本章急救詞彙 EN Term 繁中白話 English Model Sentence Voidable 合約本來有效，但受害方可以選擇撤銷 Misrepresentation renders the contract voidable, allowing the representee to elect to rescind it. Rescission 撤銷合約、回復訂約前原狀（全有或全無） Rescission is an equitable, all or nothing remedy that restores the parties to their pre contractual positions. Caveat emptor 「買家自己小心」——賣方一般無披露責任 As a general rule, silence does not amount to misrepresentation, reflecting the principle of caveat emptor. Fiction of fraud s.3(1) MO 嘅特別設計：疏忽失實陳述都當欺诈咁計賠償 Under s.3(1) of the Misrepresentation Ordinance (Cap. 284), the 'fiction of fraud' allows recovery of all losses directly flowing from the transaction. Nemo dat quod non habet 無人可以畀到好過自己嘅業權 Under s.23(1) of the SOGO (Cap. 26), a seller without title cannot pass good title, subject to exceptions such as market overt under s.24(1). Quantum meruit 「按佢應得嘅」——無合約或被阻完成時按已做工量收合理報酬 Where the defendant wrongfully prevented performance, the plaintiff recovered a reasonable sum on a quantum meruit basis (Planché v Colburn). Force majeure clause 不可抗力條款：訂明意外事件觸發、通報同後果，會排除 frustration 原則 A force majeure clause ousts the doctrine of frustration by stipulating the consequences of specified supervening events. Earnest (deposit) 訂金嘅法律本質係履約保證，違約就會被沒收，唔理對方有無損失 A deposit is an earnest of performance and may be forfeited upon the buyer's default regardless of the seller's actual loss (Polyset Ltd v Panhandat Ltd).

text: M10 Chapter 3: Principles of Contract and Consumer Law in Hong Kong (Part 2) — Phase 3 Answers Q1 — Answer: C Model Answer (EN): Under s.16(2) of the Sale of Goods Ordinance (Cap. 26), where the seller sells goods in the course of a business, there is an implied condition that the goods supplied are of merchantable (satisfactory) quality — subject to exceptions where defects were specifically drawn to the buyer's attention, or where the buyer examined the goods and the examination should have revealed the defects, or (on a sale by sample) where the defects would have been apparent on reasonable examination of the sample. 'Merchantable quality' is defined in s.2(5) of the SOGO by reference to fitness for common purposes, appearance and finish, and freedom from minor defects, qualified by reasonableness. 解題思路（繁中）: 呢題係 pinpoint section 記憶題，模擬考試對 statutory citation 嘅要求。SOGO implied terms 一條龍：s.14 = title（賣方有權賣）、s.15 = sale by description（貨對辦）、s.16(2) = merchantable quality、s.16(3) = fitness for particular purpose、s.17(2) = sale by sample。Option A (s.14(1)) 係 seller's right to sell 嘅 implied condition；Option B (s.15(1)) 係 goods must correspond with description；Option D (s.17(2)) 係 bulk corresponds with sample。三個都係 condition，但題目問嘅係 merchantable quality，所以只有 C 啱。 Rule Check: Sale of Goods Ordinance (Cap. 26) s.16(2); definition of merchantable quality at s.2(5) Common Trap（繁中）: 考生最容易亂咗 s.15 同 s.16 — 記住 15 係「description 對辦」（例如標籤寫咩就要係咩），16(2) 先係品質。另外注意 s.16(2) 只適用於 seller in the course of a business 賣貨；私人賣二手嘢唔受呢條管。 Q2 — Answer: C Model Answer (EN): The contract was discharged by frustration. A contract is frustrated where a supervening event, outside the control of the parties and without fault, renders performance impossible, illegal, or radically different from what was contemplated — including where the common purpose or foundation of the contract is destroyed. Here, viewing the fireworks display was the express common foundation of the hire contract (it was written into the contract itself), and its unexpected cancellation destroyed that foundation. Applying Krell v Henry (1903) 2 KB 740, the contract is frustrated and automatically discharged, regardless of the parties' intentions, so Mei Ling is released from her obligation to pay (subject to any loss apportionment under s.16 of the Law Amendment and Reform (Consolidation) Ordinance (Cap. 23)). Option A fails because, unlike Herne Bay Steam Boat Co v Hutton (1903) 2 KB 683, there is no residual purpose (the fireworks viewing was the sole stated purpose, not one of several); Option B confuses common mistake — the cancellation occurred after contract formation, so this is frustration, not mistake (contrast Griffith v Brymer (1903) 19 TLR 434, where the procession had already been cancelled before the contract); Option D is hopeless because Harbour Suites made no false statement of fact — silence about a possible future cancellation is not a misrepresentation (caveat emptor). 解題思路（繁中）: 呢題係典型 issue spotting 題。第一步要認到個 legal issue 係 frustration of purpose ，而唔係 common mistake 或 misrepresentation。關鍵時間線：巡遊/煙花取消發生喺 訂約之後 → frustration；如果取消咗先訂約（雙方唔知）→ common mistake（Griffith v Brymer）。第二步要區分 Krell v Henry 同 Herne Bay：前者個 purpose 係合約嘅 common foundation（寫明晒），後者仲有其他用途（環島遊）所以唔 frustrated。呢度合約白紙黑字寫明 "for the purpose of viewing the fireworks display"，所以穩陣落入 Krell v Henry。Frustration 效果係 automatic discharge — 唔使任何一方 elect。 Rule Check: Krell v Henry (1903) 2 KB 740; contrast Herne Bay Steam Boat Co v Hutton (1903) 2 KB 683; Griffith v Brymer (1903) 19 TLR 434; Law Amendment and Reform (Consolidation) Ordinance (Cap. 23) s.16 Common Trap（繁中）: 最大伏位係 Option B — 將 frustration 同 common mistake 撈亂。記住時間分界： 訂約前已存在 嘅錯誤事實 → common mistake（void）； 訂約後先發生 嘅事件 → frustration（automatic discharge）。Option D 亦係陷阱：無人講過大話，純粹沉默唔係 misrepresentation。 Q3 — Answer: D Model Answer (EN): Kelvin made a negligent misrepresentation: he honestly believed his statement but failed to exercise reasonable care in making it (relying on year old figures without checking). Doris's strongest route to damages is s.3(1) of the Misrepresentation Ordinance (Cap. 284) because: (1) there is no need to establish a special relationship or duty of care (unlike negligent misstatement at common law under Hedley Byrne & Co Ltd v Heller & Partners Ltd (1964) AC 465); (2) the burden of proof is reversed — Kelvin must prove that he had reasonable grounds to believe, and did believe, that the facts represented were true up to the time the contract was made (which he cannot, given his careless reliance on outdated figures); and (3) by the 'fiction of fraud', damages are assessed as if the misrepresentation had been made fraudulently — all losses directly flowing from the transaction, regardless of foreseeability ( Royscot Trust Ltd v Rogerson (1991) 2 QB 297). Option A fails: the tort of deceit requires fraud (statement made knowingly, without belief in its truth, or recklessly — Derry v Peek (1889) 14 App Cas 337), and Kelvin honestly believed his statement. Option B is inferior: at common law Doris bears the burden of proving a special relationship, duty of care and breach, and remoteness is limited to reasonably foreseeable losses. Option C is wrong: s.3(2) of the MO provides only a discretionary award of damages in lieu of rescission for non fraudulent misrepresentation, not damages as of right. 解題思路（繁中）: 考試真實出過 misrepresentation + remedies，呢類「揀邊條路追討」嘅 comparative analysis 係核心 skill。答題次序：先定性（honest but careless → negligent misrep，唔係 fraud），再比較三條路。記住 s.3(1) MO 三大優勢：唔使 special relationship、burden reversed、fiction of fraud（賠到盡）。Option B 係設計嚟呃人嘅 — 佢將 s.3(1) 嘅好處（burden on representor + fraud measure）錯配落 common law 度。Option C 考你有冇睇清楚 s.3(2) 只係 discretionary 同 in lieu of rescission。另外記住前提：s.3(1) 只適用於 representee 被誘導同 representor 本人 訂約（呢度 Doris 直接同 Kelvin 買，啱用）。 Rule Check: Misrepresentation Ordinance (Cap. 284) s.3(1), s.3(2); Derry v Peek (1889) 14 App Cas 337; Hedley Byrne & Co Ltd v Heller & Partners Ltd (1964) AC 465; Royscot Trust Ltd v Rogerson (1991) 2 QB 297 Common Trap（繁中）: (1) 唔好一見虛假陳述就嗌 fraud/deceit — 要睇 representor 嘅 state of mind；(2) 唔好以為 innocent/negligent misrep 喺 common law 有得賠 — innocent misrep 喺 common law 係 冇 damages 㗎（ Redgrave v Hurd ），要靠 MO；(3) s.3(2) 唔係 as of right，係 court discretion。 Q4 — Answer: B Model Answer (EN): Patrick may forfeit the HK$600,000. The payment was expressly described as "a deposit and in part payment of the purchase price" — its characterisation depends on the parties' intention objectively ascertained ( Mayson v Clouet (1924) AC 980), and these words give it a dual character: if completion occurs it is absorbed into the price, but if the buyer defaults it is forfeited. A deposit is an earnest of performance — a guarantee that the contract will be completed — and is liable to forfeiture upon the payor's default regardless of whether the payee has suffered any loss ( Howe v Smith (1884) 27 Ch D 89; Polyset Ltd v Panhandat Ltd (2002) 5 HKCFAR 234). Option A is wrong: the penalty rule applies to liquidated damages clauses stipulating sums payable on breach, not to the forfeiture of a true deposit. Option C is wrong: s.16(2) of the Law Amendment and Reform (Consolidation) Ordinance (Cap. 23) governs loss apportionment after a contract is frustrated , not after breach by the payor. Option D states the rule for advance part payments (recoverable, subject to the innocent party's set off for damages — Dies v British and International Mining and Finance Corp Ltd (1939) 1 KB 724), but the payment here was expressly characterised as a deposit, not a mere part payment. (Had Patrick's damages exceeded the deposit, he could also sue for damages, giving credit for the deposit forfeited — Shuttleworth v Clews (1910) 1 Ch 176.) 解題思路（繁中）: 呢題係 hard tier — 考 deposit vs part payment vs penalty rule 嘅三向分辨，正正係 Panelist 最愛考嘅「看似可以反駁其實唔得」嘅 doctrinal boundary。答題次序：(1) 定性 — 合約寫明 "as a deposit and in part payment"，根據 Mayson v Clouet 嘅 intention 測試，呢個係 deposit；(2) deposit 嘅法律本質係 earnest / 履約保證，買方違約 → 沒收， 唔理賣方有無實際損失 （Polyset v Panhandat — CFA 權威）；(3) penalty rule（Dunlop Pneumatic / Cavendish v Makdessi）只規管 liquidated damages clause， 唔碰 deposit forfeiture — 呢個係 Annie 論據嘅死因；(4) LARCO s.16(2) 係 frustration 嘅 loss apportionment，同 breach 無關。 Rule Check: Polyset Ltd v Panhandat Ltd (2002) 5 HKCFAR 234; Howe v Smith (1884) 27 Ch D 89; Mayson v Clouet (1924) AC 980; Dies v British and International Mining and Finance Corp Ltd (1939) 1 KB 724; Law Amendment and Reform (Consolidation) Ordinance (Cap. 23) s.16(2) Common Trap（繁中）: 最大陷阱係 Option A — 用 penalty rule 去攻擊 deposit forfeiture 係經典錯誤；penalty doctrine 只打 liquidated damages，唔打 deposit。Option D 都係伏：part payment 先可以 recoverable subject to set off，但呢度白紙黑字寫明 "deposit"，定性已經唔同。考試遇到預付款題，第一步永遠係 characterisation（deposit or part payment？）。 Q5 — Answer: Bait advertising under s.13G of the Trade Descriptions Ordinance (Cap. 362); maximum penalty: a fine of HK$500,000 and imprisonment for 5 years (s.18(1) of the TDO). Model Answer (EN): TechStyle Ltd has committed the offence of bait advertising under s.13G of the Trade Descriptions Ordinance (Cap. 362). A trader commits this offence where it advertises products for supply at a specified price and there are no reasonable grounds for believing that it will be able to offer those products for supply at that price for a period that is, and in quantities that are, reasonable — having regard to the nature of the market and the nature of the advertisement (ss.13G(1) and (2)). Here, TechStyle Ltd held only five units city wide for a heavily promoted one day flash sale to the general public and did not state the limited quantity in the advertisement; it therefore had no reasonable grounds for believing it could supply in reasonable quantities. (The defence in s.13G(3) — where the advertisement clearly states the period or quantities and the trader honours it — is unavailable.) The maximum penalty on conviction is a fine of HK$500,000 and imprisonment for 5 years (s.18(1) of the TDO); the court may also order compensation to consumers who suffered financial loss (s.18A(1) of the TDO). 解題思路（繁中）: TDO 六宗罪嘅分辨係 consumer law 嘅考核熱點。呢題嘅事實 pattern 係「廣告抵價 + 無講限量 + 實際存貨極少」→ 對正 bait advertising (s.13G) 嘅定義：無 reasonable grounds 相信能以該價供應合理數量。同 neighbouring offences 嘅分別：(1) bait and switch (s.13H) 需要 trader 發出 invitation to purchase 之後，為推銷另一產品而 拒絕展示/示範、拒絕接單或展示缺陷樣本 — 呢度 TechStyle 只係賣晒，無拒絕展示或接單嘅行為，所以唔係 13H；(2) misleading omission (s.13E) 係遺漏 material information 導致 average consumer 作出本唔會作嘅 transactional decision — 雖然無披露存貨量都似遺漏，但 TDO 對「廣告價供應量」有專門條文 13G，specific provision 應優先適用；(3) wrongly accepting payment (s.13I) 需要 收咗錢 兼意圖唔供應或無合理理由相信能供應 — 呢度無收 consumer 錢，唔啱。罰則數字要背：HK$500,000 + 5 年（s.18(1)）。 Rule Check: Trade Descriptions Ordinance (Cap. 362) ss.13G(1)–(3), s.18(1), s.18A(1) Common Trap（繁中）: (1) 13G vs 13H 係最大伏位 — 問自己：trader 有冇「拒絕展示/接單/俾缺陷樣本」去轉推另一件產品？有 → 13H；無，純粹存貨唔夠兼廣告冇講 → 13G。(2) 唔好一見「無披露」就答 13E — 有專門 offence 就用專門 offence。(3) 13I 一定要收咗錢先成立。

text: M10 Chapter 3: Principles of Contract and Consumer Law in Hong Kong (Part 2) — Phase 3 Quiz Rules: Closed book · 15 minutes · 5 questions · Submit as 1. … 2. … 3. … 4. … 5. … — 超時如實申報 Q1. Under the Sale of Goods Ordinance (Cap. 26) ('SOGO'), which section implies into a contract of sale — where the seller sells goods in the course of a business — a condition that the goods supplied are of merchantable (satisfactory) quality? A. Section 14(1) B. Section 15(1) C. Section 16(2) D. Section 17(2) Q2. Mei Ling signed a contract with Harbour Suites Ltd to hire a harbour view function suite for the evening of the Lunar New Year fireworks display. The written contract stated that the suite was hired "for the purpose of viewing the fireworks display over Victoria Harbour". Three days before the event, the Government announced that, due to an unexpected safety incident at the launch site, the fireworks display was cancelled. Mei Ling now refuses to pay the hire fee, and Harbour Suites Ltd sues her for the price. Which of the following best states Mei Ling's legal position? A. She must pay, because the suite was still available for her use and the cancellation of the fireworks display does not affect Harbour Suites Ltd's ability to perform. B. She must pay, because her contract with Harbour Suites Ltd is void for common mistake, and a void contract still requires the price to be paid. C. She is not liable to pay, because the contract was frustrated: the happening of the fireworks display was the common foundation of the contract, and its cancellation discharged both parties automatically (applying Krell v Henry (1903) 2 KB 740). D. She is not liable to pay, because Harbour Suites Ltd committed an actionable misrepresentation by failing to warn her that the fireworks display might be cancelled. Q3. Kelvin agreed to sell his coffee shop business to Doris. During negotiations, Kelvin told Doris: "The shop's weekly takings average about HK$80,000." Kelvin honestly believed this, but he was relying on year old figures and had carelessly failed to check the current books; the true average was HK$50,000. Relying on this statement, Doris bought the business from Kelvin and suffered loss. Doris now wishes to claim damages from Kelvin (in addition to rescission). Which of the following represents Doris's strongest route to damages, and why? A. The tort of deceit at common law, because Kelvin's false statement was made without any belief in its truth. B. Negligent misstatement at common law, because the burden of proof is on Kelvin and all losses directly flowing from the transaction are recoverable regardless of foreseeability. C. Section 3(2) of the Misrepresentation Ordinance (Cap. 284), because it entitles Doris to damages as of right for a negligent misrepresentation. D. Section 3(1) of the Misrepresentation Ordinance (Cap. 284), because no special relationship need be shown, the burden is on Kelvin to prove he had reasonable grounds for his belief, and damages are assessed as if the misrepresentation had been fraudulent. Q4. In March, Annie agreed to buy Patrick's flat in Mid Levels for HK$6,000,000. She paid Patrick HK$600,000, described in the contract as "a deposit and in part payment of the purchase price". In June, before completion, Annie told Patrick that she would not complete the purchase. Patrick immediately put the flat back on the market and sold it two weeks later to a third party for HK$6,100,000. Patrick has therefore suffered no loss. Annie now demands the return of her HK$600,000, arguing that Patrick lost nothing and that keeping the whole sum would be an unenforceable penalty. Which of the following best states the legal position? A. Patrick must return the HK$600,000 because, having suffered no loss, retaining it would constitute a penalty and is therefore unenforceable. B. Patrick may forfeit the entire HK$600,000 deposit, because a deposit is an earnest of performance and is liable to forfeiture upon the buyer's default regardless of whether the seller has suffered any loss (applying Polyset Ltd v Panhandat Ltd (2002) 5 HKCFAR 234 and Howe v Smith (1884) 27 Ch D 89). C. Patrick must return the HK$600,000, less only his actual expenses, because under s.16(2) of the Law Amendment and Reform (Consolidation) Ordinance (Cap. 23) a payee may retain no more than a just sum limited to his expenses. D. Patrick must return the HK$600,000, subject only to a right to set off damages, because all advance payments are impliedly conditional upon completion of the contract (applying Dies v British and International Mining and Finance Corp Ltd (1939) 1 KB 724). Q5. TechStyle Ltd placed online advertisements stating: "Flash Sale — tomorrow only: our flagship smartwatch at HK$999 (usual price HK$3,330)!" The advertisement said nothing about limited stock. TechStyle Ltd in fact held only five units of that model in the whole of Hong Kong, and all five were sold within the first ten minutes of the sale. Hundreds of consumers who visited TechStyle Ltd's stores and website later that day were told the model was sold out. Identify the offence committed by TechStyle Ltd under the Trade Descriptions Ordinance (Cap. 362), citing the relevant section, and state the maximum penalty for such an offence.

text: M10 Chapter 4: The Law of Tort and Negligence — Phase 1 速查表 + Phase 2 閃卡 Phase 1 速查表 Learning Objectives 1. Analyse the legal meaning of tort and distinguish the three types of tortious liability (intentional tort, negligence, strict liability). 2. Apply the three elements of negligence — duty of care, breach of duty, and causation/remoteness of damage — to novel fact patterns using the IRAC method. 3. Evaluate the availability of defences (contributory negligence, voluntary assumption of risk) and statutory limits on excluding liability. 4. Assess the tortious liability of professionals (accountants and auditors) for negligent misstatement to clients and third parties. 5. Distinguish the special liability regimes: employers' liability, vicarious liability, occupiers' liability and defamation. 必背考點 A. Relevant Ordinances (Cap. + section numbers) Ordinance Provision Rule Limitation Ordinance (Cap. 347) s.4(1) General limitation period for actions in tort: 6 years Limitation Ordinance (Cap. 347) s.27 Personal injuries: 3 years ; fatal cases: 3 years from date of death or personal representative's knowledge of death, whichever is later Law Amendment and Reform (Consolidation) Ordinance (Cap. 23) ('LARCO') s.21(1) Contributory negligence does not defeat the claim, but damages are reduced as the court thinks just and equitable LARCO (Cap. 23) s.21(2) Court must first find and record the total damages that would have been recoverable, then reduce by apportionment Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) s.415(2) Any provision exempting an auditor from liability for negligence/default/breach of duty/breach of trust in performing audit duties is void Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) s.415(3) Any provision by which the company (directly or indirectly) indemnifies an auditor against such liability is void Control of Exemption Clauses Ordinance (Cap. 71) ('CECO') s.7(a) Cannot exclude or restrict liability for death or personal injury resulting from negligence CECO (Cap. 71) s.7(b) For other loss/damage, exclusion only valid if the term satisfies the reasonableness requirement CECO (Cap. 71) s.7(c) Agreement to / awareness of an exemption clause is not of itself voluntary acceptance of risk CECO (Cap. 71) s.2(2) ss.7–12 apply only to business liability (subject to s.11(4)) Factories and Industrial Undertakings Ordinance (Cap. 59) ('FIUO') s.6A Proprietor of an industrial undertaking must ensure, so far as is reasonably practicable, the health and safety at work of all employees FIUO (Cap. 59) s.18 Onus on the proprietor to prove it was not practicable/reasonably practicable to do more, or that all reasonable steps were taken Occupational Safety and Health Ordinance (Cap. 509) — Statutory duties owed by employer to employees (may be pleaded together with common law safe system of work) Employees' Compensation Ordinance (Cap. 282) — Statutory compensation claim is a separate action from a common law negligence claim; no double recovery Occupiers Liability Ordinance (Cap. 314) ('OLO') s.3 Occupier owes a common duty of care — visitors reasonably safe in using the premises OLO (Cap. 314) s.2(2), s.2(3) Occupier = person with occupancy and control (not ownership) over premises, including fixed/movable structures, vessels, vehicles, aircraft OLO (Cap. 314) s.4 Landlord may assign duty to tenant , who then becomes liable as occupier OLO (Cap. 314) s.3(2) Common duty of care defined: reasonable care that the visitor (not the premises) is reasonably safe for permitted purposes OLO (Cap. 314) s.3(3)(a) Occupier must expect children to be less careful than adults (allurement/trap) OLO (Cap. 314) s.3(3)(b) Occupier may expect a skilled visitor to guard against special risks ordinarily incident to his calling (not defects in the premises) OLO (Cap. 314) s.3(4)(a) A warning does not absolve the occupier unless in all the circumstances it was enough to enable the visitor to be reasonably safe OLO (Cap. 314) s.3(4)(b) Occupier not answerable for faulty work of a competent independent contractor if he acted reasonably in selecting and checking OLO (Cap. 314) s.3(5) No obligation for risks willingly accepted by the visitor (volenti) OLO (Cap. 314) s.3(1) Occupier may extend/restrict/exclude liability by agreement , subject to CECO and other restrictions Defamation Ordinance (Cap. 21) s.26 Defence of justification does not fail merely because not every charge is proved true, if unproved charges do not materially injure reputation Hong Kong Bill of Rights Ordinance (Cap. 383) s.8, Art. 16 Defamation law must be read in light of freedom of expression B. Leading Cases (full citation as given in the LP) Duty of care Donoghue v Stevenson (1932) AC 562 — the neighbour principle : reasonable care to avoid acts/omissions you can reasonably foresee would injure persons so closely and directly affected that you ought to have them in contemplation. Manufacturer owed duty to ultimate consumer (snail in ginger beer). Anns v Merton London Borough Council — two fold test (proximity + policy negating the duty); later criticised. Yuen Kun Yeu v Attorney General of Hong Kong (1988) AC 175 PC — Privy Council: Anns first stage too ambiguous; foreseeability of harm must not be neglected. Caparo Industries plc v Dickman (1990) 2 AC 605 — three fold test : (1) foreseeability of damage; (2) close and direct relationship of proximity; (3) fair, just and reasonable to impose a duty. Auditor owes duty to shareholders as a body , not to non shareholders contemplating investment. Palsgraf v Long Island Railroad Co (1928) 248 NY 339 — no duty to a plaintiff whose injury was unforeseeable to a person of ordinary vigilance. Bourhill v Young (1943) AC 92 — plaintiff 45–50 feet away, outside the range of foreseeable harm; no liability for nervous shock. Barrett v Enfield London Borough Council (2001) 2 AC 550 — policy balancing: promoting individual autonomy, preventing indeterminate liability, protecting the vulnerable. Breach / standard of care Blyth v Birmingham Waterworks Co (1856) 11 Exch 781 — the reasonable person test (objective). Roe v Minister of Health (1954) 2 QB 66 — standard assessed by knowledge at the time of the incident ("must not look at the 1947 accident with 1954 spectacles" — Denning LJ). Bolam v Friern Hospital Management Committee (1957) 1 WLR 582 — Bolam test : not negligent if acting in accordance with a practice accepted as proper by a responsible body of skilled professionals; inexperience is no defence — the test focuses on the activity, not the person. Ho Ying Wai v Keliston Marine (Far East) Ltd (2003) 1 HKLRD 343 — GP who accepted a commercial diver fitness retainer was expected to acquire the competency of a reasonably competent practitioner in that field; liable. Bolton v Stone (1951) AC 850 — very low likelihood of risk + high cost of prevention → no breach (cricket ball). Paris v Stepney Borough Council (1951) AC 367 — greater seriousness of potential harm (one eyed worker) → higher standard; goggles should have been provided. Latimer v A.E.C. Ltd (1953) AC 643 — employer not required to eliminate risk at disproportionate cost (sawdust on flooded floor sufficient; no duty to close factory). Rimmer v Liverpool City Council (1984) 1 All ER 930 — codes of practice alert the defendant to appropriate standards; failure to follow may constitute breach. Causation / remoteness 'But for' test — plaintiff must prove on the balance of probabilities that but for the defendant's act/omission, the injury would not have occurred. Barnett v Chelsea Hospital Management Committee (1969) 1 QB 428 — hospital negligent, but victim would have died anyway → causation failed. McGhee v National Coal Board (1973) 1 WLR 1 — where precise cause is unknown, material contribution to the risk of injury suffices. Thin skull rule — defendant takes the victim as he finds him: Smith v Leech Brain & Co — liable for full extent (death from cancer triggered by foreseeable burn). Novus actus interveniens — an intervening act breaks the chain of causation only if it was not reasonably foreseeable to the defendant: Hui Kay Cheong, Herman v Chi Wo Properties Ltd (1992) HKDCLR 51 (foreseeable robbery did NOT break the chain) vs Leung Sin Fai v Perfect World Co Ltd (1998) 2 HKLRD 115 (unforeseeable inflammable liquid DID break the chain). Res ipsa loquitur — Sanfield Building Contractors Ltd v Li Kai Cheong (2003) 3 HKLRD 48 (CFA): accident of unknown cause that would not normally happen without negligence, where defendant controlled the object/activity → inference of negligence unless defendant offers an acceptable explanation consistent with reasonable care (essence per Lord Radcliffe in Barkway v South Wales Transport Co Ltd (1950) 1 All ER 392). Defences to negligence Contributory negligence — onus on the defendant; partial defence leading to apportionment under s.21 LARCO (Cap. 23). Chan Wing Kin & Anor v Fonnie Co (1983) HKLR 102 — pregnant front seat passenger not wearing seat belt NOT contributory negligent in the circumstances (fault, not mere conduct, must cause the injury). Volenti non fit injuria — complete defence; requires proof of negligence + plaintiff's full knowledge of the nature and extent of the risk + consent (explicit or implied agreement to waive liability); mere knowledge is insufficient. Simms v Leigh Rugby Football Club (1969) 2 All ER 923 — rugby player willingly accepted risks of a compliant ground. Accountants/auditors & negligent misstatement Hedley Byrne & Co Ltd v Heller & Partners Ltd (1964) AC 465 — negligent misrepresentation actionable only where a 'special relationship' exists (assumption of responsibility, equivalent to contract; relationships such as solicitor/client, banker/customer); disclaimer 'without responsibility' negated liability. Caparo Industries plc v Dickman (1990) 2 AC 605 — auditor's duty limited to shareholders' class rights, not potential investors. James McNaughton Paper Group Ltd v Hicks Anderson & Co (1991) 2 QB 113 — six criteria for duty to a third party: (1) purpose for which the statement was made; (2) purpose for which it was communicated; (3) relationship between advisor, advisee and third party; (4) size of the class to which the advisee belongs; (5) advisor's knowledge of the purpose; (6) reliance by the advisee. Accountant not liable to prospective purchaser who relied on draft accounts without consulting his own accountant. Employers' liability / vicarious liability McDermid v Nash Dredging & Reclamation Co Ltd (1987) AC 906 — employer's duty is personal and non delegable (delegation to a competent person is no defence). Four heads: safe place of work; competent employees + supervision; adequate plant and appliances; safe system of work. Davie v New Merton Board Mills (1959) 1 All ER 346 / Pearce v Round Oak Steel Works Ltd (1969) 1 WLR 595 — duty discharged by buying from reputable supplier + reasonable inspection; latent defect not discoverable by reasonable care excuses. Yuen Chung Shun v On Ascent Ltd (2016) 4 HKLRD 250 — complete failure of supervision → employer liable (with employee's contributory negligence). Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd v Wong Sau Lai (2006) 2 HKLRD 586 — unsafe system of work (no stopping mechanism on drawer); foreseeable momentary lapse under pressure → employer liable. Vicarious liability (strict liability for employee's torts in the course of employment): Dubai Aluminium Co Ltd v Salaam (2003) 2 AC 366 — employer's innocence irrelevant once employee's liability established. Salmond test (authorised wrongful act, or unauthorised mode of an authorised act); Close Connection Test from Lister v Hesley Hall Ltd (2002) 1 AC 215; applied in HK in Ming An Insurance Co (HK) Ltd v Ritz Carlton Ltd (2002) 3 HKLRD 844 (doorman's unauthorised food run in limousine still within course of employment). Occupiers' liability Chu Wo Heung & Anor v Hui Lai Wa (2002) 3 HKLRD 209 — building manager with control over external wall via DMC was an occupier of the awning; control, not ownership. Cooke v Midland Great Western Rly of Ireland (1909) AC 229 — unlocked turntable = allurement; occupier liable to child trespassers it knew played there. Contrast Latham v R Johnson & Nephew Ltd (1913) 1 KB 398 — ordinary heaps of stones, no trap/allurement → not liable. Wood v Wah Tung (E&M) Ltd (2000) HKEC 277 — frequent flooding/power failure → general safety reminder inadequate; specific warnings required. Roles v Nathan (1963) 1 WLR 1117 — chimney sweeps warned of gas risk; risk incidental to their calling → occupier not liable (s.3(3)(b) OLO equivalent). Tomlinson v Congleton BC (2004) 1 AC 46 — no duty to warn of obvious dangers . Luen Hing Fat Coating & Finishing Factory Ltd v Waan Chuen Ming (2011) 2 HKLRD 223 — occupier liable for own negligence in failing to engage/supervise a competent independent contractor. Trespassers: occupier owes no duty of reasonable care, even for concealed danger, unless harm deliberately intended (common law; OLO does not govern trespassers). Defamation Elements: (1) defamatory statement (lowers the person in the estimation of right thinking members of society / hatred, contempt or ridicule); (2) reference to the plaintiff (a purely personal action; a corporation may sue for statements disparaging its goodwill — Tung Lo Court (IO) v Tsui Wai Yip (2015) 4 HKLRD 397); (3) publication to a third party (not the defendant's spouse). Libel = permanent form; slander = transient form. Defendant's intention is irrelevant ; natural and ordinary meaning to ordinary reasonable viewers; legal innuendo must be pleaded separately. Cheung Ng Sheong Steven v Eastweek Publisher Ltd (1995) 3 HKC 601 — article attacking professor's discharge of duties = libel. Charles Sin Cho Chiu v Tin Tin Publication Development Ltd HCA 6662/1997 — group reference ('7 Honourable Men', 'tainted elements') can identify an individual plaintiff. Defences: justification (substantial truth of the imputation; s.26 Defamation Ordinance (Cap. 21)); fair comment (public interest + recognisable comment + based on true fact + honest opinion; defeated by malice ); absolute privilege (judicial/quasi judicial proceedings, public officers, Legislative Council); qualified privilege (duty/interest to communicate; lost if malicious); consent (must not exceed scope given). Remedies: damages (nominal / general compensatory / aggravated / exemplary / special) and injunction. C. IRAC Application Points (duty → breach → causation → remoteness → defences) Issue : identify which tort and which relationship (driver/passenger, professional/client, employer/employee, occupier/visitor, publisher/subject). Do not confuse negligent misstatement with ordinary negligence. Rule : state the correct test with authority — Caparo three fold test for duty; Bolam test for professional standard; but for test for factual causation; s.21 LARCO for apportionment; s.3 OLO for occupiers. Application : 1. Duty of care — run all three Caparo limbs in order: foreseeable? proximity? fair, just and reasonable?
