For pure economic loss or psychiatric harm, policy (indeterminate liability) usually narrows the duty. For statements, add Hedley Byrne 'special relationship' / James McNaughton six criteria. 2. Breach — objective reasonable person; adjust for skill (professionals held to their profession's standard; inexperience no defence); weigh likelihood ( Bolton v Stone ), seriousness ( Paris v Stepney ), cost of avoidance ( Latimer ), codes of practice ( Rimmer ). 3. Causation — but for first ( Barnett ); if scientifically uncertain, material contribution ( McGhee ); if the accident's cause is unknown but speaks of negligence, res ipsa loquitur ( Sanfield ). 4. Remoteness — foreseeable type of injury → liable for full extent (thin skull, Smith v Leech Brain ); unforeseeable intervening act breaks the chain (novus actus); foreseeable third party crime does not ( Hui Kay Cheong ). 5. Defences — contributory negligence (apportionment; onus on defendant) vs volenti (complete bar; needs full knowledge + consent); check statutory restrictions on exclusion clauses (CECO s.7; CO s.415(2)/(3)). Conclusion : give a decisive one sided answer (e.g. "Therefore, X is liable in negligence, subject to a reduction for contributory negligence") — never sit on the fence when facts are clear. 易混淆概念對比 Table 1: Negligence (ordinary) vs Negligent Misstatement 比較點 Negligence (ordinary negligence) Negligent Misstatement / Misrepresentation Nature of wrong Careless act or omission causing physical injury or property damage Careless statement/advice relied upon, causing (usually) pure economic loss Basis of duty Neighbour principle / Caparo three fold test (foreseeability + proximity + fair, just and reasonable) Caparo test plus a 'special relationship' with assumption of responsibility — Hedley Byrne v Heller (1964) AC 465 Duty to third parties Proximity judged by physical closeness, cause and effect, or control Only if James McNaughton six criteria support it (purpose, communication, relationship, class size, knowledge, reliance); auditor's duty stops at shareholders — Caparo Typical claimant Anyone foreseeably injured by the act Client or a third party the maker knew would rely on the statement Effect of disclaimer Cannot exclude death/personal injury liability at all (CECO s.7(a)) An express 'without responsibility' disclaimer can negate assumption of responsibility ( Hedley Byrne ) 點樣分辨：見到「講錯嘢／出錯 report 令人蝕錢」→ 一定諗 negligent misstatement ，第一步係搵 special relationship / assumption of responsibility ，唔好直接套 neighbour principle。考試伏位：Jun 2025 Panelists' Report 明確指出考生將 negligent misstatement 當普通 negligence 答，直接跌晒 application 分。留意純經濟損失（pure economic loss）本身係 policy 上收緊 duty 嘅訊號（preventing indeterminate liability）。 Table 2: Contributory Negligence vs Voluntary Assumption of Risk (Volenti Non Fit Injuria) 比較點 Contributory Negligence Voluntary Assumption of Risk Statutory basis s.21 LARCO (Cap. 23) Common law; OLO s.3(5) for occupiers Effect Partial defence — damages reduced by apportionment as just and equitable (s.21(2): record total first, then reduce) Complete defence — no liability at all What must be proved Plaintiff's fault contributed to his own injury (plaintiff owes no duty to defendant); onus on defendant Defendant was negligent and plaintiff had full knowledge of the nature and extent of the risk and consented (explicit/implied agreement to waive liability) Standard of proof Elements similar to negligence (causation, standard of care) Much more stringent — mere knowledge of the risk is insufficient Leading case Chan Wing Kin v Fonnie Co (1983) HKLR 102 (pregnant passenger — no contributory negligence) Simms v Leigh Rugby Football Club (1969) 2 All ER 923 (rugby player accepted inherent risks) 點樣分辨：淨係「佢知道有風險」→ 頂多 contributory negligence（扣減賠償）；要「知道 + 同意放棄追究」先係 volenti（完全免責）。考試伏位：唔好見到受害人冇戴 seat belt 就自動話 contributory negligence — 要證明係佢嘅 fault 造成傷害（ Chan Wing Kin ：孕婦唔戴反而合理）。另外 CECO s.7(c) 話明「同意豁免條款」唔等於自願承受風險。 Phase 2 閃卡 Card 1 Front: What are the three elements of the modern tort of negligence, and what test is applied to establish a duty of care? Back: Three elements: (1) duty of care; (2) breach of that duty; (3) damage caused by the breach. Duty of care — Caparo three fold test ( Caparo Industries plc v Dickman (1990) 2 AC 605): (1) damage foreseeable by the defendant; (2) close and direct relationship of proximity; (3) fair, just and reasonable to impose a duty. 💬 記住口訣「Duty–Breach–Damage」三步走；duty 嗰關要用 Caparo 三摺測試，三個 limbs 次序唔好亂：可預見 → 夠近 → 公平合理。少講一個 limb 都會失分。 Card 2 Front: State the neighbour principle from Donoghue v Stevenson (1932) AC 562 and its significance. Back: You must take reasonable care to avoid acts or omissions which you can reasonably foresee would be likely to injure your 'neighbour' — persons so closely and directly affected by your act that you ought reasonably to have them in contemplation. Significance: created a general test for duty of care without relying on recognised categories; negligence is an open concept — categories of liability are not closed. 💬 即係「薑汁啤酒蝸牛案」：製造商對最終消費者有 duty，即使冇合約關係。重點係佢打破咗「逐類案件先有人身責任」嘅舊框架，變成通用原則。 Card 3 Front: What is the Bolam test, and can a defendant rely on inexperience as a defence? Back: Bolam v Friern Hospital Management Committee (1957) 1 WLR 582: a professional is not negligent if he acted in accordance with a practice accepted as proper by a responsible body of skilled persons in that art; mere existence of a contrary body of opinion does not establish negligence. Inexperience is NOT a defence — the test focuses on the activity, not the person; the defendant is held to the standard of an ordinarily competent practitioner professing that skill. 💬 一個新牌醫生／會計師做專業嘢，就要即刻達到該專業嘅普通勝任標準，「我冇經驗」唔係藉口。 Ho Ying Wai 案：普通科醫生接咗潛水員體檢單，就要補足相關知識。 Card 4 Front: Explain the 'but for' test, and when does the 'material contribution' approach apply instead? Back: But for test: plaintiff must prove on the balance of probabilities that but for the defendant's act/omission, the injury would not have occurred. If the injury would have happened anyway → causation fails ( Barnett v Chelsea Hospital Management Committee (1969) 1 QB 428). Material contribution: where the precise cause is not scientifically known and there are multiple possible causes, it suffices that the defendant's negligence materially increased the risk / materially contributed to the injury ( McGhee v National Coal Board (1973) 1 WLR 1). 💬 舉證責任先喺原告（balance of probabilities），之後先轉去被告。 Barnett 係必考位：醫院明明疏忽，但病人點都會死 → 冇 causation → 唔使賠。 Card 5 Front: What is the thin skull rule, and which case illustrates it? Back: The defendant takes the victim as he finds him : once the type of injury is foreseeable, the defendant is liable for its full extent , even if aggravated by the plaintiff's peculiar pre existing condition. Smith v Leech Brain & Co : a foreseeable burn triggered cancer in a pre malignant tissue → liable for the death; unnecessary to show death by cancer was foreseeable. Do not confuse with foreseeability at the duty stage: the rule applies only after foreseeable harm is established; defendant need not better the plaintiff's original position. 💬 「蛋殼頭骨」原則：你撞親個人，就要接受佢本身脆弱。考試鍾意將佢同 duty 階段嘅 foreseeability 撈亂 — duty 階段係問「普通健康人會唔會受傷」，thin skull 係問「受咗傷之後賠幾多」。 Card 6 Front: Distinguish novus actus interveniens from res ipsa loquitur. Back: Novus actus interveniens: a subsequent independent act that breaks the chain of causation — but only if the intervening event was not reasonably foreseeable to the defendant. Foreseeable third party criminal acts do NOT break the chain ( Hui Kay Cheong v Chi Wo Properties (1992) HKDCLR 51); unforeseeable ones do ( Leung Sin Fai v Perfect World (1998) 2 HKLRD 115). Res ipsa loquitur: a rule of evidence — where an accident of unknown cause would not normally happen without negligence and the defendant controlled the object/activity, the court infers negligence unless the defendant gives an acceptable explanation consistent with reasonable care ( Sanfield Building Contractors Ltd v Li Kai Cheong (2003) 3 HKLRD 48). 💬 一個係「因果鏈斷咗 → 唔使賠」，一個係「事實本身就說明有疏忽 → 推定要賠」。Dec 2025 考生 novus actus 掌握差，記住關鍵字係 intervening event 可唔可以 reasonably foresee 。 Card 7 Front: Compare contributory negligence and volenti non fit injuria as defences to negligence. Back: Contributory negligence: partial defence; plaintiff's fault contributed to his own injury; damages reduced by apportionment under s.21(1) LARCO (Cap. 23); court must record total damages first (s.21(2)); onus on the defendant. Volenti: complete defence; requires defendant's negligence + plaintiff's full knowledge of the nature and extent of the risk + consent to waive liability; mere knowledge insufficient; e.g. Simms v Leigh Rugby Football Club (1969) 2 All ER 923. 💬 記住：CN = 扣分（賠少啲）；volenti = 出局（唔使賠）。Volenti 門檻高好多，「知有風險」唔等於「同意承受」。 Card 8 Front: When is a professional liable to a third party for a negligent misstatement? Back: Base rule: a 'special relationship' with assumption of responsibility is required ( Hedley Byrne v Heller (1964) AC 465); an auditor owes a duty to shareholders as a body but NOT to potential investors relying on published accounts ( Caparo v Dickman (1990) 2 AC 605). Third party duty assessed by the six James McNaughton Paper Group Ltd v Hicks Anderson & Co (1991) 2 QB 113 criteria: purpose of the statement; purpose of communication; relationship between advisor/advisee/third party; size of the class; advisor's knowledge of purpose; reliance by the advisee. A 'without responsibility' disclaimer may negate the duty. 💬 會計師／核數師章節重中之重：見到「第三方攞住份 report 去投資/借錢」即刻諗 Caparo + James McNaughton 六個因素，逐個 apply 落 facts，唔好齋背。 本章急救詞彙 EN Term 繁中白話 English Model Sentence Duty of care 謹慎責任：法律要求你對「可預見會受你行為影響嘅人」保持合理小心 Under the Caparo three fold test, a duty of care arises only where damage is foreseeable, proximity exists, and it is fair, just and reasonable to impose it. Proximity 接近性：原告同被告之間「夠近」嘅關係，可以係物理上、因果上或管理控制上 Proximity may be established by physical closeness, by cause and effect, or by the defendant's control over the relevant activity. Novus actus interveniens 介入事件：之後出現嘅獨立新原因，如果被告預見唔到，就會斬斷因果鏈 The surgeon's unforeseeable negligence was a novus actus interveniens that broke the chain of causation between the driver's breach and the patient's death. Res ipsa loquitur 事實自證：意外本身已說明有疏忽，除非被告提出合理解釋 Where a scaffold of a type that would not normally topple fell without explanation, res ipsa loquitur allowed the court to infer the contractor's negligence (Sanfield). Volenti non fit injuria 自願承受風險：完全抗辯，但必須證明受害人完全知情兼同意 The defence of volenti non fit injuria failed because mere knowledge of the risk did not amount to consent to waive liability. Contributory negligence 與有過失：受害人自己都有份造成傷害，賠償按比例扣減 Under s.21 of the LARCO (Cap. 23), the passenger's damages were reduced by 25% for his contributory negligence in not wearing a seat belt. Vicarious liability 僱主轉承責任：僱員喺受僱期間犯侵權，僱主即使無過失都要孭 Under the Close Connection Test in Lister v Hesley Hall, the employer was vicariously liable because the employee's tort was closely connected with his employment. Negligent misstatement 疏忽失實陳述：喺 special relationship 下講錯嘢令人蝕錢，要孭純經濟損失 Because the auditors never assumed responsibility to the potential investor, no duty of care arose for the alleged negligent misstatement (Caparo v Dickman).

title: M10 Chapter 4: The Law of Tort and Negligence — Phase 3 Answers
headings: M10 Chapter 4: The Law of Tort and Negligence — Phase 3 Answers
excerpt: M10 Chapter 4: The Law of Tort and Negligence — Phase 3 Answers Q1 — Answer: B Model Answer (EN): In Caparo Industries plc v Dickman (1990) 2 AC 605, the House …
text: M10 Chapter 4: The Law of Tort and Negligence — Phase 3 Answers Q1 — Answer: B Model Answer (EN): In Caparo Industries plc v Dickman (1990) 2 AC 605, the House of Lords refined the neighbour principle into a three fold test for a duty of care: (1) the plaintiff's damage or injury was foreseeable by the defendant; (2) there was a close and direct relationship of proximity between the parties; and (3) it was fair, just and reasonable in the circumstances to impose a duty of care. Option B states exactly these three limbs. 解題思路（繁中）: 呢題係 easy tier rule recall，考你分唔分到 Caparo 三摺測試同其他測試。Option A 係 Anns two fold test （proximity + policy negation）— 係 Caparo 之前嘅版本，已經被取代； Yuen Kun Yeu v Attorney General of Hong Kong (1988) AC 175 (PC) 批評 Anns 第一步忽略咗 foreseeability。Option C 講「recognised categories of liability」，正正係 Donoghue v Stevenson 之前嘅舊制度， neighbour principle 就係要擺脫佢。Option D 係 Hedley Byrne 嘅 special relationship / assumption of responsibility 框架，只適用於 negligent misstatement，唔係一般 duty of care 嘅測試。考試伏位：題目問邊個 case 嘅測試就要答邊個，唔好將 Anns、Hedley Byrne、Caparo 三個撈埋一碟。 Rule Check: Caparo Industries plc v Dickman (1990) 2 AC 605; contrast Donoghue v Stevenson (1932) AC 562 and Hedley Byrne & Co Ltd v Heller & Partners Ltd (1964) AC 465. Common Trap（繁中）: 見到「proximity」就揀 A — 記住 Anns 係 two fold，Caparo 係 three fold；Caparo 嘅獨有標誌係 foreseeability + proximity + fair, just and reasonable 三項齊全。 Q2 — Answer: B Model Answer (EN): Under s.27 of the Limitation Ordinance (Cap. 347), the time limit for commencing an action in tort for personal injuries is three years from the date the cause of action accrued (the accident). Marco must therefore commence his action by 10 June 2026. The six year period in s.4(1) of the Ordinance applies to tort actions in general, not to personal injury claims. 解題思路（繁中）: 呢題考 pinpoint section knowledge — Exam Lens 明講 open book 考試期望你準確引用條文。關鍵係分開兩條： s.4(1) = 一般 tort 六年； s.27 = 人身傷害三年。Option A 錯在用咗 s.4(1) 嘅六年落 personal injury；Option C 錯在將「知悉受傷日期」套落一般人身傷害 — 「knowledge」起算只適用於 fatal cases （由死者死亡日期或遺產代理人知悉日期起計，以較後者為準），Marco 冇死，唔適用；Option D 完全虛構，所有訴訟因由都有 limitation period。記住 fatal case 嘅三年先至可以用 knowledge 起算。 Rule Check: Limitation Ordinance (Cap. 347) s.4(1) and s.27. Common Trap（繁中）: 背咗「六年」就即刻揀 — 一見 personal injuries 就要轉 channel 去 s.27 嘅三年。另一伏位：將 fatal case 嘅 knowledge 起算規則套用落普通受傷個案。 Q3 — Answer: D Model Answer (EN): Kelvin is not liable. Liability for negligent misstatement cannot be founded on the Donoghue v Stevenson neighbour principle alone; the representor must have expressly or impliedly assumed responsibility for the statement, i.e. a 'special relationship' must exist between representor and recipient ( Hedley Byrne & Co Ltd v Heller & Partners Ltd (1964) AC 465, per Lord Reid). Here Kelvin expressly disclaimed responsibility ('I accept no responsibility'), so no assumption of responsibility arose and no duty of care was owed to Dora — just as the 'without responsibility' disclaimer defeated liability in Hedley Byrne itself. Moreover, applying Caparo v Dickman (1990) 2 AC 605, an auditor's duty in respect of published accounts does not extend to non shareholders contemplating investment. 解題思路（繁中）: 呢題係 medium tier IRAC scenario，考嘅正係 Jun 2025 Panelists' Report 點名嘅弱項： negligent misstatement ≠ ordinary negligence 。Issue：Kelvin 欠唔欠 Dora duty of care（misstatement）。Rule：Hedley Byrne special relationship + assumption of responsibility。Application：Kelvin 明確 disclaimer「accept no responsibility」，冇 assumption of responsibility；況且 Dora 係非股東潛在投資者，Caparo 都唔幫佢。Conclusion：唔使賠。Option A 錯在「anyone who foreseeably relies」— misstatement 嘅 duty 遠比 foreseeability 窄，否則就係 indeterminate liability（Caparo 第三個 limb 嘅 policy 考量）。Option B 錯在單靠 neighbour principle — Lord Reid 喺 Hedley Byrne 明講唔得。Option C 太絕對：社交場合都可以有 special relationship，重點唔係場合，係有冇 assumption of responsibility，所以 C 嘅推理唔成立。 Rule Check: Hedley Byrne & Co Ltd v Heller & Partners Ltd (1964) AC 465; Caparo Industries plc v Dickman (1990) 2 AC 605. Common Trap（繁中）: 一見「會計師講錯嘢 + 有人蝕錢」就寫 negligence 三元素 — 凡涉及 陳述 同 純經濟損失 ，第一步一定要搵 special relationship / assumption of responsibility，同埋檢查有冇 disclaimer。 Q4 — Answer: C Model Answer (EN): GuardForce is vicariously liable. Vicarious liability is a form of strict liability: once the employee's tort is established, the employer's innocent state of mind is irrelevant ( Dubai Aluminium Co Ltd v Salaam (2003) 2 AC 366). For an intentional wrong committed for the employee's own purposes, the Salmond test is unhelpful; the applicable test is the Close Connection Test from Lister v Hesley Hall Ltd (2002) 1 AC 215: whether the employee's tort is so closely connected with his employment that it would be fair and just to hold the employer vicariously liable. Rex committed the tort on duty, in uniform, while purporting to deal with a suspected theft on the very premises he was employed to protect. The tort was closely connected with his employment, so GuardForce is vicariously liable. 解題思路（繁中）: 呢題係 medium tier，考 vicarious liability 嘅 modern test。Option A 錯：故意侵權唔係自動豁免 — Lister 正正係故意性侵案都判僱主孭。Option B 錯在死抱 Salmond test 嘅「authorised act」第一枝；就算第二枝「unauthorised mode」都唔啱用， Lister 已經話對故意自肥行為 Salmond test 冇用，要用 Close Connection Test（香港 Ming An Insurance Co (HK) Ltd v Ritz Carlton Ltd (2002) 3 HKLRD 844 有跟用）。Option D 錯在混淆咗僱主 個人/非轉承責任 （breach of duty to employ competent employees）同 vicarious liability — 後者係 strict liability，唔使證明僱主自己有疏忽。Dec 2024 panel report 話考生對 vicarious liability 理解差，答咗啲 general employment law 嘢，呢題就係針對呢個伏位。 Rule Check: Lister v Hesley Hall Ltd (2002) 1 AC 215; Dubai Aluminium Co Ltd v Salaam (2003) 2 AC 366; cf. Ming An Insurance Co (HK) Ltd v Ritz Carlton Ltd (2002) 3 HKLRD 844. Common Trap（繁中）: 見到「故意打人有刑事成分」就以為僱主一定甩身 — 記住 vicarious liability 係 strict liability ，僱主清白與否唔相干，問題只剩一個：個 tort 同份工夠唔夠 close connection。 Q5 — Answer: B Model Answer (EN): SecureCo's argument fails. A novus actus interveniens breaks the chain of causation only if the intervening event was not reasonably foreseeable by the defendant; if the intervening event was something the defendant ought reasonably to have anticipated, the defendant remains liable. In Hui Kay Cheong, Herman v Chi Wo Properties Ltd (1992) HKDCLR 51, a management company that failed to provide adequate security was liable for a robbery because the burglary was a highly foreseeable consequence of its failure to safeguard the building — the criminals' act did not break the chain. By contrast, in Leung Sin Fai v Perfect World Co Ltd (1998) 2 HKLRD 115, an unforeseeable third party act (inflammable liquid in a toilet bowl) did break the chain. Here, the very purpose of SecureCo's engagement was to guard against theft; the burglary was precisely the foreseeable risk of leaving the warehouse unguarded. Causation is therefore established against SecureCo (but for the absent guard, the theft would not have occurred). 解題思路（繁中）: 呢題係 hard tier，考 Dec 2025 panel report 話考生「poor grasp」嘅 novus actus interveniens 。核心規則：介入行為要 unforeseeable 先斷到因果鏈；預見到嘅第三方犯罪行為 唔會 斷鏈（Hui Kay Cheong），預見唔到先會（Leung Sin Fai）。Option A 錯在「always breaks」— 冇呢個絕對規則，否則保安公司永遠唔使負責。Option C 錯在亂入 pure economic loss — BrightTech 係貨物被盜，屬 property damage ，唔係純經濟損失；而且 duty 方面 SecureCo 嘅合約職責就係保安，proximity 充足。Option D 錯在「intention」— 被告有冇意圖促成盜竊同因果鏈完全無關，測試係 foreseeability of the intervention 。答呢類題嘅次序：Issue (novus actus?) → Rule (foreseeable intervention唔斷鏈) → Application (保安失守→爆竊係高度可預見) → Conclusion (SecureCo liable)。 Rule Check: Hui Kay Cheong, Herman v Chi Wo Properties Ltd (1992) HKDCLR 51; contrast Leung Sin Fai v Perfect World Co Ltd (1998) 2 HKLRD 115. Common Trap（繁中）: 一見「第三者犯罪」就直覺答「斷鏈」— 呢個正係 Dec 2025 考生跌分位。口訣： foreseeable intervention = chain intact; unforeseeable intervention = chain broken 。答題時兩個 HK 案例一成一敗並列，分數先穩。

title: M10 Chapter 4: The Law of Tort and Negligence — Phase 3 Quiz
headings: M10 Chapter 4: The Law of Tort and Negligence — Phase 3 Quiz
excerpt: M10 Chapter 4: The Law of Tort and Negligence — Phase 3 Quiz Rules: Closed book · 15 minutes · 5 questions · Submit as 1. … 2. … 3. … 4. … 5. … — 超時如實申報 Q1 Whic…
text: M10 Chapter 4: The Law of Tort and Negligence — Phase 3 Quiz Rules: Closed book · 15 minutes · 5 questions · Submit as 1. … 2. … 3. … 4. … 5. … — 超時如實申報 Q1 Which of the following correctly states the three fold test for establishing a duty of care under Caparo Industries plc v Dickman (1990) 2 AC 605? A. Sufficient proximity or neighbourhood between the parties, and the absence of any policy reason that ought to negate or reduce the scope of the duty B. The plaintiff's damage was foreseeable by the defendant; there was a close and direct relationship of proximity; and it was fair, just and reasonable to impose a duty of care C. The defendant owed the plaintiff a duty by virtue of a recognised category of liability, and a reasonable person would have foreseen the plaintiff's injury D. The defendant assumed responsibility towards the plaintiff, the plaintiff relied on that assumption, and the plaintiff suffered pure economic loss as a result Q2 On 10 June 2023, Marco was injured in a traffic accident negligently caused by Kelvin. Marco now wishes to commence a tort action against Kelvin for his personal injuries . Under the Limitation Ordinance (Cap. 347), which statement is correct? A. Marco must commence his action within six years of the accident, i.e. by 10 June 2029, under s.4(1) of the Ordinance B. Marco must commence his action within three years of the accident, i.e. by 10 June 2026, under s.27 of the Ordinance C. Marco must commence his action within six years of the date he first knew of his injury, under s.27 of the Ordinance D. No limitation period applies to personal injury claims because they concern bodily integrity, so Marco may sue at any time Q3 Dora is considering investing her savings in shares of Target Ltd, a private company. At a dinner party, she asks her friend Kelvin, a chartered accountant who has just completed Target Ltd's audit, for his views. Kelvin replies: "Off the record — I accept no responsibility for this — but the company looks financially sound to me." Relying on this remark, Dora purchases shares in Target Ltd. The accounts in fact contain material errors that Kelvin carelessly overlooked during the audit, and Dora loses most of her investment. Dora sues Kelvin in tort. Which of the following is the best analysis? A. Kelvin is liable: as a professional, he owes a duty of care to anyone whom he can foresee may rely on his statements about the audited company B. Kelvin is liable: the neighbour principle in Donoghue v Stevenson (1932) AC 562 is, by itself, sufficient to found liability for his careless statement C. Kelvin is not liable: a social remark can never give rise to tortious liability, regardless of the speaker's profession or the reliance placed on it D. Kelvin is not liable: under Hedley Byrne & Co Ltd v Heller & Partners Ltd (1964) AC 465, liability for negligent misstatement requires a special relationship with an assumption of responsibility, and Kelvin's express disclaimer of responsibility negated any such assumption Q4 GuardForce Ltd employs Rex as a security guard at a shopping mall. Rex is required to wear a uniform and to patrol the mall during his shifts. One afternoon, while on duty and in uniform, Rex suspects May, a shopper, of shoplifting. Without any instruction from GuardForce, Rex grabs May's arm to detain her, twisting it and causing her a fractured wrist. May sues GuardForce Ltd. Which of the following is the best analysis? A. GuardForce is not liable: an employer is never vicariously liable for an employee's intentional torts, which are by definition outside the course of employment B. GuardForce is not liable: under the Salmond test, an employee's tort is within the course of employment only if the employer authorised the specific wrongful act, and GuardForce gave no such authorisation C. GuardForce is liable: under the Close Connection Test ( Lister v Hesley Hall Ltd (2002) 1 AC 215), Rex's tort was so closely connected with his employment — committed on duty, in uniform, in the course of dealing with a suspected theft on the premises — that it is fair and just to hold GuardForce vicariously liable D. GuardForce is liable only if it can be shown that GuardForce itself was negligent in hiring or supervising Rex; otherwise an employer cannot be liable for an act it did not commit Q5 Fortune Logistics Ltd stores valuable electronic goods for its customers in its warehouse. Under its contract with the building's management company, SecureCo Ltd, SecureCo must provide overnight security guards at the warehouse. One night, the sole guard on duty falls asleep at his post, leaving the warehouse entrance unmonitored. Thieves enter and steal goods belonging to BrightTech Ltd, a customer of Fortune Logistics. BrightTech sues SecureCo in negligence. SecureCo argues that the thieves' criminal act is a novus actus interveniens that breaks the chain of causation between any negligence on its part and BrightTech's loss. Which of the following is the best analysis? A. SecureCo's argument succeeds: a deliberate criminal act of an independent third party always breaks the chain of causation as a matter of law B. SecureCo's argument fails: the burglary was a highly foreseeable consequence of SecureCo's failure to safeguard the premises, so the intervening criminal act does not break the chain of causation ( Hui Kay Cheong, Herman v Chi Wo Properties Ltd (1992) HKDCLR 51) C. SecureCo's argument succeeds: SecureCo owed no duty of care to BrightTech because BrightTech's loss is pure economic loss, which is never recoverable in negligence D. SecureCo's argument fails, but only because SecureCo can be shown to have intended the theft; without such intention the criminal act would break the chain End of quiz. Do not open the answers file until you have submitted all five answers.

title: M10 Chapter 5: Aspects of Agency Law — Phase 1 速查表 + Phase 2 閃卡
headings: M10 Chapter 5: Aspects of Agency Law — Phase 1 速查表 + Phase 2 閃卡
A. Relevant Ordinances（考試要 pinpoint 到 Cap. + section）
B. Leading cases（full citation 以 LP 所引為準）
excerpt: M10 Chapter 5: Aspects of Agency Law — Phase 1 速查表 + Phase 2 閃卡 Phase 1 速查表 Learning Objectives 1. Analyse the essential elements of an agency relationship and …
text: M10 Chapter 5: Aspects of Agency Law — Phase 1 速查表 + Phase 2 閃卡 Phase 1 速查表 Learning Objectives 1. Analyse the essential elements of an agency relationship and the four ways an agency can be created (by written agreement, by estoppel, by ratification, by necessity). 2. Distinguish between actual authority (express and implied), usual authority and apparent authority, and apply them to third party scenarios. 3. Explain the fiduciary duties, rights and liabilities of an agent and the corresponding duties and rights of a principal. 4. Apply the disclosed principal and undisclosed principal rules to determine who may sue and be sued on the contract. 5. Advise on an agent's personal liability, including breach of warranty of authority, with statutory and case authority. 必背考點 A. Relevant Ordinances（考試要 pinpoint 到 Cap. + section） Ordinance Key provision Effect Partnership Ordinance (Cap. 38) s.7 Every partner is an agent of the firm and of his/her other partners for the purpose of the business of the partnership; one partner's acts bind all partners. Sale of Goods Ordinance (Cap. 26) ('SOGO') s.23 A sale by an agent without actual authority from the owner (principal) still gives the buyer (third party) good title if the sale is within the agent's apparent authority or usual authority . Powers of Attorney Ordinance (Cap. 31) — Principal = donor of the power; agent = donee. A Power of Attorney is conclusive evidence of the agency, subject to contrary evidence (e.g. revocation). Insurance Ordinance (Cap. 41) — Principal = insurance company; agent = insurance agent. Factors Ordinance (Cap. 48) — Principal = owner of goods; agent = mercantile agent. Prevention of Bribery Ordinance (Cap. 201) ('POBO') s.9 An offence for an employee (agent), without lawful authority or reasonable excuse, to solicit or accept an advantage/reward to do an act in relation to the principal's (employer's) affairs — e.g. secret money from a third party. Estate Agents Ordinance (Cap. 511) ('EAO') s.45 An estate agent must execute an estate agency agreement with the client before the agent can pursue a claim against the client for remuneration. Securities and Futures Ordinance (Cap. 571) — Principal = client; agent = licensed person. Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) ('CO') — Individual directors derive authority from: (1) the company as principal, (2) the articles, (3) the CO. An individual director (except CEO/MD) has no actual authority to act for the company without board authorisation (usually evidenced by board minutes). B. Leading cases（full citation 以 LP 所引為準） Case Principle Freeman & Lockyer v Buckhurst Park Property Ltd (1964) Agency by estoppel / ostensible (apparent) authority: the company held out director K as MD by paying past contracts he signed; the company was bound. Kelner v Baxter (1866) Ratification impossible where the principal did not exist at the time of the contract (pre incorporation); promoters personally liable. Gimex Development Ltd v Cua Wai Tai & Another (2000) Ratification by acquiescence: principal's failure to object to appointment of a sub agent amounted to ratification. Great Northern Railway v Swaffield (1874) Agency by necessity — three conditions: (1) agent entrusted with principal's property; (2) emergency and principal could not be contacted; (3) agent acted bona fide in the principal's interest. Ireland v Livingston (1872) Where a written order to an agent is ambiguous (two possible meanings) and the agent honestly acts on one, the principal cannot repudiate the act as unauthorised. Wong Wai Hing & Another v Hui Wei Lee (2001) Where the agent (debt collector) was expressly authorised and the agreement did not restrict the class of acts, the principal was liable for the agent's acts (even criminal acts in the course of the authorised task). Hely Hutchinson v Brayhead Ltd (1968) Implied actual authority: board's consent/acquiescence in a chairman acting as MD over a long period gave him implied actual authority to bind the company. Panorama Developments (Guildford) Ltd v Fidelis Furnishing Fabrics (1971) Apparent authority by holding out: a company secretary had apparent authority to hire cars on the company's credit; the company had to pay. Chaudhry v Prabhakar (1988) Agent's duty of care and skill: even an unpaid agent friend with car knowledge breached the duty by recommending a car he should have known was accident damaged. Boardman v Phipps (1966) Fiduciary may not earn secret profit or allow conflict between personal interest and fiduciary duty; liable to account for the profit. Cook v Deeks (1916) Directors must account to the company for secret profit; a self serving resolution ratifying their own act was ineffective. Regal Hastings Ltd v Gulliver (1942) (also cited in LP exam practice as Regal (Hastings) Ltd v Gulliver [1967] 2 AC 134) Directors/agents must not make unauthorised profit from their position; must account for the profit to the principal. Collen v Wright (1857) Breach of warranty of authority: agent who wrongly believed he had authority was liable in damages to the third party. Watteau v Fenwick (1893) Undisclosed principal: once the principal is established, ordinary agency rules apply; the principal is liable for the agent's acts even though the third party did not know of the agency. C. IRAC application points 1. Formation of agency（4 ways — Issue: "how was the agency created?"） By written agreement : express appointment (written or verbal), agent acts for remuneration/commission. By estoppel (holding out) : principal, by words or conduct, represents to a third party that the agent has authority; the third party relies on it in good faith and incurs loss. Key: the representation must come from the principal (or someone authorised by the principal), not from the agent himself . By ratification : agent acts without/exceeding authority; principal later approves with full knowledge. Four conditions: 1. The principal must exist at the time of the transaction and the agent must have been expressly contracted as an agent. 2. The principal must have been made aware of all material facts of the transaction. 3. The principal must ratify the whole transaction, not part of it. 4. The principal must ratify within a reasonable time . Effect: contract binding on principal and third party; agent's liability absolved. By necessity : urgent circumstances; authority presumed to protect the principal's property (three conditions in Great Northern Railway v Swaffield (1874)). 2. Types of authority（Issue: "was the principal bound?"） Express actual authority : expressly agreed acts; scope derived from the contract. Implied actual authority : implied from the relationship of the parties or from the agent's position (e.g. law firm charging disbursements; Hely Hutchinson v Brayhead Ltd (1968)). Usual authority : a type of implied actual authority that comes with the position the agent occupies in a trade/business/profession; may exceed actual authority to get the work done. Apparent (ostensible) authority — three requirements: 1. The principal (or someone authorised) represented to the third party that the agent had authority — by words, conduct, or previous dealings. 2. The third party relied on the representation. 3. The third party relied on it to his/her detriment. Note: apparent authority can survive the end of actual authority if the principal does not notify third parties (LP analysis of the ex MD ordering wine after leaving). 3. Duties of agent（fiduciary in nature） 1. Follow the principal's instructions (breach = breach of agency; damages, e.g. the price difference). 2. Exercise duty of care and skill ( Chaudhry v Prabhakar (1988)). 3. Avoid conflict of interest — even if the principal benefits from the transaction ( Boardman v Phipps (1966)). 4. Avoid secret profit — no benefit without the principal's consent ( Regal Hastings Ltd v Gulliver (1942)); possible POBO (Cap. 201) s.9 offence. 5. Account for transactions — account for all money received and keep proper records ( Cook v Deeks (1916)). 4. Rights of agent / Duties of principal（mirror image） Agent's rights: remuneration (only when the transaction is complete ; merely introducing a purchaser is not enough), indemnity for reasonable expenses/losses (not for unauthorised or negligent acts), and lien over the principal's goods/documents lawfully in the agent's possession until outstanding amounts are settled. Principal's duties: pay remuneration (agreed or customary), pay indemnity (except unauthorised actions or agent's default/negligence). 5. Liabilities of agent & termination consequences Personal liability: (1) acting for a non existing principal ( Kelner v Baxter (1866)); (2) acting in excess of authority (if not ratified → breach of warranty of authority); (3) acting for an undisclosed principal ; (4) committing a tortious act outside authority . Breach of warranty of authority ( Collen v Wright (1857)): agent represents he/she has authority but has none; third party relies and suffers loss; remedy = damages (actual loss). Agent's honest but mistaken belief is no defence. Principal's rights on breach: sue for breach of agency (agency terminated, damages per contract law) and recover any secret profit. Disclosed principal (named or unnamed): agent drops out; only principal and third party can sue/be sued (privity of contract). Undisclosed principal ( Watteau v Fenwick (1893)): agent may sue and be sued; the third party, on discovering the principal, may elect to sue the principal instead; the undisclosed principal may intervene and sue the third party directly, whereupon the agent loses his/her right of action. 易混淆概念對比 Table 1 — Ratification vs Agency by Estoppel / Apparent Authority（Jun 2024 考生大伏位：ratification 誤答為 estoppel） 分辨點 Ratification Agency by Estoppel / Apparent Authority Time of the key act Agent acts without authority first ; principal approves afterwards Principal's representation comes first (words/conduct/past dealings); agent then acts within that appearance of authority Who makes the representation? No prior representation needed — the principal simply adopts the act later The principal (not the agent) must have held the agent out to the third party Third party's reliance Not required; ratification works even if the third party knew the agent had no authority Third party must rely on the representation to his/her detriment Principal's existence Principal must exist at the time of the transaction ( Kelner v Baxter (1866)) Principal exists and makes the representation before the contract Leading case Kelner v Baxter (1866); Gimex Development Ltd v Cua Wai Tai (2000) Freeman & Lockyer v Buckhurst Park Property Ltd (1964); Panorama Developments (1971) 考試伏位（繁中） 見到「agent 越權 → principal 事後知情認可」就要答 ratification，唔好因為有「principal 嘅行為」就衝去答 estoppel 見到「principal 一早通知咗 supplier 呢個人係 MD/經理」先係 holding out；如果 representation 只係來自 agent 自己，estoppel 唔成立 Table 2 — Disclosed Principal vs Undisclosed Principal（Dec 2024 考生完全唔識 undisclosed principal） 分辨點 Disclosed Principal Undisclosed Principal Third party's knowledge Knows the agent acts for a principal (name disclosed or existence disclosed without name) No actual notice of the principal's existence; agent appears to be the principal Who can sue/be sued on the contract? Only principal and third party (privity of contract); agent drops out Agent may sue and be sued; third party may elect to sue the principal instead after discovering him/her Principal's right to intervene Not needed — principal is already a party Undisclosed principal may intervene and sue the third party; the agent then loses his/her right of action Authority analysis Actual/apparent authority in the normal way Ordinary agency rules still apply once the principal is established ( Watteau v Fenwick (1893)) 考試伏位（繁中） 「disclosed」唔一定要講出名——講咗「我係代人簽」但冇講名都係 disclosed 第三人發現 principal 之後係二揀一（agent 或 principal），唔係兩個都告埋；principal 介入後 agent 就冇得再告 third party Phase 2 閃卡 Card 1 Front: What are the four ways in which an agency relationship can be created? Back: By written agreement (express appointment, written or verbal) By estoppel (agency by holding out) By ratification (principal's subsequent approval of an unauthorised act) By necessity (urgent circumstances, no prior agreement needed) 💬 記口訣「W E R N」：Written、Estoppel、Ratification、Necessity。考試通常第一句就問 agency 點形成，呢四個係必背框架。 Card 2 Front: What are the four conditions for an effective ratification, and which case shows what happens if the principal did not exist? Back: The principal must exist at the time of the transaction and the agent must have been expressly contracted as an agent The principal must be aware of all material facts of the transaction The principal must ratify the whole transaction, not part of it The principal must ratify within a reasonable time Kelner v Baxter (1866): pre incorporation contract cannot be ratified; promoters personally liable 💬 四個條件：存在、知情、全盤、及時。公司未註冊就「代公司」簽約，ratify 唔到，promoters 自己孭。 Card 3 Front: When does agency by estoppel arise, and whose representation counts? Back: The principal holds out a person as agent to a third party, by words or conduct, as having authority to contract on the principal's behalf The representation must come from the principal (or someone authorised by the principal) — a representation made by the agent himself is not enough The third party must rely on it in good faith and incur a loss The principal is then prevented (estopped) from denying the agency Freeman & Lockyer v Buckhurst Park Property Ltd (1964) 💬 重點係「holding out 要由 principal 做」。Agent 自己話自己有權係冇用嘅——呢個係考試最常見嘅陷阱位。 Card 4 Front: What are the three conditions for agency by necessity under Great Northern Railway v Swaffield (1874)? Back: The agent must have been entrusted with the principal's property There was an emergency and the principal could not be contacted The agent acted bona fide in the interest of the principal 💬 三個條件：管有財產、緊急兼聯絡唔到、真誠為 principal 行事。例子：凍肉車壞雪櫃，司機自己買冰保住啲貨，可以向 principal 攞返啲使費。 Card 5 Front: What are the three requirements to establish apparent (ostensible) authority? Back: The principal (or someone authorised) represented to the third party that the agent had authority — by words, conduct, or previous dealings The third party relied on the representation The third party relied on it to his/her detriment Panorama Developments (Guildford) Ltd v Fidelis Furnishing Fabrics (1971): company secretary had apparent authority to hire cars 💬 Apparent authority 係「third party 眼中所見嘅權限」。Employee 離職後如果 principal 冇通知 third party，apparent authority 可能仍然存在，principal 照樣被綁住。 Card 6 Front: List the five duties an agent owes to the principal, with one supporting case for the fiduciary duties. Back: To follow the principal's instructions To exercise duty of care and skill ( Chaudhry v Prabhakar (1988)) To avoid conflict of interest ( Boardman v Phipps (1966)) To avoid secret profit ( Regal Hastings Ltd v Gulliver (1942)) To account for transactions ( Cook v Deeks (1916)) 💬 Fiduciary duties 係 strict obligation：就算 principal 喺交易中有著數，只要 agent 有利益衝突或者收咗 secret profit 都係 breach，利潤要全數交出。 Card 7 Front: What must a third party prove to sue an agent for breach of warranty of authority, and what is the remedy? Back: The agent represented/warranted to the third party that he/she had authority to act for the principal, but in fact had none The third party relied on that representation and incurred a loss Remedy: damages equal to the actual loss suffered Collen v Wright (1857): agent liable even though he honestly (but wrongly) believed he had authority 💬 唔使證明 agent 存心呃人——honest mistake 都照賠。所以呢個係 third party 告唔到 principal 嗰陣嘅後備武器。 Card 8 Front: In an undisclosed principal situation, who may sue and be sued on the contract? Back: The agent may sue and be sued on the contract (the third party thought he/she was dealing with the agent as principal) On discovering the principal, the third party may elect to sue the principal instead The undisclosed principal may intervene and sue the third party directly; the agent then loses his/her right of action Watteau v Fenwick (1893) 💬 Undisclosed = third party 完全唔知有 principal。佢發現之後可以「二揀一」；principal 都可以主動跳出嚟告 third party，一跳 agent 嘅告人權就冇咗。 本章急救詞彙 EN Term 繁中白話 English Model Sentence Principal 幕後嗰個，授權人哋幫佢做嘢嘅人 The principal is bound by contracts made by the agent within actual or apparent authority. Agent / Fiduciary duty 受託代 principal 行事嘅人；fiduciary duty 即係要百分百忠誠、唔可以為自己袋錢 An agent owes fiduciary duties to the principal and must account for any secret profit. Ratification 事後追認：agent 越權咗，principal 知情後照單全收 By ratifying the purchase, the principal adopted the agent's unauthorised act and was bound by the contract. Apparent (ostensible) authority 表面權限：third party 合理相信 agent 有權，因為 principal 做過啲嘢令佢咁諗 The company held the manager out as having authority, so he contracted with apparent authority. Agency by estoppel / holding out 禁反言代理：principal 令人以為某人有代理權，之後唔准反口 Agency by estoppel arises where the principal's own representation, not the agent's, induces the third party's reliance. Breach of warranty of authority 權限保證違反：agent 話自己有權其實冇，third party 有損失就可以告佢 The third party recovered damages from the agent for breach of warranty of authority. Lien 留置權：principal 冇找數，agent 可以扣住佢啲貨或文件 The unpaid auctioneer exercised a lien over the cheque until his remuneration was settled. Undisclosed principal 隱名本人：third party 根本唔知有 principal 存在 Where the principal is undisclosed, the agent may sue and be sued on the contract.

title: M10 Chapter 5: Aspects of Agency Law — Phase 3 Answers
headings: M10 Chapter 5: Aspects of Agency Law — Phase 3 Answers
Q2 — Answer: Estate Agents Ordinance (Cap. 511), s.45
excerpt: M10 Chapter 5: Aspects of Agency Law — Phase 3 Answers Q1 — Answer: D Model Answer (EN): An agency relationship can be created in four ways: (1) by written agre…
text: M10 Chapter 5: Aspects of Agency Law — Phase 3 Answers Q1 — Answer: D Model Answer (EN): An agency relationship can be created in four ways: (1) by written agreement (express appointment, in writing or verbally); (2) by estoppel (agency by holding out); (3) by ratification (the principal's subsequent approval of an act done without authority); and (4) by necessity (urgent circumstances requiring protection of the principal's property). Voluntary performance of services without an emergency creates no agency; the person is a mere volunteer. 解題思路（繁中）: 呢題係純框架 recall。四個形成方式：written agreement、estoppel、ratification、necessity。Option D「by performance」係捏造出嚟嘅——冇緊急情況、冇協議，自願幫人做嘢唔會創造 agency（如果係緊急兼聯絡唔到 principal，先有可能係 agency by necessity，但 D 明確寫 "without any emergency"）。A、B、C 都係正宗形成方式。考試伏位：唔好將「agency by necessity」同一般好心幫忙混淆——necessity 有三大嚴格條件。 Rule Check: LP Ch.5 s.5.1 (Formation of Agency); Great Northern Railway v Swaffield (1874) for the necessity conditions. Common Trap（繁中）: 以為「默示同意/事後多謝」都係一種形成方式。記住：無協議、無緊急、無追認，就無 agency。 Q2 — Answer: Estate Agents Ordinance (Cap. 511), s.45 Model Answer (EN): Section 45 of the Estate Agents Ordinance (Cap. 511) requires an estate agent to execute an estate agency agreement with the client in order to pursue a claim against the client for remuneration. Because Mr Cheung never signed an estate agency agreement with Mrs Lau, he cannot claim commission from her, even though he successfully procured a purchaser who completed the sale. 解題思路（繁中）: 地產代理追佣金的 statutory precondition：必須先同 client 簽 estate agency agreement。口頭協議唔算數。Exam Lens 強調考試要求 pinpoint section——答「Estate Agents Ordinance」而冇 Cap. 511 同 s.45 會被扣分。順帶記住：就算簽咗協議，agent 一般要「完成交易」先有佣金（merely introducing a purchaser is not enough），但呢題嘅致命位係冇書面協議。 Rule Check: Estate Agents Ordinance (Cap. 511) s.45. Common Trap（繁中）: 誤以為「成功搵到買家完成交易」就一定有佣金；或者引用錯 Ordinance（例如 Powers of Attorney Ordinance (Cap. 31)——嗰個係管 donor/donee，唔關事）。 Q3 — Answer: B Model Answer (EN): Issue: whether THT is bound by Kelvin's unauthorised purchase of teapots. Rule: where an agent acts without or in excess of authority, the principal may ratify the act, provided (1) the principal existed at the time of the transaction, (2) the principal was made aware of all material facts, (3) the principal ratifies the whole transaction, and (4) ratification occurs within a reasonable time. Application: THT existed when Kelvin signed; the managing director was told the full details of the contract; THT adopted the whole transaction by selling half the teapots at a profit, promptly upon delivery. All four conditions are satisfied. Conclusion: THT has ratified the contract and is bound to pay PorcelainCo; Kelvin's liability is absolved. 解題思路（繁中）: 呢題係 Exam Lens 點名嘅經典伏位（Jun 2024 考生將 ratification 誤答 estoppel）。分辨關鍵：時間次序同 representation 來源。 A 錯 ：estoppel/holding out 需要 principal 喺簽約前向「呢個 third party」作 representation。THT 同 PorcelainCo 從未交易過，THT 冇向 PorcelainCo hold out 過 Kelvin 有買茶壺嘅權；Kelvin「purchasing supervisor」嘅頭銜唔係 THT 向 PorcelainCo 做嘅 representation。 C 錯 ：如果 THT 冇認可，C 先啱（breach of warranty of authority, Collen v Wright (1857)）。但事實係 MD 知情後賣咗一半貨——用行為 adopt 咗成單交易，呢個就係 ratification。 D 錯 ：agency by necessity 需要 (1) 受託管有 principal 財產、(2) 緊急兼聯絡唔到 principal、(3) 真誠行事（ Great Northern Railway v Swaffield (1874)）。買茶壺根本無緊急，Kelvin 可以請示。 B 啱 ：四個 ratification 條件全部滿足——principal 存在、知悉全部重要事實、全盤（唔係部分）接納、合理時間內追認。 Rule Check: LP Ch.5 s.5.1.4 (ratification conditions); Gimex Development Ltd v Cua Wai Tai & Another (2000) (adoption/acquiescence); Collen v Wright (1857); Great Northern Railway v Swaffield (1874). Common Trap（繁中）: 見到「principal 有啲行為（賣貨）」就衝去答 estoppel。Estoppel 嘅 representation 一定係「簽約之前、由 principal 向 third party 作出」；事後認可係 ratification，唔係 estoppel。 Q4 — Answer: C Model Answer (EN): Issue: whether BathLux is bound by the tile purchase made by its former manager. Rule: an agent acting within apparent authority binds the principal. Apparent authority requires (1) a representation by the principal, by words, conduct or previous dealings, that the agent has authority; (2) reliance by the third party; (3) reliance to the third party's detriment. Termination of actual authority does not end apparent authority unless third parties are notified. Application: BathLux's conduct over five years of settled dealings represented to TileMart that Gloria had authority to order on BathLux's account; TileMart relied on that representation and parted with HK$80,000 of tiles to its detriment; BathLux never notified TileMart of Gloria's resignation. Conclusion: BathLux is bound to pay; its remedy is against Gloria personally. 解題思路（繁中）: A 錯 ：actual authority 完咗唔等於 apparent authority 完咗。Principal 有責任通知有來往嘅 third parties；唔通知，表面權限繼續存在。 B 錯 ：ratification 係用嚟處理「無權代理人事後被追認」；呢度 Gloria 喺 TileMart 眼中本來就有 apparent authority，合約一簽已綁住 BathLux，唔需要 ratify，BathLux 亦冇得「選擇唔認」。 C 啱 ：三大要求齊晒——representation by past dealings（五年嚟 BathLux 找晒數）、reliance、detriment（交咗貨）。呢個正正係 LP 內 Stan/紅酒例子同 Freeman & Lockyer 嘅應用。 D 錯 ：breach of warranty of authority 係 third party 告唔到 principal 時嘅後備（ Collen v Wright (1857)）；呢度 TileMart 可以直接告 BathLux。話「former agent 永遠綁唔到 principal」係絕對錯。 Rule Check: LP Ch.5 s.5.2.3 (three requirements for apparent authority) and s.5.3.1 Apply and Analyse 1 (ex MD ordering wine); Freeman & Lockyer v Buckhurst Park Property Ltd (1964); Panorama Developments (Guildford) Ltd v Fidelis Furnishing Fabrics (1971). Common Trap（繁中）: 以為「離職 = 權限即時歸零」。考試鍾意考「principal 冇通知 third party」呢個位——沉默嘅 principal 要孭返個 apparent authority。 Q5 — Answer: B Model Answer (EN): Issue: whether PBC is bound by a pre incorporation contract signed by Alice. Rule: one condition of effective ratification is that the principal must exist at the time of the transaction and the agent must have been expressly contracted as an agent. A company that did not exist when the contract was made cannot ratify it; the person who signed is personally liable ( Kelner v Baxter (1866)). Application: PBC did not exist when Alice signed the supply contract with Andes. PBC is therefore incapable of ratifying the contract, and it never adopted it (the board refused delivery and payment). Conclusion: Andes' claim against PBC fails; Andes should pursue Alice personally on the contract. 解題思路（繁中）: A 錯 ：「註冊成立 + 做返預期生意」唔等於 ratification。Ratification 第一個條件（principal 喺交易時已存在）永遠滿足唔到，之後做咩都補救唔到（除非另立新合約/novation，但事實冇）。 B 啱 ： Kelner v Baxter (1866) 直接對辦——公司未註冊，唔存在嘅 principal 冇能力 ratify，promoter/agent 自己孭個人責任。 C 錯 ：agency by necessity 要緊急情況、聯絡唔到 principal、真誠保護 principal 財產。簽兩年供豆合約係普通商業決定，無緊急可言；而且當時根本無 principal 嘅財產可保護。 D 錯 ：apparent authority 嘅 representation 必須來自 principal（或獲授權人士）。PBC 當時唔存在，冇可能 hold out Alice；representation 只係 Alice 自己作出，estoppel/apparent authority 唔成立。 Rule Check: Kelner v Baxter (1866); LP Ch.5 s.5.1.4 (ratification condition 1) and s.5.5.1 (personal liability — acting for a non existing principal). Common Trap（繁中）: 以為「公司成立後追認就得」或者「promoter 天然有 apparent authority」。記住 Kelner v Baxter 係 ratification 四條件嘅考試切入點：principal 唔存在 = 永遠 ratify 唔到 = promoter 個人孭鑊。

title: M10 Chapter 5: Aspects of Agency Law — Phase 3 Quiz
headings: M10 Chapter 5: Aspects of Agency Law — Phase 3 Quiz
excerpt: M10 Chapter 5: Aspects of Agency Law — Phase 3 Quiz Rules: Closed book · 15 minutes · 5 questions · Submit as 1. … 2. … 3. … 4. … 5. … — 超時如實申報 Question 1 (MCQ)…
text: M10 Chapter 5: Aspects of Agency Law — Phase 3 Quiz Rules: Closed book · 15 minutes · 5 questions · Submit as 1. … 2. … 3. … 4. … 5. … — 超時如實申報 Question 1 (MCQ) Under common law in Hong Kong, which of the following is NOT a recognised way in which an agency relationship can be created? A. By written agreement between the principal and the agent B. By estoppel, where the principal holds out a person as his agent to a third party C. By ratification, where the principal approves an act done by the agent without authority D. By performance, where a person voluntarily performs services for another without any emergency Question 2 (Short answer) Mr Cheung is a licensed estate agent in Hong Kong. He orally agreed with Mrs Lau to find a buyer for her flat and successfully procured a purchaser who completed the sale. Mrs Lau now refuses to pay Mr Cheung any commission. Identify the Ordinance (with Cap. number) and the exact section that prevents Mr Cheung from pursuing a claim for remuneration against Mrs Lau, and state in one sentence what that provision requires. Question 3 (MCQ — scenario) In relation to agency law: Kelvin is the purchasing supervisor of TeaHarvest Trading Limited ("THT"), a tea importer. His written authority is limited to purchasing tea leaves. At a trade fair, Kelvin signed a contract with PorcelainCo to buy 200 boxes of ceramic teapots for THT at a very favourable price, without seeking any approval. PorcelainCo knew Kelvin was THT's purchasing supervisor but had never dealt with THT before. When the teapots arrived, THT's managing director examined the goods, was told the full details of the contract, decided the teapots were a bargain, and sold half of them to a retailer at a profit. PorcelainCo has not been paid. Which of the following is the best analysis of THT's liability to PorcelainCo? A. THT is bound by agency by estoppel, because it held Kelvin out as its purchasing supervisor to the trading community B. THT is bound by the contract because it ratified Kelvin's unauthorised act with full knowledge of all material facts, and Kelvin's personal liability is absolved C. THT is not bound, because Kelvin had neither actual nor apparent authority to buy teapots, so PorcelainCo's only remedy is against Kelvin for breach of warranty of authority D. THT is bound by agency by necessity, because Kelvin acted in THT's commercial interest Question 4 (MCQ — scenario) In relation to agency law: Gloria was the showroom manager of BathLux Sanitaryware Limited ("BathLux") for five years. She regularly ordered tiles and fittings on BathLux's account from TileMart Supplies Limited ("TileMart"), and BathLux always settled the invoices. Gloria resigned on 1 March after a dispute with the board. BathLux did not inform TileMart or any other supplier of her departure. On 10 March, Gloria visited TileMart, ordered HK$80,000 of designer tiles on BathLux's account, collected them in a rented van, and disappeared. TileMart now demands payment from BathLux. Which of the following is the best analysis? A. BathLux is not bound, because Gloria's actual authority ended on 1 March when her employment terminated B. BathLux is bound only if it chooses to ratify the purchase, and it may freely refuse to ratify C. BathLux is bound, because Gloria had apparent authority: BathLux's conduct in past dealings represented to TileMart that she had authority, and TileMart relied on that representation to its detriment D. TileMart's only remedy is to sue Gloria for breach of warranty of authority, because an agent whose authority has ended can never bind the former principal Question 5 (MCQ — scenario) In relation to agency law: Alice, Ben and Carmen decided to set up a coffee roasting business. Two weeks before Peak Brew Coffee Limited ("PBC") was incorporated, Alice signed a two year coffee bean supply contract with Andes Beans Limited ("Andes"), signing "for and on behalf of Peak Brew Coffee Limited (a company to be incorporated)". PBC was duly incorporated a fortnight later. When Andes delivered the first shipment of beans, the newly appointed board of PBC refused to accept delivery or pay, arguing that PBC had never authorised the contract and had never adopted it after incorporation. Andes has sued PBC for breach of contract. Which of the following is the best analysis? A. PBC is bound, because it ratified the contract simply by being incorporated and carrying on the coffee roasting business contemplated by the contract B. PBC is not bound: a principal that did not exist at the time of the transaction cannot ratify it, so the contract cannot be enforced against PBC; Andes should pursue Alice personally C. PBC is bound by agency by necessity, because Alice had to secure the bean supply urgently before incorporation D. PBC is bound because Alice had apparent authority as a promoter, and Andes relied on her representation to its detriment

title: M10 Chapter 6: Money Laundering, Bribery and Corruption — Phase 1 速查表 + Phase 2 閃卡
headings: M10 Chapter 6: Money Laundering, Bribery and Corruption — Phase 1 速查表 + Phase 2 閃卡
A. Anti-Money Laundering 四大法例（Offences / Obligations / Penalties / Court Action）
E. IRAC Application Points（考試答題框架）
excerpt: M10 Chapter 6: Money Laundering, Bribery and Corruption — Phase 1 速查表 + Phase 2 閃卡 Phase 1 速查表 Learning Objectives 1. Apply the key provisions of Hong Kong's an…
text: M10 Chapter 6: Money Laundering, Bribery and Corruption — Phase 1 速查表 + Phase 2 閃卡 Phase 1 速查表 Learning Objectives 1. Apply the key provisions of Hong Kong's anti money laundering legislation (DTROPO, OSCO, AMLO, UNATMO) to factual scenarios, including the offences, disclosure obligations and penalties. 2. Explain the obligations of accountants and other designated non financial businesses and professions (DNFBPs) under the AMLO and the HKICPA AML Guidelines — customer due diligence, ongoing monitoring, suspicious transaction reporting and record keeping. 3. Analyse the role of accountants as trust or company service providers (TCSPs) under the TCSP licensing regime. 4. Apply the offences under the Prevention of Bribery Ordinance (Cap. 201) to private sector and public sector scenarios, using the IRAC approach. 5. Describe the roles and powers of the Joint Financial Intelligence Unit (JFIU) and the Independent Commission Against Corruption (ICAC). 必背考點 A. Anti Money Laundering 四大法例（Offences / Obligations / Penalties / Court Action） 1. Drug Trafficking (Recovery of Proceeds) Ordinance (Cap. 405) ('DTROPO') s.25(1) — offence: a person deals with property , knowing or having reasonable grounds to believe that the whole or part of the property directly or indirectly represents proceeds of drug trafficking . s.25(3) — penalty on conviction upon indictment under s.25(1): max 14 years' imprisonment + fine of HK$5 million . s.25A(1) — obligation: a person must disclose to an authorised officer (e.g. police officer, Customs and Excise officer) as soon as it is reasonable if he/she knows or suspects that property represents proceeds of drug trafficking. s.25A(5) — tipping off offence: knowing or suspecting that a disclosure has been made, disclosing to any other person any matter likely to prejudice any investigation . s.25A(8) — penalty for failure to disclose under s.25A(1) (and per Exhibit 6.1, tipping off): max 3 years' imprisonment + fine of HK$500,000 . s.3 — court power to issue confiscation orders (court must specify a period of less than six months for the defendant to pay). ss.10 and 11 — Court of First Instance may grant a restraint order (prohibiting dealing with realisable property) or a charging order (charge on realisable property to secure payment to the Government). Knowingly contravening either order: fine of HK$500,000 (or the property value if greater) + 5 years' imprisonment (ss.10(16) and 11(14)). 2. Organized and Serious Crimes Ordinance (Cap. 455) ('OSCO') Enacted 1994; mirrors DTROPO but covers proceeds of an indictable offence (defined in the Crimes Ordinance (Cap. 200) as one not triable summarily; for DTROPO/OSCO purposes, one that may be tried either summarily or on indictment). s.25(1) — same dealing offence as DTROPO, but for proceeds of any person's indictable offence . s.25(3) — same penalty: max 14 years' imprisonment + HK$5 million fine . s.25A(1) — same disclosure obligation; s.25A(5) tipping off; s.25A(8) penalty max 3 years + HK$500,000 . s.8 — confiscation orders; s.14 — restraint order / charging order by the Court of First Instance. 考試伏位：DTROPO 只限 drug trafficking proceeds；OSCO 涵蓋所有 indictable offence proceeds（包括 fraud、theft、tax evasion 等）。毒品案先諗 DTROPO，其他罪行諗 OSCO。 3. Anti Money Laundering and Counter Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Cap. 615) ('AMLO') — in force 1 April 2012 s.5 — criminal offence if a financial institution (FI) knowingly, or with intent to defraud a relevant authority (RA: HKMA / SFC / Insurance Authority), contravenes a specified provision (listed in s.5(11)). s.5(5) — knowing contravention: max 2 years' imprisonment + HK$1,000,000 fine . s.5(6) — contravention with intent to defraud RAs: max 7 years' imprisonment + HK$1,000,000 fine . s.5A (added by the 2018 Amendment Ordinance, effective 1 March 2018) — imposes AML/CTF requirements on DNFBPs : accounting professionals and legal professionals (when preparing/carrying out specified transactions: buying/selling real estate; managing client money, securities or assets; managing bank/savings/securities accounts; organising contributions for creation/operation/management of corporations; creation/operation/management of legal persons or arrangements; buying/selling business entities; trust or company services), estate agents (real estate transactions), and TCSP licensees . Schedule 2 — Part 2: customer due diligence (CDD) ; Part 3: record keeping ; FIs/DNFBPs must take all reasonable measures to ensure proper safeguards against contravention and to mitigate ML/TF risks. s.21 / s.21(2) — RAs may take disciplinary action against FIs: public reprimand, remedial action, pecuniary penalty. s.23 — RAs must follow guidelines when imposing pecuniary penalties. Supervisory fines can reach HK$10 million or 3 times the profit gained / costs avoided . DNFBPs (accountants, lawyers, estate agents) face no criminal sanctions under AMLO for non compliance — they are penalised via their own professional mechanisms; TCSPs via the licensing system. TCSP licensing regime (from 1 March 2018) s.1, Part 1, Schedule 1 — statutory definition of a TCS business: forming corporations/legal persons; acting/arranging a director, secretary, partner or similar; providing registered office/business address; acting/arranging trustee of an express trust or nominee shareholder (other than for a listed corporation). s.53B — licensing requirement does not apply to: qualified accounting professionals, qualified legal professionals, the HKSAR Government, authorized institutions (s.2(1) Banking Ordinance (Cap. 155)), licensed corporations (SFO (Cap. 571)) where TCS business is ancillary to principal business, and persons prescribed by regulation. s.53F(1)–(2) — offence to carry on a TCS business without a licence : fine of HK$100,000 + 6 months' imprisonment . s.53H / s.53I — fit and proper test : Registrar of Companies considers e.g. ML/TF convictions (in or outside HK), undischarged bankruptcy, failure to comply with AMLO requirements, liquidation/winding up of a corporate applicant. s.53O — licence valid for 3 years (or shorter as determined); Registrar may grant, renew, suspend, revoke, or impose conditions. Registrar may publicly reprimand defaulting TCSPs, order remedial action and impose a pecuniary penalty up to HK$500,000 . 重點：qualified accountants 免攞牌，但唔免合規 — still must comply with CDD, ongoing monitoring and record keeping under Schedule 2 of the AMLO. 4. United Nations (Anti Terrorism Measures) Ordinance (Cap. 575) ('UNATMO') s.7 — offence: provides or collects property with the intention, or knowing, or having reasonable grounds to believe that the property is to be used to commit terrorist acts . s.8 — offence: offers property or financial services to benefit a terrorist or terrorist associate . s.8A — must not, except under licence from the Secretary for Security , deal with property knowing / being reckless as to whether it is terrorist property, owned/controlled by a terrorist or terrorist associate, or held on their behalf/direction. s.12(1) — offence to fail to report knowledge or suspicion that property is terrorist property to an authorised officer as soon as practicable → penalty s.14(5): max 3 months' imprisonment + a fine . s.12(5) — tipping off offence → penalty s.14(6): max 3 years' imprisonment + a fine . s.6 — Secretary for Security may freeze funds by written notice where there are reasonable grounds to suspect they are terrorist property. s.13 — on application by the Secretary for Justice , the Court of First Instance may order forfeiture of terrorist property. ss.14(1) and 14(1A) — max penalty for ss.7, 8, 8A offences: 14 years' imprisonment + a fine . B. Leading Cases（full citations + ratio） 1. Seng Yuet Fong v HKSAR (1999) KCQ3, FAMC No. 26 of 1998 (CFA) — 'having reasonable grounds for belief' in s.25(1) DTROPO contains both an objective and a subjective element : (i) grounds that a common sense, right thinking member of the community would consider sufficient to lead a person to believe (objective); (ii) the defendant knew those grounds (subjective). Prosecution must prove both. 2. Oei Hengky Wiryo v HKSAR (No. 2) (2007) 10 HKCFAR 98 (CFA) — under s.25(1) OSCO , the prosecution need NOT prove that the property dealt with was in fact the proceeds of a predicate offence; conviction is possible if the defendant had reasonable grounds to believe it represented proceeds of crime. 3. HKSAR v Pang Hung Fai (FACC 8 of 2013) (CFA) — (i) the defendant's own perception, belief or prejudice (e.g. long standing trust in a friend) may be taken into account when assessing 'reasonable grounds to believe'; (ii) the correct test is the 'would believe' test (would a reasonable person looking at the grounds believe the property represented proceeds of an indictable offence?) — the Court of Appeal's 'could believe' test was an inappropriately low standard. 4. HKSAR v Yang Sigai (2016) HKEC 2068, FACV No. 8 of 2015 (CFA) — where the property came from overseas , the underlying offence need not be identified , and s.25(1) OSCO does not require proof of knowledge of the actual conduct that produced the property. 5. HKSAR v Yeung Ka Sing Carson (FACC Nos. 5 and 6 of 2015) (CFA) — upheld Oei Hengky Wiryo (no need to prove the predicate offence) and confirmed the Seng Yuet Fong formulation: the accused had grounds for believing, and the grounds must be reasonable such that anyone looking at them objectively would so believe. 6. HKSAR v Leung Yat Ming & Another (1999) 2 HKLRD 402 — court lifted the corporate veil (company as a cloak of deception) and convicted the defendants under s.9(3) POBO for deceiving their employer (university) by an application containing false statements. C. Prevention of Bribery Ordinance (Cap. 201) ('POBO') Definitions — s.2 Advantage : gift, loan, fee, reward or commission (money, security, property or interest); office, employment or contract; payment/release of a loan; service or favour; promise of any of these; exercise of or forbearance from rights/powers/duties. Entertainment (= food or drink, e.g. dinners, or entertainment provided with food and drink) is NOT an advantage. Agent : a public servant and any person employed by or acting for another (directors are agents of the company; the Board is generally the principal). Public servant : prescribed officers + employees of public bodies (e.g. MTR, hospitals). Offences Section Sector Offence s.3 Public Prescribed officer soliciting/accepting advantage without the Chief Executive's permission s.4 Public Public servant soliciting/accepting advantage as inducement/reward for performing duties (offeror also guilty) s.5 Public Advantage for assistance/influence in relation to a contract (offeror also guilty) s.6 / s.7 Private Advantage to withdraw/refrain from a tender / from bidding at an auction of a public body s.8 Private Advantage offered to a public servant of a department the agent is dealing with s.9(1) Private Agent, without lawful authority or reasonable excuse , solicits/accepts advantage as inducement to/reward for an act in relation to the principal's affairs s.9(2) Private Offering an advantage to an agent (the mirror offence — the offeror's side) s.9(3) Private Agent uses any receipt, account or other document with a false or erroneous statement to deceive the principal s.9(5) Private Leeway: permission applied for and given as soon as reasonably possible after the offer/acceptance s.10 Public Prescribed officer maintaining a standard of living / assets not commensurate with official emoluments Other key sections s.11 — both giver and acceptor guilty even if the purpose of the bribe is not carried out ; unavailable defences: no power/opportunity to do the act; no intention to do the act; did not in fact do the act. s.12 — penalties: ss.5 or 6 → max 10 years + HK$500,000 ; s.10 → max 10 years + HK$1,000,000 ; other sections → max 7 years + HK$500,000 . s.19 — no defence that the advantage is customary in any profession, trade, vocation or calling. s.24 — burden of proving lawful authority or reasonable excuse lies on the accused . D. JFIU and ICAC Joint Financial Intelligence Unit (JFIU) — set up 1989 ; joint operation of the HK Police Force and Customs & Excise Department. It is the central hub for suspicious transaction reports (STRs) but has no investigative power ; it refers reports to local/overseas enforcement departments. Reports arise under s.25A DTROPO, s.25A OSCO and s.12 UNATMO . 'SAFE' approach : S creen the customer/transaction; A sk questions to clarify; F ind out whether the transaction matches expectations; E valuate whether it is really suspicious. HKICPA Guidelines on AML/CTF for Professional Accountants (February 2018) — based on guidelines published under s.7 AMLO ; form part of the Code of Ethics for Professional Accountants . Breach = not liable to legal proceedings, but admissible as evidence in court proceedings under AMLO. ' must ' = mandatory/statutory; 'should/would/may' = guidance/good practice. Section 620 CDD — know the true identity of each client, business type, source/use of funds; standard CDD for all; SDD for lower risk, EDD for higher risk (e.g. PEPs — individuals with prominent public functions outside mainland China, their family members and close associates). Section 630 Ongoing Monitoring — review client documents regularly; watch transactions inconsistent with business/risk profile/source of funds; examine abnormally large or unusual transactions and record findings in writing. Section 640 STRs — must appoint a Money Laundering Reporting Officer (MLRO) ; report to the JFIU without delay ; report as soon as reasonably practicable ; internal controls to prevent tipping off ; suspicion is more than speculation but less than proof or knowledge . Section 650 — targeted financial sanctions: name checks against UN Security Council sanctions lists; STR to JFIU if terrorist related suspicion. Section 660 Record Keeping — identify/verify beneficial owner; clear and complete audit trail; records available to RAs on a timely basis; retain records at least 5 years after the transaction or cessation of the business relationship. ICAC — established February 1974 by Governor Sir Murray MacLehose; functions independently and is directly accountable to the Chief Executive (Basic Law). Three pronged strategy via three departments: Operations (law enforcement — investigates offences under the ICACO (Cap. 204), POBO and ECICO (Cap. 554)), Corruption Prevention (reviews practices/procedures), Community Relations (education and public support). Investigative powers under POBO : s.13 inspect accounts/documents, require production (s.13(3): obstruction → HK$20,000 + 1 year); s.13A CFI order for IRD material; s.14(1) require suspects to provide property/income/expenditure details; s.14C restraining order on property; s.17(1A) enter and search premises; s.17A surrender of travel documents. Under ICACO (Cap. 204) : s.10 arrest without warrant; s.10A procedure after arrest; s.10AA arrest of persons granted bail (bring before a magistrate within 24 hours ); s.12 duties of the Commissioner; s.13 powers of the Commissioner. E. IRAC Application Points（考試答題框架） Issue : 先認清係 laundering（OSCO/DTROPO）定 terrorist property（UNATMO）定 bribery（POBO）——Exam Lens 指出 Jun 2026 有考生將 anti corruption 誤判為 money laundering，issue spotting 係成敗關鍵。 Rule : pinpoint section — 答 s.25(1) OSCO 要分 DTROPO（drug trafficking）定 OSCO（indictable offence）；答 PBO 要分 s.9(1)（agent 收受）、s.9(2)（offeror）、s.9(3)（假文件）。 Application : 將 facts 逐項套入 elements（dealing? knowledge/reasonable grounds? advantage? principal's affairs? permission?）；記住 suspicion 已足夠觸發 disclosure duty ，唔使證實罪行（Oei Hengky Wiryo; HKICPA Guidelines s.640）。 Conclusion : 明確落結論 + 指出 penalty（如 s.25(3)：14 年 + HK$5M；s.25A(8)：3 年 + HK$500,000）。 易混淆概念對比 Table 1 — AML offences: Dealing vs Failure to Disclose vs Tipping off Dealing offence (s.25(1) DTROPO / s.25(1) OSCO / ss.7–8A UNATMO) Failure to disclose (s.25A(1) DTROPO/OSCO / s.12(1) UNATMO) Tipping off (s.25A(5) DTROPO/OSCO / s.12(5) UNATMO) Trigger Actually deals with the tainted property Knows or suspects property is tainted, but stays silent A disclosure/STR has been made , then leaks information Mens rea Knowing, or reasonable grounds to believe (Seng Yuet Fong two element test) Knowledge or suspicion (less than proof, more than speculation) Knowing or suspecting that a disclosure has been made + disclosure likely to prejudice investigation Max penalty 14 years + HK$5M (s.25(3)); UNATMO ss.7/8/8A: 14 years + fine (ss.14(1)/(1A)) 3 years + HK$500,000 (s.25A(8)); UNATMO: 3 months + fine (s.14(5)) 3 years + HK$500,000 (s.25A(8)); UNATMO: 3 years + fine (s.14(6)) 點樣分辨／考試伏位 被告自己有份「處理」黑錢 被告只係「知情不報」，無處理黑錢都可以中 前提係 已經有人報咗 STR——若無人報告，tipping off 唔成立（只可能中 failure to disclose）。警告客戶「有人查緊你」先係 tipping off Table 2 — POBO: s.9(1) vs s.9(2) vs s.9(3); Advantage vs Entertainment s.9(1) s.9(2) s.9(3) Who commits Agent soliciting/accepting advantage Offeror giving advantage to an agent Agent using false/erroneous receipt, account or document Gist Advantage as inducement/reward for act in relation to principal's affairs Mirror image of s.9(1) — the giver's side Intent to deceive the principal — no advantage need change hands Key authority / notes Advantage 包括 loan（s.2）；permission 要由 Board 全體批（s.9(5) 只係事後補救） 雙方都罪成，即使目的未達成（s.11） Leung Yat Ming：揭穿公司面紗後用虛假申請呃僱主 = s.9(3) Advantage vs Entertainment Advantage (s.2): gifts, loans, fees, rewards, commissions, contracts, services, favours, promises Entertainment (s.2): food or drink (e.g. dinners) and entertainment provided with it 考試伏位：請食飯 唔係 advantage ，所以單純接受晚宴唔觸犯 s.9；但 cash rebate、gift、loan 就係 點樣分辨 有冇「利益」轉移 + 有冇 principal permission 邊個係主動一方（收 vs 送） 有冇 假文件 去呃僱主——Jun 2024 考生將 s.9(3) 同 s.9(1) 答案重複，被扣分 Phase 2 閃卡 Card 1 Front: What are the four principal pieces of anti money laundering legislation in Hong Kong, and what does each primarily target? Back: Drug Trafficking (Recovery of Proceeds) Ordinance (Cap. 405) — proceeds of drug trafficking Organized and Serious Crimes Ordinance (Cap. 455) — proceeds of any indictable offence Anti Money Laundering and Counter Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Cap. 615) — regulatory regime: CDD/record keeping for FIs and DNFBPs; TCSP licensing United Nations (Anti Terrorism Measures) Ordinance (Cap. 575) — terrorist property and terrorist financing 💬 記法：「毒品 405、重罪 455、監管 615、反恐 575」。首兩條係刑事化洗黑錢，615 係合規框架，575 專門對付恐怖分子資金。 Card 2 Front: Under Seng Yuet Fong v HKSAR (1999) KCQ3, what two elements must the prosecution prove for 'having reasonable grounds for belief' in s.25(1) DTROPO? Back: Objective element : grounds that a common sense, right thinking member of the community would consider sufficient to lead a person to believe the property represents proceeds of crime; AND Subjective element : the defendant knew those grounds. Both elements must be proved. 💬 「有合理理由相信」= 客觀上一般人睇到呢啲跡象都會信（objective）+ 被告本人真係知悉呢啲跡象（subjective）。兩樣齊先定罪。 Card 3 Front: What did the CFA decide in Oei Hengky Wiryo v HKSAR (No. 2) (2007) 10 HKCFAR 98 about proving the 'predicate offence' under s.25(1) OSCO? Back: The prosecution does NOT have to prove the property dealt with was in fact the proceeds of a predicate offence. It is enough that the defendant had reasonable grounds to believe the property represented the proceeds of crime. Upheld in HKSAR v Yeung Ka Sing Carson (FACC Nos. 5 and 6 of 2015). 💬 即係話：就算啲錢最後查唔到／證唔到係黑錢，只要被告「有合理理由相信」係黑錢而照樣處理，都已經罪成。呢點係 AML 部分最常考嘅案例原則。 Card 4 Front: In HKSAR v Pang Hung Fai (FACC 8 of 2013), which test did the CFA endorse for assessing 'reasonable grounds to believe' — the 'would believe' test or the 'could believe' test — and what else may the court consider? Back: The 'would believe' test : would a reasonable person, looking at the grounds, believe that the property represented the proceeds of an indictable offence. The Court of Appeal's 'could believe' test was an inappropriately low standard. The defendant's own perception and evaluation of the facts (e.g. 30 years of friendship and trust in Kwok) may be taken into account. 💬 「Would believe」要求高過「could believe」：唔係「可能會信」就夠，而係一個合理嘅人「真係會咁信」。被告個人嘅信任背景都可以考慮。 Card 5 Front: Which bodies are DNFBPs under s.5A of the AMLO, and what must they do under Schedule 2? Back: DNFBPs: accounting professionals and legal professionals (when handling specified transactions, e.g. real estate, managing client money, trust or company services), estate agents , and TCSP licensees . Schedule 2, Part 2 : customer due diligence (CDD) requirements. Schedule 2, Part 3 : record keeping requirements. Must take all reasonable measures to ensure proper safeguards and mitigate ML/TF risks. Breach: no criminal sanctions under AMLO for DNFBPs — dealt with via professional disciplinary mechanisms / TCSP licensing regime. 💬 2018 年修訂之後，會計師、律師、地產代理同 TCSP 同銀行一樣要做 CDD 同保存紀錄。記住：會計師違規唔會坐監，但會被專業團體紀律處分。 Card 6 Front: Under the TCSP licensing regime in the AMLO: (a) who is exempt from holding a licence; (b) what is the penalty for carrying on a TCS business without a licence; (c) how long is a licence valid? Back: (a) Exempt under s.53B : qualified accounting professionals, qualified legal professionals, HKSAR Government, authorized institutions (Banking Ordinance (Cap. 155)), licensed corporations (SFO (Cap. 571)) where TCS is ancillary to principal business, prescribed persons. (b) s.53F(1)–(2) : fine of HK$100,000 and 6 months' imprisonment . (c) s.53O : 3 years (or shorter as determined by the Registrar of Companies). Fit and proper test: ss.53H–53I (ML/TF convictions, undischarged bankruptcy, non compliance with AMLO, liquidation of corporate applicant). 💬 考試陷阱：會計師做公司秘書服務 唔使攞 TCSP 牌 ，但 Schedule 2 嘅 CDD/record keeping 一樣要做足 ——「免牌唔等於免責」。 Card 7 Front: State the four conditions that must all be satisfied for an offence under s.9(1) of the POBO, and the key defences/burden rules. Back: Conditions (all must be present): 1. The person is an agent (employee or person acting for another — s.2); 2. He/she solicited or accepted an advantage ; 3. As an inducement to or reward for an act in relation to the principal's affairs ; 4. Without lawful authority or reasonable excuse (principal's permission). Defences/burden: s.9(5) : permission obtained as soon as reasonably possible after offer/acceptance; s.11 : no defence that the bribe's purpose was not carried out; s.19 : no defence that the advantage is customary; s.24 : burden of proving lawful authority/reasonable excuse is on the accused . 💬 四個條件缺一不可：agent + advantage + principal's affairs + 無批准。Answer 入面要逐項對落 facts。注意「entertainment」（請食飯）唔算 advantage，係常見 distractor。 Card 8 Front: What is the JFIU, what are its limits, and what is the 'SAFE' approach? Back: Joint Financial Intelligence Unit — set up 1989 , jointly run by the HK Police Force and the Customs and Excise Department. Central hub receiving suspicious transaction reports (STRs) made under s.25A DTROPO, s.25A OSCO and s.12 UNATMO. It has no investigative power itself — it refers reports to local and overseas enforcement departments for action.
