text: M10 Chapter 9: Internal Administration of a Company — Phase 1 速查表 + Phase 2 閃卡 Phase 1 速查表 Learning Objectives (3–5, English, action verbs) 1. Apply the accounting records, annual financial statements and simplified reporting requirements under the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) ('CO') to a given company (ss.361–380, 383, 387–391). 2. Analyse the appointment, duties, rights, liabilities and cessation of office of auditors under the CO (ss.393–430) and at common law. 3. Distinguish the decision making powers of members in general meetings from those of the board of directors, and apply the procedural rules on notices, quorum, proxies, resolutions and written resolutions (ss.548–622). 4. Classify the different types of directors (de jure, de facto, shadow, alternate, nominee, reserve, ED/NED/INED) and apply the rules on appointment, board meeting procedures, vacation of office and disqualification (CO Part 10; CWUMPO (Cap. 32) Part IVA). 5. Evaluate the validity of company decisions using the irregularity principle and the inspection rights of directors and members (ss.374–378, 620, 740). 必背考點 除另有註明外，本章所有 section 編號均指 Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) ('CO') （LP 原文：「Unless otherwise stated, all references to statutory provisions herein are made to the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622)」）。 A. Relevant Ordinances — Audit & Accounts（會計紀錄與財務報表） Topic Rule Citation Accounting records 標準 Records must be sufficient (a) to show and explain the company's transactions; (b) to disclose with reasonable accuracy, at any time, the company's financial position and financial performance; (c) to enable the directors to ensure the financial statements comply with the CO. Must contain daily entries of all sums received/expended and a record of assets and liabilities. s.373(2), s.373(3) 存放地點與披露間隔 Kept at registered office or any place approved by directors; must disclose financial position at intervals of not more than 6 months. s.374(1), s.374(3) 形式與保存期 Hard copy or electronic form; retained for 7 years . s.376(2), s.377 刑事責任 Director failing to take all reasonable steps to ensure proper accounting records commits a criminal offence. ss.373(5)–(7) 每年編製文件 Directors must prepare audited financial statements + directors' report + auditor's report each financial year. s.379 Accounting reference period First period: incorporation date → last day of the month of the anniversary of incorporation ('primary accounting reference date'); directors may specify a date within 18 months of incorporation; financial year cannot be lengthened beyond 18 months nor changed more than once every 5 years. ss.369(5)(a)–(b); ss.371(5)–(6) True and fair view Annual financial statements must give a true and fair view ; detailed requirements per HKFRS issued by HKICPA (specified body under Companies (Accounting Standards) (Prescribed Body) Regulation (Cap. 622C) s.2). s.380 財務報表內容 (1) Statement of profit or loss and comprehensive income; (2) Statement of financial position — signed by two directors ; (3) Directors' emolument notes; (4) Consolidated FS for holding companies. s.387(1); s.383(1); s.379(2) Directors' report Narrative supplement; explains principal activities and matters material for members' appreciation of the company's affairs; must be approved by directors and signed by a director or the company secretary. s.388(1); s.390; s.390(2)(a); Sch. 5; s.391(1); Companies (Directors' Report) Regulation (Cap. 622D) Simplified reporting — small private company Any 2 of 3 : total revenue ≤ HK$100m; total assets ≤ HK$100m; average employees ≤ 100. Non qualifying for 2 consecutive years → disqualified in the following financial year. s.361; ss.359(3)–(4); s.363 & Sch. 3 (guarantee companies) Simplified reporting — eligible private company Election by ≥ 75% of members' votes with no veto (or all members' written approval), plus any 2 of 3: revenue ≤ HK$200m; assets ≤ HK$200m; employees ≤ 100. s.360; s.359(1)(b); Sch. 3 永不合資格公司 Banking (Banking Ordinance (Cap. 155)); licensed corporations under SFO (Cap. 571) Part V; insurance business (other than solely as agent); business of accepting loans of money. ss.359(4)(a)–(c) Annual return Private company delivers annual return within 42 days after the company's return date (= anniversary of incorporation); specified form NAR1 ; failure = offence and fine. ss.662(1), 662(2), 662(6); s.664 & Sch. 6 Publication Private companies: no general duty to publish FS; public/guarantee companies lodge FS with annual returns → open to public inspection. Sch. 6; s.7; s.45; s.664 送交 members 時間 Reporting documents (FS + directors' report + auditor's report) sent to members at least 21 days before the AGM ; electronic means allowed with members' agreement; summary financial report possible with agreement. s.429; s.831; s.442 B. Relevant Ordinances — Inspection Rights（查閱權） Who Rule Citation Directors (statute) Accounting records open to inspection by directors at all times without charge ; directors entitled to make copies; may apply to court for assistance. Right is individual , exercisable by executive and non executive directors alike. s.374(1)(b); s.375; s.378 Directors (common law) Wider than statute: extends to corporate material, records, accounts, information and any documents reasonably assisting the director in carrying out duties. Tsai Shao Chung v Asia Television Ltd (2012) 4 HKLRD 52 (CA) Members (statute) Right to inspect (free) and obtain copies (prescribed fee) of: minutes of general meetings; register of members; register of directors and company secretaries; register of debenture holders; register of charges. Also right to receive reporting documents (electronically per s.833). s.620; s.631; ss.642, 649; s.310; s.355; s.831 Members (common law) No general right to inspect books of account or other company documents (reflection of separate legal entity). Model Articles: wider member inspection subject to directors'/GM approval. LP §9.1.4 Members — court order Application requires ≥ 2.5% of voting rights OR ≥ 5 members ; court orders only if satisfied the application is (1) in good faith and (2) for a proper purpose (must relate to applicant's status as shareholder; dominant purpose test — secondary improper purpose irrelevant). Covers any 'record or document' of the company but not subsidiaries' records (save those in the company's possession). s.740; s.740(6); Wong Kar Gee Mimi (2011) 5 HKLRD 241; Re Lehman Brown Ltd (2011) 5 HKLRD 668 C. Relevant Ordinances — Auditors（核數師） Topic Rule Citation Qualification Must be a CPA holding a practising certificate under the Professional Accountants Ordinance (Cap. 50) ('PAO'); a CPA firm can be appointed under its firm name (all partners deemed appointed); a corporate practice may be appointed; employees of the company cannot be appointed (conflict of interest). s.393; PAO s.29(2); PAO s.28A(2); s.399; s.393(2) Appointment Auditor must be appointed for each financial year ; first auditor appointed by directors before first AGM; members reappoint/appoint at first AGM — refreshed annually; if AGM dispensed with, existing auditor deemed re appointed . s.394; s.396; s.403 Casual vacancy Directors may fill; if directors fail within 1 month , members may appoint by resolution at a GM. s.397; s.395(2); s.396(1); s.396(3) Auditor's report 內容 Opinion on: (1) true and fair view; (2) consistency of directors' report with FS; (3) adequacy of accounting records; (4) agreement of FS with records. Duty to investigate items (3)–(4). Report signed by auditor; sent to members and laid before AGM. s.405; s.406(1)(b); s.406(2); s.407(2); s.407(1); s.409; s.430; s.429 Auditor's rights Access to accounting records and information/explanations from officers (non compliance = criminal offence unless not reasonably practicable); attend and speak at any general meeting; information from subsidiary undertakings; outgoing auditor may pass information to incoming auditor in good faith. s.412(1); ss.413(1)–(2); s.411(1)(a)–(b); s.412(2); s.414 Criminal liability Knowingly or recklessly causing a required statement to be omitted from the auditor's report = offence. Liability depends on whether the auditor actually held the opinion but omitted it — an honestly held (even negligent/erroneous) belief that all information was obtained is not an offence. s.408; s.408(2); s.407(2)(b); s.407(3) Civil liability (common law) Duty of care in tort and contract (implied term); reasonable care and skill; auditor provides only reasonable assurance — 'not an insurer'; 'a watch dog, but not a bloodhound'; entitled to rely on management assurances if reasonable ; once put on enquiry, must make exhaustive enquiry. Duty owed to the company , not the public at large; no 'trading loss' claims; special proximity (e.g. special audit before acquisition) may create duty to third parties. Re Kingston Cotton Mill Co (No. 2) (1896) 2 Ch 279; Re Thomas Gerrard & Son Ltd (1968) Ch 455; Re London and General Bank (No. 2) (1895) 2 Ch 673; Guang Xin Enterprises Ltd v Kwan Wong Tan & Fong (2002) 2 HKLRD 319; Yue Xiu Finance Co Ltd v Agnew (1995) 2 HKLR 186; The Registrar of HKICPA v Wong Tak Man Stephen (2017) 20 HKCFAR 556 Duty to report Report impropriety/fraud to the company immediately; statutory duty to report to regulators may override confidentiality (e.g. good faith communication to the SFC immune from civil liability). s.381, Securities and Futures Ordinance (Cap. 571) Indemnities void Articles provisions exempting an auditor from duty of care, or indemnifying an auditor for breach of that duty, are void . s.415(2); s.415(3) Resignation Written notice deposited at registered office; must give a statement of circumstances (or a statement of no circumstances); may require directors to convene a GM and circulate a cessation statement; right to attend that meeting; court may block circulation if used to secure needless publicity for defamatory matter. s.417; s.424; s.421; s.422(1)(c); s.426(3) Retirement Term expires without re appointment; retiring auditor also owes statement of circumstances; right to call meeting / cessation statement. s.416(1)(a); s.425; s.422(2) Removal Ordinary resolution of members in GM; special notice required and copy sent to the auditor; removal does not deprive auditor of compensation/damages; auditor has cessation statement and attendance rights. s.419; s.419(2); s.419(3); s.420; s.422(3); s.411 Disqualification Auditor who ceases to be eligible/becomes disqualified must immediately cease to act and notify the company in writing within 14 days ; failure = criminal offence. s.418; s.418(1)(b); s.418(2) D. Relevant Ordinances — Members' Meetings & Resolutions Topic Rule Citation AGM Required annually after each financial year; for private/guarantee companies within 9 months after the end of the accounting reference period; reporting documents laid before the AGM; members may apply to court to order an AGM on default; AGM not required if all AGM business done by written resolution and documents provided to each member. s.610(1); s.610(1)(a); s.430; ss.610(7)–(8); s.612 GM Any general meeting other than an AGM; convened by directors; members holding ≥ 1/20 (5%) of paid up voting capital may requisition a GM (company's expense); shareholders may convene where there are insufficient directors. s.565; ss.566–568; s.569 保留予股東嘅事項 Change of name ( special resolution ); alteration of articles/objects; alteration of max number of shares; allotment of shares; removal of director before expiry of term ; payment out of capital for redemption/buy back; financial assistance for share acquisition. s.107; ss.88, 89; s.88(3); s.141; s.462; ss.257–266; ss.283–289 Residual power (common law) GM acts where (1) the board cannot function (deadlock/failure to act) or (2) ratification of directors' acts in excess of powers is necessary. Re Commonwealth Printing Press Ltd, SCt(HK) (unrep.), HCCW 15/1974, 31 May 1974; Re Mandarin Capital Advisory Ltd (2011) 2 HKLRD 1003 Notice — AGM 21 days' notice; shorter only with all shareholders' consent; articles may require longer. s.571(1)(a) Notice — GM 14 days' notice; shorter if agreed by a majority representing ≥ 95% of voting rights. s.571(1)(b); s.571(3) Special notice Notice of intention to move a resolution given ≥ 28 days before the meeting; given to members with the notice of meeting; if impracticable, ≥ 14 days before by newspaper advertisement or other manner allowed by the articles. Required for: ordinary resolution to remove a director (copy to the director) and to remove an auditor (copy to the auditor). s.578(1); s.578(2); s.578(3); s.462; s.419 Chairperson Model Articles: board chairman chairs GMs; failing that, directors present elect one of themselves; without articles provision, any member may be elected by resolution; chairperson acts neutrally; limited adjournment power; declaration of result is conclusive evidence . Art. 40(1), (3); s.586; Art. 42; s.590(1) Quorum Two members present in person (Model Articles: in person or by proxy); one member company: sole member suffices; no quorum → meeting invalid. s.585(3); Art. 39(1); s.585(1); Re Alma Spinning Co (Bottomley's case) (1880) 16 Ch D 681 Voting / poll Default = show of hands; poll demandable (under the Model Articles: chairperson, ≥ 2 members present in person or by proxy, or member(s) holding ≥ 5% of total voting rights); articles provisions void if they block a poll demanded by 5 voting members / 5% holders / the chairperson; chairperson must demand a poll if proxies show a different result. Model Articles (LP §9.2.4.3); s.591(2); s.592 Proxy Proxy need not be a member; ordinary vs two way proxy forms (directors must ensure forms allow instructions); proxy votes on show of hands and poll (but multiple proxies cannot vote on show of hands); revocation effective only if received before commencement of the meeting; member attending in person overrides the proxy. s.596(1); s.601; s.588; s.588(2); s.604(3); s.605; s.606 (corporate representative) Ordinary resolution Simple majority; default type where the CO/documents do not specify. s.563; s.562(3) Special resolution ≥ 75% majority; notice must state the text and that it is proposed as a special resolution; required for alteration of constitution, change of name, reduction of capital, winding up; copy filed with the Registry within 15 days (not for change of name). s.564; s.564(4)(a)–(b); s.88(2); s.107; s.215; s.622 Minutes Records of all GM proceedings kept ≥ 10 years ; members inspect free / copy for a fee. s.618(1)(b)–(c); s.618(2); s.620; s.655(7) Irregularity principle (GM) A decision cannot be questioned if the only defect is a mere informality/irregularity and the intention of the meeting is clear — especially where the result would have been the same. Only the majority can complain unless fraud on the minority or defect of substance. Insufficient notice that is not 'full and frank' → resolutions invalid. Yip Peter v Asian Electronics Ltd (1998) 2 HKC 96; Baillie v Oriental Telephone and Electric Co Ltd (1915) 1 Ch 503 Electronic meetings GM may be held at two or more places using technology enabling members to listen, speak and vote. s.584; Part 18 Written resolutions Anything doable by ordinary/special resolution can be done by written resolution EXCEPT removal of an auditor or director before expiry of term ; requires agreement of ALL members entitled to vote ; members holding ≥ 5% voting rights may require circulation; company circulates within 21 days at its own expense; member may attach one statement of ≤ 1,000 words. s.548; s.556(1)–(2); s.549; ss.549(b), 522; s.551; ss.552–553 E. Relevant Ordinances — The Board of Directors Topic Rule Citation Definition 'Director' = any person occupying the position of director, by whatever name called. s.2(1) De facto director Person who 'assumes to act as a director', held out as a director, purports to be one, though never validly appointed; subject to the same duties as a de jure director. Test: whether the person occupied/acted in the position of director — a question of degree in context. Re Hydrodan (Corby) Ltd [1994] BCC 161 (Millett J); Deputy Commissioner of Taxation v Austin (1998) 28 ACSR 565 Shadow director Person in accordance with whose directions or instructions (excluding advice given in a professional capacity ) the directors or a majority of them are accustomed to act ; not within the general s.2(1) definition and does not necessarily owe fiduciary duties (unlike de jure/de facto). s.2; Re Unisoft Group Ltd (No. 2) [1994] BCC 766 Alternate director Acts in place of an absent director; deemed agent of the appointing director (who is vicariously liable for the alternate's torts), but remains personally liable for own acts/omissions; fiduciary duties triggered only upon actually assuming directorial authority. s.478(1)–(2); Playcorp Pty Ltd v Shaw (1993) 10 ACSR 212 Reserve director Private company with one member who is also sole director may nominate a person ≥ 18 to act on the sole director's death; ceases on resignation/revocation/cessation of sole directorship other than by death. s.455; s.455(2) ED / NED / INED Private companies: commercial distinction only. Listed companies: ≥ 3 INEDs representing ≥ 1/3 of the board; independence questioned if holds 1% shares, received financial assistance/securities, principal/partner/director of a professional adviser within 2 years, or financially dependent. New CG requirements (from 1 Jan 2022): 9 year INEDs need separate shareholder resolution; single gender boards must appoint a director of a different gender by 31 Dec 2024; mandatory nomination committee chaired by chairman or INED with INED majority. Main Board Listing Rules Ch. 3.13; Listing Rule 3.27A; Corporate Governance Code Appointment First directors named in incorporation form; consent in writing registered ≤ 15 days after incorporation; private company ≥ 1 director; public company / company limited by guarantee ≥ 2 ; subsequent appointments per articles (Model Articles: ordinary resolution). ss.453(2), 454(2); s.74; s.454(1); s.453(1); Art. 22 Board meetings — notice Any director may call; notice to each director (and alternates), need not be in writing, must state date/time/venue; period must be reasonable (less than 10 minutes can suffice if offices nearby); no general need to state business; failure may render meeting void. Art. 9; Art. 9(2)–(3); Art. 29; Browne v La Trinidad (1887) 37 Ch D 1; Yick Hok Wing v Chan Yook Ming (1997) 1 HKC 49 Board meetings — quorum & voting Quorum = 2 unless otherwise determined; an interested director is not counted in the quorum and must not vote; resolutions passed by majority ; chairperson has a casting vote on equality. Art. 11; Art. 16; Art. 7(1)(a); Art. 14; Art. 13 Board — informal decisions Written resolution (unanimous approval of eligible directors) as effective as a meeting; informal meetings valid if the directors treat the meeting as a board meeting (objective intention); unanimous agreement/acquiescence suffices without any meeting; a casual encounter cannot be turned into a board meeting at one director's option against the other's will. Art. 7(1)(b); Art. 8(2); Art. 10; Barron v Potter (1914) 1 Ch 895 Board — irregularities General rule: irregularity in convening/holding a board meeting renders it void (unlike GMs). Deliberate withholding of notice to exclude a director invalidates the meeting even if the result would have been the same — the company is entitled to the collective wisdom of all directors. Grand Field Group Holdings Ltd v Tsang Wai Lun Wayland (No. 2) (2010) 4 HKLRD 487; Billion Express Industrial Ltd v Tsang Hung Kong (2012) 5 HKC 51 Vacation of office Model Articles: ceasing to be a director under the CO; bankruptcy; mental incapacity; resignation; absence from board meetings 6 months without permission; removal by ordinary resolution. Art. 25 Removal of director Ordinary resolution notwithstanding anything in the articles ; special notice required; copy of notice sent to the director, who is entitled to be heard and to make written representations; removal does not affect compensation/damages claims; quasi partnership directors may contest (unfair prejudice — Ch. 10). s.462; s.462(4); s.463; s.462(9); Samuel Tak Lee v Chou Wen Hsien (1984) 1 WLR 1202 Resignation A director may resign at any time subject to the articles; where articles require notice, resignation effective only when properly given. s.464(1); s.464(5) Notification Changes in directors notified to the Registrar within 15 days ; register of directors updated. s.645(4); s.641 Disqualification (CWUMPO (Cap. 32) Part IVA) Grounds: (1) conviction of indictable offences (s.168E — max 15 yrs CFI / 10 yrs DC / 5 yrs Magistracy); (2) persistent breaches of filing obligations (s.168F — conclusively proved by ≥ 3 defaults in 5 years; max 5 yrs); (3) fraudulent trading/fraud in winding up (ss.168G, 168L — max 15 yrs); (4) unfit conduct as director of insolvent company (s.168H — mandatory , min 1 yr, max 15 yrs; Sch. 15 matters); (5) public interest on Financial Secretary's application (s.168I/s.168J(1); s.879(6) CO — max 15 yrs). Brackets: 10 yrs very serious; 6–10 yrs serious; 2–5 yrs minimum band. ss.168D–168P, CWUMPO (Cap. 32); Official Receiver v Chan Kin Hang Danvil (2012) 4 HKLRD J3; Re Well Bond Group Ltd (2008) 5 HKLRD 147 Scope & contravention Order bars (without leave of court): being a director, liquidator, receiver/manager, or taking part in management/formation. Contravention = offence (max 2 years' imprisonment + HK$150,000 fine) + personal liability for company debts incurred while so involved. s.168D(1); s.168M; s.168O(1), CWUMPO (Cap. 32) F. IRAC Application Points（考試答題骨架） 1. Member seeking company documents : Issue — does a member have inspection rights? Rule — no general common law right; statutory registers only (s.620, s.631, ss.642/649, s.310, s.355); court order under s.740 requires ≥ 2.5% voting rights or ≥ 5 members, plus good faith + proper purpose (dominant purpose test). Application — identify the member's purpose (investigating suspected director misconduct = proper; personal vendetta alone = improper). Conclusion — likely granted/denied. 2. Removing a director : Issue — valid removal? Rule — s.462 ordinary resolution + special notice (s.462(4), s.578(1): ≥ 28 days) + s.463 right to be heard/representations; cannot be done by written resolution (s.548). Application — check each procedural step against the facts. Conclusion — prima facie invalid if any step missed; consider whether the irregularity principle rescues it (mere informality vs substantive loss of representation rights). 3. Auditor negligence : Issue — breach of duty of care? Rule — reasonable skill and care; watch dog not bloodhound (Re Kingston Cotton Mill); entitled to rely on management only if reasonable ; once on notice of irregularity, must enquire exhaustively (Re Thomas Gerrard). Application — was the auditor put on enquiry? Was reliance reasonable? Conclusion — liable / not liable. 4. De facto vs shadow director : Issue — status of a non appointed influencer. Rule — de facto = assumes to act as director/held out (Re Hydrodan; DCT v Austin); shadow = board accustomed to act on instructions, excluding professional advice (s.2). Application — map the person's actual conduct. Conclusion — de facto → full directors' duties; shadow → not necessarily fiduciary. 5. Board vs GM irregularity : Board meeting irregularity (e.g. deliberately withheld notice) → void, even if outcome unchanged (Billion Express). GM irregularity → saved by the irregularity principle if mere informality and intention clear (Yip Peter), unless fraud on minority or defect of substance (Baillie). 易混淆概念對比 Table 1: De facto Director vs Shadow Director 比較點 De facto director Shadow director Definition A person who assumes to act as a director and is held out as one, though never validly appointed A person in accordance with whose directions or instructions the directors (or a majority) are accustomed to act Statutory basis Covered by the general definition in s.2(1) CO Defined separately in s.2 CO ; not within the general 'director' definition Key authority Re Hydrodan (Corby) Ltd [1994] BCC 161; Deputy Commissioner of Taxation v Austin (1998) 28 ACSR 565 Re Unisoft Group Ltd (No. 2) [1994] BCC 766 Fiduciary duties Yes — same duties as an appointed (de jure) director Not necessarily — CO imposes similar statutory duties but fiduciary duties not automatic Professional adviser carve out N/A — conduct based test (question of degree) Advice given in a professional capacity is excluded 點樣分辨 行為導向：睇佢有冇「做出嚟」— 簽文件、對外自稱董事、行使最高管理職能（top level management functions） 控制導向：睇佢係咪「幕後操盤」— 董事會習慣性跟佢指示行事，但佢自己唔拋頭露面 考試伏位 做咗一兩次幫手唔算 —— 要睇 time span 同 breadth of activities（DCT v Austin）；emergency/friend 嘅藉口未必成立 專業人士（律師/會計師）喺專業範疇內俾意見 ≠ shadow director；但如果意見超越專業範疇（如商業決策），就可能中招 Table 2: AGM vs GM vs Special Notice（開會通知期最易混） 比較點 Annual General Meeting (AGM) General Meeting (GM) Special notice Nature Mandatory annual meeting after each financial year Any general meeting that is not an AGM A notice of intention to move a particular resolution Timing Private/guarantee companies: within 9 months after end of accounting reference period (s.610(1)(a)) Any time in the year Given ≥ 28 days before the meeting (s.578(1)) Notice period 21 days (s.571(1)(a)) 14 days (s.571(1)(b)) Given to members at the same time as the notice of meeting (s.578(2)); fallback: ≥ 14 days by newspaper advertisement (s.578(3)) Short notice Only if all shareholders consent Majority holding ≥ 95% of voting rights (s.571(3)) Cannot be shortened by consent — statutory minimum When required Every year unless dispensed with (s.612 — written resolution route) Convened by directors (s.565); requisition by ≥ 5% paid up voting capital (ss.566–568) Removal of a director before term (s.462) and removal of an auditor (s.419) — both are ordinary resolutions 點樣分辨 記口訣：「AGM 廿一、GM 十四、special notice 廿八」；問你邊種 notice 就對返邊個 section 股東 requisition 嘅 5% 係 paid up capital carrying voting rights ，唔係人數 Special notice ≠ special resolution！前者係通知程序（28 日），後者係 75% 大多數通過 考試伏位 9 個月期限只係 private/guarantee companies；public companies 規則唔同（LP 本章未展開，唔好亂寫） 漏咗 send copy 俾被罷免嘅董事/核數師（s.463 / s.419(3)）→ 決議 prima facie invalid 考生成日將 removal of director 答做 special resolution —— 其實係 ordinary resolution + special notice ；亦唔可以用 written resolution（s.548） Phase 2 閃卡 (exactly 8 cards) Card 1 Front: What standard must a company's accounting records meet under s.373(2) of the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622), and for how long must they be retained? Back: Records must be sufficient to: (a) show and explain the company's transactions; (b) disclose with reasonable accuracy, at any time, the company's financial position and financial performance; (c) enable directors to ensure financial statements comply with the CO (s.373(2)). Must contain daily entries of all sums received/expended and a record of assets and liabilities (s.373(3)). Retention: 7 years (s.377); hard copy or electronic form (s.376(2)). Directors failing to take all reasonable steps commit a criminal offence (ss.373(5)–(7)). 💬 白話解釋：記住「三大足夠」——解釋交易、隨時反映財政狀況、幫董事確保報表合規。保存期係 7 年（s.377），唔好同 minutes 嘅 10 年（s.618(2)）搞亂。董事疏忽冇保存好係刑事罪行。 Card 2 Front: When does a private company qualify as a 'small private company' for simplified reporting, and how can it lose the exemption? Back: Qualifies by satisfying any 2 of 3 (s.361): (1) total revenue ≤ HK$100m; (2) total assets ≤ HK$100m; (3) average employees ≤ 100. A company not initially qualifying may qualify by meeting 2 conditions in 2 consecutive financial years (ss.359(3)–(4)). Disqualification: fails any 2 conditions for 2 consecutive years → loses exemption in the immediately following financial year. Eligible private company route: ≥ 75% member approval (no veto) + higher thresholds (revenue/assets ≤ HK$200m) (s.360, Sch. 3). Banks, SFO licensed corporations, insurers and money lending businesses can never qualify (s.359(4)). 💬 白話解釋：口訣「三揀二」：收入、資產、員工，三個條件滿足兩個就得。跌出資格要連續兩年唔達標先會喺第三年失去豁免。睇題目時一定要逐年 check，唔好睇一年就下結論。 Card 3 Front: A shareholder holding 3% of voting rights suspects the directors of misappropriating company funds. What is her route to inspect the company's accounting records, and what must she prove? Back: Members have no general common law right to inspect books of account; statutory inspection covers only specified registers/minutes (s.620, s.631, ss.642/649, s.310, s.355). Route: apply to court under s.740 . Threshold (s.740(6)): ≥ 2.5% of voting rights OR ≥ 5 members — a 3% holder qualifies. Must prove: (1) application made in good faith ; (2) inspection for a proper purpose (must relate to shareholder status, e.g. investigating suspected director misconduct — Re Lehman Brown Ltd (2011) 5 HKLRD 668). Dominant purpose proper = sufficient even with an improper secondary purpose (Wong Kar Gee Mimi (2011) 5 HKLRD 241). 💬 白話解釋：股東同董事查閱權差好遠 —— 董事可以隨時免費睇（s.374(1)(b)），股東就要過 s.740 兩關：先過門檻（2.5% 或 5 個人），再證明 good faith + proper purpose。答題記住 dominant purpose test：主要目的正當就得，就算有心報仇都唔緊要。 Card 4 Front: What is the common law standard of care owed by an auditor, and when is the auditor entitled to rely on management's assurances? Back: Duty of care in both tort and contract (implied term); reasonable care and skill judged by prevailing professional standards. Auditor provides reasonable assurance only — 'not an insurer', does not guarantee the accounts (Re London and General Bank (No. 2) (1895) 2 Ch 673). 'A watch dog, but not a bloodhound ' — not bound to be suspicious (Re Kingston Cotton Mill Co (No. 2) (1896) 2 Ch 279). Reliance on assurances is allowed only if reasonable : once put on notice of irregularity, must make exhaustive enquiry and inform the board (Re Thomas Gerrard & Son Ltd (1968) Ch 455). Duty owed to the company — no duty to shareholders/public at large; trading loss not recoverable (Guang Xin Enterprises Ltd v Kwan Wong Tan & Fong (2002) 2 HKLRD 319). 💬 白話解釋：核數師係看門狗唔係獵犬 —— 平時可以信管理層，但一見到可疑嘢（e.g. 改過嘅單據）就一定要查到底。兩個 case 一對記：Kingston Cotton Mill（冇可疑 → 可以信）vs Thomas Gerrard（有可疑 → 唔可以齋信）。信唔信得過，關鍵係 reasonable。 Card 5 Front: How may an auditor be removed or resign, and what procedural protections exist? Back: Removal : ordinary resolution at GM (s.419) + special notice (s.419(2)) + copy to the auditor (s.419(3)); removal does not deprive compensation/damages (s.420). Resignation : written notice deposited at registered office (s.417); must deposit a statement of circumstances (or nil statement) (s.424); company must send it to members. Auditor may require directors to convene a GM to explain the circumstances (s.421) and has a right to attend (s.422(1)(c)). Court may block circulation of the statement if used to secure needless publicity for defamatory matter (s.426(3)). Removal of an auditor before expiry of term cannot be done by written resolution (s.548). 💬 白話解釋：核數師走人唔可以靜靜哋走 —— 一定要交 statement of circumstances，等股東知道有冇被管理層阻撓查數。罷免核數師同罷免董事一樣：ordinary resolution + special notice，同埋都係 s.548 嘅 written resolution 例外。 Card 6 Front: State the notice periods for an AGM, a GM and a special notice, and the ways each may be shortened. Back: AGM: 21 days (s.571(1)(a)); shorter only with consent of all shareholders; articles may lengthen. GM: 14 days (s.571(1)(b)); shorter with consent of a majority holding ≥ 95% of voting rights (s.571(3)). Special notice: ≥ 28 days before the meeting (s.578(1)), given to members with the meeting notice (s.578(2)); fallback ≥ 14 days by newspaper advertisement if impracticable (s.578(3)). Special notice required for removing a director (s.462) or an auditor (s.419) before expiry of term. 💬 白話解釋：「21 14 28」三個數一定要背。縮短規則唔同：AGM 要全體同意，GM 要 95%，special notice 冇得縮（法定最低）。小心唔好將 special notice（通知程序）同 special resolution（75% 投票門檻）撈埋一齊。 Card 7 Front: What are the quorum and voting rules for a members' general meeting, including proxies? Back: Quorum: 2 members present in person (s.585(3)); Model Articles: in person or by proxy (Art. 39(1)); one member company: sole member suffices (s.585(1)); no quorum → meeting invalid (Re Alma Spinning Co (1880) 16 Ch D 681). Default voting = show of hands ; poll demandable (chairperson / ≥ 2 members / ≥ 5% voting rights under Model Articles); articles void if blocking poll by 5 members, 5% holders or chairperson (s.591(2)); chairperson must demand poll if proxies indicate a different result (s.592). Proxy: need not be a member (s.596(1)); two way forms must allow instructions (s.601); multiple proxies cannot vote on show of hands (s.588(2)); revocation effective only if received before the meeting starts (s.604(3)); member attending in person overrides proxy (s.605). Chairperson's declaration of result = conclusive evidence (s.590(1)). 💬 白話解釋：法定 quorum 係兩個人，一人公司例外。Proxy 最考起考生嘅兩點：(1) 撤銷 proxy 要喺會議開始前送達公司；(2) 本人親自出席投票就自動蓋過 proxy（s.605），就算撤銷通知遲咗都冇所謂。 Card 8 Front: On what grounds may the court disqualify a person from being a director under Part IVA of the Companies (Winding Up and Miscellaneous Provisions) Ordinance (Cap. 32), and what are the consequences of contravention? Back: Grounds (s.168): (1) conviction of indictable offences (s.168E — max 15/10/5 yrs by court level); (2) persistent breaches of filing provisions (s.168F — ≥ 3 defaults in 5 yrs = conclusive proof; max 5 yrs); (3) fraudulent trading/fraud in winding up (ss.168G, 168L — max 15 yrs); (4) unfit conduct as director of an insolvent company (s.168H — mandatory order; 1–15 yrs; Sch. 15 factors); (5) public interest on Financial Secretary's application (ss.168I, 168J(1); s.879(6) CO — max 15 yrs). Brackets: 10 yrs very serious; 6–10 yrs serious; 2–5 yrs minimum (Re Well Bond Group Ltd (2008) 5 HKLRD 147; Official Receiver v Chan Kin Hang Danvil (2012) 4 HKLRD J3). Contravention: offence — max 2 years' imprisonment + HK$150,000 fine (s.168M); personal liability for company debts incurred while acting (s.168O(1)). 💬 白話解釋：五大 grounds 記「定罪、累犯、欺詐、不稱職、公眾利益」。唯獨 s.168H（insolvent 公司 + unfit）係 mandatory —— court 必須頒令，其他都係 discretionary。違令最辣：坐監兩年、罰十五萬、仲要個人孭返公司債。 本章急救詞彙 EN Term 繁中白話 English Model Sentence Accounting reference period 會計參照期間，用嚟界定財政年度 The first accounting reference period begins on the date of incorporation and ends on the primary accounting reference date. True and fair view 真實公平咁反映公司財政狀況 Under s.380 of the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622), the annual financial statements must give a true and fair view. Statement of circumstances 核數師離職時交代有冇需要股東知悉嘅事項 On resignation, the auditor must deposit a statement of circumstances under s.424, or state that there are none. Special notice 動議某決議嘅特別通知，最少 28 日 Removal of a director under s.462 requires special notice given at least 28 days before the meeting (s.578(1)). Two way proxy 指明投贊成或反對嘅指定式委任代表表格 The directors must ensure that any proxy form sent to members allows two way voting instructions (s.601). De facto director 冇正式任命但實際上做緊董事嘅人 A person who assumes to act as a director is a de facto director subject to the same duties as a de jure director. Shadow director 幕後指示董事會行事嘅人（專業意見除外） A shadow director is a person in accordance with whose directions or instructions the directors are accustomed to act (s.2, CO). Disqualification order 法院頒令禁止某人做董事或參與公司管理 Under Part IVA of the CWUMPO (Cap. 32), the court may make a disqualification order for up to 15 years.

title: M10 Chapter 9: Internal Administration of a Company — Phase 3 Answers
headings: M10 Chapter 9: Internal Administration of a Company — Phase 3 Answers
Q5 — Answer: (a) Fiona = de facto director; Gordon = shadow director. (b) No — s.548.
excerpt: M10 Chapter 9: Internal Administration of a Company — Phase 3 Answers Q1 — Answer: C Model Answer (EN): For a private company (or a company limited by guarantee…
text: M10 Chapter 9: Internal Administration of a Company — Phase 3 Answers Q1 — Answer: C Model Answer (EN): For a private company (or a company limited by guarantee), the AGM must be held within 9 months after the end of the company's accounting reference period (s.610(1)(a), CO). The accounting reference period ended on 31 March 2025, so the deadline is 31 December 2025 . If the company defaults, a member may apply to the court for an order to call or direct the calling of an AGM (ss.610(7)–(8)); the AGM could only be avoided if all its business were done by written resolution with the reporting documents provided to each member (s.612), which the question excludes. 解題思路（繁中）: C 啱：private company 嘅 AGM deadline = accounting reference period 結束後 9 個月內。31 March + 9 months = 31 December。 A 錯：3 個月冇任何 statutory basis，係干擾項。 B 錯：6 個月係 s.374(3) 會計紀錄披露財政狀況嘅最長間隔，唔係 AGM 期限 —— 呢個係典型「數字搬家」伏位。 D 錯：12 個月聽落合理（「annual」嘛），但 CO 對 private/guarantee companies 寫明係 9 個月，唔可以憑常識作答。 考試伏位：AGM 舉行期限、AGM notice（21 日，s.571(1)(a)）、annual return（incorporation anniversary 後 42 日，s.662(1)）三個時限成日撈亂，要分開背。 Rule Check: Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) s.610(1)(a); ss.610(7)–(8); s.612. Common Trap（繁中）: 見到「annual」就以為係一年內（12 months）——錯。仲有：9 個月規則只適用於 private companies 同 companies limited by guarantee；如果題目係 public company，唔好套用呢個答案（LP 本章未講 public company 嘅期限）。 Q2 — Answer: B Model Answer (EN): A company may change its name only by special resolution (s.107, CO) — a resolution passed by a majority of at least 75% of the votes cast (s.564). Re appointing an auditor at the AGM is done by an ordinary resolution of the members (ss.394, 396). Removing a director before the expiry of his term requires only an ordinary resolution , albeit with special notice (s.462, s.462(4), s.578(1)). Filling a casual vacancy in the office of auditor is a matter for the directors (or, failing them, the members by ordinary resolution) — no special resolution is involved (s.397). 解題思路（繁中）: B 啱：s.107 明確規定改名要 special resolution（≥75%，s.564）。其他要 special resolution 嘅事項：alteration of constitution（s.88(2)）、reduction of capital（s.215）、winding up。 A 錯：委任/續任核數師係 AGM 上以普通決議做（s.396(1)），每年 refresh。 C 錯（最大伏位）：罷免董事係 ordinary resolution + special notice —— 好多考生因為「好嚴重」就以為要 special resolution。記住：special notice 係通知程序（28 日前通知動議），同 75% 門檻完全冇關。 D 錯：casual vacancy 由董事填補，董事一個月內唔做先輪到股東喺 GM 以普通決議委任（s.397）。 Default rule：CO 或文件冇指明決議類型時，ordinary resolution 已足夠（s.562(3)）。 Rule Check: Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) s.107; s.564; s.462; s.462(4); s.578(1); s.396(1); s.397; s.562(3). Common Trap（繁中）: 「Special notice ≠ special resolution」係本章最高頻失分位。罷免董事/核數師都係 ordinary resolution，只係通知程序升級咗。答 MCQ 時見到「removal of director = special resolution」呢類 option 要立即剔除。 Q3 — Answer: C Model Answer (EN): Issue: Whether the ordinary resolution removing Leo as a director is valid despite the procedural defects. Rule: Members may remove a director before the expiry of his term by ordinary resolution notwithstanding anything in the articles (s.462(1), CO), but special notice is required — notice of the intention to move the resolution given not less than 28 days before the meeting (s.462(4); s.578(1)). The company must also send a copy of the notice to the director concerned, who is entitled to be heard at the meeting and to make written representations (s.463). Application: Only 14 days' notice of the meeting was given and no special notice was given at all; Leo never received a copy of the notice and was denied the opportunity to be heard or to make representations. These are not mere informalities: Leo lost a substantive statutory right to make representations as to his proposed removal. The irregularity principle (Yip Peter v Asian Electronics Ltd (1998) 2 HKC 96) saves only mere informalities where the intention of the meeting is clear; it does not cure the denial of a director's s.463 rights. Conclusion: The removal is prima facie invalid. Ivy and Ken must start afresh with proper special notice and a fresh general meeting. 解題思路（繁中）: C 啱：三個程序缺陷齊晒 —— (1) 冇 28 日 special notice（s.462(4)、s.578(1)）；(2) 冇 send copy 俾 Leo（s.463）；(3) Leo 冇機會陳詞。呢啲唔係 technicality，係實質權利。 A 錯：s.462 嘅「notwithstanding anything in the articles」只係話 articles 唔可以奪走股東罷免權， 唔係 豁免法定程序。70% 票數再高都補救唔到程序缺陷。 B 錯：irregularity principle 只覆蓋「mere informality and irregularity」而且結果唔會變嘅情況。Leo 失去咗 s.463 嘅陳詞機會，complaint 超越程序層面 —— LP Exam Practice Q1(c) 嘅分析正正係咁講。 D 錯：罷免董事係 ordinary resolution（simple majority，s.563），唔係 75% special resolution —— 混淆咗 special notice 同 special resolution。 考試伏位：見到「majority 大比數通過」就答 valid 係常見錯誤；程序權利（notice + 被聽取）係獨立要求。 Rule Check: Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) s.462(1); s.462(4); s.463; s.578(1); s.578(2); Yip Peter v Asian Electronics Ltd (1998) 2 HKC 96. Common Trap（繁中）: 同學成日背咗「罷免董事 = ordinary resolution」就以為冇其他要求，漏咗 special notice 同 s.463 嘅被罷免者權利。記住完整公式： s.462 ordinary resolution + s.462(4)/s.578(1) 28 day special notice + s.463 copy & right to be heard + 唔可以用 written resolution（s.548） 。 Q4 — Answer: B Model Answer (EN): Issue: Whether M & Co breached its common law duty of care in accepting the managing director's explanation of the altered invoices. Rule: An auditor owes the company a duty of care in tort and contract to exercise reasonable skill and care. The auditor is 'a watch dog, but not a bloodhound' and may rely on management's assurances only where such reliance is reasonable (Re Kingston Cotton Mill Co (No. 2) (1896) 2 Ch 279). Once the auditor discovers irregularities — such as altered invoices — he is put on enquiry and must make an exhaustive enquiry and inform the board; he is not entitled to rest content with assurances, however much he trusts the officer (Re Thomas Gerrard & Son Ltd (1968) Ch 455). Application: M & Co actually discovered the altered invoices — suspicion was aroused. From that point, blind reliance on Owen's bare assurance was not reasonable; a sample verification, exhaustive enquiry into the alterations and a report to the full board were required. Conclusion: M & Co is likely liable in negligence to the company. 解題思路（繁中）: B 啱：關鍵事實係核數師 已經發現 改過嘅單據 —— 一旦被 put on enquiry，信賴管理層就唔再 reasonable，必須 exhaustive enquiry（Thomas Gerrard）。 A 錯：Kingston Cotton Mill 嘅 reliance 之所以合理，係因為當時 冇任何嘢引起懷疑 ，而且證明文件嚟自「acknowledged competence and high reputation」嘅經理。呢度已經見到 altered invoices，事實唔同，rule 嘅例外情況唔啱用。 C 錯：「auditor is not an insurer」只係界定 duty 嘅範圍（reasonable assurance），唔係 negligence 嘅免死金牌 —— 佢唔可以豁免「被發現異常後唔追查」呢種 breach。 D 錯：s.408 係刑事罪行，針對 明知或罔顧 咁漏咗 report 入面應有嘅 statement；而且 LP 講明，如果核數師真誠相信資料齊全（即使判斷錯或疏忽），唔構成該罪行。呢度係 civil negligence 問題，criminal liability 亦唔會「automatically」establish civil liability。 考試伏位：兩個 case 嘅分水嶺係「有冇被 put on notice」；答題時第一句就要指出呢個 distinction。 Rule Check: Re Thomas Gerrard & Son Ltd (1968) Ch 455; Re Kingston Cotton Mill Co (No. 2) (1896) 2 Ch 279; Re London and General Bank (No. 2) (1895) 2 Ch 673; Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) s.408. Common Trap（繁中）: 背咗「watch dog not bloodhound」就逢 auditor 題都答 not liable —— 呢句格言只保護 冇可疑跡象 下嘅合理信賴。凡係 fact pattern 寫明核數師「發現咗/留意到」異常，答案方向多數係 liable（Thomas Gerrard 路線）。 Q5 — Answer: (a) Fiona = de facto director; Gordon = shadow director. (b) No — s.548. Model Answer (EN): (a) Fiona — de facto director. Although never validly appointed, she has 'assumed to act as a director': she is held out as a director (signing contracts as 'Director of PRL') and exercises top level management functions (negotiating with creditors, countersigning cheques) over a sustained three year period. Under the statutory definition, a director is 'any person occupying the position of director, by whatever name called' (s.2(1), CO); see also Re Hydrodan (Corby) Ltd [1994] BCC 161 (Millett J) and Deputy Commissioner of Taxation v Austin (1998) 28 ACSR 565 (occupation of the position of director is a question of degree). Consequence: Fiona is subject to the same duties (including fiduciary duties) as a validly appointed de jure director. Gordon — shadow director. He is a person in accordance with whose directions or instructions the directors (or a majority of them) are accustomed to act (s.2, CO). His instructions are given in a private, not professional, capacity, so the carve out for professional advice does not help him; see Re Unisoft Group Ltd (No. 2) [1994] BCC 766. Unlike a de facto director, a shadow director does not necessarily owe fiduciary duties to the company, though the CO imposes similar statutory duties on him. (b) No. Anything that may be done by ordinary or special resolution at a general meeting may be done by written resolution, except the removal of an auditor or a director before the expiry of the term of office (s.548, CO). Fiona's removal must therefore be effected by an ordinary resolution at a general meeting with special notice (s.462; s.462(4); s.578(1)), with a copy of the notice sent to her and her right to be heard respected (s.463). 解題思路（繁中）: (a) Fiona：未經任命但「做晒出嚟」——對外自稱 Director、行使最高管理職能、為期三年（唔係一次性幫手）。按 DCT v Austin，question of degree：length of time + breadth of activities 都指向 de facto director。呢個身份受 s.2(1) 嘅廣義定義覆蓋，所以 full directors' duties 上身。 Gordon：佢唔露面，但 Sam 同 Tina「accustomed to act」on his instructions —— textbook shadow director（s.2）。注意 carve out：如果佢係以 專業身份 （retired accountant 提供專業意見）俾 advice 就唔算；題目特登寫明「private capacity」就係封咗呢條出路。 伏位：Fiona 同 Gordon 容易對調 —— 記住「拋頭露面做嘢 = de facto；幕後發號施令 = shadow」。另外 shadow director 唔一定孭 fiduciary duties，de facto 就一定孭。 (b) 考 s.548 嘅例外：written resolution 萬能， 唯獨 罷免董事/核數師（任期屆滿前）唔用得。所以一定要返 GM + special notice 路線。 考試伏位：見到 unanimous shareholder agreement 就以為 written resolution 搞得掂 —— 罷免董事係法定例外，全體同意都冇用。 Rule Check: Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) s.2(1); s.2 (definition of shadow director); s.548; s.462; s.462(4); s.463; s.578(1); Re Hydrodan (Corby) Ltd [1994] BCC 161; Deputy Commissioner of Taxation v Austin (1998) 28 ACSR 565; Re Unisoft Group Ltd (No. 2) [1994] BCC 766. Common Trap（繁中）: (1) 將 de facto 同 shadow 撈亂 —— 前者靠 conduct/held out，後者靠 accustomed to act on instructions；(2) 以為專業人士必然豁免 shadow director 身份 —— 只有「advice given in a professional capacity」先豁免，意見一旦超越專業範疇就可能中招（LP Exam Practice Q1(a) 嘅 Andrew 正係咁）；(3) 忘記 s.548 例外，以為 written resolution 可以罷免董事。 Self study note: all section references are to the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) unless otherwise stated, consistent with the Learning Pack convention.

title: M10 Chapter 9: Internal Administration of a Company — Phase 3 Quiz
headings: M10 Chapter 9: Internal Administration of a Company — Phase 3 Quiz
excerpt: M10 Chapter 9: Internal Administration of a Company — Phase 3 Quiz Rules: Closed book · 15 minutes · 5 questions · Submit as 1. … 2. … 3. … 4. … 5. … — 超時如實申報 Q…
text: M10 Chapter 9: Internal Administration of a Company — Phase 3 Quiz Rules: Closed book · 15 minutes · 5 questions · Submit as 1. … 2. … 3. … 4. … 5. … — 超時如實申報 Q1. Harbour Bright Ltd is a private company limited by shares incorporated in Hong Kong. Its accounting reference period ended on 31 March 2025 . The directors ask you what is the latest date by which the company must hold its annual general meeting ('AGM') in respect of that financial year, assuming the AGM is not dispensed with under s.612 of the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) ('CO'). Which of the following is correct? A. 30 June 2025 B. 30 September 2025 C. 31 December 2025 D. 31 March 2026 Q2. The board of directors of Clear Water Trading Ltd, a private company, is planning the company's agenda and wishes to know which of the following matters requires a special resolution of the members under the CO. Which one is it? A. Re appointing the existing auditor at the AGM B. Changing the company's name C. Removing a director before the end of the director's term of office D. Appointing a person to fill a casual vacancy in the office of auditor Q3. Ivy and Ken hold 45% and 25% respectively of the voting shares in Golden Meadow Ltd, a private company. Leo holds the remaining 30% and is one of its three directors. Ivy and Ken wish to remove Leo from the board before the expiry of his term. They sent a notice to members on 1 May giving notice of a general meeting to be held on 15 May , at which an ordinary resolution to remove Leo was passed by 70% of the votes cast. No notice of the proposed resolution to remove Leo was given to the company or members in advance of the meeting notice, no copy of the notice was sent to Leo, and Leo was given no opportunity to make representations. Leo challenges the validity of his removal. Which of the following best states the position? A. The removal is valid: s.462 of the CO allows members to remove a director by ordinary resolution notwithstanding anything in the articles, and 70% is well above a simple majority. B. The removal is valid: under the irregularity principle, the intention of the majority was clear and the result would have been the same had the correct procedure been observed. C. The removal is prima facie invalid: a resolution to remove a director requires special notice of at least 28 days before the meeting (s.462(4) and s.578(1) of the CO), and Leo was denied his statutory right to receive a copy of the notice and to be heard and make representations (s.463), which goes beyond a mere informality. D. The removal is invalid: removing a director before the expiry of his term requires a special resolution supported by at least 75% of the votes cast. Q4. M & Co, a firm of certified public accountants (practising), has audited the financial statements of Jade Garden Restaurant Ltd for several years. During the latest audit, M & Co came across a number of altered purchase invoices which had the effect of inflating the company's reported profit. M & Co raised the matter with the managing director, Owen, who assured the engagement partner that the alterations were routine corrections of suppliers' errors. M & Co had always regarded Owen as a man of the highest integrity, accepted his explanation without further enquiry, and issued an unqualified auditor's report . The fraud was later discovered and the company went into liquidation. The liquidator sues M & Co for negligence. Which of the following best states the likely outcome? A. M & Co is not liable: an auditor is a watch dog but not a bloodhound, and was justified in relying on the managing director's certificates and assurances (Re Kingston Cotton Mill Co (No. 2) (1896) 2 Ch 279). B. M & Co is likely liable: having discovered the altered invoices, the auditors were put on enquiry and had a duty to make an exhaustive enquiry and to inform the board; they were not entitled to rest content with Owen's bare assurances (Re Thomas Gerrard & Son Ltd (1968) Ch 455). C. M & Co is not liable: an auditor is not an insurer and does not guarantee that the accounts correctly show the true position of the company's affairs (Re London and General Bank (No. 2) (1895) 2 Ch 673). D. M & Co is liable because it committed a criminal offence under s.408 of the CO by omitting a required statement from the auditor's report, and criminal liability automatically establishes civil liability. Q5. (Short answer — answer in no more than 120 words.) Pearl River Logistics Ltd ('PRL') is a private company with two formally appointed directors, Sam and Tina. Fiona has never been appointed as a director, but over the past three years she has negotiated settlements with PRL's creditors, countersigned company cheques, signed supply contracts describing herself as 'Director of PRL', and has been introduced to suppliers as the person running the company. Meanwhile, Sam and Tina have, on every major decision, acted strictly in accordance with the instructions of Fiona's husband, Gordon, who is a retired accountant giving the instructions in a private capacity. Answer the following: (a) Identify Fiona's and Gordon's respective status under the CO, citing the relevant statutory provision and/or case authority for each, and state one consequence that follows for Fiona. (b) Assuming Fiona is treated as a director, can the members of PRL remove her before the expiry of her term by way of a written resolution instead of holding a general meeting? Give the reason and the statutory basis. End of quiz. Do not look at the answers file until you have submitted your answers.
