text: M10 Chapter 10: Contentious Matters — Phase 1 速查表 + Phase 2 閃卡 Phase 1 速查表 Learning Objectives 1. Apply the rules on a company's contractual capacity and execution formalities (ss.121, 124–129, Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) ('CO')) and the indoor management rule (Royal British Bank v Turquand (1856) 119 ER 775; ss.117–119 CO) to decide whether a company is bound. 2. Analyse when the corporate veil may be lifted by statute (s.275, Companies (Winding Up and Miscellaneous Provisions) Ordinance (Cap. 32) ('CWUMPO')) or at common law (mere façade, evasion of legal obligations, fraud), applying Prest v Petrodel Resources Ltd (2013) UKSC 34, (2013) 2 AC 415. 3. Identify and apply directors' fiduciary duties (good faith, proper purposes, no conflict, no profit, no misappropriation) and the statutory duty of reasonable care, skill and diligence (s.465 CO). 4. Evaluate the company's remedies for breach of directors' duties, including avoidance, restitution, disgorgement of profits, equitable compensation and accessory liability (knowing receipt / dishonest assistance). 5. Distinguish and apply shareholders' remedies: the rule in Foss v Harbottle (1843) 2 Hare 461, common law and statutory derivative actions (ss.731–733 CO), unfair prejudice remedies (ss.724–725 CO), members' personal actions, and just and equitable winding up. 必背考點 A. Relevant Ordinances（以 LP 所引 section numbers 為準；除特別註明外均為 CO (Cap. 622)） Section Rule（考試必背） s.115 A company has the capacity and the rights, powers and privileges of a natural person — ultra vires doctrine abolished (Companies Ordinance 1997; memorandum abolished by the new CO 2012). s.121 How a company contracts: (2) contracts under seal / executed per s.127(3); (3) written contracts signed by a person with express or implied authority; (4) oral contracts by an authorised person. s.124(1), (2), (4) Common seal is OPTIONAL; if adopted, it must be a metallic seal with the company's name engraved legibly; non compliant use is an offence. s.125 / s.126 Official seal for executing documents outside Hong Kong (engraved with the place of use; binds as if common seal, s.125(6)); securities seal. s.127(3), (5), (6) Execution without seal: signed by two directors (or the sole director) or a director + company secretary, expressed to be executed by the company → deemed executed under seal (s.127(5)); good faith purchaser for value may rely on a document purporting to be signed per s.127(3) (s.127(6)). s.128(1), (2) / s.129 Deed: executed per s.127 + expressed as a deed + delivered as a deed (presumed delivered on execution, s.128(2)); attorney may execute deeds (s.129). ss.117–119 Codified indoor management rule: in favour of a person dealing with a company IN GOOD FAITH, the directors' power to bind the company is free of any limitation under any relevant document (s.117(1)); good faith presumed (s.117(2)(b)); knowledge alone of the limitation is NOT bad faith (s.117(2)(c)); no duty to enquire (s.117(2)(d)). s.461 Acts of a director remain valid despite a defective appointment or disqualification — but NOT for persons with notice of the defect (Morris v Kanssen (1946) AC 459). s.86 / s.86(2) Articles take effect as a contract under seal between the company and each member, and between members inter se. s.116 Member's right to restrain the company from acting outside its objects or powers as stipulated in the articles. ss.430, 739–743 Right to receive financial statements; right to inspect company records. s.465(1), (2), (5) Statutory duty of reasonable care, skill and diligence — mixed standard: (2)(a) objective (reasonably expected of a person carrying out that director's functions) + (2)(b) subjective (the knowledge, skill and experience THAT director has); applies to shadow directors (s.465(5)). ss.536, 538(1), (4) Director with a direct/indirect MATERIAL interest in a transaction with the company must declare its nature and extent to the other directors — at a board meeting or by written notice; a general notice for a category of contracts suffices. ss.500(1)–(2), 496, 505, 506, 511–515 Loans to directors (or their controlled bodies / holding company directors) require members' 'prescribed approval' (s.496); exceptions: loan ≤ 5% of net assets (s.505), expenditure for company purposes (s.506), ordinary course of business (s.511), intra group (s.512); breach → transaction voidable, account for gains, indemnify loss (ss.513–515). s.373(5)–(7) Strict liability offence: failure to take all reasonable steps to ensure proper accounting records are kept. s.731 'Misconduct' = fraud, negligence, breach of duty or default in compliance with any Ordinance or rule of law (wider than equitable fraud). s.732(1)–(3) Statutory derivative action (Division 4, Part 14): sue for misconduct against the company; sue where the company failed to sue because of misconduct; intervene where the company failed to diligently continue/discontinue/defend. s.733(1)(a)–(c) Leave of court required: (a) appears to be in the company's interests (LOW threshold); (b) serious question to be tried AND company has not brought proceedings; (c) member served written notice on the company of intention to apply. s.724(1) Unfair prejudice petition by a MEMBER: affairs conducted unfairly prejudicial to members generally or some members; or an actual or proposed act/omission is or would be prejudicial. s.725 Court may make ANY order it thinks fit: restrain conduct; order proceedings in the company's name; appoint receiver/manager; regulate future affairs; buy out order (member or company purchases shares); damages to a member (but reflective loss NOT recoverable). （註：LP 正文此處印作 "s.752"，對照條例及 Exam Lens (ss.723–727) 應為 s.725） s.275 CWUMPO (Cap. 32) Fraudulent trading — persons knowingly party to carrying on business with intent to defraud creditors are personally liable (statutory veil lifting). s.3 IGCO (Cap. 1); s.87 MO (Cap. 227) 'Persons' in criminal statutes includes a body corporate; procedural rules for prosecuting a corporation. B. Leading Cases（full citations as given in the LP） Contracting & Indoor Management Royal British Bank v Turquand (1856) 119 ER 775 — origin of the indoor management rule: outsiders in good faith may assume internal acts (e.g. authorising resolutions) were duly performed; no duty to inspect internal regularity. Northside Developments Pty Ltd v Registrar General (1990) 170 CLR 146 — rule covers three categories: (1) due appointments of directors/officers/agents; (2) conferral of authority; (3) satisfaction of conditions governing exercise of authority. Seal affixed → contract regarded as entered by the company directly. The rule presupposes actual/ostensible authority; it cannot CREATE authority (also Thanakharn Kasikorn Thai Chamkat v Akai Holdings Ltd (2010) 13 HKCFAR 479). Pacific Foundation Finance Ltd v Fairyoung Holdings Ltd (1999) 3 HKC 448 — rule unavailable to a party with actual or constructive notice of the irregularity. National Commercial Bank Ltd v Albert Hwang (2002) 2 HKLRD 408 — rule needs some act by the company suggesting the outsider was dealing with the company; a stranger impersonating a director does not bind the company. Exceptions: (1) actual/constructive notice of irregularity ( Morris v Kanssen (1946) AC 459 ; Wong Kam San v Yeung Wing Keung (2007) 2 HKLRD 267 — dramatic shareholding change put allottees on enquiry; Bank of East Asia v Labour Buildings (unrep.) HCMP 769/2002 — bank had notice, but company ADOPTED the loan); (2) forgery renders the document a nullity ( Ruben v Great Fingall Consolidated (1906) AC 439 ), unless the company held out the forger as authorised ( Lovett v Carson Country Homes Ltd (2009) 2 BCLC 196 ); (3) insiders cannot rely on the rule (Morris v Kanssen). Good Lion Ltd v Chung Sai Wing (2008) 6 HKC 443 — incorrect name on the seal does not invalidate execution if the seal was intended to be the company's. Corporate Liability (Attribution) Meridian Global Funds Management Asia Ltd v Securities Commission (1995) 2 AC 500 — three rules of attribution: primary (constitution/company law), general (agency), special (statutory interpretation — whose act/knowledge counts as the company's for that rule). 'Directing mind and will' is only a starting point, not the proper test. Tesco Supermarkets Ltd v Nattrass (1972) AC 153 / Tesco Stores Ltd v Brent LBC (1997) 1 WLR 1037 — directing mind normally = board or MD; a store manager is 'another person', not the company. R v Chung Yat (1978) HKLR 355 — company liable under Buildings Ordinance (Cap. 123) where directors/foreman acted with knowledge and recklessness. R v Gateway Foodmarkets Ltd (1997) IRLR 189 — statutory duty breached at store management level attributable to the company. Bilta (UK) Ltd v Nazir (No. 2) (2015) 2 WLR 1168 — where the company is the VICTIM of its directors' fraud, their wrongdoing is NOT attributed to the company as a defence to the company's claim against them. Moulin Global Eyecare Trading Ltd v Commissioner of Inland Revenue (2014) 17 HKCFAR 218 — contrast: directors' fraudulent knowledge WAS attributed to the company (to deny attribution would frustrate the tax statute). Chan Kit Man v Rayable Consultants Ltd and Ajax Engineers & Surveyors Ltd (1999) 2 HKLRD 577 — corporate manslaughter; company convicted, HK$3 million fine; attribution does not exclude the individual agent's own liability. Lifting the Corporate Veil Hashem v Shayif (2008) EWHC 2380 — seven principles: piercing rests on established principles (NOT mere 'interests of justice'); impropriety + control BOTH required; ownership/control alone insufficient; deceptive intent at incorporation unnecessary (façade at time of transaction suffices); pierce only so far as necessary. Prest v Petrodel Resources Ltd (2013) UKSC 34, (2013) 2 AC 415 — veil pierced only where a person under an EXISTING legal obligation/liability deliberately evades it by interposing a controlled company; pierce only for that purpose; only when other remedies are of no assistance. Gilford Motor Co v Horne (1933) 1 Ch 935 — company formed as a 'device or stratagem' to evade a restraint of trade covenant → veil lifted, injunction granted. Jones v Lipman (1962) 1 WLR 832 — vendor transferred land to his own company to escape specific performance → company a 'mask'; veil pierced, specific performance ordered. Lee Sow Keng v Kelly McKenzie Ltd (2004) 3 HKLRD 517 — shareholders diverted business/goodwill to a new same named company to defeat an employee's judgment debt → veils of BOTH companies pierced. Toptrans Ltd v Delta Resources Co Inc (2005) 1 HKLRD 635 — common control alone insufficient; 'shenanigans' must be shown; veil NOT lifted. Winland Enterprises Group Inc v Wex Pharmaceuticals Inc (2012) 2 HKLRD 757 — shared management/directors/staff within a group is irrelevant per se; illegitimate purpose must be PROVED. China Ocean Shipping Co v Mitrans Shipping Co (1995) 3 HKC 123 — no piercing where the company was incorporated BEFORE the obligation arose (evasion covers existing liabilities only). Re Darby (1911) 1 KB 95 — fraud: veil pierced so fraudsters behind a company bore promoters' fiduciary duties. Re FG (Films) Ltd (1953) 1 All ER 615 — agency analysis: a mere nominee/agent subsidiary — technically NOT veil piercing; separate entities maintained. Re Yung Kee Holdings Ltd (2014) 2 HKLRD 313 — separate legal entity maintained within a group; subsidiary's HK business ≠ sufficient connection to wind up the BVI parent. Directors' Duties Sources: rules of equity, CO, articles, employment contract, Listing Rules, Companies Registry Guide on Directors' Duties (non binding). Five fiduciary duties: (1) good faith in the interests of the company; (2) proper purposes; (3) no conflict; (4) no secret profits; (5) no misappropriation of company assets. Who owes: de jure directors (executive AND non executive) owe full duties; de facto directors owe duties insofar as they perform directors' functions; shadow directors do NOT automatically owe general fiduciary duties — only where circumstances justify, typically for the directions/instructions they give ( Vivendi SA v Richards (2013) BCC 771 ). Duties owed TO THE COMPANY, not shareholders/creditors — exceptions: special facts creating direct/close contact with shareholders ( Peskin v Anderson (2001) 1 BCLC 372 ); creditors' interests must be considered on insolvency, but the duty remains owed to the company ( Lonrho Ltd v Shell Petroleum Co Ltd (1980) WLR 627; Yukong Line Ltd of Korea v Rendsburg Investments Corp of Liberia (No. 2) (1998) 1 WLR 294 ). Re Smith & Fawcett Ltd (1942) Ch 304 — good faith duty is primarily SUBJECTIVE; but if no reasonable director could so regard the act, the court may reject the claimed honest belief (objective evidential check). Regentcrest Plc v Cohen (2001) 2 BCLC 80 — breach if the director (1) entirely fails to consider the company's interest or (2) takes irrelevant matters into account / omits relevant ones. Re Neath Rugby Ltd (No. 2), Hawkes v Cuddy (2009) 2 BCLC 427 — nominee directors owe duties to the COMPANY, not the nominator; may consider nominator's interests only if genuinely believing the decision is in the company's best interests. Tradepower (Holdings) Ltd v Tradepower (Hong Kong) Ltd (2009) 12 HKCFAR 417 — disposition of assets for no consideration when insolvent: breach; self ratification by wrongdoer shareholders ineffective where company insolvent/in serious difficulty. Tam Po Kei v Tam Bo Kin (No. 1) (2011) 1 HKLRD 537 — dividends paid without proper declaration → director liable to account. Howard Smith Ltd v Ampol Petroleum Ltd (1974) AC 821 — proper purposes: identify the SUBSTANTIAL/DOMINANT purpose; allotting shares primarily to dilute a shareholder and facilitate a takeover = improper. Wong Kam San v Yeung Wing Keung (2007) 2 HKLRD 267 — allotment whose substantial purpose is to destroy an existing majority or create a new one is unconstitutional and unlawful. Primlake Ltd v Matthews Associates (2007) 1 BCLC 666 — de facto director paying himself unjustified sums = improper purpose/self enrichment. Transvaal Lands Co v New Belgium (Transvaal) Land Development Co (1914) 2 Ch 488 — no conflict: even a small shareholding in the counterparty triggers disclosure; non disclosure → transaction voidable (even if commercially fair); abstaining from voting does NOT cure non disclosure. Man Luen Corp v Sun King Electronic Printed Circuitry Board Factory Ltd (1981) HKC 407 — disclosure to the BOARD alone insufficient where the articles/position require informed consent of MEMBERS in general meeting. Newgate Stud Co v Penfold (2008) 1 BCLC 46 — transactions with the director's close relatives/partnership require informed consent; strictly applied even if beneficial to the company. Boardman v Phipps (1967) 2 AC 46 — no profit rule: fiduciaRY liable to account for profits from opportunity/knowledge obtained in the fiduciary position (allowance for skill and work possible). Boston Deep Sea Fishing and Ice Co v Ansell (1888) 39 Ch D 339 — secret commissions/bribes must be accounted for even if the company could not itself have received them. Regal (Hastings) Ltd v Gulliver (1967) 2 AC 134 (HL) — directors liable to account for profits on shares subscribed via their directorship EVEN THOUGH the company could not have taken the opportunity and they acted in good faith throughout. Chinese United Establishments Ltd v Cheung Siu Ki (1997) 2 HKC 212 — opportunity arriving in a personal capacity can still breach the no conflict rule if there is an actual conflict. Bishopsgate Investment Management Ltd (in liquidation) v Maxwell (No. 2) (1994) 1 All ER 261 — giving away company assets for no consideration to a family company = prima facie improper purpose. Re City Equitable Fire Insurance Co Ltd (1925) Ch 407 — care/skill/diligence: intermittent duties; no liability for mere errors of judgment; justified in trusting officials absent grounds for suspicion. Dorchester Finance Co Ltd v Stebbing (1989) BCLC 498 — non executive directors liable: signing blank cheques and total non involvement = breach; delegation ≠ absolution from supervision. Law Wai Duen v Boldwin Construction Co Ltd (2001) 3 HKLRD 430 — executive and non executive directors bear the SAME duties; a 'technical' director cannot take a neutral role; right of inspection essential to performing duties. Brumder v Motornet Service and Repairs Ltd (2013) 3 All ER 412 — director cannot hide behind the company for his own failure to ensure regulatory compliance. Re Rontex Intl Holdings Ltd (unrep.) HCMP 1869/2008, 18 March 2010 — failure to carry out adequate due diligence before investments = breach of duty of care. Shareholders' Remedies Foss v Harbottle (1843) 2 Hare 461 — two limbs: (1) proper plaintiff principle (company sues for wrongs to itself; shareholders lack locus standi); (2) irregularity principle (no member action for an informality ratifiable by ordinary resolution of the majority). Common law derivative action grounds: (1) ultra vires or illegal conduct (e.g. unlawful return of capital against s.212 CO; unlawful financial assistance against s.275 CO); (2) fraud on the company / fraud on the minority (equitable fraud — covers breach of fiduciary duty even in good faith; negligence alone insufficient UNLESS directors profited; requires wrongdoer CONTROL preventing the company suing — deadlock suffices, no need for 50%+). Smith v Croft (No. 2) (1988) Ch 114 — minority has locus standi for ultra vires recovery, but the court considers the views of INDEPENDENT shareholders; action struck out where independent majority genuinely opposed it. Waddington Ltd v Chan Chun Hoo (2008) 11 HKCFAR 370 — plaintiff in a (multiple) derivative action must show a prima facie case that the company is entitled to relief AND that the action falls within a Foss v Harbottle exception (usually fraud on the minority); reflective loss objection rejected. Re Li Chung Shing Tong (Holdings) Ltd (2011) 5 HKLRD 274 — s.733 leave thresholds are LOW: prima facie in the company's interest + serious question to be tried; court slow to refuse unless prospects are hopeless. O'Neill v Phillips (1999) 1 WLR 1092 — unfairness ordinarily requires breach of the terms on which the member agreed the affairs would be conducted; mere breakdown of trust and confidence without exclusion from management ≠ right to a buy out. Re Ching Hing Construction Co Ltd (unrep.) HCCW 889/1999 — excessive director remuneration assessed by objective commercial criteria; equitable understandings can generate unfairness even if not legally enforceable. Rayfield v Hands (1960) Ch 1 — articles enforceable member v member (s.86); directors qua members ordered to buy the plaintiff's shares at fair value. Members' personal actions arise from: constitution (e.g. right to transfer shares, pre emption/class rights, proper notice, right to vote, exclude improper votes), common law (e.g. special resolution compliance, declared dividends, restrain improper dilution/alteration of articles), contract, and statute (s.116; ss.739–743; s.430; s.179 winding up petition as contributory — see Chapter 13 / CWUMPO (Cap. 32)). C. IRAC Application Points（答題框架） Issue 1: Is the company bound by the contract? Rule: s.121 CO (mode of contracting) → authority (actual/ostensible, agency law) → indoor management rule (Turquand; ss.117–119 CO) → exceptions (notice, forgery, insider; note s.117(2)(c) knowledge ≠ bad faith). Application: ask (1) was there actual/apparent authority at all (National Commercial Bank v Albert Hwang — the rule cannot create authority); (2) is the third party in good faith/put on enquiry (Wong Kam San); (3) any forgery (Ruben). Conclusion: bound / not bound; note company may still ADOPT the transaction (Bank of East Asia v Labour Buildings). Issue 2: Should the veil be pierced? Rule: separate legal entity is the default, even in groups (Yung Kee); pierce only for control + impropriety (Hashem v Shayif); evasion must be of an EXISTING obligation (Prest v Petrodel; China Ocean Shipping — timing!). Application: identify the specific existing obligation evaded / fraud perpetrated; check timing of incorporation; check whether remedies short of piercing suffice. Conclusion: pierce only so far as necessary for that wrong. Issue 3: Director in breach? Rule: identify duty (good faith — subjective test (Re Smith & Fawcett; Regentcrest); proper purpose — dominant purpose (Howard Smith); no conflict — s.536 disclosure; no profit (Regal (Hastings)); care/skill/diligence — s.465(2) mixed standard). Application: status of director (de jure / de facto / shadow — Vivendi); informed consent of members in general meeting cures conflict; company insolvent → creditors' interests (Tradepower). Conclusion: breach + company's remedies (avoidance (voidable; void if no authority), restitution/constructive trust, disgorgement, equitable compensation, accessory liability via knowing receipt / dishonest assistance, common law damages for duty of care only). Issue 4: What can the shareholder do? Rule: Foss v Harbottle two limbs → wrong to company = derivative action (common law grounds; or statutory ss.731–733 with s.733(1) leave + written notice); wrong to member personally = personal action (s.86 articles; statute); majority abuse prejudicing minority qua member = unfair prejudice s.724 → s.725 orders (buy out most common); breakdown/substratum lost = just and equitable winding up. Application: capacity! (member qua member, not employee/creditor); control by wrongdoers; alternative relief available? (court may strike out petition); reflective loss not recoverable. Conclusion: pick the remedy whose plaintiff, wrong and relief match the facts — exam 最常考 derivative action vs unfair prejudice 嘅揀擇。 易混淆概念對比 對比 1: Common Law Derivative Action vs Statutory Derivative Action vs Unfair Prejudice Petition 維度 Common Law Derivative Action Statutory Derivative Action (ss.731–733 CO) Unfair Prejudice Petition (ss.724–725 CO) Nature of wrong Wrong done TO THE COMPANY — only ultra vires/illegal conduct OR fraud on the company (equitable fraud; needs wrongdoer control) 'Misconduct' against the company = fraud, negligence, breach of duty or default in compliance with any Ordinance or rule of law (s.731) — WIDER, covers pure negligence Conduct of the company's affairs unfairly prejudicial to MEMBERS' interests qua members (or an actual/proposed prejudicial act/omission, s.724(1)) Whose claim / who benefits Company's cause of action; shareholder sues ON BEHALF of the company; recovery goes to the company Same — company's claim; relief goes to the company Member's OWN claim; relief benefits the member (e.g. buy out of his/her shares, damages to the member) Court gatekeeping No leave procedure, but court may strike out if a majority of INDEPENDENT members oppose (Smith v Croft (No. 2)) Leave of court mandatory: s.733(1)(a)–(c) — company's interest (low threshold), serious question to be tried, company has not sued, written notice served on the company No leave; but court may strike out if a readily available alternative relief (e.g. offer to buy shares) gives all the petitioner can reasonably expect Typical trigger facts Controlling directors loot the company and block board action Same, plus negligence based claims and intervention in pending proceedings (s.732(3)) Exclusion from management in a quasi partnership, excessive director remuneration, share dilution, long term no dividend policy 點樣分辨 / 考試伏位 Negligence ALONE is not 'fraud on the company' unless directors profited — 呢個係分界位 見到 negligence 或 statutory default → 行 statutory 路線；記住 leave + notice 係程序伏位；唔可以用嚟逼公司做日常商業決定或處理股東私人恩怨 受損必須係 qua member（員工/債權人身份受損唔計）；純粹 trust breakdown 而無 exclusion ≠ unfair prejudice (O'Neill v Phillips)；reflective loss 唔 recoverable 對比 2: Common Law Indoor Management Rule vs Codified Rule (ss.117–119 CO) 維度 Common Law Rule (Royal British Bank v Turquand (1856) 119 ER 775) Codified Rule (ss.117–119 CO) Protection Outsider in good faith may assume internal acts (resolutions, appointments, conferral of authority) were duly performed Directors' power to bind the company regarded as free of any limitation under any relevant document, in favour of a person dealing in good faith (s.117(1)) Effect of NOTICE of irregularity Rule FAILS if the outsider has actual or constructive notice (Morris v Kanssen; Wong Kam San) Knowledge alone that the act exceeds directors' powers ≠ bad faith (s.117(2)(c)); no duty to enquire (s.117(2)(d)) — wider protection Burden of proof Outsider effectively must show good faith and absence of notice Good faith PRESUMED unless the company proves the contrary (s.117(2)(b)) Prerequisites Presupposes actual or ostensible authority under normal agency principles — cannot create authority (National Commercial Bank v Albert Hwang) Applies where the transaction is entered by the board or an agent acting under the board's authority 點樣分辨 / 考試伏位 Forgery = nullity (Ruben v Great Fingall); insiders 唔可以用 考生常伏：以為知情的 third party 一定唔受保護 —— 普通法下係，但 s.117(2)(c) 下單純知情唔係 bad faith；答題時兩條路線都要行一次 Phase 2 閃卡 (exactly 8 cards) Card 1 Front: State the indoor management rule and its case origin. Name its three common law exceptions. Back: Persons dealing with a company in good faith may assume that acts within its constitution and powers have been properly and duly performed; they are not bound to enquire into internal regularity. Origin: Royal British Bank v Turquand (1856) 119 ER 775. Exceptions: (1) actual or constructive notice of the irregularity; (2) forgery (document is a nullity — Ruben v Great Fingall Consolidated (1906) AC 439); (3) insiders cannot rely on it (Morris v Kanssen (1946) AC 459). 💬 白話：同公司做嘢嘅外人，唔使揭開公司「房門」查佢內部手續辦妥未。但如果你本身知有問題、文件係偽冒、或者你係「自己人」，就唔受保護。 Card 2 Front: Under s.465(2) CO, what is the standard for a director's duty of care, skill and diligence? Back: Standard of a reasonably diligent person with BOTH: (a) objective element — the general knowledge, skill and experience reasonably expected of a person carrying out that director's functions; and (b) subjective element — the general knowledge, skill and experience that director actually has. Shadow directors are also caught (s.465(5)). Mere errors of judgment are NOT breaches (Re City Equitable Fire Insurance Co Ltd (1925) Ch 407); non executive and executive directors bear the same duties (Law Wai Duen v Boldwin Construction Co Ltd (2001) 3 HKLRD 430). 💬 白話：標準係「合理勤奮嘅人」做你個位應有嘅本事（客觀），再加你自己實際有嘅本事（主觀）—— 兩者取其高。所以會計師出身嘅 NED 會被要求高啲（Dorchester Finance）。 Card 3 Front: Why were the directors in Regal (Hastings) Ltd v Gulliver (1967) 2 AC 134 (HL) liable even though the company could not have taken the opportunity and they acted in good faith? Back: The no profit rule is STRICT: a director must not profit by reason of, or through an opportunity/knowledge resulting from, his/her position as director. Good faith, absence of loss to the company, and the company's inability to take the opportunity are ALL irrelevant. Purpose: to completely eliminate the possibility of abuse of the fiduciary position. Escape route: informed consent of the company in general meeting after full disclosure. 💬 白話：「公司都食唔到單生意，我自己食有咩問題？」—— 有問題。只要機會係因你董事身份而嚟，賺咗就要呕返出嚟（account of profits），善意都冇用。想安全食，先攞股東大會知情同意。 Card 4 Front: State the test for breach of the duty to exercise powers for proper purposes, with authority. Back: Rule: directors must exercise each power for the purpose for which it was conferred (ascertained from the articles). Test: if exercised for multiple purposes, breach occurs if the SUBSTANTIAL or DOMINANT purpose was improper (Howard Smith Ltd v Ampol Petroleum Ltd (1974) AC 821). Classic example: allotting shares primarily to dilute a shareholder / facilitate a takeover rather than to raise capital = improper (also Wong Kam San v Yeung Wing Keung (2007) 2 HKLRD 267 — allotment to destroy an existing majority is unconstitutional). 💬 白話：唔好問「董事有冇權配股」，要問「佢配股嘅主要目的係乜」。權力本身合法，目的唔正都係 breach。 Card 5 Front: State the two limbs of the rule in Foss v Harbottle (1843) 2 Hare 461. Back: Proper plaintiff principle: where a wrong is done to the company (e.g. directors' breach of duty), the company is the proper plaintiff; shareholders lack locus standi. Irregularity principle: a member cannot sue over a mere informality or irregularity that the majority can cure/ratify by ordinary resolution in general meeting. Main escape routes: derivative actions (common law: ultra vires/illegal conduct; fraud on the company) and statutory derivative action (ss.731–733 CO). 💬 白話：公司先係受害人，所以公司先係原告；小事大多數可以追認，法庭唔會管。多數派控制晒公司唔肯告自己？先輪到小股東用 derivative action 代公司出頭。 Card 6 Front: What must a member show to obtain leave of the court to bring a statutory derivative action under s.733(1) CO? Back: (a) Interest of the company: on the face of the application it appears to be in the company's interests that leave be granted — LOW threshold (s.733(1)(a); Re Li Chung Shing Tong (Holdings) Ltd (2011) 5 HKLRD 274). (b) Serious question to be tried — at least a probability of success, not certainty (s.733(1)(b)). (b) The company has not itself brought the proceedings. (c) The member has served WRITTEN NOTICE on the company of the intention to apply for leave (s.733(1)(c)). 💬 白話：四部曲 —— 對公司有利（表面睇落係就得）、有實質可審嘅問題、公司自己冇告、事先書面通知公司。門檻刻意設得低，但程序（notice）唔做得漏。 Card 7 Front: List the elements of an unfair prejudice claim under s.724(1) CO and the key orders available. Back: Elements: (1) the complaint concerns the company's AFFAIRS (widely interpreted); (2) it affects the member's interest QUA MEMBER; (3) the conduct is UNFAIR (assessed liberally but ordinarily requires breach of the agreed terms or inequitable reliance on strict legal powers — O'Neill v Phillips (1999) 1 WLR 1092); (4) it is PREJUDICIAL (injury/detriment, financial or otherwise); (5) assessed OBJECTIVELY (reasonable bystander). Orders (s.725): restrain the conduct; order proceedings in the company's name; appoint receiver/manager; regulate future affairs; BUY OUT of a member's shares (most common); damages (no reflective loss). 💬 白話：五個元素記「Affairs–Member–Unfair–Prejudice–Objective」。最關鍵伏位：受損要係股東身份受損，做員工/債主蝕底唔計；常見結局係多數派買走小股東啲股。 Card 8 Front: When will a court pierce the corporate veil at common law? (State the control + impropriety framework.) Back: Default: separate legal entity is maintained, even within groups (Re Yung Kee Holdings Ltd (2014) 2 HKLRD 313). Requirements (Hashem v Shayif (2008) EWHC 2380): (1) CONTROL of the company by the wrongdoer AND (2) IMPROPRIETY — use of the company as a façade to evade an EXISTING legal obligation or perpetrate fraud; both must be shown. Piercing only so far as necessary for that wrong, and only when other remedies fail (Prest v Petrodel Resources Ltd (2013) UKSC 34, (2013) 2 AC 415). Mere control / common management is insufficient (Toptrans; Winland); company formed before the obligation arose → no evasion (China Ocean Shipping Co v Mitrans Shipping Co (1995) 3 HKC 123). Statute: fraudulent trading — s.275 CWUMPO (Cap. 32). 💬 白話：「揭面紗」要有兩樣嘢齊：控制 + 不當目的（走數/呃人），而且要走嘅數必須係已經存在嘅法律責任。單憑「兩間公司同一班人」係唔夠嘅。 本章急救詞彙 EN Term 繁中白話 English Model Sentence Indoor management rule 外人善意假定公司內部手續辦妥，毋須查證 Under the indoor management rule in Royal British Bank v Turquand (1856) 119 ER 775, the bank was not bound to enquire whether the authorising resolution had been passed. Corporate veil 隔開公司同股東嘅法律面紗，權責分開 The court will only pierce the corporate veil where control and impropriety are both established. Rules of attribution 決定邊個人嘅行為/知識當作公司嘅行為/知識 Under the rules of attribution in Meridian Global Funds Management Asia Ltd v Securities Commission (1995) 2 AC 500, the officer's knowledge was attributed to the company. Fiduciary duty 董事對公司嘅忠誠義務，公司利益放喺個人利益之上 By diverting the contract to his own company, the director breached his fiduciary duty of loyalty. Proper plaintiff principle 公司受害，公司先係合適原告 Under the proper plaintiff principle in Foss v Harbottle (1843) 2 Hare 461, the minority shareholder had no locus standi to sue for the wrong done to the company. Derivative action 股東代公司興訟，訴訟利益歸公司 The member applied for leave under s.733 of the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) to commence a statutory derivative action on behalf of the company. Unfair prejudice remedy 公司事務以不公平損害股東利益嘅方式進行時，股東可申請嘅濟助 The petitioner's exclusion from management of the quasi partnership was unfairly prejudicial, and the court ordered a buy out of his shares under s.725 of the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622). Buy out order 法院命令一方（多數派或公司）以公平價買走另一方股份 A buy out order is the most common relief where the relationship between the shareholders has irretrievably broken down.

title: M10 Chapter 10: Contentious Matters — Phase 3 Answers
headings: M10 Chapter 10: Contentious Matters — Phase 3 Answers
Q1 — Answer: The proper plaintiff principle and the irregularity principle; a derivative action
excerpt: M10 Chapter 10: Contentious Matters — Phase 3 Answers Q1 — Answer: The proper plaintiff principle and the irregularity principle; a derivative action Model Answ…
text: M10 Chapter 10: Contentious Matters — Phase 3 Answers Q1 — Answer: The proper plaintiff principle and the irregularity principle; a derivative action Model Answer (EN): The rule in Foss v Harbottle (1843) 2 Hare 461 has two limbs: 1. Proper plaintiff principle — where a wrong is done to the company (e.g. a breach of directors' duties owed to the company), the proper plaintiff to sue is the company itself; shareholders have no locus standi to sue for the company's loss. 2. Irregularity principle — a member is not entitled to sue over a mere informality or irregularity that can be cured by a vote of the company in general meeting where the intention of the majority is clear, because the majority could simply ratify it by ordinary resolution. Where the wrongdoers control the company and prevent it from suing, a member may bring a derivative action on the company's behalf — at common law for (i) ultra vires or illegal conduct or (ii) fraud on the company (equitable fraud, requiring wrongdoer control), or under statute (ss.732–733 CO, with leave of the court). 解題思路（繁中）: 呢題係基本 framework recall。記住兩個 limb 缺一不可：一個講「邊個告」（proper plaintiff），一個講「小事唔使告」（irregularity）。伏位係將 derivative action 同 unfair prejudice 混淆 —— derivative action 係代公司告、利益歸公司；unfair prejudice 係股東自己嘅 claim。如果答案只寫「company should sue」而冇講 irregularity limb，會蝕分。 Rule Check: Foss v Harbottle (1843) 2 Hare 461; Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) ss.731–733 Common Trap（繁中）: 考生常答「fraud on the minority」就當係例外而冇交代 control 元素；LP 明言 negligence alone 唔算 fraud on the company，除非董事從中獲利 —— 呢個 nuance 係區分高分低分嘅位。 Q2 — Answer: B Model Answer (EN): Section 117 of the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) codifies the indoor management rule: under s.117(1), in favour of a person dealing with a company in good faith, the power of the company's directors to bind the company, or authorise others to do so, is regarded as free of any limitation under any relevant document of the company. Good faith is presumed (s.117(2)(b)); knowledge of the limitation alone is not bad faith (s.117(2)(c)); and the outsider need not enquire (s.117(2)(d)). Beacon Bank dealt with Marble Ltd in good faith, so the facility binds Marble Ltd despite the missing ordinary resolution. 解題思路（繁中）: Pinpoint section 題，開卷考試都會考你搵唔搵到正確條文。 A (s.115) 錯：s.115 係講公司擁有自然人的 capacity and rights, powers and privileges（廢除 ultra vires 後嘅能力條文），同董事權限限制無關。 B (s.117) 啱：codified indoor management rule，同普通法 Turquand 規則並行。 C (s.124) 錯：s.124 係 common seal（而家係 optional），係簽立形式問題，唔係內部管理規則。 D (s.461) 錯：s.461 係話董事任命有瑕疵或唔合資格時，其行為仍然有效 —— 係另一條保護外人嘅條文，但唔係 codified indoor management rule。 考試伏位：普通法下如有 actual/constructive notice 就唔受保護（Wong Kam San v Yeung Wing Keung (2007) 2 HKLRD 267），但 s.117(2)(c) 話單純知情唔算 bad faith —— 兩條路線嘅差異係常見陷阱。 Rule Check: Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) s.117(1), s.117(2)(b)–(d); Royal British Bank v Turquand (1856) 119 ER 775 Common Trap（繁中）: 唔好將 s.117 同 s.461 撈亂：s.117 處理董事權限受章程/決議限制嘅情況；s.461 處理董事任命本身有瑕疵嘅情況。事實唔同、條文唔同。 Q3 — Answer: A Model Answer (EN): The court is likely to pierce the corporate veil. Piercing requires both control of the company by the wrongdoer and impropriety connected to the use of the company structure to avoid or conceal liability (Hashem v Shayif (2008) EWHC 2380). A person under an existing legal obligation who deliberately evades it by interposing a company under his control may have the veil pierced for that purpose (Prest v Petrodel Resources Ltd (2013) UKSC 34, (2013) 2 AC 415). Here, Harvest's judgment debt to Pearl Ltd already existed; Kelvin then formed Frost, transferred the business, goodwill and assets for HK$1, and stripped Harvest of assets precisely to frustrate enforcement. As in Lee Sow Keng v Kelly McKenzie Ltd (2004) 3 HKLRD 517 (and Jones v Lipman (1962) 1 WLR 832), the corporate veil should be pierced and Frost and Kelvin made liable for the judgment debt. 解題思路（繁中）: IRAC: Issue = veil piercing；Rule = control + impropriety，evasion 必須針對 existing obligation；Application = judgment 已存在先成立 Frost、HK$1 象徵式轉讓、故意令 Harvest 無資產；Conclusion = pierce。 B 錯：Hashem v Shayif 第 5 點講明公司唔使一開始就有欺騙意圖，重點係做交易嗰陣係咪被當 façade 用。 C 錯：呢句本身係真（Toptrans：common control 唔夠），但佢唔係答案 —— 因為本案唔單止有 control，仲有 impropriety（逃避現存 judgment debt），兩個元素齊晒。 D 錯：impropriety 嘅範圍闊過刑事罪行，evasion of existing legal obligations 已經足夠（Prest v Petrodel）。 考試伏位：如果事實改成「公司喺債務產生之前成立」，就會變 China Ocean Shipping Co v Mitrans Shipping Co (1995) 3 HKC 123 —— 唔 pierce。Timing 係呢類題嘅分水嶺。 Rule Check: Prest v Petrodel Resources Ltd (2013) UKSC 34, (2013) 2 AC 415; Lee Sow Keng v Kelly McKenzie Ltd (2004) 3 HKLRD 517; Hashem v Shayif (2008) EWHC 2380; cf. Toptrans Ltd v Delta Resources Co Inc (2005) 1 HKLRD 635 Common Trap（繁中）: 最大陷阱係 C —— 佢陳述嘅法律原則正確，考生一見「control alone is insufficient」就揀，但題目問嘅係邊句反映本案法律位置；本案事實已超越 mere control（有故意走數嘅 impropriety），所以 C 唔係 best answer。答 MCQ 要睇「邊句 apply 到事實」，唔係「邊句本身啱」。 Q4 — Answer: C Model Answer (EN): Doris is liable to account to Summit for the profits. Under the no profit rule (part of the no conflict rule), a director must not obtain any benefit or gain by reason of, or through an opportunity or knowledge resulting from, his/her position as director. The rule is strict: liability arises even if the director acted in good faith, even if the company suffered no loss, and even if the company could not have taken up the opportunity itself (Regal (Hastings) Ltd v Gulliver (1967) 2 AC 134 (HL); Boston Deep Sea Fishing and Ice Co v Ansell (1888) 39 Ch D 339). The lease offer came to Doris in her capacity as a director of Summit, and she never obtained the informed consent of the company in general meeting. She must therefore disgorge the profits (subject to any allowance for skill and work). 解題思路（繁中）: IRAC: Issue = diversion of corporate opportunity / secret profit；Rule = no profit rule (Regal (Hastings))；Application = 機會以董事身份送上門、冇喺股東大會披露兼攞 informed consent；Conclusion = account of profits。 A 錯：公司冇能力承接唔係辯護 —— Regal (Hastings) 正正係咁判。 B 錯：good faith 唔係辯護；no profit rule 嚴格到連善意都唔使考慮。 C 啱：directorship → opportunity → no informed consent → liable to account。 D 錯：呢個唔係 s.465 duty of care 問題（冇疏忽大意嘅成分），而係 fiduciary no conflict/no profit 問題；remedy 係 disgorgement of profits，唔係 common law damages for loss（common law compensation 只適用於 breach of duty of care）。 考試伏位：如果 Doris 事先喺 general meeting 全面披露兼獲批准，就可以合法把握機會；另外 LP 話機會喺公司業務範圍以外、而且唔係因董事身份得知，先可能免責（Chinese United Establishments Ltd v Cheung Siu Ki (1997) 2 HKC 212 顯示就算 personal capacity 得知，有 actual conflict 一樣中）。 Rule Check: Regal (Hastings) Ltd v Gulliver (1967) 2 AC 134 (HL); Boardman v Phipps (1967) 2 AC 46; Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) s.536 (disclosure duty) Common Trap（繁中）: 考生最易畀「board genuinely declined」呃到，以為公司拒絕咗董事就可以接。錯 —— 董事會拒絕 ≠ 股東知情同意；LP 明言要 informed consent of the company in general meeting。記住「公司唔要」唔等於「你可以要」。 Q5 — Answer: A Model Answer (EN): The petition is likely to fail. Under s.724(1) of the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622), the unfair prejudice remedy protects a member's interests in his/her capacity AS A MEMBER. Where a member has dual roles (e.g. employee, director, creditor), he/she cannot rely on the remedy for conduct affecting his/her interests in those other capacities. Here the dismissal only prejudices Marcus qua employee (loss of salary); his rights qua member — voting rights, dividends, share value — are untouched, and Nova is a purely commercial company with no quasi partnership understanding that Marcus would participate in management. His remedy, if any, lies in an employment claim, not an unfair prejudice petition. 解題思路（繁中）: IRAC: Issue = unfair prejudice capacity 問題；Rule = s.724(1) 要求 prejudice to interests qua member；Application = Nova 係純商業公司、冇參與管理嘅共同理解、股東權益零受損；Conclusion = petition 失敗，應行 employment law 路線。 A 啱：qua member / qua employee 嘅分界係 s.724 嘅核心限制。 B 錯：wrongful exclusion from management 係 unfairly prejudicial 只適用於 quasi partnership（基於 trust and confidence 嘅公司）；Nova 係商業公司，而且 Marcus 從來冇管理參與權。O'Neill v Phillips (1999) 1 WLR 1092 亦話單純 trust breakdown 唔夠。 C 錯：s.724 冇任何最低持股門檻 —— 呢個係捏造嘅 distractor。 D 錯：derivative action 係代公司追討對公司嘅 misconduct；解僱 Marcus 唔係對 Nova 嘅 wrong，而且 Marcus 嘅損失係佢自己嘅 —— 完全走錯路線。 考試伏位：Panelists 多次批評考生 issue spotting 失敗。見到股東受委屈唔好即刻寫 unfair prejudice —— 先問「佢邊個身份蝕底？」同「公司性質係咪 quasi partnership？」。 Rule Check: Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) s.724(1); O'Neill v Phillips (1999) 1 WLR 1092; cf. Re Ching Hing Construction Co Ltd (unrep.) HCCW 889/1999 Common Trap（繁中）: 兩個常見錯：(1) 以為 unfair prejudice 係「股東唔開心就告得」—— 其實要影響 member qua member 嘅利益；(2) 將 quasi partnership 嘅 exclusion from management 原則亂套落普通商業公司。答題第一句應該先界定受損利益嘅 capacity。

excerpt: M10 Chapter 10: Contentious Matters — Phase 3 Quiz Rules: Closed book · 15 minutes · 5 questions · Submit as 1. … 2. … 3. … 4. … 5. … — 超時如實申報 Q1. (Short answer…
text: M10 Chapter 10: Contentious Matters — Phase 3 Quiz Rules: Closed book · 15 minutes · 5 questions · Submit as 1. … 2. … 3. … 4. … 5. … — 超時如實申報 Q1. (Short answer) State the TWO limbs of the rule in Foss v Harbottle (1843) 2 Hare 461, and name the type of action by which a member may nevertheless sue on the company's behalf where the wrongdoers control the company. Q2. (MCQ) Beacon Bank lends HK$8 million to Marble Ltd. The facility agreement is signed by two directors of Marble Ltd. Unknown to Beacon Bank, Marble Ltd's articles prohibit the directors from approving any borrowing above HK$2 million without an ordinary resolution of the members, and no such resolution was passed. Beacon Bank knew nothing of the restriction. Which section of the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) codifies the indoor management rule so that, in favour of a person dealing with a company in good faith, the power of the company's directors to bind the company is regarded as free of any limitation under any relevant document of the company? A. Section 115 B. Section 117 C. Section 124 D. Section 461 Q3. (MCQ) Kelvin is the sole director and 95% shareholder of Harvest Logistics Ltd ('Harvest'), which operates a cold storage business. Harvest loses a breach of contract claim brought by a former customer, Pearl Ltd, and judgment is entered against Harvest for HK$2.4 million. One week after judgment, Kelvin incorporates Frost Logistics Ltd ('Frost'), of which he is also the sole director and shareholder. He transfers Harvest's customer contracts, refrigerated trucks and goodwill to Frost for HK$1, deliberately leaves Harvest with no assets, and instructs Harvest's solicitors not to defend any enforcement proceedings. Pearl Ltd now seeks to enforce its judgment against Frost and Kelvin. Which statement BEST reflects the legal position? A. The court is likely to pierce the corporate veil because Frost was interposed as a façade to evade Harvest's existing legal obligation to Pearl Ltd. B. The court cannot pierce the corporate veil because Frost was not incorporated with any deceptive intent at the time of its incorporation. C. The court cannot pierce the corporate veil because Kelvin's control of both companies is, by itself, never a sufficient ground to disregard separate legal personality. D. The court cannot pierce the corporate veil because veil piercing requires proof of conduct punishable as a criminal offence, and no crime has been committed. Q4. (MCQ) Doris is a director of Summit Retail Ltd ('Summit'), which operates a chain of gift shops. The landlord of a prime shop premises approaches Doris in her capacity as a director and offers Summit a five year lease at a below market rent. The Summit board genuinely declines the offer because the company lacks the funds to refurbish the premises. Doris then forms her own company, takes up the lease through it, and earns substantial profits. Doris acted honestly throughout, believed Summit could not have taken up the lease, and never disclosed her actions to the members in general meeting. Summit's new management discovers the facts and sues Doris. Which statement is CORRECT? A. Doris is not liable because Summit could not itself have taken up the lease, so Summit suffered no loss. B. Doris is not liable because she honestly believed that taking the lease was not harmful to Summit. C. Doris is liable to account to Summit for the profits because the opportunity came to her by reason of her position as a director, and good faith and the company's inability to take the opportunity are irrelevant. D. Doris is liable only for breach of the statutory duty of care, skill and diligence under s.465 of the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622), and Summit may recover damages for its loss. Q5. (MCQ) Marcus holds 20% of the shares of Nova Components Ltd ('Nova'), a purely commercial electronics distributor with twelve unrelated shareholders. Marcus is also employed by Nova as its warehouse manager, but he has never been a director and there has never been any understanding that he would participate in management. Following a dispute with the majority shareholders, Nova summarily dismisses Marcus from his employment, cutting off his salary. His shares continue to carry full voting rights, dividends are declared as usual, and the value of his shares is unaffected. Marcus petitions the court under s.724 of the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622), complaining that the dismissal is unfairly prejudicial to his interests. Which statement BEST reflects the likely outcome? A. The petition is likely to fail because the dismissal prejudices Marcus in his capacity as an employee, not in his capacity as a member of Nova. B. The petition is likely to succeed because any wrongful exclusion of a person associated with the company from its operations is automatically unfairly prejudicial. C. The petition is likely to fail because unfair prejudice relief is only available where the petitioner holds at least 25% of the voting shares. D. Marcus must instead bring a statutory derivative action under ss.732–733 of the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622), because dismissal of an employee is misconduct committed against the company.

text: M10 Chapter 11: Company Capital and Financing Companies — Phase 1 速查表 + Phase 2 閃卡 Phase 1 速查表 Learning Objectives 1. Compare and contrast the different classes of share capital and the different rights held by shareholders and debenture holders. 2. Analyse the legal implications of raising loan capital, including types of debentures, company charges and the registration of charges under the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) ("CO"). 3. Apply the common law rules on priority between competing fixed and floating charges in the event of receivership and winding up. 4. Explain and apply the doctrine of capital maintenance, including reduction of capital, redemption/buy back of shares, financial assistance and distributions of dividends. 5. Advise on the procedures for the issue, transfer and variation of class rights of shares. 以下所有 "s." 條文引用，除特別註明外，均指 Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622)。 必背考點 A. Debt Financing vs Equity Financing（法律層面 4 大分別） Repayment obligation ：debt 有固定還款義務（principal + interest），與公司業績無關；equity 無固定還款期，capital 被鎖定，只在 liquidation、permitted reduction of capital 或 share re purchase 時退回 → share capital 又稱 risk capital 。 Control ：equity investor 成為 member 有股東權；debt investor 仍是 outsider（loan documents 可給予有限控制，如 nominee director 或委任 receiver）。 Costs ：debt financing 一般成本較低。 Gearing ratio = total debt / total equity，反映 credit worthiness。 公司越過章程借款上限，貸款 仍然有效 （ss.116–117）。 B. Debentures（Ordinances + 分類） Definition ：s.307 — debenture 包括 bonds 及任何其他 debt securities，不論是否構成對公司資產的 charge。 Register of debenture holders ：發行 a series of debentures 或 debenture stock 時須備存（s.308(2) 列明內容：holder 姓名地址職業、持有數額、登記及終止日期）； single debenture（如普通銀行貸款）不適用 。開放查閱：members 及 debenture holders 免費每日至少 2 小時，其他人付費（s.310）。 Allotment registration ：allotment of debentures / debenture stock 須於配發後 1 個月內 向 Companies Registry 登記（s.316）——不涵蓋 single debenture。 Transfer ：必須有 instrument of transfer 方可登記（s.320）；登記須於 instrument 交付後 2 個月內 完成（s.321）； 無 stamp duty ；死亡/破產/法律施行而轉移（transmission）不需 instrument（s.320(2)）。 Private company 不得邀請公眾認購其 debentures 或 shares（s.11(1)）。 Types ：(1) redeemable / irredeemable（s.327 容許 irredeemable；s.328 容許 reissue redeemed debentures）；(2) convertible — 發行可換股 debenture 須先獲 members 批准（s.140(1)(b)）；(3) debenture stock（可拆細發行予不同認購人，各持有人 rank equally）；(4) bearer debenture（交付文件即轉讓）。 C. Types of Security Mortgage ：legal title 轉移予 mortgagee；mortgagor 保留 equity of redemption ；只有協議無轉讓 = equitable mortgage。Mortgagee 於 default 時可 (1) 接管及出售（普通法 + Conveyancing and Property Ordinance (Cap. 219) s.51 & Schedule 4，只適用於土地）；(2) foreclosure （消滅 equity of redemption 及債務）。 Charge ： 不轉移 title ，chargee 只取得 equitable proprietary interest；default 時向法院申請 power of sale（可明示或依普通法產生）。 Pledge ：possessory security，轉移 possession 而非 ownership； pledgee 無 foreclosure 權 。 Guarantee = personal security（與 real security 相對）。 D. Fixed vs Floating Charges（核心考點） Re Yorkshire Woolcombers Association （Romer LJ）三大 floating charge 特徵： 1. charge 針對一 類 present and future 資產； 2. 該類資產在 ordinary course of business 中不時變動； 3. 在 chargee 採取行動前，公司可在日常業務中自由處理該類資產。 Crystallisation （floating → fixed）觸發事件： 法院作出 compulsory winding up order（ 僅提交 petition 或委任 provisional liquidator 不算 ）； 公司通過 voluntary winding up resolution； chargee 委任 receiver（不影響其他 chargee 的 floating charges）； 雙方約定事件，如 default、其他 floating charge crystallised、chargee 發出轉換通知。 Automatic crystallisation clause ：對後設 chargee 的效力取決於其是否 notice ；因 s.334 要求登記設立 charge 的 instrument，已登記 floating charge 可引發 constructive notice 。 Negative pledge clause 違反常觸發自動結晶（Cox v Dublin City Distillery (No. 2) (1915) IR 345）。 Romalpa clause / retention of title clause ：Aluminium Industrie Vaassen BV v Romalpa Aluminium Ltd (1976) WLR 676 — 賣方保留貨物 title 直至付清價款，可及於製成品或出售收益，效果等同 floating charge。 E. Registration of Charges（伏位密集） Specified charges（s.334 清單） ：(1) uncalled share capital；(2) 如由自然人簽立須登記為 bill of sale 的文書所設/證明的 charge；(3) land 或其權益；(4) book debts；(5) goodwill 或 intellectual property；(6) floating charge。就登記而言 charge 包括 mortgage （s.333(1)）；pledge、lien 不需登記 。 程序（s.335(1)） ：向 Registrar 交付 (1) specified form 的 particulars 陳述 + (2) 設立/證明 charge 文書的 certified copy。 期限 ：charge 設立後 1 個月內 （由設立翌日起計）（s.335(5)(a)）。 後果 ：逾期不登記 → charge 對 liquidator 及 creditors 無效（void） （s.337(4)），但在 chargee 與公司之間 仍然有效 ，對 unsecured creditor 及買方亦然；公司及其 responsible persons 負 刑事責任 （s.337(2)）。 延期 ：法院可因 accidental / inadvertence / sufficient cause、不損害 creditors/members 且 just and equitable 而延長期限（s.346(3)）；獲准延期則無刑事責任（s.346(4)）。 公司自身 register of charges ：範圍更闊—— 所有 fixed 及 floating charges 均須登記（s.352(2)）；不登記不影響效力但有刑事責任（s.352(3)）；members 及 creditors 付費可查閱（s.355）。 Non Hong Kong companies ：就其在香港財產設立的 specified charges 同樣須登記，程序相同（s.336）；不登記同樣 void + 刑事責任（s.337）。 F. Priority Between Competing Charges（普通法規則；登記本身不賦予優先權） Real property（土地） ：另須按 Land Registration Ordinance (Cap. 128) ("LRO") 登記；規則見 LRO ss.2A, 3, 5 — 基本機制：1 個月內登記 → first in time 優先；其一逾期 → 如期登記者優先；兩者均逾期 → 按登記日期（s.3(1)）；第一 charge 未登記而第二 chargee 是 bona fide purchaser for value without notice → 第一 charge 對其 void（s.3(2)）；均未登記 → 普通法。 Personal property ： 1. Fixed vs Fixed ：first in time prevails（Re Weniger's Policy (1910) 2 Ch 291 — 另有 further advance 時須查詢有否收到其他 charge 的 notice，否則優先權被押後）。 2. Floating vs Floating ：一般 first in time；但第一份 floating charge 保留權力可設立優先的後續 floating charge（Re Benjamin Cope & Sons Ltd (1914) 1 Ch 800 — 訂明 "rank pari passu" 亦不能推翻先設立者的優先）；可用 subordination agreement 調整。 3. Fixed vs Floating ： fixed 一般優先 （Wheatley v Silkstone and Haigh Moor Coal Co (1885) 29 Ch 715）；但若 floating charge 在後設 fixed charge 之前已 crystallised ，則結晶後的 charge 優先。 Debts / choses in action ：以 notice 定優先——第一個向 debtor 發出 charge 通知的 chargee 優先。 Winding up 分配次序 ：fixed chargee 取 proceeds（扣除變現成本、receiver 報酬等）→ 餘額給 general creditors → members；floating chargee 之前還要先滿足 preferential creditors （僱員欠款、政府法定債項）。Unsecured creditor 排最後，資產不足時按 pari passu 比例分配。 G. Share Capital Authorised capital 已廢除 ——無上限。 類型： issued capital （已發行 × 發行價）； paid up / unpaid ； called up （paid up + 已催繳未付）/ uncalled 。 Class rights ：同類股份權利須完全一致（s.178(1)）；variation 受 ss.176–184 規管： 默認規則（章程無規定時）：holders 至少 75% total voting rights 書面同意 （s.180(1)） 或 在 class meeting 通過 special resolution （s.180(3)）； variation 後 14 日內書面通知該類股東（s.181）；1 個月內向 Registrar 提交通知（含 statement of capital）及決議副本（s.184）； 持不少於 10% 該類投票權的持有人可向法院申請 disallow variation；法院信納 variation unfairly prejudice 申請人所代表的 members 時可推翻（s.182(1), (5)）。 White v Bristol Aeroplane Co Ltd (1953) Ch 65 (CA) ：發行與現有股份 rank pari passu 的新股，只影響既有股東權利的 enjoyment ， 不是 variation of class rights ，無需 class consent。 Issue of shares ：創辦成員股份視為於註冊日發行（s.112）；其後發行 = allotment ，章程無限制則數量不限（s.85(2)）； non pro rata allotment 須 members 在 general meeting 事先批准， ordinary resolution 即可 （ss.140–141）；程序：subscription contract → (non pro rata 時股東批准) → board 批准及發股證 → 2 個月內 登記入 register of members（s.143；登記才成為 member，s.2）→ 1 個月內 向 Registrar 提交 return of allotment（s.142）。 Transfer of shares ：sale & purchase contract → instrument of transfer 連同舊股證交公司批准（s.150）→ contract notes + ad valorem stamp duty 各 0.1% （以代價或股份價值較高者計，Stamp Duty Ordinance (Cap. 117) s.19(1)）→ 董事批准登記並更新 register of members（s.627）→ 註銷舊證發新證（s.155）。 Transmission （死亡/破產/法院 vesting order）屬法律施行轉移。 Register of members （s.627 內容）；可電子形式（s.655）；須存於 registered office 或香港其他地方（s.628）；前成員記錄保存 10 年 （s.627(5)）。 Share certificate 在無相反證據時是 title 的證明（s.137），但真正 title 以 register of members 為準（s.2）。 H. Doctrine of Capital Maintenance 及其四大禁制與例外 普通法原則：share capital 不得退回股東（winding up 除外），因為 creditors 依賴公司已繳資本作為信用基礎。四大禁制： 1. Reduction of share capital → 只可循兩途：(a) special resolution + solvency statement （Sub division 2 of Division 3 of Part 5）；(b) special resolution 經法院確認 （Sub division 3 of Division 3 of Part 5；s.226）。Solvency statement 由 全體董事 作出（s.220）；solvency test 見 s.205（能償還 12 個月內到期債務）。法院考慮：股東獲公平對待、方案已妥善解釋、creditors 利益受保障、有可辨識目的。 Re Fok Ying Tung Ming Yuan Development Co Ltd (2016) 2 HKLRD 292 ：法院以資產負債表上的 share capital 為準；公司有巨額 accumulated loss 卻描述為無虧損屬誤導，且核數師發出 disclaimer → 拒絕確認。 2. Self acquisition of shares → s.267 禁止；例外： Redeemable shares ：s.234(1) 容許發行（章程可禁止/限制，s.234(2)）； 不得只有 redeemable shares （s.234(3)）；只限 fully paid 股份方可 redeem/buy back（s.268）；redemption 後股份視為註銷（s.269(1)）；資金來源：distributable profits / 為此目的新發行股份所得 / 依 Sub division 6 of Division 4 of Part 5 動用 capital。 Buy back（unlisted company） ：合約須事先經 special resolution 批准（s.244）。若以 share capital 支付：special resolution 批准 + 付款須在決議後第 5 至第 7 週之間 （s.258）；董事作出 solvency statement 並向全體 members 提供， special resolution 須在 solvency statement 日期後 15 日內通過 （s.259）。 3. Financial assistance for acquisition of shares → 禁止公司 直接或間接 資助他人收購本公司股份（收購前或當時），包括 子公司資助收購控股公司股份 （s.275(1)）。"Financial assistance" 定義廣：gift、guarantee/security/indemnity/release/waiver、loan、或令 net assets 重大減少的其他資助（s.274(1)）。違反有 刑事責任 （s.275(4)），但交易本身 不因此當然無效 （s.276，仍可因董事違反 fiduciary duties 等其他理由被撤銷）。 例外（ss.277–289） ： 全體董事作 solvency statement + (i) 資助 ≤ 5% paid up capital ，或 (ii) 全體股東一致同意 ，或 (iii) ordinary resolution 通過（ss.283–285）； principal purpose exception ：資助並非交易主要目的，只是附帶於公司某更大目的，且真誠為公司利益而給予（s.278）； 法院命令。 Ricco (Int'l) Co Ltd v Uni Harvest Int'l Ltd (2017) 6 HKC 487 ：須區分 "a purpose" 與 "the reason why a purpose was formed"——業務擴展只是配股的 reason ，不是可开脫的 larger purpose ；10 年延誤本身（無 prejudice）不阻礙救濟。 Carney v Herbert (1985) AC 301 ：子公司 mortgage 構成非法 financial assistance，但非法部分可 sever ——personal guarantee 仍然可執行。 4. Dividends other than out of profits → distribution 只可從 profits available for distribution 支付（s.297(1)）= accumulated realised profits − accumulated realised losses（s.297(2)），即 自成立以來累計 ，往年虧損須先彌補。須參考最近期財務報表（s.302；中期報表亦可，ss.302、305）。違法分派：董事/核數師可能 breach of duty； member 明知構成違反的事實 （不論是否知悉屬違法）須退還（s.301）。GM 宣派的股息 不得超過董事建議的數額 （Model Articles Art. 91(1)）；董事可派 interim dividends（Art. 91(2)）；可以 bonus shares / capitalisation of profits 方式支付（Arts. 77, 79）。 I. IRAC Application Points（答題框架示範） Charge 優先權題 ： Issue — 哪個 creditor 優先受償？ Rule — 先查是否 specified charge（s.334）及有否在 1 個月內登記（s.335(5)(a)）；未登記 → s.337(4) void against liquidator/creditors；再按財產類型套用普通法（fixed vs floating：Wheatley；先結晶者優先；自動結晶條款視乎 notice）。 Application — 逐項對應事實（設立日期、登記日期、結晶事件）。 Conclusion — 排定受償次序。 Buy back / reduction 題 ： Issue — 回購/減資是否有效？ Rule — s.267 禁制 → s.244 + ss.258–259 程序（時限！）或 s.234 redeemable shares；reduction 則 s.220 solvency statement 或 s.226 法院確認 + Re Fok Ying Tung 的 balance sheet 原則。 Application — 逐步核對 solvency statement 日期、special resolution 日期、付款週數。 Conclusion — 有效/無效及補救。 Financial assistance 題 ： Issue — 是否構成 prohibited financial assistance？ Rule — s.275(1) + s.274(1) 廣義定義；例外 s.278 / ss.283–285；Ricco 的 purpose vs reason 區分。 Application — 資助形式（guarantee/loan/gift）、目的、董事 solvency statement、批准方式。 Conclusion — 刑事責任（s.275(4)）但交易不當然無效（s.276）。 Class rights 題 ： Issue — 是否 variation of class rights？ Rule — s.178(1)、s.180；White v Bristol Aeroplane 的 rights vs enjoyment 區分。 Application — 權利本身有否改變，還是僅商業上被攤薄。 Conclusion — 如需 variation：75% 書面同意或 class meeting special resolution；10% 持有人可入稟（s.182）。 易混淆概念對比 表 1：Fixed Charge vs Floating Charge 比較點 Fixed Charge Floating Charge
