Aeroplane 唔使 class consent Phase 2 閃卡 Card 1 Front: State the four legal differences between debt financing and equity financing. Back: Repayment obligation: debt = fixed amount (principal + interest), independent of business performance; equity = no fixed repayment, capital locked up except on liquidation / permitted reduction / buy back (risk capital) Control: equity investors become members with shareholder rights; debt investors remain outsiders Costs: debt generally cheaper Gearing ratio = total debt / total equity; used by lenders to assess borrowing capacity 💬 記住口訣「還錢、控制、成本、槓桿」。Equity 最關鍵一句：capital 鎖死，業績好先至有股息，所以叫 risk capital；債權人唔使理公司賺唔賺錢，到期就要還。 Card 2 Front: What is a "debenture" under the CO, and what are the four types of debentures? Back: s.307 CO: includes bonds and any other debt securities of the company, whether or not constituting a charge on the company's assets Four types: (1) redeemable / irredeemable (ss.327–328); (2) convertible (members' approval required — s.140(1)(b)); (3) debenture stock (certificates for fractions of the whole, holders rank equally); (4) bearer debentures (transfer by mere delivery) Registration: allotment of debentures/stock within 1 month (s.316); transfer registered within 2 months of lodgment (s.321); no stamp duty on debenture transfers 💬 Debenture 即係公司出嘅「借據文件」。考試最常考定義（s.307）同埋時間限制：allotment 一個月、transfer 登記兩個月。Single debenture（普通銀行貸款）唔使登記，呢個係伏位。 Card 3 Front: List Romer LJ's three characteristics of a floating charge and the events of crystallisation. Back: Re Yorkshire Woolcombers Association: (1) charge on a class of assets, present and future; (2) the class changes from time to time in the ordinary course of business; (3) until the chargee takes a step, the company may carry on business and deal with the assets in the ordinary way Crystallisation: (1) court order for compulsory winding up (NOT mere petition / provisional liquidator); (2) resolution for voluntary winding up; (3) appointment of receiver by the chargee; (4) agreed events (default, crystallisation of other floating charges, notice to convert) 💬 三特徵記「一類資產、不時變、自由處理」。結晶事件最易中伏：petition 未結晶，order 先結晶。結晶後 floating 變 fixed，公司唔可以再自由賣啲資產。 Card 4 Front: What must be delivered to the Registrar to register a charge, by when, and what are the consequences of non registration? Back: Deliver (s.335(1)): (1) statement of particulars in specified form; (2) certified copy of the instrument creating/evidencing the charge Deadline: within one month of creation, starting the day after creation (s.335(5)(a)) Non registration: charge VOID against the liquidator and creditors (s.337(4)) — but remains valid between chargee and company; criminal offence for company and responsible persons (s.337(2)) Court may extend time if failure was accidental / inadvertence / sufficient cause, not prejudicial and just and equitable (s.346(3)); extension removes criminal liability (s.346(4)) 💬 大伏位：「void」唔係對所有人無效——只係對 liquidator 同其他 creditors 無效，對公司本身仍然有效。仲有 chargee 可以自己登記（s.335(3)），費用可向公司追返（s.335(7)）。 Card 5 Front: State the common law priority rules for competing charges over personal property, with authorities. Back: Fixed vs fixed: first in time prevails (Re Weniger's Policy (1910) 2 Ch 291 — further advance postponed if chargee failed to enquire about notice of intervening charge) Floating vs floating: first in time, unless the first charge reserved power to create a later charge with priority; pari passu wording does not displace earlier priority (Re Benjamin Cope & Sons Ltd (1914) 1 Ch 800); subordination agreement can regulate priorities Fixed vs floating: fixed generally prevails (Wheatley v Silkstone and Haigh Moor Coal Co (1885) 29 Ch 715); BUT an earlier floating charge that crystallised before the later fixed charge has priority Charges over debts/choses in action: priority by notice — first chargee to notify the debtor wins 💬 一句總結：「fixed 大過 floating，先結晶當 fixed 計」。記住 Wheatley：floating charge 唔阻止公司之後再畀人 fixed charge，所以 floating chargee 通常會加 negative pledge + automatic crystallisation clause 自保。 Card 6 Front: What is the default procedure for varying class rights, and what did White v Bristol Aeroplane decide? Back: Same class = rights uniform in all respects (s.178(1)); variation governed by ss.176–184 Default (articles silent): written consent of holders of ≥75% of total voting rights of the class (s.180(1)) OR special resolution at a class meeting (s.180(3)) Notice to class shareholders within 14 days (s.181); filing with Registrar within 1 month (s.184); ≥10% of class voting rights may apply to court to disallow for unfair prejudice (s.182(1), (5)) White v Bristol Aeroplane Co Ltd (1953) Ch 65 (CA): issuing new shares ranking pari passu with existing shares affects only the ENJOYMENT of rights, not the rights themselves — NOT a variation, no class consent needed 💬 考試見「發新股攤薄咗我嘅投票權」九成係 White v Bristol Aeroplane——唔係 variation。Variation 係指改變權利本身，例如取消 preference dividend。10% 入稟門檻同 14 日通知都係數字伏位。 Card 7 Front: Explain the doctrine of capital maintenance and the four transactions it generally prohibits, with their statutory gateways. Back: Common law: share capital may not be returned to members except on winding up — creditors rely on paid up capital as the fund of credit Four prohibited transactions + gateways: 1. Reduction of capital → special resolution + solvency statement by ALL directors (s.220; solvency test s.205) OR special resolution confirmed by court (s.226; Re Fok Ying Tung Ming Yuan Development Co Ltd (2016) 2 HKLRD 292) 2. Self acquisition → prohibited (s.267); redeemable shares (s.234, fully paid only s.268, cancelled s.269(1)); buy back by unlisted company with contract pre approved by special resolution (s.244); if funded out of capital: payment 5–7 weeks after SR (s.258), SR within 15 days of solvency statement (s.259) 3. Financial assistance → prohibited directly or indirectly, incl. subsidiary for holding company (s.275(1)); exceptions ss.277–289 4. Dividends → only out of profits available for distribution (s.297(1)–(2)) 💬 背誦框架：「一個原則、四條禁令、每條禁令一條生路」。時限數字最易考：buy back 用 capital 支付 = 5–7 週內付款、SR 要喺 solvency statement 後 15 日內通過。 Card 8 Front: What is the rule against financial assistance for acquisition of shares, its exceptions and the leading cases? Back: Prohibition: company must not give financial assistance directly or indirectly for acquiring its own shares (before or at acquisition); extends to subsidiary assisting acquisition of holding company's shares (s.275(1)) Definition (s.274(1)): gift; guarantee/security/indemnity/release/waiver; loan; other assistance reducing net assets by a material extent Consequences: criminal liability (s.275(4)); transaction NOT invalid per se (s.276) Exceptions (ss.277–289): solvency statement by ALL directors + (≤5% of paid up capital / unanimous shareholder approval / ordinary resolution) (ss.283–285); principal purpose exception — assistance incidental to some larger purpose, given in good faith in the company's interest (s.278); court order Ricco (Int'l) Co Ltd v Uni Harvest Int'l Ltd (2017) 6 HKC 487: distinguish "a purpose" from "the reason why a purpose was formed" — business expansion was merely a reason, exception failed Carney v Herbert (1985) AC 301: illegal mortgage severable; personal guarantee enforceable 💬 Ricco 係答題關鍵：「幫公司擴張業務」只係 reason 唔係 purpose，唔好以為講句「為公司好」就過到 s.278。仲要記住違規係刑事，但交易本身唔會自動無效。 本章急救詞彙 EN Term 繁中白話 English Model Sentence Gearing ratio 借貸相對股東資金嘅比率，用嚟衡量公司仲可以借幾多 The gearing ratio is calculated by dividing the company's total debt by its total equity. Debenture 公司發出嘅借據文件，證明一筆貸款（s.307 定義好闊） Under s.307 of the CO, a debenture includes bonds and any other debt securities of the company, whether or not constituting a charge on its assets. Floating charge 浮喺一類會變動嘅資產上面嘅押記，公司日常可以照樣買賣 A floating charge hovers over a class of circulating assets until it crystallises into a fixed charge. Crystallisation Floating charge 「凝固」變 fixed charge 嘅過程 Upon the appointment of a receiver, the floating charge crystallises and the company may no longer deal with the charged assets. Equity of redemption 借款人還清債務後取回按揭物業嘅權利 The mortgagor retains the equity of redemption, entitling him to have the property re transferred upon discharge of the secured liabilities. Pari passu 大家按比例平分，冇人排先 Where the company's assets are insufficient, the proceeds are divided pari passu among the unsecured creditors. Solvency statement 全體董事簽嘅聲明，確認公司通過償債能力測試 A reduction of capital by special resolution must be supported by a solvency statement made by all the directors under s.220 of the CO. Financial assistance 公司出錢/擔保幫人買自己嘅股票，原則上犯法 Providing a guarantee to secure a loan for the purchase of the company's own shares constitutes financial assistance prohibited by s.275(1) of the CO.

title: M10 Chapter 11: Company Capital and Financing Companies — Phase 3 Answers
headings: M10 Chapter 11: Company Capital and Financing Companies — Phase 3 Answers
Q5 — Answer: The court is likely to REFUSE confirmation.
excerpt: M10 Chapter 11: Company Capital and Financing Companies — Phase 3 Answers Q1 — Answer: B Model Answer (EN): The security is a floating charge. In Re Yorkshire W…
text: M10 Chapter 11: Company Capital and Financing Companies — Phase 3 Answers Q1 — Answer: B Model Answer (EN): The security is a floating charge. In Re Yorkshire Woolcombers Association, Romer LJ identified three characteristics: (1) the charge is on a class of assets, present and future; (2) that class changes from time to time in the ordinary course of business; and (3) until the chargee takes some step, the company may carry on business and deal with the assets in the ordinary way. All three are present: the charge covers present and future stock in trade, the inventory constantly changes, and BLL retains freedom to deal until notice is given. It will become a fixed charge only upon crystallisation. 解題思路（繁中）: 分辨 fixed vs floating 嘅關鍵唔係份文件寫得幾仔細，而係公司仲可唔可以自由處理啲資產。BLL 可以喺日常業務中自由買賣存貨 → 三個 Romer LJ 特徵齊晒 → floating charge。A 錯：用描述方式識別資產唔等於 fixed charge，floating charge 都要話到明係邊類資產。C 錯：charge 唔涉及 title 轉移，唔係 mortgage；「涵蓋將來資產」反而係 floating charge 嘅典型特徵。D 錯：pledge 係 possessory security，貸方要管有資產；題目講明存貨留喺 BLL 手上，所以唔係 pledge（仲有 pledgee 無 foreclosure 權）。考試伏位：記住「公司仲玩得郁啲資產 = floating」。 Rule Check: Re Yorkshire Woolcombers Association (Romer LJ's three characteristics, as cited in the LP); CO (Cap. 622) s.334(6) (floating charge is a specified charge). Common Trap（繁中）: 以為「寫明係邊啲資產」就係 fixed charge；或者以為「future assets」令佢變成 mortgage。仲有：floating charge 唔需要公司先停止營業先有效——佢一設立就存在，只係結晶前公司可以自由處理資產。 Q2 — Answer: A Model Answer (EN): A charge on book debts is a "specified charge" under s.334 and must be registered within one month of creation (the period starting on the day after creation) by delivering a statement of particulars in the specified form and a certified copy of the instrument (s.335(1), s.335(5)(a)). The charge was created on 2 May, so the deadline was 2 June; delivery on 20 June is late. Under s.337(4), an unregistered specified charge is void against the liquidator and creditors of the company. However, it remains valid as between the chargee (Bank N) and the company, and also as against unsecured creditors and purchasers of the charged property. The company and its responsible persons also commit a criminal offence (s.337(2)), though the court may extend time under s.346(3) if the failure was accidental or due to inadvertence, which would remove the criminal liability (s.346(4)). 解題思路（繁中）: 呢題考 pinpoint section + 「void 對邊個 void」。Book debts 明明喺 s.334 清單入面（第 4 項），所以 D 錯。期限計法：設立翌日起計一個月，2 May 設立 → 2 June 到期，20 June 先交 = 逾期。B 錯：s.337(4) 唔係令 charge 對全世界無效，只係對 liquidator 同 creditors 無效；chargee 同公司之間仍然有效。C 錯：刑事責任係額外嘅，唔係唯一後果——唔登記嘅實體法後果先係重點（失去對 liquidator/creditors 嘅優先權）。考試伏位：「valid against the company but void against the liquidator and creditors」呢句要背到。 Rule Check: CO (Cap. 622) s.334 (specified charges, incl. charge on book debts), s.335(1) & s.335(5)(a), s.337(4), s.337(2), s.346(3)–(4). Common Trap（繁中）: 考生最常犯兩個錯：(1) 以為唔登記 = 成個 charge 無效（其實只係對 liquidator/creditors 無效）；(2) 以為刑事責任取代民事後果（其實兩者並存）。記住登記本身唔賦予優先權，但唔登記會令優先權喪失。 Q3 — Answer: B Model Answer (EN): The proposal is not a variation of class rights. Shares belong to the same class if the rights attached are in all respects uniform (s.178(1)), and variation of class rights requires written consent of holders of at least 75% of the class's voting rights or a special resolution at a class meeting (s.180(1), (3)). However, in White v Bristol Aeroplane Co Ltd (1953) Ch 65 (CA), the issue of new preference and ordinary shares ranking pari passu with existing shares was held NOT to be a variation: the rights attached to the existing preference shares (e.g. the 8% cumulative dividend) remain untouched; the existing holders are affected only in the enjoyment of their rights as a matter of business. Ms Lau's consent as a class is therefore not required, and her s.182(1) remedy (available only where there IS a variation) does not arise. (Note: as the allotment is non pro rata, approval of the members in general meeting by ordinary resolution is still required under ss.140–141 — but that is a separate issue.) 解題思路（繁中）: 呢題係經典 White v Bristol Aeroplane 應用。分辨方法：問「股票上附著嘅權利改咗未？」Ms Lau 嘅 8% cumulative preference dividend 一蚊都冇改變，改嘅只係佢嘅相對商業地位 → enjoyment only → 唔係 variation。A 錯：dilution 唔等於 variation，呢個正正係 White v Bristol Aeroplane 嘅 holding。C 錯：s.182(1) 嘅入稟權只喺有 variation 嘅情況下先存在，呢度根本冇 variation，所以無從入稟。D 錯：章程無規定時，s.180 默認規則就係要 75% 書面同意或 class meeting special resolution——「從來唔使同意」係大錯。額外位：non pro rata allotment 仍要 members 以 ordinary resolution 批准（ss.140–141），但嗰個係另一個 issue，唔好溝埋。 Rule Check: CO (Cap. 622) s.178(1), s.180(1) & (3), s.182(1); White v Bristol Aeroplane Co Ltd (1953) Ch 65 (CA). Common Trap（繁中）: 一見「攤薄/dilution」就衝去答 variation + s.180，係最常見伏位。記住：variation = 權利本身變；enjoyment affected = 商業效果變。仲有，唔好將 s.182 嘅 10% 入稟門檻亂套落冇 variation 嘅情況。 Q4 — Answer: C Model Answer (EN): The guarantee is prohibited financial assistance. A company is prohibited from giving financial assistance directly or indirectly for the purpose of acquiring shares in the company, and the prohibition extends to a subsidiary giving assistance for the acquisition of shares in its holding company (s.275(1)). A guarantee falls squarely within the wide definition of financial assistance in s.274(1). The principal purpose exception in s.278 does not apply: following Ricco (Int'l) Co Ltd v Uni Harvest Int'l Ltd (2017) 6 HKC 487, one must distinguish "a purpose" from "the reason why a purpose was formed"; the anticipated benefit to NFL's business from the group expansion is merely the reason or motive for giving the guarantee, not a separate larger purpose. Breach carries criminal liability (s.275(4)), but the transaction is not invalid per se (s.276) — though it may still be set aside on other grounds such as directors' breach of fiduciary duty (cf. Carney v Herbert (1985) AC 301 on severance). 解題思路（繁中）: 典型 IRAC：Issue = NFL 嘅 guarantee 係咪 prohibited financial assistance？Rule = s.275(1)（連子公司資助收購控股公司股份都包）+ s.274(1)（guarantee 明確喺定義內）+ s.278 例外 + Ricco 嘅 purpose/reason 區分。Application = 「集團擴張對 NFL 有利」只係动机/reason，唔係獨立嘅 larger purpose → 例外失效。Conclusion = 違法，有刑事責任，但交易唔自動無效。A 錯：正正係 Ricco 推翻嘅論點。B 錯：s.275(1) 明確延伸至子公司，呢個係白撞選項。D 錯：s.276 話明 validity 唔受影響 per se；Carney v Herbert 仲話埋非法部分可以 sever。考試伏位：記住「違法 ≠ 交易無效」，同埋 s.278 例外好窄。 Rule Check: CO (Cap. 622) s.275(1), s.274(1), s.275(4), s.276, s.278; Ricco (Int'l) Co Ltd v Uni Harvest Int'l Ltd (2017) 6 HKC 487; Carney v Herbert (1985) AC 301. Common Trap（繁中）: 兩大陷阱：(1) 以為講句「為公司利益/更大商業目的」就過到 s.278——Ricco 話 motive/reason 唔係 purpose；(2) 以為違反 s.275 會令成個收購交易無效——s.276 話唔會，頂多因董事 breach of fiduciary duty 等其他理由先會被撤銷。 Q5 — Answer: The court is likely to REFUSE confirmation. Model Answer (EN): A reduction of capital by special resolution confirmed by the court falls under Sub division 3 of Division 3 of Part 5 (s.226). The court's main consideration is whether shareholders' and creditors' interests are prejudiced — the shareholders must be treated equitably, the proposal properly explained, creditors safeguarded, and there must be a discernible purpose. In Re Fok Ying Tung Ming Yuan Development Co Ltd (2016) 2 HKLRD 292, the court held that it approaches a reduction on the basis of the share capital shown in the company's balance sheet at the time of reduction: where the company carries accumulated losses, those losses reduce the capital actually available, and a description of the reduction that fails to reflect this is misleading to future creditors. The court also relies heavily on up to date audited financial statements that are unqualified or carry only immaterial qualifications. Here, Marble Arch Ltd's balance sheet shows accumulated losses of HK$30 million, yet the resolution asserts that "capital exceeds its needs" — a misleading description — and the auditors have issued a disclaimer of opinion, depriving the court of reliable financial statements. Creditors (current and future) would be prejudiced. Following Re Fok Ying Tung, the petition should be dismissed and confirmation refused. 解題思路（繁中）: 呢題係 hard tier，考一個相對冷門但 LP 有詳細講嘅案例。思路：Issue = 法院會唔會確認減資？Rule = s.226 法院確認途徑 + 法院四大考慮（公平對待股東、方案解釋、保障債權人、有可辨識目的）+ Re Fok Ying Tung 兩個原則：(1) 以 balance sheet 上嘅 share capital 為準，accumulated losses 會扣減可用資本；(2) 法院依賴無保留（或只有輕微保留）意見嘅經審計報表。Application = 公司虧蝕 HK$30m 卻聲稱「資本超出需要」= 誤導性描述，會誤導未來債權人；核數師出 disclaimer = 法院冇可靠報表可依；反對嘅 creditor 利益受損。Conclusion = 拒絕確認。攞分位：一定要引 Re Fok Ying Tung 全名同年份，同埋點出「accumulated losses 減少可用資本」呢個核心 ratio。 Rule Check: CO (Cap. 622) s.226 (Sub division 3 of Division 3 of Part 5); Re Fok Ying Tung Ming Yuan Development Co Ltd (2016) 2 HKLRD 292. Common Trap（繁中）: 考生成日只背「special resolution + solvency statement 或法院確認」就收工，完全唔提法院確認嘅實質審查標準。呢題嘅伏位係事實入面嘅「accumulated losses + disclaimer of opinion」——兩個都係 Re Fok Ying Tung 嘅翻版事實，見到就要即刻諗起呢個案。唔好答「只要股東一致同意就得」——保障 creditor 先係成個 doctrine of capital maintenance 嘅核心。

title: M10 Chapter 11: Company Capital and Financing Companies — Phase 3 Quiz
headings: M10 Chapter 11: Company Capital and Financing Companies — Phase 3 Quiz
excerpt: M10 Chapter 11: Company Capital and Financing Companies — Phase 3 Quiz Rules: Closed book · 15 minutes · 5 questions · Submit as 1. … 2. … 3. … 4. … 5. … — 超時如實…
text: M10 Chapter 11: Company Capital and Financing Companies — Phase 3 Quiz Rules: Closed book · 15 minutes · 5 questions · Submit as 1. … 2. … 3. … 4. … 5. … — 超時如實申報 Unless otherwise stated, all statutory references are to the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) ("CO"). Q1 (MCQ — 4 options) Bright Logistics Ltd ("BLL") granted Bank M a charge over "all stock in trade and inventory of the company, present and future". The charge instrument expressly allows BLL to sell, replace and deal with the inventory in the ordinary course of its business until Bank M gives notice to the contrary. Which of the following BEST describes this security? A. A fixed charge, because the instrument identifies the charged assets by description B. A floating charge, because it hovers over a changing class of present and future assets with which BLL may deal in the ordinary course of business C. A legal mortgage, because the charge extends to future assets of the company D. A pledge, because the inventory remains in BLL's possession Q2 (MCQ — 4 options) On 2 May, Castor Engineering Ltd created a charge over its book debts in favour of Bank N. The company secretary overlooked the matter and no documents were delivered to the Registrar of Companies until 20 June. No court order extending time has been obtained. Which of the following statements is CORRECT? A. The charge is void against the liquidator and creditors of the company under s.337(4), although it remains valid as between Bank N and the company B. The charge is void ab initio against all persons, including the company itself C. The charge remains fully valid against everyone; late registration only gives rise to criminal liability under s.337(2) D. The charge is valid because a charge over book debts is not a "specified charge" under s.334 Q3 (MCQ — scenario) Pelican Retail Ltd has issued ordinary shares and 8% cumulative preference shares. The board proposes to capitalise part of the company's reserves by issuing 500,000 NEW preference shares, ranking pari passu with the existing preference shares, to the existing ordinary shareholders. Ms Lau, an existing preference shareholder, objects, arguing that the proposal is a variation of class rights which requires the written consent of holders of at least 75% of the voting rights of her class or a special resolution at a class meeting under s.180. Which of the following is the BEST analysis? A. Ms Lau is correct: any issue of new shares of the same class dilutes existing class members and therefore amounts to a variation requiring s.180 consent B. Ms Lau is wrong: following White v Bristol Aeroplane Co Ltd (1953) Ch 65, the proposal affects only the enjoyment of the existing preference shareholders' rights, not the rights themselves, so it is not a variation and no class consent is required C. Ms Lau is correct: because the new shares are issued to ordinary shareholders only, the preference shareholders are unfairly prejudiced and may apply to court under s.182(1) to have the issue disallowed D. Ms Lau is wrong: variation of class rights never requires class consent under the CO; it is governed solely by the articles Q4 (MCQ — scenario) Nero Holdings Ltd ("NHL") is the holding company of Nero Foods Ltd ("NFL"), its wholly owned subsidiary. Mr Chan agrees to buy all the shares in NHL from its existing shareholder for HK$8 million, funded by a bank loan. At the bank's request, NFL provides a guarantee of Mr Chan's loan. NFL's directors argue that the guarantee is lawful because NFL's business will benefit from Mr Chan's planned expansion of the group, so the assistance was given for a "larger purpose" in good faith in NFL's interest. Which of the following is the BEST analysis? A. The guarantee is lawful: it falls squarely within the principal purpose exception in s.278 because the group's expansion is a larger purpose of NFL B. The guarantee is lawful: a subsidiary is always free to guarantee loans for the acquisition of its holding company's shares because s.275(1) only catches the issuing company itself C. The guarantee is prohibited financial assistance under s.275(1) (a guarantee being within s.274(1)); following Ricco (Int'l) Co Ltd v Uni Harvest Int'l Ltd (2017) 6 HKC 487, the expected business benefit is merely the "reason" for giving the assistance, not a separate "larger purpose", so the s.278 exception fails — although the underlying transaction is not invalid per se (s.276) D. The guarantee is prohibited, and therefore the sale of NHL's shares to Mr Chan is automatically void and cannot be enforced by either party Q5 (Short answer — 3–5 sentences) Marble Arch Ltd, a Hong Kong private company, passed a special resolution under s.226 for the court to confirm a reduction of its share capital from HK$10 million to HK$4 million by returning HK$6 to each shareholder per share, on the stated basis that "the company's capital exceeds its needs". The company's latest balance sheet in fact shows accumulated losses of HK$30 million, and its auditors issued a disclaimer of opinion on the financial statements. A creditor objects to the petition. Advise whether the court is likely to confirm the reduction, citing the relevant authority and reasoning.

title: M10 Chapter 12: Listed Companies and the Regulation of Financial Markets — Phase 1 速查表 + Phase 2 閃卡
headings: M10 Chapter 12: Listed Companies and the Regulation of Financial Markets — Phase 1 速查表 + Phase 2 閃卡
A. Relevant Ordinances & Rules (按 LP 引用為準)
B. Leading Cases (full citations — 以 LP 所引為準)
excerpt: M10 Chapter 12: Listed Companies and the Regulation of Financial Markets — Phase 1 速查表 + Phase 2 閃卡 Phase 1 速查表 Learning Objectives 1. Identify the key regulato…
text: M10 Chapter 12: Listed Companies and the Regulation of Financial Markets — Phase 1 速查表 + Phase 2 閃卡 Phase 1 速查表 Learning Objectives 1. Identify the key regulators of Hong Kong's financial markets (SFC, HKEX, HKMA, AFRC, IA, Financial Secretary) and distinguish the legal status of the Securities and Futures Ordinance (Cap. 571) from the Listing Rules. 2. Apply the prospectus regime under the Companies (Winding Up and Miscellaneous Provisions) Ordinance (Cap. 32), including exemptions, contents, registration, and civil/criminal liability for misstatements. 3. Explain the listing requirements for the Main Board and GEM Board, the role of sponsors, and the continuing disclosure obligations of listed issuers (notifiable transactions, connected transactions, public float, disclosure of interests). 4. Apply the Codes on Takeovers and Mergers and Share Buy backs, including the 30% mandatory general offer trigger and directors' duties during an offer. 5. Analyse the six types of market misconduct under Parts XIII–XIV of the SFO, in particular insider dealing under s.270, and apply the statutory defences. 必背考點 A. Relevant Ordinances & Rules (按 LP 引用為準) Regulators & framework SFC — statutory body established under the Securities and Futures Ordinance (Cap. 571) ('SFO') , Part II; six regulatory objectives in s.4 SFO (fairness/efficiency/transparency; public understanding; investor protection; minimise crime and misconduct; reduce systemic risk; assist Financial Secretary). HKEX — operates markets via wholly owned subsidiaries SEHK (equities/debt) and HKFE (derivatives); makes and administers the Listing Rules pursuant to s.23 SFO . Listing Rules are NOT statute — breach gives regulatory sanctions only: private reprimand, public criticism, public censure, requisition for rectification, and (most severe) delisting/rejection of application. No criminal or civil liability per se. HKMA — banking stability, Linked Exchange Rate system, Exchange Fund, FMIs. AFRC — established under the Accounting and Financial Reporting Council Ordinance (Cap. 588) ; investigates auditors of listed entities (relevant irregularities, s.4 AFRCO ; enquiry powers s.9). IA — established under the Insurance Ordinance (Cap. 41) . Market Misconduct Tribunal (MMT) — established under Part XIII SFO ; independent; chaired by a High Court judge or former judge; hears civil market misconduct proceedings. Public issue of shares — prospectus regime (CWUMPO Cap. 32 + SFO) Public company defined negatively: neither a private company nor a company limited by guarantee — s.12 Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) ('CO') ; private company cannot invite the public to subscribe — s.11(1) CO . "Prospectus" widely defined — s.2 CWUMPO ("any prospectus, notice, circular, brochure, advertisement or other document offering shares or debentures…"). Prohibition on public offer without a compliant prospectus — s.38(3) CWUMPO ; "offer to the public" includes a section of the public; not an offer to the public if not calculated to result in shares becoming available to others — s.48A(2) CWUMPO (e.g. employee share schemes). Exemptions ( Sch.17 CWUMPO , underwriters s.38(3)(a) , SFC exemption power s.38A ): professional investors (incl. high net worth individuals with portfolio ≥ HK$8m); minimum consideration ≥ HK$500,000; offers to ≤ 50 persons or total consideration ≤ HK$5m; qualifying persons (directors/employees); charity/educational establishments; SFC granted exemptions. Contents — Sch.3 CWUMPO (business, share capital, directors, 3 year turnover, material contracts, details of offer, substantial holders, auditor's report, land valuation report HK$3m or 10% of assets); expert consent — s.38C ; checklist at ss.38(1), 38(1A), 38D(2), Sch.3, Sch.18 Pt.1. LR Chapter 11A also applies — compliance with LR does not guarantee compliance with the CO/CWUMPO. Authorisation & registration — s.38D(1) CWUMPO : authorised by the SFC (for listing applicants, via the HKEX) and registered with the Registrar of Companies ( s.38D(7) ). Liability for misstatement: Civil: s.40 CWUMPO (false/misleading statements incl. material omissions; directors, promoters, company and persons authorising issue liable — s.40(1); compensation to subscribers — s.40(7); defences: no consent / reasonable grounds to believe truth). Civil: s.108 SFO (fraudulent, reckless or negligent misrepresentation inducing subscription; damages; does NOT apply where s.40 CWUMPO applies); s.277 SFO (false/misleading disclosure inducing transactions — also market misconduct). Criminal: s.40A CWUMPO (untrue statement in prospectus; defences: immaterial / reasonable grounds of belief); s.107 SFO (fraudulent or reckless misrepresentation to induce acquisition/subscription); general criminal law (e.g. conspiracy to defraud). Advertising restrictions — s.38B CWUMPO (no extracts/abridged versions/advertisements except Sch.19 exceptions or SFC approved ads under s.105 SFO ); s.103(1) SFO blanket prohibition on unauthorised invitations to the public (exception: CWUMPO compliant prospectus, s.103(3)(a) ). Listing on the SEHK (Main Board Listing Rules 'LR'; GEM Rules) Methods of listing (LR Ch.7): offers for subscription, offers for sale, placing, introduction, rights issue, open offer, capitalisation issue, consideration issue, exchange. Main Board qualifications (LR Ch.8, as from Jan 2022): profit test (≥ HK$35m latest year + ≥ HK$45m aggregate prior two years; 3 year track record); OR market cap/revenue/cash flow test (mkt cap ≥ HK$2bn + revenue ≥ HK$500m + 3 yr aggregate operating cash flow ≥ HK$100m); OR market cap/revenue test (mkt cap ≥ HK$4bn + revenue ≥ HK$500m); public float ≥ 25% + ≥ 300 shareholders; public mkt cap ≥ HK$125m; total mkt cap ≥ HK$500m; ≥ 2 executive directors ordinarily resident in HK; ≥ 3 INEDs = ≥ 1/3 of board. GEM (as at July 2019): 2 year trading record; positive 2 year aggregate operating cash flow ≥ HK$30m; mkt cap ≥ HK$150m; 2 year management / 1 year ownership continuity; ≥ 25% float + ≥ 100 shareholders; public mkt cap ≥ HK$45m; ≥ 3 INEDs = 1/3 of board. New regimes: LR Ch.8A weighted voting rights (innovative companies; mkt cap ≥ HK$40bn, or ≥ HK$10bn + revenue ≥ HK$1bn); LR Ch.18A pre revenue biotech (mkt cap ≥ HK$1,500m; ≥ 2 years' operation; working capital ≥ 125% of costs for 12 months); LR Ch.18B SPACs (from 1 Jan 2022; De SPAC deadline 36 months; target must satisfy all new listing requirements). Sponsor: corporation/authorised financial institution licensed for Type 6 regulated activity (advising on corporate finance) ; due diligence duties (understand business, identify risks/irregularities, ensure listing criteria met, ensure adequate prospectus disclosure, ensure internal controls and competent directors); see HKEX Practice Note 21. Price stabilisation: Securities and Futures (Price Stabilizing) Rules (Cap. 571W) — permitted stabilising action within 30 days after IPO. Continuing obligations of listed issuers LR Ch.13 continuing obligations (avoid false market; advances 8% asset ratio; pledging of shares by controlling shareholder; winding up; monthly returns; public float; annual/interim reports, etc.). Inside information disclosure — now statutory: Part XIVA SFO general duty of disclosure; directors must use best endeavours to ensure compliance and may incur personal liability. Notifiable transactions (LR Ch.14.06) — five ratios: assets, profits, revenue, consideration, equity capital. Six categories (ascending): share transaction (<5%, share consideration); disclosable (one ratio ≥5%, all <25%); major (one ratio ≥25%, all <75% disposal/100% acquisition); very substantial disposal (≥75%); very substantial acquisition (≥100%); reverse takeover. Requirements scale up: announcement → circular → shareholders' approval. Connected transactions ( LR Ch.14A ): connected persons include directors/chief executives, substantial shareholders (≥10%), past directors (12 months), close relatives, associates (spouse, children, trustees, ≥30% controlled companies), supervisors (PRC issuers). Required actions: written agreement (14A.34); annual report disclosure (14A.71/14A.49); announcement (14A.35/14A.36); independent shareholders' approval with interested parties abstaining (14A.36–39); independent board committee of INEDs (14A.40–43); independent financial adviser (14A.44–45); circular (14A.46–48). Minimum public float: ≥ 25% at all times (LR Ch.13); inform HKEX and restore if breached; trading may be suspended. Disclosure of interests — Part XV SFO : substantial shareholders ≥ 5% of any class of voting shares ( s.310 ); directors & chief executives ( s.341 ); deemed interests of spouse/children/controlled corporations/trusts ( ss.316, 344 ); registers kept by the listed company ( ss.336, 352 ). Takeovers & share buy backs (Codes on Takeovers and Mergers and Share Buy backs 'TC' + CO) Mandatory general offer trigger: person (with concert parties) crossing 30% of voting rights ; acting in concert holdings aggregated. Scheme of arrangement — s.166 CO ; cancellation or transfer scheme; driven by target (only if target supportive; common for privatisations); approval: ≥75% of votes cast by disinterested shareholders + votes against ≤ 10% of disinterested shares + court sanction. Key TC Rules: offer first to offeree board (R1.1); independent board committee + independent financial adviser (R2.1); delisting resolution 75% independent shareholders (R2.2); announcement of offer (R3); no frustrating action without shareholders' approval (R4); board not to resign mid offer (R7); equal information to all shareholders (R8.1); highest standard of accuracy; directors jointly and severally responsible (R9.1–9.3); profit forecasts with due care (R10.1); valuations by named independent valuer (R11.1). Sanction: "Cold Shoulder Order" (denial of market access). Share buy backs (listed): (1) on market — ordinary resolution, valid until next AGM ( s.239(3) CO ); (2) off market general offer — ordinary resolution ( s.238(1) CO ); (3) off market other than general offer — special resolution (differential treatment → onerous approval). TC supplements the statutory regime. Corporate Governance Code (Appendix 14 LR, renamed 'Corporate Governance Code' from 1 Jan 2022) Part 1: mandatory disclosure in CG Report (12 headings: CG practices, board, chairman/CEO, NEDs, committees, company secretary, directors' securities transactions/Model Code, risk management & internal control, auditor's remuneration, diversity, shareholders' rights, investor relations). Part 2: Principles + Code Provisions (CPs) + Recommended Best Practices (RBPs); "comply or explain" — deviation from a CP without explanation breaches the Listing Rules; RBPs are guidance only. Key CPs: C.2.1 chairman and chief executive roles separated; C.5.1 ≥ 4 board meetings p.a. at quarterly intervals; C.5.3 ≥ 14 days' notice of regular board meetings; C.6.1 company secretary an employee (or disclose senior contact of external provider); C.6.3 company secretary reports to chairman/CEO; B.3.1 nomination committee duties; D.2.1 annual review of risk management/internal control; D.2.6 whistleblowing policy; D.2.7 anti corruption policy; E.1.5 disclose remuneration policy and senior management remuneration by band; F.1.1 dividend policy; F.2.1 separate resolutions (no bundling). ESG Reporting Guide (Appendix 27): ESG reports published with annual reports. Market misconduct (SFO Parts XIII & XIV) Inside information — s.245 SFO : (1) about the listed corporation / its shareholder or officer / its listed securities or derivatives; (2) specific; (3) not generally known to those accustomed or likely to deal; (4) likely to materially affect price if generally known. Six types of market misconduct (civil, Part XIII): insider dealing ( s.270 ); false trading ( s.274 ); price rigging ( s.275 ); disclosure of information about prohibited transactions ( s.276 ); disclosure of false or misleading information inducing transactions ( s.277 ); stock market manipulation ( s.278 ). Insider dealing (s.270): connected person (director, employee, substantial shareholder of the corporation or a related corporation — s.247 ) with information he knows is inside information who (a) deals, (b) counsels or procures another to deal, or (c) discloses knowing/having reasonable cause to believe the other will deal. Covers tippees too. Defences ss.271–273 (e.g. qualification shares; good faith underwriting; liquidator/receiver/trustee; no profit or loss avoidance motive s.271(3); Chinese walls s.271(2); innocent agents; equal information off market; trustees on advice; pre acquired subscription rights) — onus on defendant, balance of probabilities. False trading (s.274): intention to create false/misleading appearance of active trading or of the market (wash sales; matched orders); actual effect unnecessary — "real chance" suffices; defence s.274(6) (purposes did not include creating the false appearance; defendant proves the negative on balance of probabilities). Price rigging (s.275): wash sale or fictitious/artificial transaction with effect (or intention) of maintaining/increasing/reducing/stabilising/causing fluctuations in price; defence s.275(4). s.276: disclosing that a prohibited transaction will affect prices (secondary misconduct); defences s.276(2). s.277: disclosure of false/misleading information (as to material fact or omission) likely to induce dealings, with knowledge/recklessness/negligence; defences s.277(2)–(4) (mere reproducers/publishers, IT retransmitters, live broadcasters). s.278: two or more transactions intended to induce dealings by affecting/maintaining price; legitimate price stabilisation under Cap. 571W (made pursuant to s.282 SFO) is a defence. Dual regime: civil market misconduct (Part XIII, MMT, balance of probabilities) vs criminal offences (Part XIV, ss.291–299, proof beyond reasonable doubt; e.g. s.291 mirrors s.270). Other offences: s.300 (fraudulent/deceptive devices), s.302 (falsely representing futures dealings), s.384 (false or misleading information to the SFC). B. Leading Cases (full citations — 以 LP 所引為準) Securities and Futures Commission v Chan Pak Hoe Pablo (2011) 5 HKC 484 — "specific" information needs sufficient particularity to be identified, defined and unequivocally expressed; contrast mere rumour/vague hopes; lack of precision does not defeat specificity; ongoing negotiations needing further approval can still be inside information. Securities and Futures Commission v Young Bik Fung (2016) 1 HKLRD 1249 — tipping by a solicitor who learnt of a privatisation at his firm; tippees who knew the information was confidential price sensitive information liable; inference from circumstantial evidence. Leung Chi Keung v Market Misconduct Tribunal (2012) 2 HKLRD 786 — two elements: (1) information connection (specific, non public, price sensitive); (2) person connection to a defined insider; "connected person" test is objective (what others might reasonably expect of the position); a Chinese wall is only a relevant consideration; information need not be "certain". HKSAR v Fu Kor Kuen Patrick (2012) 15 HKCFAR 524 — circular warrant trading for commission rebates; s.295(5) deeming provision; statutory defence in s.295(7) succeeded — persuasive burden on defendants on balance of probabilities; genuine economic purpose (rebate farming) negatived the purpose of creating a false appearance. HKSAR v Li Jialin (2014) 2 HKLRD 538 — price rigging: chairman's cross account trades with no change in beneficial ownership; "price" = nominal price (last traded price informed by bid/ask queues) per s.296(1) SFO. SEHK Circular dated 18 December 2018 re Golden Meditech Holdings Ltd (Stock Code: 801) — privatisation structured as disposal was a very substantial disposal (Rules 14.48, 14.49, 14.51); failure to announce (Rule 14.34) and obtain shareholders' approval = breach. SEHK Circular dated 20 July 2018 re SRE Group Ltd (Stock Code: 1207) — undisclosed guarantees for chairman connected parties were connected transactions; breach of LR 14A.35, 14A.36, 14A.46, 14A.49. Disciplinary Proceedings against Daqing Dairy and Its Directors (SFC Takeovers Bulletin Issue 27, Dec 2013) — failure to dispatch offeree board circular under TC Rule 8.4; Cold Shoulder Order (2 years) + public censure. SFC Takeovers and Mergers Panel decision re ENM Holdings Ltd (announcement 2 July 2015) — nominee acquisition hiding concert party stake to avoid mandatory offer; Cold Shoulder Orders (10 years / 2 years). C. IRAC Application Points Issue : classify first — is the question about (a) prospectus liability, (b) listing/continuing obligations, (c) disclosure of interests, (d) takeovers, or (e) market misconduct? 每類有唔同嘅 statute/rule source，分清 SFO（刑事/民事法律責任）vs Listing Rules/TC（監管後果）係第一步。 Rule : state the pinpoint provision — e.g. insider dealing = s.270 SFO + definition of inside information s.245 + connected person s.247; disclosure of interests = ss.310/341/316/344 SFO; mandatory offer = 30% under TC; prospectus misstatement = s.40 (civil) / s.40A (criminal) CWUMPO. Application : map facts to elements one by one — for insider dealing check (i) information connection (specific? not generally known? price sensitive? — apply Chan Pak Hoe and Leung Chi Keung ); (ii) person connection (director/employee/substantial shareholder or tippee); (iii) dealing limb vs counselling/procuring limb vs disclosure limb; then consider defences (ss.271–273). Conclusion : decisive — e.g. "Therefore X engaged in insider dealing under s.270 SFO and Y, as tippee, is equally liable." 如果涉及 Listing Rules 違反，結論要講明後果係監管制裁（public censure / Cold Shoulder Order / delisting），唔係刑事責任。 考試伏位 : (1) spouse/children/controlled company shares are deemed interests — hiding by transferring to spouse does NOT escape Part XV; (2) negotiation stage information can still be "specific"; (3) 30% trigger counts concert parties' aggregate holdings; (4) compliance with Listing Rules ≠ compliance with CWUMPO prospectus law; (5) GEM vs Main Board thresholds 數字要熟（HK$80m 3 yr profit / HK$30m 2 yr cash flow; HK$500m vs HK$150m mkt cap）。 易混淆概念對比 Comparison 1: Market misconduct — civil regime vs criminal regime under the SFO 項目 Civil regime (Part XIII SFO) Criminal regime (Part XIV SFO) Forum Market Misconduct Tribunal (chaired by High Court judge/former judge) Criminal courts Provisions s.270 (insider dealing), ss.274–278 ss.291–299 (mirror provisions, e.g. s.291 mirrors s.270) Standard of proof Balance of probabilities Beyond reasonable doubt Enforcer SFC (proceedings before MMT) Prosecution (DoJ) Outcome Regulatory/civil orders (e.g. Cold Shoulder Order, disqualification, disgorgement) Criminal sanctions (fines, imprisonment) 點樣分辨：睇題目講 "market misconduct" 定 "offence/charged"。MMT 處理 civil limb；同一行為可以同時觸發兩個 regime。考試伏位：唔好以為 insider dealing 只係刑事 — LP 強調 dual regime，寫答案要兩邊都提。 Comparison 2: Insider dealing (s.270) vs False trading (s.274) vs Price rigging (s.275) 項目 Insider dealing (s.270) False trading (s.274) Price rigging (s.275) Core vice Trading on / tipping inside information (unfair informational advantage) Creating false or misleading appearance of active trading or of the market Wash sale or fictitious/artificial transaction affecting the price Key element Inside information + connected person + deal/counsel/disclose Intention to create false appearance (wash sales, matched orders); real chance suffices No change in beneficial ownership + effect/intention to move or stabilise price Defence ss.271–273 (e.g. no profit motive, Chinese walls) s.274(6): purposes did not include creating false appearance s.275(4): same structure as s.274(6) Leading case SFC v Chan Pak Hoe ; SFC v Young Bik Fung ; Leung Chi Keung v MMT HKSAR v Fu Kor Kuen Patrick (defence succeeded — rebate farming) HKSAR v Li Jialin ("price" = nominal price) 點樣分辨：問「佢係咪知咗啲未公開嘅價格敏感消息先買賣？」→ insider dealing。問「佢係咪左手交右手製造交投暢旺假象？」→ false trading（重點係 appearance of activity）。問「左手交右手之餘，效果係推高/穩定個價？」→ price rigging。考試伏位：false trading 同 price rigging 都涉及 wash sales，分別在於 aim/effect 係 "appearance of trading/market" 定 "price"；一個事實可以同時構成兩者，記住分開討論。 Phase 2 閃卡 Card 1 Front: Under the SFO, which body hears civil market misconduct proceedings, and how is it constituted? Back: The Market Misconduct Tribunal (MMT), established under Part XIII of the Securities and Futures Ordinance (Cap. 571). It is independent of the SFC and the government; chaired by a judge or former judge of the High Court of Hong Kong. Civil regime: balance of probabilities; the criminal regime sits separately in Part XIV (ss.291–299, beyond reasonable doubt). 💬 白話解釋：SFC 係「捉人」嗰個，MMT 係「審案」嗰個（民事線），記住 Part XIII = civil、Part XIV = criminal，考試成日問 dual regime。 Card 2 Front: What does s.38(3) of the CWUMPO prohibit, and what are the main prospectus exemptions under Sch.17? Back: S.38(3) CWUMPO (Cap. 32): a company must not offer shares to the public without a prospectus complying with the CWUMPO. Sch.17 exemptions: offers to professional investors (incl. individuals with portfolio ≥ HK$8m); minimum consideration ≥ HK$500,000; offers to ≤ 50 persons or total consideration ≤ HK$5m; offers to qualifying persons (directors/employees/officers/consultants); charity/educational establishments; takeovers/share repurchases compliant with the Takeover Codes. Also: underwriting invitations in good faith (s.38(3)(a)); SFC exemption power (s.38A). 💬 白話解釋：招股就一定要招股書，但係「專業投資者、大額、少人數、自己友」呢幾類就豁免。記三個數字：HK$8m（portfolio）、HK$500,000（minimum consideration）、50 人 / HK$5m（small scale）。 Card 3 Front: State the three alternative financial tests for a Main Board listing (LR Ch.8, as from Jan 2022). Back: Profit test: profit ≥ HK$35m in the most recent year AND ≥ HK$45m aggregate for the two preceding years (3 year track record; total mkt cap ≥ HK$500m). Market cap/Revenue/Cash flow test: mkt cap ≥ HK$2bn; revenue ≥ HK$500m (latest audited year); positive aggregate operating cash flow ≥ HK$100m over 3 preceding years. Market cap/Revenue test: mkt cap ≥ HK$4bn; revenue ≥ HK$500m (latest audited year). All tests: 3 year management continuity, 1 year ownership continuity, ≥ 25% public float, ≥ 300 shareholders, ≥ 3 INEDs (≥ 1/3 of board). 💬 白話解釋：主板三條路 —「有盈利」、「有市值有收入有現金流」、「超大市值有收入」。GEM 就簡單啲：兩年正經營現金流 ≥ HK$30m + 市值 ≥ HK$150m。數字係必考位。 Card 4 Front: Define "inside information" under s.245 of the SFO. Back: Information: 1. About (i) a listed corporation, (ii) a shareholder or officer of it, or (iii) its listed securities or their derivatives; 2. Specific — sufficient particularity to be identified, defined and unequivocally expressed ( SFC v Chan Pak Hoe Pablo (2011) 5 HKC 484 ); 3. Not generally known to persons accustomed or likely to deal in those securities; and 4. Likely to materially affect the price of the listed securities if generally known. 💬 白話解釋：四個元素 = 「關於間公司/股東/證券」+「具體」+「未公開」+「會郁個價」。記住 Chan Pak Hoe：講緊嘅交易傾緊、仲未簽，都可以係 specific information — 唔係謠言咁虛就得。 Card 5 Front: What are the three limbs of insider dealing under s.270 of the SFO, and who is a "connected person"? Back: A person connected with a listed corporation, having information he knows is inside information, who: (1) deals in the listed securities of the corporation or a related corporation; (2) counsels or procures another to deal; or (3) discloses the information knowing/having reasonable cause to believe the other will deal or procure another to deal. Connected person (s.247): director, employee or substantial shareholder of the listed corporation or a related corporation (parent/subsidiary/sister). Tippees who receive inside information from a connected person and deal are also caught. Defences: ss.271–273 (onus on defendant, balance of probabilities). 💬 白話解釋：三招都中 — 自己買賣、叫人買賣、爆畀人知佢會買賣。收料嗰個（tippee）都一齊中。考試鍾意考「淨係講咗畀朋友聽」夠唔夠成 — 答案係夠（disclosure limb）。 Card 6 Front: When is a mandatory general offer triggered under the Takeover Codes, and what is the relevance of "acting in concert"? Back: Trigger: a person initially holding less than 30% of voting rights acquires voting rights taking his holding to 30% or more of the voting rights of the listed company. Concert parties: the Takeover Codes aggregate the collective holdings of persons acting in concert when testing the 30% threshold. Effect: the offeror must make a general offer to all shareholders, protecting minorities' right to exit on a change of control ( ENM Holdings — hiding a concert party stake via nominees breached the Codes; Cold Shoulder Orders imposed). 💬 白話解釋：一過 30% 就要向全部股東提出全面收購，冇得揀。搵人代持（nominee）夾埋過 30% 都照計 — ENM 案就係咁，結果 Cold Shoulder Order 十年唔准掂市場。 Card 7 Front: Distinguish a "notifiable transaction" from a "connected transaction" under the Listing Rules, and outline the key requirements for a connected transaction. Back: Notifiable transactions (LR Ch.14): classified by SIZE using five ratios (assets, profits, revenue, consideration, equity capital) — share / disclosable / major / very substantial disposal / very substantial acquisition / reverse takeover. Connected transactions (LR Ch.14A): classified by PARTIES — transaction with a connected person (director, chief executive, ≥10% substantial shareholder, past director within 12 months, close relatives, associates). Connected transaction requirements: written agreement (14A.34); annual report disclosure (14A.71/49); announcement (14A.35/36); independent shareholders' approval with interested shareholders abstaining (14A.36–39); independent board committee of INEDs (14A.40–43); independent financial adviser (14A.44–45); circular (14A.46–48). 💬 白話解釋：Notifiable 睇「幾大單」，Connected 睇「同邊個做」。Connected transaction 因為唔係 arm's length，所以要獨立股東批准 + INED 委員會 + 獨立財務顧問三重保障，利益相關股東要避席唔准投票。 Card 8 Front: What are the civil and criminal liabilities for misstatements in a prospectus, and the respective defences? Back: Civil — s.40 CWUMPO: false or misleading statement (incl. material omission); directors, promoters, the company and persons who authorised issue liable to compensate subscribers (s.40(1), (7)). Defences: issued without consent; reasonable grounds to believe the statement true. Civil — s.108 SFO: fraudulent/reckless/negligent misrepresentation inducing subscription; damages (inapplicable where s.40 CWUMPO applies). Criminal — s.40A CWUMPO: authorising issue of a prospectus with an untrue statement. Defences: statement immaterial; reasonable grounds to believe and did believe it true up to issue. Criminal — s.107 SFO: fraudulent or reckless misrepresentation to induce acquisition/subscription. Also: s.277 SFO (false/misleading disclosure inducing transactions — market misconduct); general law of misrepresentation; conspiracy to defraud. 💬 白話解釋：招股書講大話，民事刑事都走唔甩。民事主戰場係 s.40 CWUMPO（董事、promoters、公司都要賠）；刑事係 s.40A CWUMPO 同 s.107 SFO。防線係「有合理理由相信係真」或「唔關我事我冇同意出」。 本章急救詞彙 EN Term 繁中白話 English Model Sentence Initial Public Offering (IPO) 公司第一次向公眾發售股份 The first time a company offers its shares to the public is known as an Initial Public Offering. Prospectus 招股書 — 向公眾投資者介紹公司嘅文件，受 CWUMPO 嚴格規管 Under s.38(3) of the CWUMPO, a company must not offer shares to the public without a compliant prospectus. Sponsor 保薦人 — 持 Type 6 牌照、幫公司做上市申請同盡職審查嘅機構 A sponsor must be licensed for Type 6 regulated activities (advising on corporate finance) and must conduct due diligence on the listing applicant. Public float 公眾持股量 — 上市公司至少要 25% 股份喺公眾手上 An issuer must maintain a public float of at least 25% of its total issued share capital at all times under Chapter 13 of the Listing Rules. Connected person 關連人士 — 董事、主要股東（≥10%）、過去 12 個月嘅董事及佢哋嘅 associates A substantial shareholder holding 10% or more of a listed issuer is a connected person under Chapter 14A of the Listing Rules. Mandatory general offer 強制性全面收購 — 持股達 30% 就要向全體股東提出收購 When a person's holding reaches 30% of the voting rights, the Takeover Codes require a mandatory general offer to all shareholders. Inside information 內幕消息 — 具體、未公開、會重大影響股價嘅消息（s.245 SFO） Inside information is specific information not generally known which would likely materially affect the price of the listed securities if generally known. Cold Shoulder Order 冷淡對待令 — 禁止違規者直接或間接參與證券市場嘅制裁 The Takeovers Panel imposed a Cold Shoulder Order denying the director access to the securities markets for ten years.

title: M10 Chapter 12: Listed Companies and the Regulation of Financial Markets — Phase 3 Answers
headings: M10 Chapter 12: Listed Companies and the Regulation of Financial Markets — Phase 3 Answers
excerpt: M10 Chapter 12: Listed Companies and the Regulation of Financial Markets — Phase 3 Answers Q1 — Answer: B Model Answer (EN): The Listing Rules are made pursuant…
text: M10 Chapter 12: Listed Companies and the Regulation of Financial Markets — Phase 3 Answers Q1 — Answer: B Model Answer (EN): The Listing Rules are made pursuant to s.23 of the Securities and Futures Ordinance (Cap. 571) but are not statute. They are a set of rules applicable to issuers who choose to list on the HKEX — effectively the "playbook" of the HKEX. Breach of the Listing Rules does not give rise to criminal or civil liability per se; the consequences are regulatory: the HKEX may impose a private reprimand, a public statement with criticism, a public censure, a requisition for rectification, and at the extreme, delisting or rejection of a listing application. 解題思路（繁中）: 呢題考 Listing Rules 嘅法律地位，係 LP 12.1.3.3 嘅核心比較。A 錯：Listing Rules 唔係立法會制定嘅 primary legislation，違反亦唔會有刑事責任。C 錯：Listing Rules 由 HKEX 頒布（依據 SFO s.23），唔係 SFC 嘅 subsidiary legislation；MMT 處理嘅係 SFO 下嘅 market misconduct，唔關 Listing Rules 事。D 錯：LP 冇講 Listing Rules 只適用於香港註冊公司；規則綁定嘅係所有選擇喺 HKEX 上市嘅 issuers。B 係唯一準確描述「非法例、無刑事民事責任、但 HKEX 有監管制裁（最嚴重係除牌）」嘅選項。 Rule Check: Securities and Futures Ordinance (Cap. 571) s.23; LP §12.1.3.3 (Listing Rules: Legal Status and Enforcement). Common Trap（繁中）: 學生最易將 Listing Rules 當成法例嚟答「違反會坐監/罰款」。記住分層：SFO = statute（刑事+民事責任）；Listing Rules / Takeover Codes = 監管規則（public censure、Cold Shoulder Order、delisting）。考試凡問 "consequences of breach" 一定要分清呢兩層。 Q2 — Answer: C Model Answer (EN): Under s.310 of the Securities and Futures Ordinance (Cap. 571), a substantial shareholder of a listed corporation is a person (individual or corporation) who is interested in 5% or more of any class of voting share capital of the listed corporation. Such a person must disclose the interest under Part XV of the SFO, and the listed corporation must keep a register of the disclosed interests (s.336 of the SFO). "Interest" is widely defined and includes deemed interests through a spouse, children, controlled corporations and trusts (ss.316 and 344 of the SFO). 解題思路（繁中）: 呢題考精準嘅百分比門檻，四個選項全部都係本章出現過嘅數字，所以係典型「鄰近概念」distractors。A（10%）係 Chapter 14A Listing Rules 下 "connected person" 嘅 substantial shareholder 門檻 — 唔同 regime 唔同數字。B（25%）係 public float 嘅最低要求。D（30%）係 Takeover Codes 下 mandatory general offer 嘅觸發線。C（5%）先係 SFO Part XV s.310 嘅 substantial shareholder 披露門檻。 Rule Check: Securities and Futures Ordinance (Cap. 571) ss.310, 316, 336, 344; LP §12.3.2.4 (Disclosure of Interests). Common Trap（繁中）: 四個百分比（5% / 10% / 25% / 30%）分別屬於四個唔同制度：Part XV 披露 5%、connected person 10%、public float 25%、mandatory offer 30%。考試最鍾意將佢哋溝埋，溫習時要整齊排成一條線記。 Q3 — Answer: B Model Answer (EN): Wendy has engaged in insider dealing under s.270 of the SFO. Issue: whether a sale made to avoid a loss, before disclosure of an adverse confidential judgment, constitutes insider dealing. Rule: under s.245 of the SFO, inside information is specific information about a listed corporation, not generally known to persons likely to deal in its securities, which would likely materially affect the price if generally known ( SFC v Chan Pak Hoe Pablo (2011) 5 HKC 484 ). Under s.270, a person connected with the corporation (a director, employee or substantial shareholder — s.247) who deals in its listed securities whilst possessing information she knows to be inside information engages in insider dealing. Application: the judgment is specific (a decided court order for a quantified sum), non public and plainly price sensitive (40% of net assets; the price fell 30% on announcement). Wendy is an officer/employee of the company and dealt in its shares. The s.271(3) defence (absence of a profit or loss avoidance motive) cannot assist her: her very purpose was to avoid a loss. Conclusion: Wendy engaged in insider dealing under s.270 of the SFO (and is equally exposed to the mirror criminal offence in s.291 under Part XIV). 解題思路（繁中）: IRAC 四步：(I) 賣股避損係咪 insider dealing；(R) s.245 定義 + s.270 dealing limb + s.247 connected person；(A) 逐個元素對應事實 — 判決具體（有判決金額）、未公開、price sensitive（公佈後跌 30% 證明），Wendy 係 company secretary = officer/employee，佢落盤賣股 = deals；(C) 成立。A 錯：s.271(3) 嘅 defence 係「冇謀利 或避損 意圖」— Wendy 正正係為咗避損，所以反而係失敗關鍵，唔係免責理由。C 錯：false trading (s.274) 重點係製造交投/市場假象（wash sales、matched orders），單純一個人真實賣自己嘅股完全唔啱。D 錯：s.278 要求兩宗或以上交易且意圖誘使他人買賣，Wendy 得一次真實沽貨，冇呢個意圖。 Rule Check: Securities and Futures Ordinance (Cap. 571) ss.245, 247, 270, 271(3), 291; Securities and Futures Commission v Chan Pak Hoe Pablo (2011) 5 HKC 484 . Common Trap（繁中）: 學生最常犯兩個錯：(1) 以為「冇賺錢」就冇罪 — 法例包埋 loss avoidance，s.271(3) defence 反而要求你證明連避損意圖都冇；(2) 見到「影響股價」就亂揀 s.274/s.278 — 記住 insider dealing 嘅 fingerprint 係「未公開價格敏感消息 + 自己人 + 買賣/教唆/披露」。 Q4 — Answer: B Model Answer (EN): Issue: whether the joint acquisition triggers a mandatory general offer. Rule: under the Codes on Takeovers and Mergers and Share Buy backs, a person who initially holds less than 30% of the voting rights of a listed company and acquires voting rights taking his holding to 30% or more must make a mandatory general offer to all shareholders; the collective holdings of persons acting in concert are aggregated for this purpose. Application: Mr. Fu (18%) and Ms. Kam (14%) consult and vote together under a long standing arrangement — they are acting in concert, and their holdings are aggregated (32% even before the latest acquisition, 34% after). The 30% threshold is therefore crossed, triggering the mandatory general offer obligation; concealing the arrangement (as in the ENM Holdings decision, where Cold Shoulder Orders were imposed) does not avoid it. Conclusion: a mandatory general offer is required. 解題思路（繁中）: A 錯：呢個係題目刻意設計嘅陷阱 — 單獨睇每人都低過 30%，但 Takeover Codes 明文會將 acting in concert 人士嘅持股加埋計，18% + 14% + 2% = 34%，一早過線。C 錯：Part XV 披露責任（個人 ≥5%）固然存在，但唔係「唯一」責任 — 題目問嘅係收購義務，而 acting in concert 過 30% 觸發 mandatory general offer 先係核心 issue；揀 C 即係 spot 錯 issue。D 錯：呢個係將 connected transaction / notifiable transaction 嘅股東批准機制亂搬過嚟，Takeover Codes 下冇呢個程序。B 準確點出 concert party aggregation 同 mandatory offer 後果。 Rule Check: Codes on Takeovers and Mergers and Share Buy backs (mandatory general offer at 30% of voting rights; aggregation of concert parties' holdings); SFC Takeovers and Mergers Panel Decision in Relation to Shares of ENM Holdings Limited (announcement dated 2 July 2015) ; LP §12.3.3.1. Common Trap（繁中）: 最大伏位係「逐個人單獨計」而忽略 acting in concert aggregation — ENM 案就係用 nominee 隱藏一致行動持股，結果中 Cold Shoulder Order。答題時見到「朋友/親人一齊投票、代持、聯名公司買股」就要即刻諗 concert parties。 Q5 — Answer: B Model Answer (EN): Issue: whether Kelvin's self dealing circular trades are conclusively false trading, or whether a statutory defence is available. Rule: wash sale style dealings fall within the deeming provision in s.295(5) of the SFO (offers to sell and buy at substantially the same price involving the same or an associate's offers), but s.295(7) provides a statutory defence — as does s.274(6) for the civil misconduct — where the defendant proves on the balance of probabilities that the purposes of the transactions did not include creating a false or misleading appearance of active trading ( HKSAR v Fu Kor Kuen Patrick (2012) 15 HKCFAR 524 ). Application: Kelvin's daily self dealing at substantially the same prices falls within s.295(5). However, the evidence of a genuine economic purpose — earning commission rebates ("commission farming") — may, as in Fu Kor Kuen Patrick , support an inference that creating a false appearance was not among his purposes; the persuasive burden lies on him. Conclusion: Kelvin is prima facie caught but may succeed on the statutory defence on the facts given. 解題思路（繁中）: 呢題係 hard tier，考「deeming provision + 法定免責辯護」兩層分析，原型係 CFA 嘅 Fu Kor Kuen Patrick 案。A 錯：自我交易只係觸發 s.295(5) 嘅 deemed false trading，唔係「conclusively guilty」— s.295(7) 明確畀辯護。C 錯：price rigging (s.275) 同 false trading 係兩個獨立罪名，檢控官揀咗 false trading 條 charge 就唔會「只能」變 price rigging；而且本案重點係交投假象唔係價格操縱。D 錯：自己同名戶口之間嘅買賣仍然係 "transactions"，正正係 wash sale 嘅典型。B 準確覆述判決：burden 喺被告、balance of probabilities、真正經濟目的（賺回佣）可以成立 defence。 Rule Check: Securities and Futures Ordinance (Cap. 571) ss.274(6), 295(1)(a), 295(5), 295(7); HKSAR v Fu Kor Kuen Patrick (2012) 15 HKCFAR 524 . Common Trap（繁中）: 學生通常背咗「wash sale = false trading」就以為一定入罪，忽略埋 s.274(6)/s.295(7) 嘅 purpose defence 同埋被告要「證明一個 negative」（證明自己冇製造假象嘅意圖）。考試遇到 circular trading 題，記住三段式：deeming → burden on defendant → genuine economic purpose 可脫身。

title: M10 Chapter 12: Listed Companies and the Regulation of Financial Markets — Phase 3 Quiz
headings: M10 Chapter 12: Listed Companies and the Regulation of Financial Markets — Phase 3 Quiz
excerpt: M10 Chapter 12: Listed Companies and the Regulation of Financial Markets — Phase 3 Quiz Rules: Closed book · 15 minutes · 5 questions · Submit as 1. … 2. … 3. ……
text: M10 Chapter 12: Listed Companies and the Regulation of Financial Markets — Phase 3 Quiz Rules: Closed book · 15 minutes · 5 questions · Submit as 1. … 2. … 3. … 4. … 5. … — 超時如實申報 Q1. Which of the following statements about the Listing Rules of the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong is CORRECT? A. The Listing Rules are primary legislation enacted by the Legislative Council, and breach of them is a criminal offence. B. The Listing Rules are made pursuant to s.23 of the Securities and Futures Ordinance (Cap. 571); breach does not give rise to criminal or civil liability per se, but the HKEX may impose regulatory sanctions such as a public censure or delisting. C. The Listing Rules are subsidiary legislation made by the Securities and Futures Commission, enforceable through proceedings in the Market Misconduct Tribunal. D. The Listing Rules bind only companies incorporated in Hong Kong and have no application to overseas issuers listed on the HKEX. Q2. Under Part XV of the Securities and Futures Ordinance (Cap. 571), a "substantial shareholder" of a listed corporation who must disclose his interest is a person interested in what percentage of any class of voting share capital of the listed corporation? A. 10% or more B. 25% or more C. 5% or more D. 30% or more Q3. Wendy is the company secretary of Harvest Bright Ltd, a company listed on the Main Board of the HKEX. At a board meeting she learns that the High Court has just handed down a confidential judgment ordering Harvest Bright Ltd to pay damages equal to 40% of its net assets. No announcement has been made. Before the company announces the judgment, Wendy sells her entire holding of Harvest Bright shares through her brokerage account, avoiding a substantial loss when the price falls 30% on the announcement. Applying the Securities and Futures Ordinance (Cap. 571), which of the following is the MOST accurate analysis of Wendy's conduct? A. No liability arises because Wendy did not make any profit from the sale. B. Wendy has engaged in insider dealing under s.270 of the SFO: she is a connected person (an officer/employee) who dealt in the listed securities whilst possessing information she knew to be specific, non public and price sensitive, and the absence of a profit motive does not assist her because her purpose was to avoid a loss. C. Wendy has engaged in false trading under s.274 of the SFO because her sale created a misleading appearance of active trading in the shares. D. Wendy has engaged in stock market manipulation under s.278 of the SFO because her sale was likely to reduce the price of the shares. Q4. Mr. Fu holds 18% of the voting rights of Sunrise Logistics Ltd, a listed company. His business partner Ms. Kam holds 14%. They have a long standing arrangement under which they consult each other and vote together on all resolutions of the company, and they have just jointly acquired a further 2% through a company they jointly control. None of the acquisitions has been disclosed to the market as giving rise to any offer obligation. Applying the Codes on Takeovers and Mergers and Share Buy backs, which of the following is the MOST accurate conclusion? A. No obligation arises because neither Mr. Fu nor Ms. Kam individually holds 30% or more of the voting rights. B. Mr. Fu and Ms. Kam are persons acting in concert; their holdings are aggregated (34% in total), so the 30% threshold has been crossed and a mandatory general offer to all shareholders of Sunrise Logistics Ltd is triggered. C. The only obligation is for Mr. Fu and Ms. Kam to disclose their interests under Part XV of the SFO, because their individual holdings each exceed 5%. D. Sunrise Logistics Ltd must convene a general meeting to approve the acquisitions by special resolution before they take effect. Q5. For several weeks, Kelvin bought and sold the same listed warrants every trading day using two securities accounts under his own name, selling to himself at substantially the same prices. His trades accounted for the bulk of the daily turnover in those warrants. The evidence shows Kelvin's dominant purpose was to generate commission rebates offered by his broker for high trading volume, and there is no evidence he intended to mislead the market about trading activity. Kelvin is charged with creating a false or misleading appearance of active trading contrary to ss.295(1)(a) and (6) of the SFO. Applying HKSAR v Fu Kor Kuen Patrick (2012) 15 HKCFAR 524 , which of the following is the MOST accurate statement of Kelvin's position? A. Kelvin is inevitably guilty: any wash sale is conclusively an offence and no defence is available once self dealing is proved. B. Kelvin's conduct falls within the deeming provision (s.295(5)), but he may rely on the statutory defence (s.295(7), mirroring s.274(6)) if he proves on the balance of probabilities that the purposes of his trades did not include creating a false or misleading appearance — and a genuine economic purpose of earning rebates may satisfy that defence. C. Kelvin is not guilty because price rigging under s.275, not false trading, is the only possible charge where beneficial ownership does not change. D. Kelvin is not guilty because trading between accounts under the same name can never amount to a "transaction in securities" within the meaning of the SFO.
