headings: M6 Chapter 2: Fair Value Measurement — Phase 3 Model Answers
excerpt: M6 Chapter 2: Fair Value Measurement — Phase 3 Model Answers Q1 — Answer: B Model Answer (EN): Under HKFRS 13, fair value is defined as the price that would be …
text: M6 Chapter 2: Fair Value Measurement — Phase 3 Model Answers Q1 — Answer: B Model Answer (EN): Under HKFRS 13, fair value is defined as the price that would be received to sell an asset (or paid to transfer a liability) in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date . Statement B reproduces this definition exactly. 解題思路（繁中）: 呢題係定義題，考兩個核心原則。A 錯 — "paid to acquire" 係 entry price ，fair value 係 exit price （賣出唔係買入）。C 錯 — fair value 係 market based measurement，用 market participants 嘅假設，唔係 entity specific 嘅自用現金流（嗰個係 value in use 嘅概念）。D 錯 — 賣家財困下嘅即時出售係 distress sale / forced transaction ，唔符合 orderly transaction 嘅假設（要有足夠市場曝光期）。考試伏位：定義每個字都有分 — "received to sell"、"orderly"、"market participants"、"measurement date" 缺一不可。 Rule Check: HKFRS 13.9 (definition); HKFRS 13.A (orderly transaction) Common Trap（繁中）: 同學成日將 "received to sell" 同 "paid to acquire" 調轉，又以為用自己公司嘅 forecast 就得 — 記住：exit price + 市場參與者角度，entity specific 假設永遠唔得。 Q2 — Answer: C Model Answer (EN): Under HKFRS 13, transport costs are adjusted in measuring fair value because location is a characteristic of the asset (a commodity). Transaction costs (brokerage fees) are not adjusted — they are not a characteristic of the asset; they are specific to the transaction and differ depending on how the entity transacts. Fair value per bag = market price − HK$25 transport costs only. 解題思路（繁中）: 口訣「運輸扣得，佣金唔扣得」。A 錯 — 連 brokerage fees 都扣，混淆咗「揀 most advantageous market」同「計 fair value」兩個步驟（揀市場時先會扣 transaction costs）。B 錯 — 倒轉咗兩者嘅處理。D 錯 — transport costs 係資產特性（location），必須扣。考試伏位：呢個雙重處理係 LP Knowledge Check 同款伏位 — transaction costs 只用嚟揀 most advantageous market，計最終 FV 時永遠唔扣。 Rule Check: HKFRS 13.25–26 (transaction costs and transport costs, as applied in LP §2.1.2) Common Trap（繁中）: 見到題目兩個成本都列出嚟，就以為兩個都要處理 — 其實一個扣一個唔扣。仲要記住「揀市場」同「計 FV」對 transaction costs 嘅處理係相反嘅。 Q3 — Answer: C (HK$785) Model Answer (EN): Step 1 — Determine the principal market (market with the greatest volume and level of activity, based on market wide data): West market (80,000 units) . Step 2 — Fair value is the price in the principal market, adjusted for transport costs but not for transaction costs: Fair value = HK$800 − HK$15 = HK$785 per unit . 解題思路（繁中）: 三步走：(1) 有交易量數據 → 一定有 principal market（West，80,000 units 最旺），即使 Central 價錢最高都唔准轉場；(2) FV = 該市場價 − transport costs；(3) transaction costs 唔扣。A (HK$800) 錯 — 直接用報價，唔記得扣 transport costs。B (HK$805) 錯 — 用咗 Central market（840 − 35），係「邊個價高用邊個」嘅直覺錯誤。D (HK$760) 錯 — 連 transaction costs 都扣埋（800 − 15 − 25），混淆咗 most advantageous market 嘅 net proceeds 計法。考試伏位：principal market 存在時，most advantageous market 完全唔使理。 Rule Check: HKFRS 13.17–18 (principal market; most advantageous market only in its absence); HKFRS 13.19 (access to the market); HKFRS 13.25–26 (transport costs adjusted, transaction costs not) Common Trap（繁中）: 兩大錯法 — (1) 用價錢最高嘅市場（應該用交易量最高嘅）；(2) 將 transaction costs 扣埋入 FV（佢哋只用嚟揀 most advantageous market）。 Q4 — Answer: C Model Answer (EN): The valuation uses both Level 2 inputs (P/E multiples of comparable listed companies) and Level 3 inputs (the internally developed discount for lack of marketability). Under HKFRS 13, a fair value measurement is categorised in its entirety in the same level as the lowest level input that is significant to the entire measurement . Because the unobservable adjustment is significant , the whole measurement is classified as Level 3 . 解題思路（繁中）: 呢題考「in entirety」規則。A 錯 — comparable 公司上市唔等於輸入係 Level 1；Level 1 要 identical item 喺活躍市場嘅未調整報價，unlisted shares 永遠唔會係。B 錯 — 雖然 multiples 係 observable，但重大 unobservable adjustment 會將成個 measurement 拉落 Level 3（呢個係最似啱嘅 distractor — 如果個 discount 唔重大 ，先會歸 Level 2）。D 錯 — HKFRS 13 唔准拆開分級，成個 measurement 只歸一個 level。考試伏位：關鍵詞係 "significant" — 題目改做 "not significant" 答案就會變 Level 2（對照 LP Knowledge Check Q7(ii)）。 Rule Check: HKFRS 13.72–90 (fair value hierarchy and categorisation in its entirety) Common Trap（繁中）: 同學見到大部分輸入係 observable 就揀 Level 2 — 記住一粒老鼠屎（significant unobservable input）就足以令成個估值降級做 Level 3。 Q5 — Answer: HK$10,000 Model Answer (EN): Step 1 — Probability weighted expected cash flows: HK$6,000 × 30% = HK$1,800 HK$10,000 × 40% = HK$4,000 HK$16,000 × 30% = HK$4,800 Expected cash flows = HK$10,600 Step 2 — Discount rate = risk free rate + risk premium = 3.5% + 2.5% = 6% Step 3 — Fair value = HK$10,600 ÷ 1.06 = HK$10,000 解題思路（繁中）: 呢題完全跟 LP Apply and Analyse 3 嘅現值技術框架（Exhibit 2.5）：先計 probability weighted expected cash flows（唔係直接用最可能嘅 HK$10,000），再將 time value of money（risk free rate 3.5%）加上 price for bearing uncertainty（risk premium 2.5%）組成折現率 6%，最後折現。常見錯法：(1) 唔折現直接用 HK$10,600；(2) 只用 risk free rate 折（10,600 ÷ 1.035 = 10,242），漏咗 risk premium；(3) 用最可能現金流 HK$10,000 折現（= 9,434），唔做 probability weighting。三個都係 LP 強調嘅 present value elements 漏咗其中一環。 Rule Check: HKFRS 13.61–62 (income approach / valuation techniques); HKFRS 13.B10–B30 (present value techniques) Common Trap（繁中）: 折現率一定要兩層加埋 — risk free rate + risk premium；同埋 expected cash flows 係 probability weighted，唔係「最可能發生」嗰個數。

excerpt: M6 Chapter 2: Fair Value Measurement — Phase 3 Quiz Rules: Closed book · 15 minutes · 5 questions · Submit as 1. … 2. … 3. … 4. … 5. … — 超時如實申報 Question 1 (MCQ)…
text: M6 Chapter 2: Fair Value Measurement — Phase 3 Quiz Rules: Closed book · 15 minutes · 5 questions · Submit as 1. … 2. … 3. … 4. … 5. … — 超時如實申報 Question 1 (MCQ) Mantis Limited is measuring the fair value of a warehouse in accordance with HKFRS 13 Fair Value Measurement. Which of the following statements correctly describes fair value under HKFRS 13? A. The price that would be paid to acquire an equivalent asset in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date B. The price that would be received to sell the asset in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date C. The entity specific value of the asset, based on the cash flows the entity itself expects to generate from continuing use D. The price that would be received to sell the asset in an immediate sale when the seller is under financial pressure Question 2 (MCQ) Gecko Logistics Limited is measuring the fair value of a consignment of coffee beans at its year end. The beans must be transported to the selected market, and Gecko will incur transport costs of HK$25 per bag and brokerage fees (transaction costs) of HK$40 per bag on the sale. According to HKFRS 13, which of the following is correct regarding the measurement of the fair value of the coffee beans? A. Both transport costs and brokerage fees are deducted from the market price B. Only the brokerage fees are deducted from the market price C. Only the transport costs are deducted from the market price D. Neither transport costs nor brokerage fees are deducted from the market price Question 3 (Calculation MCQ) Terrapin Trading Limited sells a single product, Model Z, and has access to three markets. Market information at the measurement date is as follows: East market West market Central market Total market trade volume (units, per trade publications) 50,000 80,000 65,000 Price per unit (HK$) 820 800 840 Transport costs per unit (HK$) 20 15 35 Transaction costs per unit (HK$) 30 25 40 In accordance with HKFRS 13, what is the fair value of one unit of Model Z? A. HK$800 B. HK$805 C. HK$785 D. HK$760 Question 4 (MCQ) Heron Holdings Limited holds 8% of the voting shares of Coral Bay Limited, a private company, and measures the investment at fair value at each reporting date in accordance with HKFRS 9 and HKFRS 13. At 31 December 20X8, Heron values the investment using price to earnings multiples of comparable listed companies (an observable input), adjusted by a discount for lack of marketability. The discount is developed from Heron's own internal estimates (an unobservable input) and is assessed as significant to the entire measurement. Within which level of the fair value hierarchy should this fair value measurement be categorised in accordance with HKFRS 13? A. Level 1, because the comparable companies are listed B. Level 2, because the price to earnings multiples are observable inputs C. Level 3 in its entirety, because the significant unobservable adjustment determines the classification D. Partly Level 2 (for the multiples) and partly Level 3 (for the discount) Question 5 (Calculation — short answer) Kingfisher Tech Limited is measuring the fair value of a specialised machine, Model Q, using a present value technique under the income approach in accordance with HKFRS 13. Model Q will generate cash flows for one year only. The possible cash flows and associated probabilities are: Possible cash flows Probability HK$6,000 30% HK$10,000 40% HK$16,000 30% The risk free rate for one year cash flows is 3.5%, and the risk premium for an asset with the same risk profile is 2.5%. Calculate the fair value of Model Q, showing your workings.

excerpt: M6 Chapter 3: Revenue Recognition — Phase 1 速查表 + Phase 2 閃卡 Phase 1 速查表 Learning Objectives 1. Define revenue and distinguish it from other income within the s…
text: M6 Chapter 3: Revenue Recognition — Phase 1 速查表 + Phase 2 閃卡 Phase 1 速查表 Learning Objectives 1. Define revenue and distinguish it from other income within the scope of HKFRS 15 Revenue from Contracts with Customers . 2. Apply the five step revenue recognition model to identify contracts, identify performance obligations, determine the transaction price, allocate it, and recognise revenue when (or as) performance obligations are satisfied (HKFRS 15 para. 2). 3. Determine whether a performance obligation is satisfied over time or at a point in time, and measure progress using output or input methods (HKFRS 15 paras. 35–38, B14–B15). 4. Account for contract costs (costs to obtain and costs to fulfil a contract), right of return, warranties, consignments and principal–agent arrangements. 5. Prepare the presentation and disclosure requirements for revenue, contract balances and capitalised contract costs (HKFRS 15 paras. 113–120). 必背考點 A. Recognition（認唔認、幾時認） Core principle (HKFRS 15 para. 2): recognise revenue to depict the transfer of promised goods or services to customers in an amount that reflects the consideration to which the entity expects to be entitled. The Five Step Model（必背順序）: 1. Identify the contract(s) with a customer 2. Identify the performance obligations in the contract 3. Determine the transaction price 4. Allocate the transaction price to the performance obligations 5. Recognise revenue when (or as) the performance obligation is satisfied Step 1 — Contract criteria (HKFRS 15 para. 9, Exhibit 3.3): account for a contract only when ALL of: approved by all parties (written, oral or customary business practice — para. 10 level); rights to goods/services are identifiable; payment terms are identifiable; contract has commercial substance; it is probable the consideration will be collected (customer is able and intends to pay). A wholly unperformed contract where each party can terminate without penalty is NOT yet a contract (HKFRS 15 para. 12). Step 2 — Performance obligations (HKFRS 15 para. 22): a promise to transfer (a) a distinct good or service (or bundle), or (b) a series of distinct goods/services that are substantially the same with the same pattern of transfer (para. 23). Administrative set up tasks that transfer nothing are NOT performance obligations (para. 25). "Free"/marketing items ARE performance obligations if distinct (no exception for incidental goods). Distinct (HKFRS 15 paras. 27–28) — BOTH required: 1. Capable of being distinct : customer can benefit from it on its own or with readily available resources (regularly sold separately = indicator); 2. Distinct within the context of the contract : promise is separately identifiable from other promises. Indicators of NOT separately identifiable (para. 29): significant integration service; significant modification/customisation; highly interdependent/interrelated. Step 5 — Over time vs point in time (HKFRS 15 paras. 35–37, Exhibit 3.7): satisfied over time if ANY ONE of: 1. customer simultaneously receives and consumes the benefits as the entity performs (e.g. cleaning services); 2. the entity's performance creates or enhances an asset the customer controls as it is created/enhanced; 3. the asset has no alternative use to the entity AND the entity has an enforceable right to payment for performance completed to date (assessed at contract inception and not changed). Otherwise satisfied at a point in time — when the customer gains control . Indicators (para. 38): present right to payment; legal title; physical possession; significant risks and rewards of ownership; customer acceptance. Measuring progress (over time): output methods (value transferred to customer, e.g. time elapsed — 1/12 per month) or input methods (costs incurred to date ÷ total expected costs) — HKFRS 15 paras. B14–B15. Specific issues: Right of return (HKFRS 15 para. B21): recognise revenue only for consideration expected to be entitled to; recognise a refund liability for expected returns AND an asset (right to recover products) with a corresponding adjustment to cost of sales. Revenue IS still recognised on transfer for goods not expected to be returned. Consignments (HKFRS 15 paras. B77–B78): no revenue on delivery to the consignee/dealer — control has not passed. Indicators: entity controls goods until a specified event; entity can require return or redirect goods; dealer has no unconditional obligation to pay. Principal vs Agent (HKFRS 15 paras. B34, B37): an entity is a principal if it controls the good/service before transfer → recognise revenue gross ; an agent arranges for another party to provide it → recognise revenue net (commission) . Indicators of control: primarily responsible for fulfilment; inventory risk; discretion in setting prices. Misidentifying an agent as a principal overstates revenue . B. Measurement（計幾多） Step 3 — Transaction price (HKFRS 15 para. 47–48): the consideration the entity expects to be entitled to, excluding amounts collected on behalf of third parties . Consider four effects: 1. Variable consideration (discounts, rebates, refunds, performance bonuses, penalties — paras. 51–54): estimate using expected value method (probability weighted; many similar contracts) or most likely amount method (only two possible outcomes); apply the chosen method consistently throughout the contract. 2. Significant financing component (paras. 60–65): split into a revenue component (= notional cash selling price, using a discount rate from a separate financing transaction at inception) and a loan component (interest revenue/expense under HKFRS 9). Practical expedient: no adjustment if the financing period is one year or less . Applies even when the offer is advertised as "interest free". 3. Non cash consideration: measure at fair value . 4. Consideration payable to a customer (paras. 70–73): reduce the transaction price, UNLESS the payment is in exchange for a distinct good/service from the customer (then account as a normal purchase from a supplier). Step 4 — Allocation (HKFRS 15 para. 73 & 76): allocate the transaction price to each performance obligation based on relative stand alone selling prices at contract inception. Best evidence = observable price when sold separately (para. 77); list price is NOT presumed to be the SSP; estimate if not observable. Bundle discount (para. 81): allocate proportionately to ALL performance obligations, UNLESS observable evidence shows the discount relates to only one or more (but not all) of them → then allocate only to those. Contract costs (HKFRS 15 paras. 91–100): Costs to obtain (paras. 91–93): capitalise if incremental (would not have been incurred if the contract had not been obtained, e.g. sales commission) and expected to be recovered; OR not incremental but explicitly chargeable to the customer. Practical expedient (para. 94): expense immediately if the amortisation period would be one year or less . Costs to fulfil (paras. 95–96): if within scope of another standard (HKAS 2 / HKAS 16 / HKAS 38) apply that standard; otherwise capitalise only if the costs (1) relate directly to an identifiable contract, (2) generate/enhance resources to satisfy future performance obligations, and (3) are expected to be recovered. Expense as incurred: general & administrative costs (unless explicitly chargeable), wasted materials/labour, costs relating to past performance. Amortisation (paras. 99–100): systematic basis consistent with the transfer of the related goods/services; a change in the expected timing of transfer is a change in accounting estimate . Warranties (Exhibit 3.8): Assurance type (warranty required by law / only assures compliance with agreed specifications, not sold separately) → account under HKAS 37 (provision/expense); revenue recognition unaffected. Service type (customer can buy it separately / provides a service beyond assurance) → separate performance obligation under HKFRS 15 ; allocate transaction price; recognise as contract liability then revenue over the warranty period. C. Key Journal Entries（Dr/Cr 必須平衡） 1. Sale with significant financing component （cash price HK$5,800; nominal HK$6,500 payable in 24 months; 5.86%）: 2. Conditional right to consideration → Contract asset （laptops delivered before server; payment conditional）: 3. Capitalised incremental costs of obtaining a contract （sales commission HK$660,000）: （Non recoverable costs, e.g. base salaries and non reimbursable travel → expense as incurred: Dr Salaries expense / Dr Travel expense, Cr Cash.） 4. Sale with service type warranty （desktop HK$4,400 + extended warranty HK$800, cash HK$5,200 on 1 May 20X2）: D. Disclosure（披露要求） HKFRS 15 requires entity specific disclosures so users understand the nature, amount, timing and uncertainty of revenue and cash flows: Revenue from contracts with customers disclosed separately from other revenue; impairment losses (HKFRS 9) on receivables and contract assets (para. 113). Disaggregation of revenue into categories (e.g. geographical region, customer type, contract type, contract duration, timing of transfer, sales channels). Contract balances (para. 116): opening/closing balances of receivables, contract assets, contract liabilities; revenue recognised that was in the opening contract liability; revenue from performance obligations satisfied in previous periods. Performance obligations (para. 119): when typically satisfied; significant payment terms; nature of goods/services (highlight agency arrangements); obligations for returns/refunds; types of warranties. Transaction price allocated to remaining performance obligations (para. 120): aggregate amount + explanation of when it will be recognised (qualitative or quantitative time bands). Significant judgements affecting amount/timing of revenue (with HKAS 1 material accounting policy information). Capitalised contract costs: judgements, amortisation method, closing balances, amortisation and impairment losses. 易混淆概念對比 Comparison 1: Assurance type Warranty vs Service type Warranty Assurance type warranty Service type warranty Nature Only assures the good complies with agreed specifications (e.g. statutory manufacturer's warranty) Provides a service beyond assurance (e.g. purchased extended warranty) Separate performance obligation? No — bundled with the good Yes Accounting standard HKAS 37 — warranty provision & expense HKFRS 15 — contract liability, then revenue over warranty period Effect on revenue No effect on revenue recognition Transaction price allocated to warranty; defers revenue Total obligation May exceed transaction price (separate HKAS 37 liability) Limited to the transaction price of the contract 📌 點樣分辨： 問自己兩條問題 — (1) 客戶可唔可以 另外買 呢個 warranty？(2) 佢有冇提供 assurance 以外嘅 額外服務 ？兩條都「No」→ assurance type → HKAS 37。 考試伏位： 法律規定嘅 manufacturer warranty 一定係 assurance type；題目話「extended warranty sold separately」→ service type，記住要 allocate transaction price 同認 contract liability，唔好直接全部認做收入。 Comparison 2: Principal vs Agent Principal Agent Nature of promise Provides the specified goods/services itself Arranges for another party to provide them Control test Controls the good/service before transfer to customer Does NOT control before transfer Indicators (HKFRS 15 para. B37) Primarily responsible for fulfilment; bears inventory risk; discretion in setting prices Another party fulfils; no inventory risk; principal sets the price Revenue recognised Gross amount of consideration Net commission/fee only P&L impact Revenue and cost of sales both grossed up Revenue = commission only; no related cost of sales 📌 點樣分辨： 睇邊個 負責履行承諾 、邊個 承擔存貨風險 、邊個 有定價權 。就算 agent 負責收錢（collects cash on behalf of principal），都唔影響 agent 嘅判斷。 考試伏位： 將 agent 錯誤當 principal 會 誇大 revenue （net profit 一樣，但 revenue 同 expense 同時 gross up）—— 呢個正正係 examiner 最鍾意考嘅 implication。 Phase 2 閃卡 Card 1 Front: State the core principle of HKFRS 15 and list, in order, the five steps of the revenue recognition model. Back: Core principle: recognise revenue to depict the transfer of promised goods or services to customers in an amount that reflects the consideration to which the entity expects to be entitled (HKFRS 15 para. 2). Step 1: Identify the contract(s) with a customer Step 2: Identify the performance obligations in the contract Step 3: Determine the transaction price Step 4: Allocate the transaction price to the performance obligations Step 5: Recognise revenue when (or as) each performance obligation is satisfied 💬 白話解釋：五步曲要順序背到出嚟 — 「合約 → 履約義務 → 交易價 → 分攤 → 認收入」。考官報告話好多考生連呢個 basic outline 都寫唔出，呢 5 步係送分位。 Card 2 Front: Under HKFRS 15 para. 9, what five criteria must ALL be met before a contract with a customer is accounted for under the revenue recognition principles? Back: The contract is approved by all parties (written, oral or customary practice); Each party's rights regarding the goods/services are identifiable; Payment terms are identifiable; The contract has commercial substance; It is probable the entity will collect the consideration. Note: a wholly unperformed contract that either party can terminate without penalty is not yet a contract (para. 12). 💬 白話解釋：記住「批咗、權利清、付款清、有實質、收得返」五件事，缺一不可。「收得返」係 probable 層級；另外，大家都可以零代價取消嘅框架協議根本未算 contract，唔好急住認收入。 Card 3 Front: When is a promised good or service "distinct" under HKFRS 15 paras. 27–28? What indicators show promises are NOT separately identifiable? Back: BOTH criteria required: 1. Capable of being distinct — customer can benefit from it on its own or with readily available resources; 2. Distinct within the context of the contract — separately identifiable from other promises. NOT separately identifiable when: significant integration service into a combined output; significant modification/customisation; highly interdependent or interrelated (para. 29). Non distinct items are combined until a distinct bundle is identified. 💬 白話解釋：兩關都要過 —「自己有用」+「喺份合約入面獨立」。賣車連引擎：引擎單獨有用，但合約承諾係「一架車」，integration service 令佢哋綁死 → 一個 performance obligation。「免費贈品」只要 distinct 都要 allocate 價錢。 Card 4 Front: How is variable consideration estimated under HKFRS 15, and when is each estimation method appropriate? Back: Two methods (paras. 51–54): 1. Expected value — probability weighted sum; appropriate for a large number of similar contracts; 2. Most likely amount — single most likely outcome; appropriate when only two possible outcomes (e.g. performance bonus achieved or not). Use the method that better predicts the entitlement; apply it consistently throughout the contract; use all reasonably available information. 💬 白話解釋：「大量類似合約 → expected value（加權平均）；得兩個結果 → most likely amount（二選一）」。揀咗方法就要一份合約內貫徹用，唔可以中途換。 Card 5 Front: How does an entity account for a significant financing component in a contract with a customer? What practical expedient is available? Back: Split consideration into a revenue component (notional cash selling price , discounted at a rate reflecting a separate financing transaction at inception) and a loan component (interest revenue or interest expense under HKFRS 9). Entity financing the customer (payment after delivery) → interest revenue ; customer financing the entity (payment in advance) → interest expense . Practical expedient: no adjustment if the financing period is one year or less . Applies even to arrangements advertised as "interest free" if the contract price differs from the cash selling price. 💬 白話解釋：「零息分期」≠ 冇融資成分！只要合約價高過現金價、還款期超過一年，就要拆開 revenue（用現金價）同 interest revenue 兩部份。一年或以內可以偷懶唔拆。 Card 6 Front: State the three criteria for a performance obligation satisfied OVER TIME, and the indicators that control of a good has passed for point in time recognition. Back: Over time if ANY ONE (HKFRS 15 paras. 35–37): 1. Customer simultaneously receives and consumes the benefits as the entity performs; 2. Entity creates/enhances an asset the customer controls as it is created/enhanced; 3. Asset has no alternative use to the entity AND the entity has an enforceable right to payment for performance completed to date. Point in time — control indicators (para. 38): present right to payment; legal title; physical possession; significant risks and rewards; customer acceptance. Progress: output methods (e.g. time elapsed) or input methods (e.g. costs incurred ÷ total expected costs) (paras. B14–B15). 💬 白話解釋：三個 over time 條件係「ANY 一個中就得」，常見伏位：第三個條件要「no alternative use AND enforceable right to payment」 兩者齊全 。得返「起咗一半嘅資產冇替代用途」但冇收錢權 → 仍然係 point in time。 Card 7 Front: Which costs of obtaining/fulfilling a contract are capitalised under HKFRS 15, and what practical expedient applies? Back: Costs to obtain (paras. 91–93): capitalise incremental costs expected to be recovered (e.g. sales commissions), plus non incremental costs explicitly chargeable to the customer. Practical expedient (para. 94): expense immediately if the amortisation period would be one year or less — this is an accounting policy choice . Costs to fulfil (paras. 95–96): apply other standards first (HKAS 2/16/38); otherwise capitalise only if costs relate directly to the contract, generate/enhance resources for future performance obligations, and are recoverable. Expense as incurred: general & admin costs (unless chargeable), wasted materials/labour, costs relating to past performance. Amortisation: systematic, consistent with transfer of related goods/services; changes = change in accounting estimate (paras. 99–100). 💬 白話解釋：commission = incremental cost，要 capitalize（唔係即時 expense，更加唔係扣 transaction price）。但攤銷期 ≤1 年可以揀即時 expense — 呢個係 policy choice，MCQ 好鍾意考「must capitalise / must expense」呢類絕對字眼，其實答案係「有得揀」。 Card 8 Front: How is a sale with a right of return accounted for under HKFRS 15 para. B21? Back: Recognise revenue only for the consideration the entity expects to be entitled to (no revenue for products expected to be returned); Recognise a refund liability for amounts received/receivable for expected returns; Recognise an asset for the right to recover products on settling the refund liability, with a corresponding adjustment to cost of sales. Portfolio approach may be applied if results would not differ materially. 💬 白話解釋：賣 100 部機預計退 8 部 → 92 部認 revenue，8 部認 refund liability + recoverable asset。伏位：唔係「等退貨期完先全部認收入」— 貨嘅 control 一過戶，預計唔會退嗰部份就要即刻認收入。 本章急救詞彙 EN Term 繁中白話 English Model Sentence Performance obligation 合約入面承諾俾客戶嘅貨或服務 Each distinct promised good or service is identified as a separate performance obligation. Transaction price 預期有權收取嘅代價（唔計代第三方收嘅錢） The transaction price excludes amounts collected on behalf of third parties, such as sales taxes. Contract asset 已轉移貨品但收款權附帶其他條件 A contract asset arises when the right to consideration is conditional on something other than the passage of time. Contract liability 收咗錢但仲欠客戶貨或服務 Cash received before the service is rendered is recognised as a contract liability. Refund liability 預計要退返俾客戶嘅款項 For sales with a right of return, a refund liability is recognised for the expected returns. Stand alone selling price (SSP) 單獨出售嘅價錢，用嚟分攤交易價 The transaction price is allocated in proportion to the relative stand alone selling prices. Significant financing component 付款時間造成嘅重大融資成分 Where payment is deferred for two years, the contract contains a significant financing component. Incremental costs of obtaining a contract 唔攞到份約就唔會使嘅成本（如佣金） Sales commissions are incremental costs of obtaining a contract and are capitalised if recoverable.

excerpt: M6 Chapter 3: Revenue Recognition — Phase 3 Answers Q1 — Answer: A Model Answer (EN): The contract contains ONE performance obligation: the combined commercial …
text: M6 Chapter 3: Revenue Recognition — Phase 3 Answers Q1 — Answer: A Model Answer (EN): The contract contains ONE performance obligation: the combined commercial kitchen. Although the ovens, refrigeration units and worktops may each be capable of being distinct (the customer could benefit from them with other readily available resources), they are not distinct within the context of the contract : KitchKraft provides a significant service of integrating and substantially modifying the components into the combined output for which the customer contracted. Non distinct goods/services are combined until a distinct bundle is identified. 解題思路（繁中）: 「Distinct」要過兩關：capable of being distinct 兼 distinct within the context of the contract。呢題啲零件過到第一關，但 KitchKraft 提供重大 integration 及 customisation 服務，令承諾喺合約語境下 唔係 separately identifiable ，所以第二關過唔到 → 合成一個 performance obligation。Distractor B 只考慮第一關，漏咗 context test；C 錯將「合約提到嘅每項嘢」都當獨立 PO（installation 係 integration 嘅一部分，並非獨立承諾）；D 嘅「goods and services are always separately identifiable」係絕對化錯誤陳述。 考試伏位： 見到「significant integration / customisation」關鍵字，即刻諗住合併計。 Rule Check: HKFRS 15 paras. 27–29 (distinct criteria and indicators of not being separately identifiable) Common Trap（繁中）: 以為「可以獨立賣」就等於「separate performance obligation」— 必須同時通過「distinct within the context of the contract」測試；顯著整合服務（significant integration service）係最常見嘅合併原因。 Q2 — Answer: C Model Answer (EN): TixHub is an agent : the organiser is primarily responsible for fulfilment (staging the concert), TixHub bears no inventory risk, and TixHub has no pricing discretion (the organiser sets the HK$500 price). TixHub therefore does not control the service before it is transferred to the customer and recognises revenue only at the net commission amount: HK$500 − HK$460 = HK$40 per ticket. 解題思路（繁中）: Principal vs agent 睇三個指標：邊個主要負責履行、邊個有存貨風險、邊個有定價權 — 三個都指向 organiser，所以 TixHub 係 agent，只認 commission HK$40。Distractor A 係 principal 先會用嘅 gross 做法，會 誇大 revenue ；B 係 remittance 金額，同收入定義無關；D 錯在混淆「唔係 principal」同「冇收入」— agent 照樣認 commission revenue。 考試伏位： agent 負責收錢（collect on behalf）唔影響判斷；「net profit 一樣」唔代表 revenue presentation 冇分別。 Rule Check: HKFRS 15 paras. B34, B37 (principal–agent considerations; indicators of control) Common Trap（繁中）: 見到平台收足 HK$500 就以為 revenue 係 gross 數 — agent 永遠只認淨佣金；錯誤 gross up 會同時谷大 revenue 同 expense。 Q3 — Answer: C Model Answer (EN): Workings — allocation on relative stand alone selling prices: Performance obligation SSP Allocation of HK$8,100 Exercise bike HK$7,200 7,200 / 9,000 × 8,100 = HK$6,480 Maintenance plan (1 yr) HK$1,800 1,800 / 9,000 × 8,100 = HK$1,620 Total HK$9,000 HK$8,100 Bike: point in time — HK$6,480 recognised on delivery (1 January 20X5). Maintenance: over time (customer simultaneously receives and consumes the benefits) — HK$1,620 / 12 = HK$135 per month. January 20X5 revenue = 6,480 + 135 = HK$6,615 . 解題思路（繁中）: 先按 relative SSP 分攤個 bundle discount（HK$900 discount 按比例攤），再判斷每個 PO 嘅 timing：bike 係 point in time 即日認；maintenance 係 over time 每月認 1/12。Distractor A 將成個 HK$8,100 直線攤 12 個月，冇分 PO；B 只認咗 bike，漏咗一個月 maintenance；D 用 SSP 原價（7,200 + 1,800/12 = 7,350）而冇分攤 discount。 考試伏位： 分攤係用 relative SSP 比例 落 transaction price，唔係直接用 SSP 認收入。 Rule Check: HKFRS 15 paras. 73–77 (allocation based on relative stand alone selling prices); para. 81 (discount allocation); paras. 35–38 (over time vs point in time) Common Trap（繁中）: 忘記 bundle discount 要攤落每個 PO；或者將整個合約金額當一個 PO 直線攤分 — 凡係混合「即日交貨 + 長期服務」嘅合約，一定要拆開計 timing。 Q4 — Answer: B Model Answer (EN): The performance obligation is satisfied over time : the asset has no alternative use to BuildSpan AND BuildSpan has an enforceable right to payment for performance completed to date (third criterion satisfied). Using the input method: Progress = costs incurred ÷ total expected costs = 1,200,000 / 4,800,000 = 25% Revenue for the year = 25% × HK$6,000,000 = HK$1,500,000 解題思路（繁中）: 先過 over time 測試：第三個條件「no alternative use AND enforceable right to payment」兩者齊全 → over time。再用 input method：cost to cost 25% × 合約價。Distractor A 直接當 costs incurred 係 revenue（利潤歸零，唔合理）；C 係 30%（錯用 1,200/4,000 或憑空加成）；D 係按時間直線攤（9 個月 / 總期）— 但題目講明用 input method 按成本計進度。 考試伏位： input method 分母係 total expected costs （已發生 + 預計將發生），唔係已發生成本或合約價。 Rule Check: HKFRS 15 paras. 35–37 (over time criteria, incl. no alternative use + enforceable right to payment); para. B15 (input methods) Common Trap（繁中）: 「No alternative use」同「enforceable right to payment」係 AND 關係 — 只中一個唔算 over time；計 progress 時記得用累計成本對總預期成本，唔好用時間比例代替題目指定嘅 input method。 Q5 — Answer: B Model Answer (EN): Cash received before performance creates a contract liability . The service is satisfied over time (customer simultaneously receives and consumes the benefits). By 30 June 20X5, 4 of 12 months have elapsed: 36,000 × 4/12 = HK$12,000 of revenue is recognised. Remaining contract liability at year end = HK$24,000 (8 months of service still to be provided). 解題思路（繁中）: 「先收錢、後做嘢」→ contract liability （唔係 revenue，唔係 contract asset）。之後按時間推移（output method — time elapsed）逐步將 liability 轉做 revenue：4/12 × 36,000 = 12,000。Distractor A 收款即全數認收入，違反 over time 原則；C 用咗 contract asset （方向完全倒轉 — asset 係「做咗嘢未收錢」先至用）兼收款日先認收入；D 年結時全數 36,000 認收入，冇按 4/12 計算。 考試伏位： contract asset vs contract liability 方向：perform first + right conditional → asset；cash first + obligation outstanding → liability。 Rule Check: HKFRS 15 para. 35 (over time — simultaneous receipt and consumption of benefits); para. 106 / Appendix A (contract liability: obligation to transfer goods/services for which consideration has been received) Common Trap（繁中）: 混淆 contract asset 同 contract liability 嘅方向；以及年結時「懶方便」全數認收入而唔按時間比例（4/12）攤分 — 記住 mid year 起約一定要 pro rate。

excerpt: M6 Chapter 3: Revenue Recognition — Phase 3 Quiz Rules: Closed book · 15 minutes · 5 questions · Submit as 1. … 2. … 3. … 4. … 5. … — 超時如實申報 Question 1 KitchKra…
text: M6 Chapter 3: Revenue Recognition — Phase 3 Quiz Rules: Closed book · 15 minutes · 5 questions · Submit as 1. … 2. … 3. … 4. … 5. … — 超時如實申報 Question 1 KitchKraft Limited (KitchKraft) enters into a contract with a hotel to design, supply and install a fully customised commercial kitchen. KitchKraft will source ovens, refrigeration units and steel worktops from third party manufacturers, and then perform a significant service of integrating and substantially modifying these components on site so that they function as a single combined kitchen system. The customer contracted for one integrated commercial kitchen. In accordance with HKFRS 15, how many performance obligations does the contract contain? A. One — the components are not distinct within the context of the contract because KitchKraft provides a significant service of integrating them into a combined output B. Three — the ovens, refrigeration units and steel worktops are each capable of being distinct goods C. Four — the three components plus the installation service, because installation is a separate promise in the contract D. Two — the supply of the components and the installation service, because goods and services are always separately identifiable Question 2 TixHub Limited (TixHub) operates an online platform selling concert tickets on behalf of event organisers. For a concert with a ticket price of HK$500, TixHub collects HK$500 from each concertgoer, remits HK$460 to the organiser and retains HK$40 as its fee. The ticket prices are set by the event organisers; the organisers are responsible for staging the concert; and TixHub bears no inventory risk on unsold tickets. In accordance with HKFRS 15, what amount of revenue should TixHub recognise for each ticket sold? A. HK$500 B. HK$460 C. HK$40 D. Nil — no revenue is recognised because the organiser fulfils the performance obligation Question 3 On 1 January 20X5, FitPeak Limited (FitPeak) sells a bundle to a customer for HK$8,100, comprising an exercise bike and a one year maintenance plan that commences on the delivery date. FitPeak regularly sells the exercise bike separately for HK$7,200 and the maintenance plan separately for HK$1,800. Both the bike and the maintenance plan are distinct performance obligations. The bike is delivered (and control transfers) on 1 January 20X5; the maintenance service is provided evenly over the year. In accordance with HKFRS 15, how much revenue should FitPeak recognise in January 20X5? A. HK$675 B. HK$6,480 C. HK$6,615 D. HK$7,350 Question 4 On 1 April 20X5, BuildSpan Limited (BuildSpan) enters into a fixed price contract to construct a highly customised production line directly on the customer's premises for HK$6,000,000. The customised asset has no alternative use to BuildSpan, and the contract gives BuildSpan an enforceable right to payment for performance completed to date (costs incurred plus a reasonable margin) if the customer terminates the contract. BuildSpan measures progress using an input method based on costs incurred. Total expected contract costs are HK$4,800,000. For the year ended 31 December 20X5, costs incurred to date amount to HK$1,200,000. In accordance with HKFRS 15, how much revenue should BuildSpan recognise for the year ended 31 December 20X5? A. HK$1,200,000 B. HK$1,500,000 C. HK$1,800,000 D. HK$2,000,000 Question 5 On 1 March 20X5, ServTech Limited (ServTech) receives HK$36,000 in cash from a customer for a 12 month equipment maintenance contract that commences on the same date. ServTech's reporting date is 30 June 20X5. The maintenance service is provided evenly over the contract period, and the customer simultaneously receives and consumes the benefits as ServTech performs. In accordance with HKFRS 15, which set of journal entries correctly records the above transactions? A. 1 March 20X5: Dr Cash 36,000 / Cr Service revenue 36,000; no entry required on 30 June 20X5 B. 1 March 20X5: Dr Cash 36,000 / Cr Contract liability 36,000; 30 June 20X5: Dr Contract liability 12,000 / Cr Service revenue 12,000 C. 1 March 20X5: Dr Contract asset 36,000 / Cr Service revenue 36,000; 30 June 20X5: Dr Cash 36,000 / Cr Contract asset 36,000 D. 1 March 20X5: Dr Cash 36,000 / Cr Contract liability 36,000; 30 June 20X5: Dr Contract liability 36,000 / Cr Service revenue 36,000 End of quiz. Answers are in M6_Ch03_Phase3_Answers.md — 唔好偷睇！

excerpt: M6 Chapter 4: Inventories — Phase 1 速查表 + Phase 2 閃卡 Phase 1 速查表 Learning Objectives 1. Describe the scope and definition of inventories under HKAS 2 and classi…
text: M6 Chapter 4: Inventories — Phase 1 速查表 + Phase 2 閃卡 Phase 1 速查表 Learning Objectives 1. Describe the scope and definition of inventories under HKAS 2 and classify inventories into raw materials, work in progress and finished goods. 2. Apply acceptable methods of assigning costs to inventories, including the allocation of fixed and variable production overheads based on normal capacity. 3. Calculate the cost of inventories and cost of sales under the FIFO and weighted average cost formulas. 4. Calculate net realisable value (NRV) and prepare the adjustments required when NRV falls below cost, including reversals of write downs. 5. Prepare the disclosures in respect of inventories required by HKAS 2. 必背考點 1. Recognition（範圍與定義） HKAS 2.6 — Definition of inventories : assets that are (a) held for sale in the ordinary course of business; (b) in the process of production for such sale; or (c) in the form of materials or supplies to be consumed in the production process or in the rendering of services. 三大類別（按完成程度）: Raw materials — 未開始加工； Work in progress (WIP) — 正在轉化為製成品； Finished goods — 可供出售。 Manufacturer 通常三類齊全；merchandiser (retailer/wholesaler) 一般只有 finished goods。 Expensing 時點 : 存貨售出時，其 carrying amount 於確認相關收入之同期確認為 expense (cost of sales)；若曾 write down 至 NRV，相關 expense 更早已確認。 2. Measurement — Initial measurement at cost HKAS 2.11 — Costs of purchase : purchase price + import duties and other taxes + transport, handling and other costs directly attributable to acquisition。 Trade discounts, rebates and similar items must be DEDUCTED 。 HKAS 2.12 — Costs of conversion : direct costs (direct materials, direct labour) + systematically allocated production overheads (fixed + variable)。 HKAS 2.13 — Overhead allocation : Fixed production overheads : allocated based on normal capacity （正常營運下數個期间的平均預期產量，計及 routine maintenance）。 產量低於 normal capacity → 每單位分配的 fixed overhead 不得增加 ；unallocated overhead (unused capacity) 於發生當期 expensed。 產量異常高 → 每單位分配額 調低 ，確保存貨不高於 cost。 Variable production overheads : allocated based on actual use 。 HKAS 2.15 — Other costs : 只計入使存貨達致「現時地點及狀況」(present location and condition) 的成本，例如 specific customer design costs、若干 non production overheads。 HKAS 2.16 — Costs EXCLUDED (expensed as incurred) : abnormal amounts of wasted materials, labour or other production costs; storage costs（除非屬生產過程中下一階段前必需）; administrative overheads that do not contribute to bringing inventories to their present location and condition; selling costs (e.g. marketing, sales staff costs, freight outwards / distribution)。 3. Measurement — Cost formulas（成本流轉假設） HKAS 2.23 — Specific identification : 用於 not ordinarily interchangeable 的存貨，或為 specific projects 生產並分開隔離的貨品/服務。 HKAS 2.24 — Interchangeable items : 用 FIFO 或 weighted average cost formula。 LIFO is NOT permitted （LP 引 IAS 2 para. BC 9 作為禁止依據）。 HKAS 2.25 — Consistency : 性質及用途相近的存貨必須使用同一 cost formula；HKAS 2 不指定公式，屬 policy choice，但應配合存貨性質及管理實務（如 perishable goods 宜用 FIFO）。 HKAS 2.27 : Weighted average : 以期初存貨加本期購入/產出的加權平均成本計算；可定期計算或每次進貨更新（moving average）。適合成本穩定、不易腐壞的存貨。 FIFO : 假設先購入/生產的先售出；期末存貨為最近購入/生產的項目。適合 fast moving 或 perishable 存貨。 Inventory accounting systems : Perpetual method : 每宗交易（purchase/sale/return）即時更新存貨帳；cost of sales 於銷售時點記錄；資訊較準確及時但成本較高。 Periodic method : 定期（月/年）盤點更新； Cost of sales = Opening inventory + Purchases − Purchase returns − Closing inventory ；較簡易但較不準確。 4. Measurement — Subsequent: Lower of cost and NRV HKAS 2.28 : inventories are measured at the lower of cost and net realisable value (NRV) 。 HKAS 2.6 — NRV definition : the estimated selling price in the ordinary course of business LESS the estimated costs of completion AND the estimated costs necessary to make the sale （e.g. marketing and distribution costs）。 Cost 可能無法收回的情況 (HKAS 2.28)：存貨 damaged or obsolete；售價下跌；completion 或銷售成本上升。 HKAS 2.30 : NRV 按評估時最可靠證據估計；須計及報告期後直接相關的價格/成本波動，但僅限於 確認報告期末已存在狀況 者。 HKAS 2.33 — Reversal : 每期期末重新評估 NRV。若導致 write down 的情況不再存在，或有 clear evidence 顯示 NRV 上升，須撥回 write down —— 但僅以原 write down 金額為上限 （即存貨絕不可高於 original cost）。Reversal 確認為當期 inventories expense 的減少。 5. Disclosure（HKAS 2.36–2.39） HKAS 2.36 要求披露： (a) 計量存貨的 accounting policies，包括所用 cost formula ； (b) 存貨 total carrying amount 及按適當分類（RM / WIP / FG）的 carrying amount（HKAS 2.36(b)）； (d)/(e) 當期確認為 expense 的存貨金額（cost of sales）及當期 write down 金額（HKAS 2.36(e)）； (f) 當期 write down 的 reversal 金額（作為 expense 減項）； (g) 導致 reversal 的 circumstances or events ； (h) pledged as security for liabilities 的存貨 carrying amount（HKAS 2.36(h)）。 HKAS 2.38 : cost of sales 包括已售存貨成本、unallocated production overheads、abnormal production costs。 HKAS 2.39 : 若損益表按性質分類費用 (by nature)，須披露 raw materials、labour 等及存貨淨變動。 考試伏位 : HKAS 2 並 不要求 RM/WIP/FG 之間變動的 reconciliation（只需分類 carrying amounts）。 6. Key Journal Entries（Dr/Cr 必須平衡） (1) Write down of inventories to NRV (HKAS 2.28): Account Dr (HK$) Cr (HK$) Loss on write down of inventories x,xxx     Inventories x,xxx (2) Reversal of a previous write down — capped at original write down (HKAS 2.33): Account Dr (HK$) Cr (HK$) Inventories x,xxx     Loss on write down of inventories x,xxx (3) Sale of goods under the perpetual method（兩 entry 同時做）: Account Dr (HK$) Cr (HK$) Cash / Accounts receivable x,xxx     Sales revenue x,xxx Cost of sales x,xxx     Inventories x,xxx (4) Purchase of raw materials on credit (perpetual): Account Dr (HK$) Cr (HK$) Inventories (raw materials) x,xxx     Accounts payable x,xxx 易混淆概念對比 Table 1: FIFO vs Weighted Average Cost（HKAS 2.27） 比較點 FIFO Weighted Average Cost Cost flow assumption 先買入的先賣出；closing inventory = 最近購入成本 每次進貨（或期末）重算平均單位成本 價格上升時 COGS 較 低 （舊平貨先出）→ profit 較高 較 高 （平均價被新貴貨拉高）→ profit 較低 Closing inventory 反映 較接近現時成本 平滑後的混合成本 適用存貨 Fast moving / perishable（如時令植物、短保質期食品） 成本穩定、不易腐壞（如長期固定價供應的瓷磚） 點樣分辨 / 考試伏位 題目講「shelf life」「spoilage」「first purchased sold first」→ FIFO 題目講「stable input costs」「fixed price supply contract」→ WAC；moving average 記得 每次 purchase 後先重算 平均價才扣減銷售 Table 2: Net Realisable Value (NRV) vs Fair Value (FV) 比較點 NRV (HKAS 2.6) Fair Value (HKFRS 13) 定義 Estimated selling price in the ordinary course of business − costs of completion − costs necessary to make the sale Price received to sell an asset in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date 性質 Entity specific 價值（實體日常生意能賣幾多） Market based measurement 用途 HKAS 2 存貨後續計量（lower of cost and NRV） 適用於多個準則的公允價值計量 點樣分辨 / 考試伏位 MCQ 常見 "definition swap" 伏：將 HKFRS 13 fair value 定義當 NRV 選項；記住 NRV 必須 扣兩樣嘢 （completion + selling costs），漏咗 costs of completion 嘅選項都係錯 見到「market participants」「orderly transaction」字眼 = fair value，唔係 NRV Phase 2 閃卡 Card 1 Front: Under HKAS 2.6, what three categories of assets qualify as "inventories"? Back: Assets held for sale in the ordinary course of business (finished goods) Assets in the process of production for such sale (work in progress) Materials or supplies to be consumed in the production process or in the rendering of services (raw materials) 💬 繁中白話：記住「賣緊、做緊、用緊」三部曲 —— 未做完嘅材料、做緊嘅半製品、做完等賣嘅貨，三樣都係 inventory。 Card 2 Front: According to HKAS 2.11 and 2.16, which costs are included in / excluded from the cost of inventories? Back: Included (HKAS 2.11): purchase price, import duties and other taxes, transport, handling, other directly attributable acquisition costs; less trade discounts and rebates Excluded (HKAS 2.16) — expensed as incurred: abnormal waste; storage costs (unless necessary before a further production stage); non contributing administrative overheads; selling costs (incl. freight outwards) 💬 繁中白話：問自己「呢舊錢係咪令貨品達到而家嘅地點同狀態？」係 → 入 cost；唔係（例如儲起製成品、運俾客、賣嘢佣金、不正常浪費）→ 即刻 expense。 Card 3 Front: How are fixed and variable production overheads allocated to inventories under HKAS 2.13, and what happens when production is abnormally low or abnormally high? Back: Fixed production overheads: allocated based on normal capacity Variable production overheads: allocated based on actual use Low/idle production: per unit fixed overhead allocation not increased ; unallocated overhead expensed in the period Abnormally high production: per unit allocation decreased so inventories are not measured above cost 💬 繁中白話：fixed overhead 用「正常產能」做分母，唔好用「實際產量」。產量少咗，每件貨唔會因而背多啲 overhead；多餘嗰份直接出 P&L。產量異常多就要反過來調低每單位分配額。 Card 4 Front: Which cost formulas are permitted by HKAS 2 for interchangeable inventories, and when must specific identification be used (HKAS 2.23–2.25)? Back: Interchangeable items: FIFO or weighted average cost (HKAS 2.24) LIFO is prohibited (LP cites IAS 2 para. BC 9) Not ordinarily interchangeable / segregated for specific projects: specific identification (HKAS 2.23) Same formula must be used for inventories of a similar nature and use (HKAS 2.25) 💬 繁中白話： interchangeable（件件一樣）→ FIFO 或 WAC 二揀一；每件都獨一無二（如訂造遊艇）→ specific identification；LIFO 喺 HKAS 2 係 禁品 ，見到即刻剔走。 Card 5 Front: Define net realisable value (NRV) under HKAS 2.6 and state the measurement rule in HKAS 2.28. Back: NRV = estimated selling price in the ordinary course of business − estimated costs of completion − estimated costs necessary to make the sale Inventories are measured at the lower of cost and NRV Write down triggers: damaged/obsolete goods; decline in sales price; increase in completion or selling costs 💬 繁中白話： NRV = 賣價 − 未完成成本 − 賣嘢使費，兩樣扣項缺一不可。存貨永遠取 cost 同 NRV 嘅 較低者 —— 資產唔可以報大數。 Card 6 Front: Give the journal entries for (a) a write down of inventories to NRV and (b) a reversal of a previous write down (HKAS 2.28, 2.33). Back: (a) Write down: Dr Loss on write down of inventories / Cr Inventories (b) Reversal: Dr Inventories / Cr Loss on write down of inventories Reversal is capped at the amount of the original write down — inventories can never be carried above cost 💬 繁中白話：減值 → Dr Loss、Cr Inventory；翻生 → 調轉。但翻生有「天花板」：最多返到原本 cost，唔准升穿。記住 credit 邊唔係 "revaluation surplus"，係沖返個 loss account。 Card 7 Front: How does the perpetual inventory system differ from the periodic system, and what is the cost of sales formula under the periodic system? Back: Perpetual: inventory accounts updated on every transaction ; cost of sales recorded at point of sale; more accurate and timely but more onerous Periodic: updated via physical stock count at period end; less accurate but cheaper Periodic cost of sales = Opening inventory + Purchases − Purchase returns − Closing inventory 💬 繁中白話：perpetual = 每單交易即時入帳，隨時知庫存；periodic = 期末先數貨，COGS 靠「期初 + 買 − 退 − 期末」倒挤出嚟。考試見到「physical count」「updated periodically」就係 periodic。 Card 8 Front: List the main disclosure requirements for inventories under HKAS 2.36. Back: Accounting policies for measuring inventories, including the cost formula used Total carrying amount and carrying amount by classification (e.g. RM, WIP, FG) Amount of inventories recognised as an expense (cost of sales) Amount of any write down recognised as expense Amount of any reversal of write down (as a reduction of expense) Circumstances/events leading to the reversal Carrying amount of inventories pledged as security for liabilities 💬 繁中白話：口訣「Policy、分類、Expense、減值、撥回、原因、抵押」七件事。留意：分類之間的 movement reconciliation 唔使 披露 —— 呢個係常見 MCQ 伏。 本章急救詞彙 EN Term 繁中白話 English Model Sentence Net realisable value (NRV) 估計賣價減埋完工同銷售成本後，真正落到袋嘅錢 Inventories are measured at the lower of cost and net realisable value in accordance with HKAS 2.28. Normal capacity 正常營運下、計及例行維修後，幾個期間平均預期做到嘅產量 Fixed production overheads are allocated to inventories based on the normal capacity of the production facilities (HKAS 2.13). Cost formula 將可售貨品成本分配去 COGS 同期末存貨嘅方法（FIFO / WAC） The same cost formula shall be used for all inventories having a similar nature and use to the entity (HKAS 2.25). Specific identification 逐件貨認住佢嘅實際成本，適用於唔可以互換嘅貨 Specific identification of cost is required for items that are not ordinarily interchangeable (HKAS 2.23). Write down 存貨成本高過 NRV 時，將帳面值調低嘅動作 The entity recognised a write down of inventories to net realisable value as an expense in the period. Reversal of write down 之前減值嘅原因消失，將減值撥返（上限係原來減值額） The reversal of the write down is limited to the amount of the original write down, so inventories are not carried above cost (HKAS 2.33). Perpetual inventory system 每單交易即時更新存貨帳嘅制度 Under the perpetual method, cost of sales is recorded at the point the sale is made. Work in progress (WIP) 做咗一半、未變成製成品嘅存貨 The manufacturer's statement of financial position includes raw materials, work in progress and finished goods.

title: M6 Chapter 4: Inventories — Phase 3 Answers
excerpt: M6 Chapter 4: Inventories — Phase 3 Answers Q1 — Answer: B Model Answer (EN): Under HKAS 2.11, the costs of purchase include the purchase price, import duties a…
text: M6 Chapter 4: Inventories — Phase 3 Answers Q1 — Answer: B Model Answer (EN): Under HKAS 2.11, the costs of purchase include the purchase price, import duties and other taxes, transport, handling and other costs directly attributable to the acquisition of the inventories. Import duties and freight inwards on timber are therefore included in cost. Storage costs of finished goods, abnormal waste and selling costs (sales commissions) are excluded under HKAS 2.16 and expensed as incurred. 解題思路（繁中）: 判斷標準只有一條：「呢項成本係咪令存貨達致現時嘅地點同狀態？」Import duties + freight inwards 係買料必要使費 → 入 cost（B 啱）。A 係儲起製成品嘅倉租 —— 貨已做完，儲存唔係生產下一階段前必需，HKAS 2.16 明確剔除；C 係 abnormal waste，正常浪費先入 cost，異常浪費即刻 expense；D 係 selling costs，同貨品嘅 location and condition 無關，必定 expense。 Rule Check: HKAS 2.11 (costs of purchase); HKAS 2.16 (costs excluded from inventories) Common Trap（繁中）: 考生最易中伏係將「storage costs」一刀切全部當 expense 或全部當 cost —— 關鍵係睇佢係咪生產下一階段 必需 （如熟成過程）先入 cost。另外 trade discount/rebate 記得要 扣減 purchase cost，唔係當其他收入。 Q2 — Answer: B (HK$24,000) Model Answer (EN): Fixed production overheads are allocated based on normal capacity , not actual production (HKAS 2.13). Normal capacity allocation rate = HK$1,152,000 ÷ 9,600 units = HK$120 per unit Fixed overhead allocated to April production = 600 units × HK$120 = HK$72,000 Budgeted fixed overhead for April = HK$1,152,000 ÷ 12 = HK$96,000 Unallocated overhead expensed = HK$96,000 − HK$72,000 = HK$24,000 解題思路（繁中）: 產量低於 normal capacity 時，每單位分配率 唔准加碼 —— 照用 HK$120/unit，所以只有 600 × 120 = HK$72,000 入咗存貨成本，剩低 HK$24,000 即時出 P&L。Distractor A（HK$0）係用實際產量做分母（96,000 ÷ 600 = HK$160/unit），將所有 overhead 吸晒落存貨 —— HKAS 2.13 明令禁止；D（HK$96,000）係將成個月 overhead 全數 expense，完全冇分配落存貨；C（HK$72,000）係調轉咗 allocated 同 unallocated 嘅概念。 Rule Check: HKAS 2.13 (allocation of fixed production overheads based on normal capacity; unallocated overhead recognised as an expense in the period incurred) Common Trap（繁中）: 伏位在「分母」：見到「production significantly below plan / equipment breakdown」就要即刻諗 normal capacity，唔好用實際產量。相反，若產量 異常高 ，分配率要 調低 避免存貨高於成本 —— 兩個方向都要識。 Q3 — Answer: C Model Answer (EN): Under HKAS 2.23, the cost of inventories of items that are not ordinarily interchangeable , and goods produced and segregated for specific projects , must be assigned using specific identification . Each Regatta yacht is built to an individual customer's design and is not interchangeable, so specific identification is required. FIFO and weighted average cost (HKAS 2.24) apply only to interchangeable items; LIFO is not permitted under HKAS 2 (LP cites IAS 2 para. BC 9). 解題思路（繁中）: 題眼係「no two yachts are interchangeable」+「built to an individual customer's design」—— 每件貨獨一無二、為特定項目而生產，就一定要 specific identification（C 啱）。A、B 只適用於可以互換嘅存貨；D 係雙重錯：既唔啱性質，而且 LIFO 喺 HKAS 2 根本 被禁止 ，任何情況都唔揀得。 Rule Check: HKAS 2.23 (specific identification); HKAS 2.24 (FIFO/weighted average for interchangeable items); IAS 2 para. BC 9 (LIFO not permitted, as cited in the LP) Common Trap（繁中）: MCQ 好鍾意將 LIFO 放落選項度引你 —— 記住 HKAS 2 得三個公式：specific identification、FIFO、weighted average。另外「same cost formula for inventories of similar nature and use」(HKAS 2.25) 都係常考點。 Q4 — Answer: C (HK$5,000) Model Answer (EN): NRV = estimated selling price − costs of completion − costs to make the sale; compare with cost item by item (HKAS 2.6, 2.28). Product line Cost (HK$) NRV (HK$) Write down per unit (HK$) Units Write down (HK$) Down jackets 850 880 − 0 − 40 = 840 10 200 2,000 Trail shoes 420 450 − 50 − 10 = 390 30 100 3,000 Total 5,000 Both lines have NRV below cost, so total write down = HK$2,000 + HK$3,000 = HK$5,000 , recognised as an expense in the period. 解題思路（繁中）: NRV 要 扣兩樣嘢 ：costs of completion 加 costs to make the sale。Distractor A（HK$0）係齋用賣價同 cost 比（880 850、450 420 所以「唔使減值」）—— 完全冇扣 completion 同銷售成本；B（HK$2,000）係只減咗 down jackets，trail shoes 嗰邊漏扣 HK$50 completion costs，以為 450 − 10 = 440 高過 cost 420；D（HK$14,000）係將全部 completion + selling costs 當成 write down（40×200 + 60×100 = 14,000），冇做 cost vs NRV 嘅比較。 Rule Check: HKAS 2.6 (definition of NRV); HKAS 2.28 (inventories measured at the lower of cost and NRV) Common Trap（繁中）: 三大伏位：(1) 漏扣 costs of completion；(2) 齋睇 selling price 唔計任何銷售成本；(3) 用「總額對總額」比較而唔係逐項/逐類比較。記住 NRV 測試係 item by item ，唔可以話 A 產品賺嘅補返 B 產品蝕嘅。 Q5 — Answer: A Model Answer (EN): At 31 December 20X5, NRV (HK$295,000) exceeds the written down carrying amount (HK$260,000), so the previous write down is reversed. The reversal restores the carrying amount to the lower of cost (HK$300,000) and NRV (HK$295,000) , i.e. HK$295,000 — a reversal of HK$35,000 (within the HK$40,000 original write down cap). The entry is: Account Dr (HK$) Cr (HK$) Inventories 35,000     Loss on write down of inventories 35,000 The reversal is recognised as a reduction in the amount of inventories recognised as an expense in the period. 解題思路（繁中）: 兩個上限要同時 check：(1) 撥回額唔可以超過 原本 write down （HK$40,000）；(2) 撥回後帳面值唔可以高過 lower of cost and NRV —— 呢度 NRV 得 HK$295,000，低過 cost HK$300,000，所以只可以撥 HK$35,000（A 啱）。B（HK$40,000）全數撥返會令帳面值 = HK$300,000 NRV HK$295,000，違反 lower of cost and NRV；C 用錯 account —— 存貨 冇 revaluation surplus 呢樣嘢（嗰個係 HKAS 16 PPE 嘅概念），reversal 係沖返 Loss on write down；D 方向完全調轉，變成再減值多一次。 Rule Check: HKAS 2.33 (reversal of write down limited to the original write down); HKAS 2.28 (lower of cost and NRV) Common Trap（繁中）: 考生成日記住「reversal capped at original write down」就機械式撥足 HK$40,000，忘記咗 reversal 之後個帳面值 仲要過多次 lower of cost and NRV 測試 —— 兩個 cap 取其嚴。另外 reversal 嘅 credit 係 expense 嘅減少（冲 loss account），唔係 revenue，亦唔係 OCI/surplus。

text: M6 Chapter 4: Inventories — Phase 3 Quiz Rules: Closed book · 15 minutes · 5 questions · Submit as 1. … 2. … 3. … 4. … 5. … — 超時如實申報 Q1. Ploverhill Limited manufactures solid wood dining tables in its Dongguan factory. In accordance with HKAS 2, which of the following costs should be included in the cost of Ploverhill's inventories? A. Storage costs of finished tables held in the company's showroom warehouse B. Import duties and freight inwards incurred on shipments of timber raw materials C. Abnormal amounts of timber wasted during a machine malfunction D. Commissions paid to sales staff on contracts signed with retailers Q2. Dragonkiln Limited manufactures ceramic dinnerware. Its budgeted fixed production overhead for the year is HK$1,152,000 and the normal capacity of its production facility is 9,600 units per year. In April 20X7, an equipment breakdown meant only 600 units were produced (normal monthly output is 800 units). In accordance with HKAS 2, what amount of fixed production overhead should be recognised as an expense (i.e. unallocated overhead) in April 20X7? A. HK$0 B. HK$24,000 C. HK$72,000 D. HK$96,000 Q3. Regatta Yachts Limited builds racing yachts, each constructed to an individual customer's design and specification; no two yachts are interchangeable. In accordance with HKAS 2, which cost formula should Regatta use to assign costs to its yacht inventories? A. First in, first out (FIFO) B. Weighted average cost C. Specific identification D. Last in, first out (LIFO) Q4. Summit Outdoor Limited sells two product lines. At its year end, the following information is available: Product line Units on hand Cost per unit (HK$) Estimated selling price per unit (HK$) Estimated costs of completion per unit (HK$) Estimated costs to make the sale per unit (HK$) Down jackets 200 850 880 – 40 Trail shoes 100 420 450 50 10 In accordance with HKAS 2, what is the total write down of inventories that Summit Outdoor should recognise as an expense in the period? A. HK$0 B. HK$2,000 C. HK$5,000 D. HK$14,000 Q5. Lantern House Limited holds a line of decorative lamps with a cost of HK$300,000. At 31 December 20X4, the lamps were written down to their net realisable value of HK$260,000. At 31 December 20X5, there is clear evidence that the NRV of the lamps has recovered to HK$295,000. In accordance with HKAS 2, which journal entry should Lantern House record at 31 December 20X5? A. Dr Inventories HK$35,000 / Cr Loss on write down of inventories HK$35,000 B. Dr Inventories HK$40,000 / Cr Loss on write down of inventories HK$40,000 C. Dr Inventories HK$35,000 / Cr Revaluation surplus HK$35,000 D. Dr Loss on write down of inventories HK$35,000 / Cr Inventories HK$35,000

title: M6 Chapter 5: Property, Plant and Equipment — Phase 1 速查表 + Phase 2 閃卡
headings: M6 Chapter 5: Property, Plant and Equipment — Phase 1 速查表 + Phase 2 閃卡
B. Measurement at Recognition（初始計量）
C. Measurement After Recognition（後續計量）
必記 Journal Entries（全部平衡）
對比一：Cost Model vs Revaluation Model（HKAS 16.30 vs 16.31）
對比二：Capitalise（直接歸屬成本）vs Expense（唔准資本化）
excerpt: M6 Chapter 5: Property, Plant and Equipment — Phase 1 速查表 + Phase 2 閃卡 Phase 1 速查表 Learning Objectives 1. Apply the recognition criteria of HKAS 16 to initial a…
text: M6 Chapter 5: Property, Plant and Equipment — Phase 1 速查表 + Phase 2 閃卡 Phase 1 速查表 Learning Objectives 1. Apply the recognition criteria of HKAS 16 to initial and subsequent expenditure on property, plant and equipment (PPE). 2. Determine the cost of an item of PPE at initial recognition, including directly attributable costs and dismantling/restoration obligations. 3. Account for PPE after recognition under both the cost model and the revaluation model, including depreciation, impairment and revaluation journal entries. 4. Account for the derecognition of PPE, including computation of the gain or loss on disposal and the treatment of any related revaluation surplus. 5. Prepare the disclosures required by HKAS 16 for each class of PPE. 必背考點 A. Recognition（確認） HKAS 16.6 ：PPE = tangible items held for use in production/supply of goods or services, for rental to others, or for administrative purposes, expected to be used during more than one period 。 HKAS 16.7 ：確認條件（兩個都要滿足）： 1. it is probable that future economic benefits will flow to the entity; and 2. the cost can be measured reliably 。 唔符合條件 → 即時 expense （實務上好多公司設 monetary threshold，低過門檻直接費用化）。 HKAS 16.12 ：day to day servicing / repairs and maintenance → profit or loss as incurred （只係維持原有 capacity，唔係提升）。 Subsequent costs： 提升 capacity／延長 useful life／提高產出質量或數量 → capitalise； 只係維持 → expense。Component approach：重大部件（如飛機引擎）當獨立資產逐件折舊及重置資本化。 B. Measurement at Recognition（初始計量） HKAS 16.15 ：initially measured at cost 。 HKAS 16.16 ：Cost 包括三大元素： 1. Purchase price （含 import duties 及 non refundable purchase taxes，扣除 trade discounts 及 rebates）； 2. Directly attributable costs （HKAS 16.17）：employee benefits from construction/acquisition、site preparation (16.17(b))、initial delivery and handling、installation and assembly、testing costs、professional fees；qualifying asset 嘅 borrowing costs 按 HKAS 23 資本化； 3. Dismantling/removal/restoration obligations （HKAS 16.16(c) 及 16.18）：initial estimate 按 HKAS 37 計量， capitalise 入資產成本 （Dr Asset / Cr Provision），唔係即時費用化。 HKAS 16.19–20 ： 不得 資本化嘅成本：opening new facility (16.19(a))、introducing new product（廣告）、conducting business in new location、staff training、initial operating losses、abnormal wastage、administration and general overheads、relocation/reorganisation costs、閒置或未達產能時嘅成本。 HKAS 16.20A ：資產未 ready 前測試產出嘅樣本， proceeds 及成本都入 profit or loss （唔准扣減資產成本）。 HKAS 16.23 ：cost = cash price equivalent ；deferred payment 超出正常信貸期，差額作 interest（除非按 HKAS 23 資本化）。 Asset exchange：以 取得資產嘅 fair value 計量（等於付出代價 FV + 現金）；差額認 gain/loss。 Self constructed asset（HKAS 16.22）：原則同外購一樣。 C. Measurement After Recognition（後續計量） HKAS 16.29 ：accounting policy choice — cost model 或 revaluation model ，按 class （同類同性質同用途，HKAS 16.37）一致應用。 Cost model（HKAS 16.30） ：cost − accumulated depreciation − accumulated impairment losses。 Revaluation model（HKAS 16.31） ： fair value at revaluation date − subsequent accumulated depreciation − subsequent impairment losses；只適用於 FV 能可靠計量嘅資產。 HKAS 16.36 ：重估一項 → 成個 class 都要重估 （唔准揀嚟重估）。 HKAS 16.38 ：revaluations 要 with sufficient regularity ，確保 carrying amount 與 FV 無重大差異。 HKAS 16.39 ：重估 增值 → credit OCI（revaluation surplus） ；例外：如屬逆轉同一資產先前喺 P&L 確認嘅減值 → 嗰部分入 P&L 。 HKAS 16.40 ：重估 減值 → P&L ；例外：先用盡同一資產 revaluation surplus 嘅 credit balance（debit OCI）， 超出部分先入 P&L 。 HKAS 16.35 ：重估調整兩法（policy choice）： Net method ：eliminate accumulated depreciation against gross carrying amount，再將 carrying amount 調至 FV； Gross method ：gross carrying amount 按比例重列，accumulated depreciation 調整至等於 gross 與 revalued carrying amount 之差。 HKAS 16.41 ：revaluation surplus 可 直接 轉 retained earnings（ 唔經 P&L ）：(i) 隨資產使用，按「重估後折舊 − 原成本折舊」之差逐期轉；及/或 (ii) derecognition 時全數轉。 Impairment（HKAS 16.63 → HKAS 36 ）：carrying amount recoverable amount 即減值；revalued asset 嘅 impairment loss 當 revaluation decrease 處理（HKAS 16.39–40 規則）；reversal 當 revaluation increase。 D. Depreciation（折舊） HKAS 16.6, 16.50 ：depreciation = systematic allocation of depreciable amount （cost − residual value）over useful life 。 HKAS 16.43–47 ：每個成本重大嘅 component 分開折舊 。 HKAS 16.48–49 ：depreciation 入 P&L，除非計入另一資產成本（如生產設備折舊 → Dr Inventories / Cr Accumulated depreciation）。 HKAS 16.55 ： 開始 折舊 = 資產處於 location and condition necessary to be capable of operating as intended（ ready for use 就開始，唔係開始用先折 ）； 停止 = earlier of held for sale（HKFRS 5）或 derecognised；閒置資產 繼續折舊 （usage method 下 charge 可為零）。 HKAS 16.56–57 ：useful life 考慮 expected usage、wear and tear、technical/commercial obsolescence、legal limits；useful life 可以 短過 economic life（entity specific）。 HKAS 16.58–59 ：freehold land 一般 唔折舊 （無限 useful life）；但 quarries、landfill 等有限壽命土地要折；含 dismantling/restoration 成本嘅部分要折。 HKAS 16.62 ：三個認可方法： straight line / diminishing balance / units of production ； HKAS 16.62A：禁止 revenue based depreciation 。 HKAS 16.51, 60–61 ：residual value、useful life、depreciation method 至少每年年結檢討 ；改變屬 change in accounting estimate（HKAS 8）→ 前瞻性（prospective）處理，唔准追朔調整 。 Diminishing balance 伏位：rate 乘以 carrying amount（唔扣 residual value） ；residual value 只作為下限（floor）。 E. Derecognition（終止確認） HKAS 16.67 ：disposed of 或 no future economic benefits expected → derecognise。 HKAS 16.71 ：Gain/loss = net disposal proceeds − carrying amount （carrying amount 計到出售日，記得計返至出售日嘅折舊）。 HKAS 16.68 ：gain/loss 入 P&L ，但 gains 唔准列入 revenue （列入 other income）。 Revalued asset 出售：gain/loss 按 revalued carrying amount 計；revaluation surplus 直接轉 retained earnings（HKAS 16.41）， 唔 recycle 經 P&L 。 F. Disclosure（披露） HKAS 16.73 ：每個 class 披露 — measurement basis、depreciation methods、useful lives or depreciation rates、gross carrying amount 及 accumulated depreciation（連 impairment）期初期末、 carrying amount 期初到期末 reconciliation （additions、disposals、business combinations acquisitions、revaluations、impairment losses/reversals、depreciation）。 HKAS 16.77 （revalued assets 額外披露）：effective date of revaluation、whether an independent valuer was involved、 如用 cost model 會係幾多 (16.77(e))、revaluation surplus 變動及分配限制、HKFRS 13 嘅 fair value hierarchy 資料。 另加 HKAS 36（impairment）、HKAS 8（estimate changes）、HKAS 1（estimation uncertainty）嘅相關披露。 必記 Journal Entries（全部平衡） 1. 購入 PPE（含未付部分） Account Dr Cr PPE 680 Cash 50 Trade payables 5 Loan payable 625 2. Dismantling obligation（HKAS 16.16(c) + HKAS 37） Account Dr Cr PPE（discounted estimate） 920,619 Provision for make good obligations 920,619 3. 折舊 Account Dr Cr Depreciation expense (P&L) XXX Accumulated depreciation XXX 4. Impairment（cost model） Account Dr Cr Impairment loss (P&L) XXX Accumulated impairment losses XXX 5. Revaluation increase（net method，首次重估）— gross 200 / acc dep 50 / FV 168（HK$'000） Account Dr Cr Accumulated depreciation 50 PPE 50 PPE 18 Revaluation surplus (OCI) 18 6. Revaluation decrease 超出 surplus — 減值 9，surplus 餘額只有 6 → Dr surplus 6（OCI）+ Dr loss 3（P&L） Account Dr Cr Revaluation surplus (OCI) 6 Revaluation loss (P&L) 3 PPE 9 7. 出售（cost model）— cost 800 / acc dep 525 / proceeds 250 Account Dr Cr Cash 250 Accumulated depreciation 525 Loss on sale (P&L) 25 Plant 800 8. Revalued asset 出售後轉 surplus（唔經 P&L） Account Dr Cr Revaluation surplus XXX Retained earnings XXX 易混淆概念對比 對比一：Cost Model vs Revaluation Model（HKAS 16.30 vs 16.31） 比較點 Cost Model (HKAS 16.30) Revaluation Model (HKAS 16.31) Carrying amount Cost − accumulated depreciation − accumulated impairment losses FV at revaluation date − subsequent accumulated depreciation − subsequent impairment losses 適用範圍 任何 PPE 只限 FV 能 可靠計量 嘅資產 政策一致性 按 class 一致應用（16.29） 重估一項 → 成個 class 都要重估 （16.36）；regularity 要求（16.38） 價值上升 唔認（無 upward adjustment） Credit OCI — revaluation surplus （16.39） 價值下跌 Impairment → P&L （HKAS 36） 先扣 revaluation surplus（OCI），超出部分 → P&L （16.40） Impairment 是否適用 適用 一樣適用 ，但當 revaluation decrease 處理 💬 點樣分辨／考試伏位 ：睇題目 policy 講明用邊個 model；revaluation model 唔代表唔使折舊、唔使減值（兩者都照做）。最常伏位： 減值時忘記先扣盡 surplus ；或將 revaluation increase 錯誤入 P&L。 對比二：Capitalise（直接歸屬成本）vs Expense（唔准資本化） 比較點 Capitalise（HKAS 16.16–17） Expense（HKAS 16.19–20） 原則 令資產達到 location and condition necessary for intended use 所必需 資產 ready 後發生，或屬經營/推廣性質 例子 Purchase price（扣 discount）、import duties、 non refundable taxes（如 stamp duty） 、site preparation、delivery & handling、installation、testing、professional fees、dismantling obligation、qualifying borrowing costs Refundable taxes（如 VAT） 、opening ceremony、staff training、advertising、initial operating losses、abnormal wastage、general admin overheads、recurring operating costs（如年度保險、年檢費） Subsequent costs 提升 capacity / 延長 life / 提高產出 → capitalise（component replacement 都計） Repairs & maintenance（只恢復原狀）→ expense（16.12） Testing 產出樣本 Testing 成本本身資本化 賣樣本 proceeds 入 P&L （16.20A），唔准扣資產成本 💬 點樣分辨／考試伏位 ：問自己「呢筆錢係咪令資產 ready for use 所必需？」——係就 capitalise。考試常混： VAT（refundable → expense）vs stamp duty（non refundable → capitalise） ； transit insurance（資本化）vs annual insurance（費用化） ； initial testing（資本化）vs opening function（費用化） 。 Phase 2 閃卡 Card 1 Front: Under HKAS 16.7, what are the two criteria for recognising the cost of an item of PPE as an asset? Back: It is probable that future economic benefits associated with the item will flow to the entity; and The cost of the item can be measured reliably . Failing items → expense when incurred (HKAS 16.7). 💬 兩個條件缺一不可：「好大機會有將來利益流入」＋「成本可靠計量」。記唔齊兩個條件係常見扣分位。 Card 2 Front: List the three elements of cost of an item of PPE under HKAS 16.16, and name four examples of directly attributable costs under HKAS 16.17. Back: Elements: (1) purchase price (incl. import duties, non refundable taxes, net of trade discounts/rebates); (2) directly attributable costs; (3) initial estimate of dismantling/removal/site restoration obligations. Directly attributable examples: site preparation; initial delivery and handling; installation and assembly; testing costs; professional fees; employee benefits from construction/acquisition. 💬 口訣：「買價＋搞掂佢用到嘅直接成本＋拆遷復原責任」。VAT 可退 → 唔計；stamp duty 唔可退 → 計。 Card 3 Front: Which costs must be EXCLUDED from the cost of PPE under HKAS 16.19–20? Back: Costs of opening a new facility; introducing a new product/service (advertising); conducting business in a new location or with a new class of customer (incl. staff training); Administration and other general overheads; abnormal wastage; Costs incurred while the asset is idle or operating below full capacity; initial operating losses; relocation/reorganisation costs. Proceeds from selling items produced during testing → P&L (HKAS 16.20A). 💬 見到「開幕、培訓、廣告、搬遷、閒置」呢啲字眼，一律費用化。 Card 4 Front: State the measurement rules for the cost model (HKAS 16.30) and the revaluation model (HKAS 16.31), and the class rule in HKAS 16.36. Back: Cost model: cost less accumulated depreciation and accumulated impairment losses . Revaluation model: fair value at the revaluation date less subsequent accumulated depreciation and subsequent impairment losses; only where FV can be measured reliably; revaluations with sufficient regularity (16.38). HKAS 16.36: if one item is revalued, the entire class must be revalued. 💬 揀咗 revaluation model 唔可以「逐件揀嚟估」——成個 class 一齊重估，但唔同 class 可以用唔同 model。 Card 5 Front: How are revaluation increases and decreases accounted for under HKAS 16.39 and 16.40? Back: Increase → credit OCI (revaluation surplus) ; EXCEPT recognise in P&L to the extent it reverses a previous revaluation decrease of the same asset recognised in P&L (16.39). Decrease → P&L ; EXCEPT debit OCI to the extent of any existing credit balance in the revaluation surplus for that asset; excess → P&L (16.40). Entries decided asset by asset , though revaluation is whole of class. 💬 口訣：「升 → OCI；跌 → P&L；逆轉優先，跟返上次條路」。跌落嚟先食盡 surplus，多出嚟先碰 P&L。 Card 6 Front: When does depreciation commence and cease under HKAS 16.55? What are the three permitted methods and the prohibition in HKAS 16.62A? Back: Commences: when the asset is in the location and condition necessary to be capable of operating as intended by management (ready for use, even if not yet used). Ceases: at the earlier of classification as held for sale (HKFRS 5) and derecognition; idle assets keep depreciating (charge can be zero under usage method). Methods: straight line; diminishing balance; units of production (16.62). Revenue based depreciation is not appropriate (16.62A). 💬 「Ready for use 即開始折」係大伏位——唔係「開始用」先折。Diminishing balance 唔扣 residual value（佢只係下限）。 Card 7 Front: How is a change in residual value, useful life or depreciation method accounted for? Back: Review residual value, useful life and method at least at each financial year end (HKAS 16.51). Treat as a change in accounting estimate under HKAS 8 → apply prospectively (no cumulative catch up): allocate the revised depreciable amount over the remaining useful life from the date of re estimate. 💬 千祈唔好返轉頭改舊數。新折舊 = 改估嗰刻嘅 carrying amount ÷ 剩餘 useful life。 Card 8 Front: State the derecognition rules for PPE under HKAS 16.67–72, including the treatment of gains and of revaluation surplus on disposal. Back: Derecognise on disposal or when no future economic benefits are expected from use or disposal (16.67). Gain/loss = net disposal proceeds − carrying amount (carrying amount updated for depreciation to disposal date) → P&L (16.71). Gains are NOT classified as revenue (16.68) — include in other income. Revaluation surplus on a disposed revalued asset → transferred directly to retained earnings , not through P&L (16.41). 💬 賣 PPE 嘅 gain 唔係 revenue！仲有 surplus 轉 RE 係 equity 內部轉賬，永遠唔經 P&L。 本章急救詞彙 EN Term 繁中白話 English Model Sentence Carrying amount 賬面值（成本減累計折舊同減值） The plant's carrying amount is its cost of HK$100m less accumulated depreciation of HK$20m and accumulated impairment losses of HK$5m. Depreciable amount 應折舊金額（成本減剩餘價值） The depreciable amount of HK$20,000 (cost HK$25,000 less residual value HK$5,000) is allocated over five years. Residual value 剩餘價值：假設資產而家已經到咗退役年齡同狀態，而家賣到幾多錢（扣埋出售成本） The residual value is the estimated amount currently obtainable from disposal if the asset were already of the age and condition expected at the end of its useful life. Useful life vs Economic life Useful life 係「我公司預計用幾耐」（entity specific，可以短啲）；economic life 係「件資產本身經濟上用得幾耐」 Because CDE replaces executive vehicles every four years, the vehicles' useful life (4 years) is shorter than their economic life (7–10 years). Revaluation surplus 重估盈餘：重估增值入 OCI 累積喺 equity 嘅儲備 The revaluation increase of HK$40,000 is credited to the revaluation surplus in other comprehensive income. Component approach 部件法：重大部件當獨立資產，各自折舊同重置資本化 Under the component approach, the aircraft engines and seats are depreciated separately from the airframe. Derecognition 終止確認：出售或無將來利益時，將資產賬面值移出賬簿 The carrying amount of the plant is derecognised on sale, and the resulting gain of HK$25,000 is recognised in profit or loss. Accumulated depreciation 累計折舊：contra asset（資產減項），唔係負債 Accumulated depreciation is a contra asset deducted from the gross carrying amount, not a liability.
