excerpt: M6 Chapter 7: Lease Accounting — Phase 3 Quiz Rules: Closed book · 15 minutes · 5 questions · Submit as 1. … 2. … 3. … 4. … 5. … — 超時如實申報 Q1. On 1 March 20X9, L…
text: M6 Chapter 7: Lease Accounting — Phase 3 Quiz Rules: Closed book · 15 minutes · 5 questions · Submit as 1. … 2. … 3. … 4. … 5. … — 超時如實申報 Q1. On 1 March 20X9, Lantern Logistics Limited (Lantern) enters into a five year contract with Victoria Storage Limited (Victoria) for the use of a specified floor area (Unit 8) in Victoria's warehouse in Kwai Chung. The contract states that Victoria may, at any time and without Lantern's consent, relocate Lantern's goods to another comparable unit in the same warehouse complex. Victoria frequently exercises this right in practice, because it can lease premium ground floor units to other customers at significantly higher rentals, and the cost of moving Lantern's goods (which are stored on movable pallets) is minimal. In accordance with HKFRS 16, which of the following statements is correct? A. The contract contains a lease because Unit 8 is explicitly specified in the contract. B. The contract contains a lease because Lantern obtains substantially all of the economic benefits from using the storage space. C. The contract does not contain a lease because Victoria has a substantive substitution right, so there is no identified asset. D. The contract does not contain a lease because Lantern does not have the right to operate the warehouse. Q2. On 1 April 20X9, Harbour Retail Limited (Harbour Retail) enters into a lease of a shop unit with a four year non cancellable period and an option to extend the lease for a further two years at a rental set at 30% below the prevailing market rate. At the commencement date, Harbour Retail has just completed significant leasehold improvements to the shop unit at its own expense, which are expected to generate economic benefits over the next seven years and can only be enjoyed through continued tenancy of the unit. In accordance with HKFRS 16, what is the lease term at the commencement date? A. Four years, because only the non cancellable period of a lease is ever included in the lease term. B. Six years, because Harbour Retail is reasonably certain to exercise the extension option. C. The lease term cannot be determined until Harbour Retail actually exercises the extension option. D. Seven years, because the leasehold improvements are expected to generate benefits over seven years. Q3. On 1 January 20X9, Bamboo Manufacturing Limited (Bamboo) enters into a four year lease of a machine with Peak Equipment Limited. Annual lease payments of HK$80,000 are payable in arrears on 31 December each year. In addition, the contract requires a variable payment each year equal to 2% of Bamboo's annual sales; Bamboo estimates this variable payment will be approximately HK$10,000 per year. Bamboo guarantees that the residual value of the machine at the end of the lease term will be at least HK$20,000; Bamboo expects it will need to pay HK$5,000 under this residual value guarantee. The interest rate implicit in the lease is 6% per annum and is known to Bamboo. (Round your answer to the nearest HK$.) In accordance with HKFRS 16, what is the initial measurement of the lease liability at 1 January 20X9? A. HK$293,051 B. HK$281,169 C. HK$325,000 D. HK$315,820 Q4. On 1 January 20X9, Coral Trading Limited (Coral) enters into a lease of office premises. The lease liability is initially measured at HK$500,000. Annual lease payments of HK$120,000 are payable in arrears on 31 December each year. The interest rate implicit in the lease is 5% per annum. Coral's reporting date is 31 December. In accordance with HKFRS 16, which journal entry should Coral record on 31 December 20X9 in respect of the lease payment? A. Dr Lease liability HK$120,000; Cr Cash HK$120,000 B. Dr Interest expense HK$25,000; Dr Lease liability HK$95,000; Cr Cash HK$120,000 C. Dr Interest expense HK$25,000; Cr Lease liability HK$25,000 D. Dr Right of use asset HK$95,000; Dr Interest expense HK$25,000; Cr Cash HK$120,000 Q5. On 1 January 20X9, Dragon Motors Limited (Dragon Motors), a dealer of commercial vehicles, enters into a finance lease of a delivery van with Sunrise Catering Limited. The fair value of the van is HK$400,000 and its carrying amount in Dragon Motors' inventory is HK$320,000. The present value of the lease payments accruing to Dragon Motors, discounted at the market rate of interest, is HK$380,000. There is no unguaranteed residual value. Costs incurred by Dragon Motors in obtaining the lease amount to HK$8,000. In accordance with HKFRS 16, which of the following correctly states the amounts Dragon Motors should recognise in profit or loss at the commencement date (excluding the subsequent finance income)? A. Revenue HK$380,000; cost of goods sold HK$320,000; selling profit HK$60,000; lease costs of HK$8,000 expensed B. Revenue HK$400,000; cost of goods sold HK$320,000; selling profit HK$80,000; lease costs of HK$8,000 included in the net investment in the lease C. Revenue HK$nil; the lease is purely a financing arrangement, so only finance income is recognised over the lease term D. Revenue HK$400,000; cost of goods sold HK$320,000; selling profit HK$80,000; lease costs of HK$8,000 expensed End of quiz. 唔准翻書，交卷後先好對答案。

title: M6 Chapter 8: Borrowing Costs — Phase 1 速查表 + Phase 2 閃卡
headings: M6 Chapter 8: Borrowing Costs — Phase 1 速查表 + Phase 2 閃卡
A. Recognition criteria（邊啲 borrowing costs 要資本化？）
excerpt: M6 Chapter 8: Borrowing Costs — Phase 1 速查表 + Phase 2 閃卡 Phase 1 速查表 Learning Objectives 1. Explain the criteria for capitalisation of borrowing costs under HKA…
text: M6 Chapter 8: Borrowing Costs — Phase 1 速查表 + Phase 2 閃卡 Phase 1 速查表 Learning Objectives 1. Explain the criteria for capitalisation of borrowing costs under HKAS 23, including the definition of a qualifying asset. (LO 2.08.01) 2. Determine the commencement date, suspension and cessation of the capitalisation period. 3. Calculate the borrowing costs eligible for capitalisation for specific borrowings (actual costs less investment income) and for general borrowings (capitalisation rate × expenditures). (LO 2.08.02) 4. Prepare journal entries to record capitalised and expensed borrowing costs. 必背考點 A. Recognition criteria（邊啲 borrowing costs 要資本化？） 規則 內容 Citation Core principle Borrowing costs that are directly attributable to the acquisition, construction or production of a qualifying asset form part of the cost of that asset. All other borrowing costs are recognised as an expense in the period incurred. HKAS 23.1, HKAS 23.8 Directly attributable Borrowing costs that would have been avoided if the expenditure on the qualifying asset had not been made. HKAS 23.10 Qualifying asset An asset that necessarily takes a substantial period of time to get ready for its intended use or sale. May include: inventories, manufacturing plants, power generation facilities, intangible assets, investment properties. HKAS 23.5, HKAS 23.7 NOT qualifying assets Financial assets; inventories manufactured or otherwise produced over a short time period / in large quantities on a repetitive basis; assets ready for their intended use or sale when acquired . HKAS 23.7, HKAS 23.4(b) Scope exclusion The cost of equity (actual or imputed) is not within the scope of HKAS 23 — only debt related costs (bank loans, overdrafts, bonds). HKAS 23.1 Borrowing costs defined Interest and other costs an entity incurs in connection with the borrowing of funds. HKAS 23.5 B. Measurement rules（計幾多？） B1. Capitalisation period（資本化期間） 階段 規則 Citation Commencement Begin capitalising on the commencement date — the date when the entity first meets ALL THREE conditions: (1) it incurs expenditures for the asset (cash paid, other assets transferred, or interest bearing liabilities assumed); (2) it incurs borrowing costs ; (3) it undertakes activities necessary to prepare the asset for its intended use or sale. Activities include technical/administrative work prior to physical construction (e.g. obtaining permits), but NOT holding the asset with no development (e.g. land banking). HKAS 23.17 Suspension Suspend capitalisation during extended periods in which active development of the qualifying asset is suspended (e.g. construction put on hold due to an economic downturn). HKAS 23.20 Cessation Cease capitalisation when substantially all the activities necessary to prepare the asset for its intended use or sale are complete — normally when physical construction is complete, even if routine administrative work or minor modifications remain. HKAS 23.22 B2. Specific borrowings（專項借款）— HKAS 23.12 Eligible amount = actual borrowing costs incurred on that borrowing during the period LESS any investment income on the temporary investment of those borrowings. Investment income on surplus funds is NOT revenue — it is netted off against borrowing costs capitalised. 計法： Loan principal × interest rate × (months in capitalisation period / 12) − investment income B3. General borrowings（一般借款）— HKAS 23.14 Eligible amount = capitalisation rate × expenditures on the qualifying asset （按支出加權、按時間比例 pro rate）。 Capitalisation rate = weighted average of borrowing costs applicable to borrowings outstanding during the period, excluding borrowings made specifically for a qualifying asset. 上限規則： borrowing costs capitalised in a period cannot exceed the total borrowing costs incurred during that period. (HKAS 23.14) B4. Key journal entries（Dr/Cr 必須平衡） Case 1 — Specific borrowing, fully capitalised（如 Chee Entertainment 模式）： Case 2 — Specific borrowing, part capitalised / part expensed（如 Beeston Biotech 模式，commencement date 遲過 drawdown date）： Case 3 — General borrowings（如 Marshall Green Energy 模式）： C. Disclosure requirements 本章 LP 聚焦 recognition 與 measurement；HKAS 23 要求披露 the amount of borrowing costs capitalised during the period 及 the capitalisation rate used to determine eligible borrowing costs。 ⚠️ 不確定提示：以上 disclosure 要點為 HKAS 23 標準正文內容（para. 26），LP 本章正文未列出具體段落號，考試如問 disclosure 以「amount capitalised + capitalisation rate」兩點作答。 易混淆概念對比 Table 1: Specific borrowings vs General borrowings Specific borrowings General borrowings Meaning Funds borrowed specifically to obtain a particular qualifying asset Funds borrowed generally , part of which is used on the qualifying asset Eligible amount Actual borrowing costs incurred on that borrowing, less investment income on temporary investment of surplus funds Capitalisation rate × expenditures on the asset (time apportioned) Rate used Actual rate on that specific loan Weighted average of all general borrowings outstanding (exclude specific borrowings) Investment income Deducted from capitalisable costs (NOT recognised as revenue) Not relevant — income on general funds is normal investment income 點樣分辨 題目話「borrowed to construct/finance project X」→ specific；話「drew on existing borrowings / general pool of funds」→ general。考試伏位：specific borrowing 嘅 investment income 唔可以入 revenue，要扣減資本化金額（Jun 2024 panelist 話呢度成日錯）。 考試伏位：記住 capitalisation rate 唔好用 simple average，要用 weighted average；仲要按月份 pro rate。 Table 2: Commencement vs Suspension vs Cessation of capitalisation Commencement Suspension Cessation Trigger ALL THREE met: expenditures incurred + borrowing costs incurred + preparation activities underway Extended periods of suspended active development Substantially all activities to prepare the asset for use/sale are complete Typical example Loan drawn, first payment made, construction/permit work started Construction on hold due to economic downturn Physical construction complete; only routine admin work or minor modifications left Borrowing costs in period Capitalise from this date onwards Expense during suspension period Expense after this point 考試伏位 三個條件 齊先有得開始 ，用 最遲 嗰個 date（e.g. 借錢 1 June 但 1 July 先找數兼動工 → 1 July）。Technical/admin work（拎 permits）計 activity，但 land banking 唔計 。 「Extended period」先 suspend；短暫停工（如季節性 delay 係工程必要一部分）唔使 suspend。 唔好等到甩埋所有 paperwork 先停——physical construction complete 就 cease。 Phase 2 閃卡 Card 1 Front: Under HKAS 23, what is a "qualifying asset"? Give three examples and two exclusions. Back: An asset that necessarily takes a substantial period of time to get ready for its intended use or sale (HKAS 23.5). Examples: manufacturing plants, power generation facilities, investment properties (also inventories / intangible assets). Exclusions: financial assets; inventories produced over a short period / in large quantities on a repetitive basis; assets ready for use or sale when acquired. 💬 白話：「substantial period」即係要起好耐先用得嗰啲資產。買架現成車返嚟即刻用 → 唔係；起 3 年嘅廠房 → 係。大量生產嘅罐頭汽水雖然係 inventory，但係重複性大量製造，唔使資本化利息。 Card 2 Front: State the core principle of HKAS 23 regarding recognition of borrowing costs. Back: Borrowing costs directly attributable to the acquisition, construction or production of a qualifying asset → capitalise as part of the cost of that asset (HKAS 23.8). All other borrowing costs → expense in the period incurred. Cost of equity (actual or imputed) is outside the scope of HKAS 23. 💬 白話：借錢起嘢，利息就跟埋個資產成本；借錢做一般生意，利息就即刻 expense。發股集資嘅成本 HKAS 23 完全唔理。 Card 3 Front: What are the THREE conditions that must ALL be met before capitalisation of borrowing costs can commence? Back: (HKAS 23.17) 1. The entity incurs expenditures for the asset (cash paid / other assets transferred / interest bearing liabilities assumed); 2. The entity incurs borrowing costs ; and 3. The entity undertakes activities necessary to prepare the asset for its intended use or sale (includes pre construction technical/administrative work like permits; excludes land banking). 💬 白話：三個條件「晒冷」先可以開始計，所以 commencement date = 三樣嘢入面 最遲發生 嗰日。攞住塊地乜都唔做（land banking）唔算 activities。 Card 4 Front: When must capitalisation of borrowing costs be (a) suspended and (b) ceased? Back: (a) Suspend during extended periods when active development is suspended (HKAS 23.20). (b) Cease when substantially all activities necessary to prepare the asset for intended use or sale are complete — normally at completion of physical construction, even if routine admin work / minor modifications remain (HKAS 23.22). 💬 白話：suspend 係「暫停」——經濟差停工一年嗰啲；cease 係「收工」——樓起好咗就停，唔好等埋啲小執小修。暫停/停止期間嘅利息全部入 P/L。 Card 5 Front: How are borrowing costs on a SPECIFIC borrowing measured for capitalisation? What happens to investment income earned on surplus funds? Back: (HKAS 23.12) Capitalise the actual borrowing costs incurred on that borrowing during the period, less any investment income on the temporary investment of those borrowings. Investment income is netted against borrowing costs capitalised — it is NOT recognised as revenue . 💬 白話：借咗 HK$20m 但未用得晒，擺去投資賺咗利息 → 呢啲利息收入唔係 revenue，係要 扣減 資本化金額。呢點係 past paper 常客。 Card 6 Front: How is the capitalisation rate determined for GENERAL borrowings, and how is it applied? Back: (HKAS 23.14) Capitalisation rate = weighted average of borrowing costs applicable to borrowings outstanding during the period, excluding borrowings made specifically for a qualifying asset. Apply the rate to the expenditures on the qualifying asset (time apportioned). Cap: amount capitalised cannot exceed total borrowing costs incurred in the period. 💬 白話：一般借款冇得話邊筆錢起邊個項目，所以用加權平均利率（唔係 simple average！）乘以項目支出，再按月份 pro rate。 Card 7 Front: A company borrowed HK$785m at 4.75% on 1 June 20X7; construction payment and activities began 1 July 20X7. Year end 31 December 20X7. How much interest is capitalised vs expensed? Back: Total interest incurred: HK$785m × 4.75% × 7/12 = HK$21,751,042 Commencement date = 1 July 20X7 (all three conditions met only then) Capitalised: HK$785m × 4.75% × 6/12 = HK$18,643,750 → Dr R&D facility Expensed: HK$3,107,092 → Dr Interest expense (P/L) 💬 白話：借錢日唔係 commencement date！6 月嗰個月未找數未動工，利息要 expense。考試最鍾意考「借錢早過動工」呢個時間差。 Card 8 Front: Prepare the journal entry to capitalise HK$885,417 of borrowing costs on a manufacturing plant funded by a specific loan facility (interest paid in cash). Back: Debit goes to the asset (cost of qualifying asset), not to Interest expense. If part of the interest relates to periods before commencement, split: Dr asset (capitalised portion) + Dr Interest expense (pre commencement portion) / Cr Cash (total). 💬 白話：資本化 = Dr 資產、唔係 Dr expense。記住個 entry 要平衡，有得分拆嘅話兩個 Dr 加埋要等於 Cr。 本章急救詞彙 EN Term 繁中白話 English Model Sentence Borrowing costs 借錢嘅利息同相關成本（只包 debt，唔包 equity 成本） Borrowing costs are interest and other costs that an entity incurs in connection with the borrowing of funds. Qualifying asset 要花好長時間先整到可以用/賣嘅資產 A qualifying asset is an asset that necessarily takes a substantial period of time to get ready for its intended use or sale. Directly attributable 唔起呢個項目就唔使俾嘅成本 Directly attributable borrowing costs are those that would have been avoided if the expenditure on the qualifying asset had not been made. Commencement date 三個條件首次齊集嗰日，即開始資本化之日 The commencement date is the date when the entity first meets all three conditions in HKAS 23.17. Capitalisation rate 一般借款嘅加權平均利率 The capitalisation rate is the weighted average of the borrowing costs applicable to borrowings outstanding during the period, excluding specific borrowings. Suspension of capitalisation 停工好耐嗰段期間，利息要停資本化 Capitalisation is suspended during extended periods in which active development of a qualifying asset is suspended. Cessation of capitalisation 資產大致起好嗰刻，之後利息全部 expense Capitalisation ceases when substantially all the activities necessary to prepare the qualifying asset for its intended use or sale are complete. Investment income offset 專項借款未用嘅錢賺到嘅利息，要扣返資本化金額 Investment income on the temporary investment of specific borrowings is deducted from borrowing costs eligible for capitalisation.

title: M6 Chapter 8: Borrowing Costs — Phase 3 Answers
headings: M6 Chapter 8: Borrowing Costs — Phase 3 Answers
excerpt: M6 Chapter 8: Borrowing Costs — Phase 3 Answers Q1 — Answer: B Model Answer (EN): B is correct. Under HKAS 23.5, a qualifying asset is an asset that necessarily…
text: M6 Chapter 8: Borrowing Costs — Phase 3 Answers Q1 — Answer: B Model Answer (EN): B is correct. Under HKAS 23.5, a qualifying asset is an asset that necessarily takes a substantial period of time to get ready for its intended use or sale. A cruise terminal taking 30 months to construct satisfies this definition (manufacturing plants and similar long construction assets are listed as possible qualifying assets in HKAS 23.7). A is not qualifying: inventories manufactured in large quantities on a repetitive basis over a short period are excluded (HKAS 23.4(b)/23.7). C is not qualifying: assets ready for their intended use when acquired are excluded. D is not qualifying: financial assets are explicitly excluded. 解題思路（繁中）: 考「qualifying asset」定義。A 係大量重複生產、兩日搞掂嘅 inventory —— HKAS 23 明確排除，唔使因為佢係 inventory 就以為可以資本化。C 買返嚟即刻用得 → 「ready for intended use when acquired」唔係 qualifying asset。D 係 financial asset，直接排除。B 起 30 個月，明顯係 substantial period。考試伏位：唔好以為「inventory 一定係/一定唔係」——關鍵係生產期長短同埋係咪大量重複製造。 Rule Check: HKAS 23.5, HKAS 23.7, HKAS 23.4(b) Common Trap（繁中）: 見到「inventory」就諗起 HKAS 23.7 話 inventories 可以係 qualifying assets，但忘記咗「manufactured in large quantities on a repetitive basis / short time period」嘅排除條款。 Q2 — Answer: D Model Answer (EN): D is correct. Under HKAS 23.17, capitalisation commences on the date when the entity first meets ALL three conditions: (1) expenditures for the asset are incurred; (2) borrowing costs are incurred; and (3) activities necessary to prepare the asset for its intended use or sale are undertaken. Borrowing costs began on 1 February 20X8, expenditures on 1 April 20X8, and preparation activities on 1 May 20X8. All three are first simultaneously met on 1 May 20X8. Note that obtaining development permits counts as a preparatory activity, but merely holding the asset (e.g. land banking) does not. 解題思路（繁中）: 三個條件「齊腳」先可以開始，所以 commencement date = 三個日子入面 最遲 嗰個。A（1 Jan）純粹干擾，同年初無關；B（1 Feb）只有 borrowing costs，未找數未動工；C（1 Apr）有 borrowing costs + expenditures，但 activities 未開始；D（1 May）三樣齊晒。考試伏位：題目講明拎 permits 都計 activities（technical/administrative work），但如果公司只係揸住塊地乜都唔做（land banking），就唔計。 Rule Check: HKAS 23.17 Common Trap（繁中）: 以為借錢嗰日（1 Feb）就可以開始資本化 —— 呢個係 past paper 反覆測試嘅弱點（commencement of capitalisation 被 panelist 點名為常錯位）。 Q3 — Answer: B Model Answer (EN): Capitalised = HK$40,000,000 × 6.00% × 7/12 = HK$1,400,000 (1 June – 31 December 20X8). Workings: Commencement date = 1 June 20X8 (expenditures incurred, borrowing costs incurred, and activities underway all first met on this date). Capitalisation period in the year = 7 months (June to December). Interest from 1 April to 31 May (2 months) = HK$40m × 6.00% × 2/12 = HK$400,000 → expensed in profit or loss. Since the funds were borrowed specifically for the hub and no surplus funds were invested, the actual borrowing costs incurred during the capitalisation period are capitalised in full (HKAS 23.12). 解題思路（繁中）: A（HK$1,800,000）= 成個借款期 9 個月（Apr–Dec）全數資本化 —— 錯在 4、5 月未動工未找數，未過 commencement date，嗰兩個月利息要 expense。C（HK$1,200,000）= 只計 6 個月，數錯月份。D（HK$2,400,000）= 成 12 個月全年度利息，完全無視 drawdown 同 commencement 都係年中。正確係 B：由 1 June commencement date 起計 7 個月。考試伏位：specific borrowing 如果有 temporarily invested 嘅 surplus funds，投資收入要扣減資本化金額（本题話明冇投資，所以唔使扣）。 Rule Check: HKAS 23.12, HKAS 23.17 Common Trap（繁中）: 「借錢日 = 資本化開始日」嘅謬誤；仲有月份數錯（Jun–Dec 係 7 個月唔係 6 個月 —— 用 12 − 5 嚟數）。 Q4 — Answer: C Model Answer (EN): Capitalised = Expenditures × capitalisation rate × time apportionment = HK$24,000,000 × 5.60% × 5/12 = HK$560,000 . Workings (HKAS 23.14 — capitalisation rate = weighted average of general borrowings outstanding, excluding specific borrowings): Borrowing Rate Weight Contribution HK$60m bank loan 5.00% 60/150 2.00% HK$90m bonds 6.00% 90/150 3.60% Total HK$150m 5.60% HK$24m × 5.60% × 5/12 = HK$560,000. Cap check: capitalised HK$560,000 < total borrowing costs incurred (HK$60m × 5% + HK$90m × 6% = HK$8,400,000) — cap not breached. 解題思路（繁中）: A（HK$500,000）= 只用 5.00% 最低利率 —— 錯，一般借款要用 weighted average。B（HK$550,000）= 用 simple average (5%+6%)/2 = 5.50% —— 錯，兩筆借款本金唔同，一定要按金額加權。D（HK$1,344,000）= 5.60% 乘足 12 個月，冇按 5 個月 pro rate —— 錯。正確 C：HK$24m × 5.60% × 5/12。考試伏位：(1) weighted average 唔係 simple average；(2) 記住乘月份比例；(3) 記住上限規則 —— 資本化金額唔可以超過期內實際總借貸成本。 Rule Check: HKAS 23.14 Common Trap（繁中）: 用 simple average 利率（唔加權）或者唔做 time apportionment —— 兩者都係 distractor 嘅來源，亦係真實考生常犯錯誤。 Q5 — Answer: D Model Answer (EN): Total Dr (7,200,000) = Total Cr (7,200,000). The entry mirrors the LP treatment for general borrowings: only the eligible amount (expenditures × capitalisation rate, time apportioned) is debited to the asset; all remaining borrowing costs are expensed (HKAS 23.8, 23.14). 解題思路（繁中）: A 將全部 HK$7.2m 入 expense —— 錯，直接歸屬 qualifying asset 嘅部分必須資本化（唔係 optional）。B 將全部利息資本化 —— 錯，只有合資格嘅 HK$450k 先可以入資產成本，其餘係一般融資成本。C 只入咗資本化部分，完全冇記錄其餘 HK$6.75m 利息 —— 錯，entry 唔平衡之餘仲漏咗 expense。D 正確：Dr 資產 450k + Dr Interest expense 6,750k = Cr Cash 7,200k，借貸平衡。考試伏位：CBE 格式可能用 journal entry grid 考呢種 entry —— 記住「Dr asset（合資格部分）+ Dr Interest expense（剩餘部分）/ Cr Cash（總額）」呢個三段式結構。 Rule Check: HKAS 23.8, HKAS 23.14 Common Trap（繁中）: 以為資本化係 accounting policy choice（其實 HKAS 23 強制資本化直接歸屬嘅 borrowing costs）；或者整個 entry 得一半，漏記 expensed 部分。

title: M6 Chapter 8: Borrowing Costs — Phase 3 Quiz
headings: M6 Chapter 8: Borrowing Costs — Phase 3 Quiz
excerpt: M6 Chapter 8: Borrowing Costs — Phase 3 Quiz Rules: Closed book · 15 minutes · 5 questions · Submit as 1. … 2. … 3. … 4. … 5. … — 超時如實申報 Question 1 According to…
text: M6 Chapter 8: Borrowing Costs — Phase 3 Quiz Rules: Closed book · 15 minutes · 5 questions · Submit as 1. … 2. … 3. … 4. … 5. … — 超時如實申報 Question 1 According to HKAS 23 Borrowing Costs , which of the following assets of Kestrel Holdings Limited is a qualifying asset? A. Smartphones assembled in large quantities on a repetitive production line, each taking two days to complete B. A cruise terminal under construction that is expected to take 30 months to complete and make ready for use C. A completed office floor purchased from a developer, ready for immediate occupation D. A portfolio of listed equity securities held for trading Question 2 Harbour Vista Properties Limited is constructing a ferry pier that meets the definition of a qualifying asset under HKAS 23. The relevant dates are: 1 February 20X8 — the company drew down a bank loan and began incurring borrowing costs 1 April 20X8 — the company paid the first construction costs to the contractor 1 May 20X8 — the company began activities necessary to prepare the pier for its intended use (obtaining development permits and commencing site works) In accordance with HKAS 23, on which date should Harbour Vista Properties Limited commence capitalisation of borrowing costs? A. 1 January 20X8 B. 1 February 20X8 C. 1 April 20X8 D. 1 May 20X8 Question 3 Falcon Logistics Limited borrowed HK$40 million from Metro Bank on 1 April 20X8 at a fixed interest rate of 6.00% per annum, specifically to construct an automated distribution hub. The hub is a qualifying asset; construction is expected to take 20 months. Construction activities began on 1 June 20X8, when the first payment of HK$15 million was made to the contractor. Falcon Logistics did not invest any surplus funds. Interest is paid annually. The company's year end is 31 December 20X8. In accordance with HKAS 23, what amount of borrowing costs should Falcon Logistics capitalise as part of the cost of the distribution hub for the year ended 31 December 20X8? A. HK$1,800,000 B. HK$1,400,000 C. HK$1,200,000 D. HK$2,400,000 Question 4 Lantau Renewables Limited is constructing a wind turbine assembly plant, a qualifying asset, funded entirely from its general borrowings. Its borrowings, outstanding unchanged throughout the year, are: HK$60 million bank loan at 5.00% per annum HK$90 million bonds issued at par at 6.00% per annum Expenditure on the plant of HK$24 million was incurred evenly from the commencement date, and five months have elapsed between the commencement date and the financial year end. No borrowings were made specifically for the plant. In accordance with HKAS 23, what amount of borrowing costs should be capitalised for the year? A. HK$500,000 B. HK$550,000 C. HK$560,000 D. HK$1,344,000 Question 5 Tamar Cold Storage Limited is constructing a refrigerated warehouse (a qualifying asset) funded from its general borrowings. Its total borrowing costs incurred during the year were HK$7,200,000, all paid in cash, and the borrowing costs eligible for capitalisation have been determined as HK$450,000. Which journal entry correctly records the borrowing costs for the year in accordance with HKAS 23? A. Dr Interest expense (P/L) 7,200,000; Cr Cash 7,200,000 B. Dr Refrigerated warehouse 7,200,000; Cr Cash 7,200,000 C. Dr Refrigerated warehouse 450,000; Cr Cash 450,000 D. Dr Refrigerated warehouse 450,000; Dr Interest expense (P/L) 6,750,000; Cr Cash 7,200,000

excerpt: M6 Chapter 9: Intangible Assets — Phase 1 速查表 + Phase 2 閃卡 Phase 1 速查表 Learning Objectives (3–5, English, action verbs) 1. Define an intangible asset and apply …
text: M6 Chapter 9: Intangible Assets — Phase 1 速查表 + Phase 2 閃卡 Phase 1 速查表 Learning Objectives (3–5, English, action verbs) 1. Define an intangible asset and apply the identifiability, control and future economic benefits criteria in accordance with HKAS 38. 2. Apply the recognition criteria and initial measurement rules for separately acquired intangible assets, intangible assets acquired in a business combination, and internally generated intangible assets. 3. Distinguish the research phase from the development phase and determine which expenditures may be capitalised under the six recognition criteria of HKAS 38.57. 4. Account for subsequent measurement of intangible assets under the cost model and the revaluation model, including amortisation, residual value, impairment (HKAS 36) and revaluation journals. 5. Prepare the disclosure requirements for intangible assets under HKAS 38, distinguishing internally generated from other intangible assets. 必背考點 A. Recognition（確認） 考點 Rule Reference Definition An intangible asset is an identifiable non monetary asset without physical substance . HKAS 38.8 Identifiability Identifiable if it is separable (can be sold, transferred, licenced, rented or exchanged) or arises from contractual or other legal rights (regardless of transferability). HKAS 38.12 Control Entity can obtain the future economic benefits and restrict others' access (usually via enforceable legal rights). Skilled workforce, market share, uncontracted customers → fail control test . HKAS 38.13 Future economic benefits Revenue, cost savings or other benefits; assessed using reasonable and supportable assumptions . HKAS 38.13, 38.17 Recognition criteria Recognise if, and only if: (1) probable future economic benefits will flow to the entity; and (2) cost can be measured reliably . HKAS 38.21 Subsequent expenditure Generally expensed as incurred (rarely adds to, or is distinguishable from, the existing asset). Applies to both acquired and internally generated intangibles. HKAS 38.20 Research vs Development（核心考點） 考點 Rule Reference Research definition Original and planned investigation undertaken with the prospect of gaining new scientific or technical knowledge and understanding . HKAS 38.8 Research costs Always expensed as incurred — probable future economic benefits cannot be demonstrated. HKAS 38.54 Development definition Application of research findings or other knowledge to a plan or design for new or substantially improved materials, devices, products, processes, systems or services before commercial production or use . HKAS 38.8 Development capitalisation — ALL SIX criteria ("PIRATE") ① technical feasibility of completion; ② intention to complete and use/sell; ③ ability to use or sell; ④ how the asset will generate probable future economic benefits ; ⑤ availability of adequate technical, financial and other resources ; ⑥ ability to measure expenditure reliably . HKAS 38.57 Cannot distinguish phases Treat all expenditure as research phase (expense) until costs can be reliably allocated. HKAS 38.53 Prohibited internally generated intangibles Internally generated brands, mastheads, publishing titles, customer lists and similar items shall not be recognised. HKAS 38.63 Internally generated goodwill Never recognised — not an identifiable resource controlled by the entity measurable reliably at cost. HKAS 38.48–49 B. Measurement（計量） Initial measurement（HKAS 38.24: all intangible assets initially measured at COST） Source Initial measurement Reference Separately acquired Cost = purchase price (incl. import duties and non refundable purchase taxes, after deducting trade discounts/rebates) + directly attributable costs of preparing the asset for intended use (e.g. legal fees to draw up acquisition contract). General/administration type costs (e.g. executives' time) are expensed . HKAS 38.27–28 Acquired in a business combination Fair value at acquisition date (HKFRS 13), even if not recognised in the acquiree's own books (e.g. internally generated brand of acquiree). HKFRS 3; HKAS 38.68 Goodwill in a business combination Residual = consideration − fair value of identifiable net assets acquired; recognised only in a business combination. HKFRS 3 Internally generated (development) Cost = expenditure from the date ALL six HKAS 38.57 criteria are first met; earlier expensed amounts are not reinstated. HKAS 38.57 Subsequent measurement — two models (policy choice applied per class of assets, HKAS 38.72) Model Carrying amount Reference Cost model Cost − accumulated amortisation − accumulated impairment losses HKAS 38.74 Revaluation model Fair value at revaluation date − subsequent accumulated amortisation − subsequent accumulated impairment losses. Only permitted if an active market exists (HKFRS 13 definition: transactions with sufficient frequency and volume). Rarely exists for brands, mastheads, patents, trademarks; may exist for licences, quotas, franchises, taxi licences. Cannot revalue assets never previously recognised; cannot initially recognise at other than cost. HKAS 38.75–76, 38.78 Revaluation increase Recognise in OCI and accumulate in equity under revaluation surplus — except to the extent it reverses a previous revaluation decrease of the same asset recognised in P&L (then credit P&L first). HKAS 38.85 Revaluation decrease Recognise in profit or loss — except to the extent a credit balance exists in revaluation surplus for that asset (debit OCI/surplus first, remainder to P&L). HKAS 38.86 Active market disappears Use last revalued amount − subsequent amortisation/impairment; disappearance is an impairment indicator → test under HKAS 36. HKAS 38.81 Amortisation & useful life 考點 Rule Reference Finite vs indefinite Assess whether useful life is finite or indefinite. Indefinite ≠ infinite : only when there is no foreseeable limit to the period of net cash inflows. HKAS 38.88 Contractual/legal rights Useful life = shorter of expected useful life and the contractual/legal period (renewal only if at holder's option without significant cost). HKAS 38.94, 38.96 Finite life — amortisation Depreciable amount allocated on a systematic basis over useful life reflecting the pattern of benefits; if pattern cannot be determined reliably → straight line . Begins when the asset is available for use ; ceases at earlier of HKFRS 5 held for sale classification or derecognition. Charge to P&L unless included in carrying amount of another asset (e.g. inventories). HKAS 38.97, 38.99 Residual value Assumed zero unless: third party contractually committed to buy, or an active market exists that will likely still exist at end of useful life. Reviewed each year end; change = change in estimate (HKAS 8). HKAS 38.100, 38.102 Indefinite life Not amortised ; impairment test annually AND whenever there is an indication (HKAS 36). Review indefinite assessment each period; change to finite = change in estimate (HKAS 8) and an impairment indicator. HKAS 38.107–110 Impairment Both cost model and revaluation model intangibles are subject to impairment under HKAS 36 . HKAS 36 C. Disclosure（披露） Requirement Reference By class of intangible assets, distinguishing internally generated from other intangibles: useful lives (indefinite/finite) or amortisation rates; amortisation methods; gross carrying amount and accumulated amortisation/impairment at beginning and end; line item(s) of the income statement containing amortisation; a reconciliation of opening to closing carrying amount (additions split: internal development / separately acquired / business combinations; disposals & held for sale; revaluation and impairment movements in OCI and P&L; amortisation; other changes). HKAS 38.118 Indefinite life assets: carrying amount and reasons/factors supporting the indefinite assessment; description, carrying amount and remaining amortisation period of any individually material intangible asset. HKAS 38.122 Changes in useful life assessment, amortisation method or residual values with material effect → disclose nature and impact (change in estimate per HKAS 8). HKAS 38.121 Revalued intangibles: effective date of revaluation; carrying amount of revalued assets; carrying amount had the cost model been used ; revaluation surplus opening/closing, changes and distribution restrictions. HKAS 38.124 D. Key Journal Entries（必識分錄） 1. Separate acquisition of an intangible asset Dr HK$ Cr HK$ : : Intangible asset (e.g. Patent) 500,000     Cash 500,000 2. Research phase expenditure (expensed) Dr HK$ Cr HK$ : : Research expense (P&L) 200,000     Cash / Payables 200,000 3. Development phase expenditure — all six criteria met (capitalised) Dr HK$ Cr HK$ : : Intangible asset — capitalised development costs 350,000     Cash / Payables 350,000 4. Amortisation of a finite life intangible asset Dr HK$ Cr HK$ : : Amortisation expense (P&L) 60,000     Accumulated amortisation 60,000 5. Revaluation increase — net method （cost 240,000; accumulated amortisation 90,000; revalued to 270,000） Step 1 — net out accumulated amortisation: Dr HK$ Cr HK$ : : Accumulated amortisation 90,000     Intangible asset 90,000 Step 2 — uplift carrying amount (150,000 → 270,000): Dr HK$ Cr HK$ : : Intangible asset 120,000     Revaluation surplus (OCI) 120,000 6. First time revaluation decrease（無 surplus 餘額） Dr HK$ Cr HK$ : : Loss on revaluation (P&L) 45,000     Intangible asset 45,000 （若同一資產之前曾向上重估並有 surplus 餘額：先 Dr Revaluation surplus (OCI) 至歸零，餘額先入 P&L。） 易混淆概念對比 對比表 1：Research Phase vs Development Phase Research Phase Development Phase Definition (HKAS 38.8) Original and planned investigation to gain new scientific or technical knowledge Application of research findings to a plan/design for new or substantially improved products/processes before commercial use Typical activities Obtaining new knowledge; searching for/evaluating/selecting alternatives for materials, products, processes Design/construction/testing of pre production prototypes ; design of tools, jigs, moulds with new technology; pilot plant not of commercially feasible scale Accounting treatment Always expense (HKAS 38.54) Capitalise only if ALL six criteria in HKAS 38.57 met ; otherwise expense If phases cannot be distinguished Treat everything as research → expense all (HKAS 38.53) — 💬 點樣分辨／考試伏位： 記口訣： Research = 搵知識（investigative, high risk）→ 必費用化；Development = 用知識做嘢（application）→ 六條件齊先可資本化 。 伏位一：「search for / evaluation and final selection of alternatives」聽落似做緊產品，其實係 research 。 伏位二：「pilot plant」要睇規模—— not of economically feasible scale for commercial production 先係 development。 伏位三：六個條件要 ALL 滿足，差一個都係 expense；而且係由 全部條件首次達成當日 起先開始資本化，之前已費用化嘅支出 不得重撥 。 伏位四（Jun 2025 panel report）：考生常混淆 definition 同 recognition criteria ——定義啱唔代表可以資本化。 對比表 2：Cost Model vs Revaluation Model（HKAS 38.72–86） Cost Model Revaluation Model Carrying amount Cost − accumulated amortisation − accumulated impairment (HKAS 38.74) FV at revaluation date − subsequent accumulated amortisation − impairment (HKAS 38.75) Availability Always available Only if an active market exists (HKFRS 13: sufficient frequency & volume of transactions) Typical assets Patents, brands, trademarks, mastheads (unique, no active market) Licences, production quotas, franchise agreements, taxi licences, broadcast rights Value increases Not reflected in financial statements Increase → OCI / revaluation surplus (HKAS 38.85) Value decreases Only via HKAS 36 impairment → P&L Decrease → P&L , unless surplus balance exists for that asset → debit OCI first (HKAS 38.86) Policy scope Applied per class of intangible assets Same class rule; asset in class without active market → must use cost model for that asset 💬 點樣分辨／考試伏位： 伏位一： goodwill 永遠唔可以 revalue （唔 separable，無 active market）；acquired brand name 都係 unique，無 active market。 伏位二：revaluation model 唔可以 用嚟首次確認資產（initial recognition 永遠係 cost）——business combination 嗰個 fair value 係 HKFRS 3 嘅要求，唔係 revaluation。 伏位三：revaluation decrease 落 P&L 前，要睇 同一資產 嘅 revaluation surplus 有冇 credit balance；increase 入 OCI 前，要睇同一資產有冇之前入過 P&L 嘅 decrease（先 reversal 入 P&L）。 伏位四：active market 消失 = impairment indicator （要按 HKAS 36 做減值測試），唔係「唔使理」。 Phase 2 閃卡 (exactly 8 cards) Card 1 Front: What is the definition of an intangible asset under HKAS 38, and what are its three key attributes? Back: An identifiable non monetary asset without physical substance (HKAS 38.8). Three attributes: identifiability (separable OR arises from contractual/other legal rights, HKAS 38.12); control over the benefits (HKAS 38.13); future economic benefits (HKAS 38.13, 38.17). 💬 白話解釋：無形資產要過三關——「認得出（可分割或有法律權利）」、「控制到（啲利益入你袋、人哋攞唔到）」、「有錢景（未來經濟利益）」。 skilled workforce、market share 呢啲過唔到 control 關，所以唔係資產。 Card 2 Front: State the recognition criteria for an intangible asset and its initial measurement basis (HKAS 38.21, 38.24). Back: Recognise if, and only if : (1) it is probable that expected future economic benefits will flow to the entity; and (2) the cost can be measured reliably (HKAS 38.21). All intangible assets, regardless of origin, are measured initially at cost (HKAS 38.24). 💬 白話解釋：兩個條件係 "AND" 關係，缺一不可。記住所有無形資產出世嗰刻一律用 cost——revaluation model 唔可以用嚟做首次確認。 Card 3 Front: What is included in the cost of a separately acquired intangible asset (HKAS 38.27–28)? Back: Purchase price (including import duties and non refundable purchase taxes , after deducting trade discounts/rebates); plus Directly attributable costs of preparing the asset for its intended use (e.g. legal fees to draw up the acquisition contract). Exclude: general/administration type costs (e.g. senior executives' time negotiating the deal) → expense. 💬 白話解釋：同 PPE 邏輯一樣——「為咗令件資產用得返而直接使嘅錢」先入 cost。高層飞去美國傾 deal 嘅人工係「唔買都會使」嘅錢，要費用化。 Card 4 Front: List the SIX criteria for capitalising development costs (HKAS 38.57). Back: 1. Technical feasibility of completing the asset for use/sale; 2. Intention to complete and use or sell it; 3. Ability to use or sell it; 4. How it will generate probable future economic benefits ; 5. Availability of adequate technical, financial and other resources to complete it; 6. Ability to measure the expenditure reliably . 💬 白話解釋：口訣 P I R A T E ：Probability of benefits、Intention、Resources、Ability to use/sell、Technical feasibility、Expenditure measurable。六個 ALL 要齊，考試鍾意出一條差一個條件嘅 scenario 考你費用化。 Card 5 Front: Which internally generated items does HKAS 38 explicitly prohibit from recognition, and why is internally generated goodwill never recognised? Back: Prohibited: internally generated brands, mastheads, publishing titles, customer lists and similar items (HKAS 38.63). Internally generated goodwill is not recognised (HKAS 38.48–49): it is not an identifiable resource (not separable, no contractual/legal rights) controlled by the entity that can be measured reliably at cost . Goodwill is recognised only when acquired in a business combination (HKFRS 3). 💬 白話解釋：自己做嘅品牌同客戶名單永遠唔入賬——因為啲支出同「發展成盤生意」嘅錢分唔開。Goodwill 只可以「買返嚟」，唔可以「自己種」。 Card 6 Front: How are revaluation increases and decreases of intangible assets treated (HKAS 38.85–86)? Back: Increase → OCI, accumulated in equity as revaluation surplus ; except to the extent it reverses a previous decrease of the same asset previously recognised in P&L → recognise in P&L first (HKAS 38.85). Decrease → P&L ; except to the extent a credit balance exists in the revaluation surplus for the same asset → debit OCI first, excess to P&L (HKAS 38.86). 💬 白話解釋：基本原則係「升 OCI、跌 P&L」，但要有 symmetry ：之前跌過入 P&L，而家升返要先補返 P&L；之前升過有 surplus，而家跌要先食 surplus。記住係按 same asset 計，唔係按 class。 Card 7 Front: Compare the subsequent accounting for finite life vs indefinite life intangible assets (HKAS 38.97, 38.107–110). Back: Finite life : amortise depreciable amount systematically over useful life (straight line if pattern unreliable); amortisation starts when available for use ; charge to P&L (HKAS 38.97, 38.99). Indefinite life : not amortised ; impairment test annually + on indication (HKAS 38.107–108); review the indefinite assessment each period ; change to finite = change in estimate (HKAS 8) and impairment indicator (HKAS 38.109–110). "Indefinite" does not mean "infinite" — it means no foreseeable limit to cash flows (HKAS 38.88). 💬 白話解釋：indefinite 唔等於無限，只係「睇唔到盡頭」。Indefinite life 唔攤銷但 每年必做 impairment test ；finite life 只係有 trigger 先做。由 indefinite 轉 finite 係 change in estimate（prospective） ，同時係減值訊號。 Card 8 Front: When may the residual value of a finite life intangible asset be non zero (HKAS 38.100)? Back: Residual value is assumed zero , unless : 1. a third party has contractually committed to buy the asset at the end of its useful life; or 2. there is an active market for the asset (HKFRS 13) and it will likely still exist at the end of the useful life. Changes in residual value = change in accounting estimate → HKAS 8 (HKAS 38.102). 💬 白話解釋：無形資產預設殘值係 零 ——呢點同 PPE 好大分別。只有兩個例外：有人簽約包底買返，或者有 active market 而且到期時市場仲存在。 本章急救詞彙 EN Term 繁中白話 English Model Sentence Intangible asset 無形資產：睇唔到摸唔到、可識別嘅非貨幣資產 An intangible asset is an identifiable non monetary asset without physical substance. Identifiability 可識別性：可以拆開賣，或者源自合約／法律權利 A broadcast licence satisfies the identifiability criterion because it arises from a contractual or other legal right. Separable 可分割：可以獨立於公司出售、轉讓、授權或出租 A trademark is separable because it can be sold to another party independently of the entity. Internally generated goodwill 內部產生商譽：自己建立嘅聲譽，永遠唔入賬 Internally generated goodwill shall not be recognised as an asset under HKAS 38. Development costs 開發成本：六個條件全部滿足先可以資本化 Expenditure on the development phase is capitalised only when all six criteria in HKAS 38.57 are met. Active market 活躍市場：交易夠頻密、夠量，持續有價格資訊 The revaluation model may only be applied if fair value can be determined by reference to an active market. Amortisation 攤銷：無形資產版本嘅折舊，有限年期先入 P&L The depreciable amount of a finite life intangible asset is allocated on a systematic basis over its useful life. Revaluation surplus 重估盈餘：重估升值入 OCI 後喺權益累積嘅儲備 A revaluation increase is recognised in other comprehensive income and accumulated in equity under the heading of revaluation surplus.

title: M6 Chapter 9: Intangible Assets — Phase 3 Answers
headings: M6 Chapter 9: Intangible Assets — Phase 3 Answers
excerpt: M6 Chapter 9: Intangible Assets — Phase 3 Answers Q1 — Answer: B Model Answer (EN): A ferry operating licence purchased from another company for HK$1,500,000 is…
text: M6 Chapter 9: Intangible Assets — Phase 3 Answers Q1 — Answer: B Model Answer (EN): A ferry operating licence purchased from another company for HK$1,500,000 is a separately acquired intangible asset. It is identifiable (it arises from contractual/legal rights and is separable), the entity controls the benefits, and the agreed purchase price demonstrates both probable future economic benefits and reliable measurement of cost. It is recognised at cost (HKAS 38.21, 38.24, 38.27). A (incorrect): an internally generated customer list is explicitly prohibited from recognition (HKAS 38.63) — the expenditure cannot be distinguished from the cost of developing the business as a whole. C (incorrect): training expenditure fails the control criterion — the entity cannot prevent trained staff from leaving (HKAS 38.13, 38.15–16); it is expensed. D (incorrect): a self built reputation is internally generated goodwill , which shall not be recognised (HKAS 38.48–49); it is not an identifiable resource measurable reliably at cost. 解題思路（繁中）: 呢題考「三大屬性＋禁止清單」。正解 B 係 separately acquired：有價有交易，兩個 recognition tests 自動過。A 係內部產生客戶名單（HKAS 38.63 明令禁止）；C 培訓支出過唔到 control test（員工隨時走）；D 聲譽 = internally generated goodwill，永遠唔入賬。記住 goodwill 只可以喺 business combination「買返嚟」先確認（HKFRS 3）。 Rule Check: HKAS 38.8, 38.12–13, 38.21, 38.24, 38.27, 38.48–49, 38.63 Common Trap（繁中）: 以為「花咗錢、有價值」就係資產——training 同 reputation 都創造價值，但分別敗喺 control 同 identifiability/reliable measurement。考試見到 internally generated brands / customer lists / mastheads / publishing titles 即刻排除。 Q2 — Answer: C Model Answer (EN): The design, construction and testing of a pre production prototype is a development phase activity — it is the application of research findings to a plan or design for a new or substantially improved product before commercial production or use (HKAS 38.8). A (incorrect): the search for and evaluation of alternatives for materials/compounds is a research activity (HKAS 38.8). B (incorrect): activities aimed at obtaining new scientific knowledge fall within the definition of research. D (incorrect): the formulation, evaluation and final selection of possible applications of research findings is a research activity (HKAS 38.8). 解題思路（繁中）: Research = 搵新知識、搵 alternatives、評估同揀選研究方向；Development = 將研究成果「落地」——做 prototype、design tools/jigs/moulds、pilot plant（非商業規模）。呢題四個選項全部係 HKAS 38.8 嘅標準例子，考你有冇背熟邊啲歸 research、邊啲歸 development。 Rule Check: HKAS 38.8 (definitions of research and development) Common Trap（繁中）: 「evaluation and final selection of applications of research findings」聽落好後期、似 development，其實 LP 明確歸入 research。仲有 pilot plant 要「not of an economically feasible scale for commercial production」先係 development activity。 Q3 — Answer: C (HK$1,937,500) Model Answer (EN): Workings: Cost of separately acquired licence = purchase price 1,800,000 + legal fees (directly attributable) 120,000 + non refundable purchase tax 80,000 = HK$2,000,000 (HKAS 38.27–28). Useful life = shorter of legal term (10 years) and expected benefit period (8 years) = 8 years (HKAS 38.94). Residual value = nil (no third party commitment; no active market) (HKAS 38.100). Amortisation for 3 months (1 Oct – 31 Dec 20X5), straight line (pattern not determinable): 2,000,000 / 8 × 3/12 = HK$62,500 (HKAS 38.97). Carrying amount = 2,000,000 − 62,500 = HK$1,937,500 (cost model, HKAS 38.74). Distractor analysis: A (HK$1,743,750): wrongly excludes legal fees and the non refundable tax from cost (1,800,000 − 1,800,000/8 × 3/12 = 1,800,000 − 56,250). B (HK$1,750,000): wrongly charges a full year of amortisation (2,000,000 − 250,000) despite the 1 October acquisition. D (HK$1,950,000): wrongly uses the 10 year legal life (2,000,000 − 2,000,000/10 × 3/12 = 2,000,000 − 50,000). 解題思路（繁中）: 三步曲：①砌 cost——purchase price＋directly attributable costs（legal fees 入；non refundable tax 入）；②揀 useful life——合約/法律年期同預期受益期 取短 （8 年）；③攤銷要 pro rate （年中買入，月攤），residual value 預設零。三個 distractor 分別對應三個典型錯誤：漏咗直接歸屬成本、唔 pro rate、用錯 legal life。 Rule Check: HKAS 38.27–28, 38.74, 38.94, 38.97, 38.100 Common Trap（繁中）: 考試最鍾意「legal life 長過經濟效益期」嘅伏位——記住 contractual/legal rights 產生嘅無形資產，useful life 係 shorter of 兩者。另外 intangible asset 嘅 residual value 預設係零 ，唔好自己加返個殘值。 Q4 — Answer: A Model Answer (EN): Development phase expenditure is capitalised because all six HKAS 38.57 criteria were demonstrated: Dr HK$ Cr HK$ : : Intangible asset — capitalised development costs 480,000     Cash 480,000 Amortisation commences when the asset is available for use (1 July 20X5), straight line over 4 years, nil residual value: 480,000 / 4 × 6/12 = HK$60,000 (HKAS 38.97): Dr HK$ Cr HK$ : : Amortisation expense (P&L) 60,000     Accumulated amortisation 60,000 B (incorrect): charges a full year of amortisation (120,000) even though the software was available for use for only 6 months. C (incorrect): expenses the development costs — that is the research phase treatment (HKAS 38.54); once all HKAS 38.57 criteria are met, capitalisation is required. D (incorrect): no amortisation — that treatment applies only to indefinite life intangibles (HKAS 38.107); a 4 year useful life is finite. 解題思路（繁中）: 兩張分錄：①資本化（Dr Intangible / Cr Cash）——六個條件齊就必須 capitalise，唔係選擇；②攤銷由 available for use 日期起計，年中可用就 pro rate（6/12 = 60,000）。B 係全年攤銷錯誤；C 將 development 當 research 費用化；D 錯用 indefinite life 處理。分錄題記住：amortisation expense 入 P&L，credit 落 Accumulated amortisation 。 Rule Check: HKAS 38.57, 38.97, 38.99, 38.100, 38.107 Common Trap（繁中）: 攤銷起點係「available for use」（可以按管理層意圖運作）嗰日，唔係年頭、唔係真正開始賣嗰日。年中可用 → 按月 pro rate，係 QP 最常見嘅計分位。 Q5 — Answer: A (HK$760,000) Model Answer (EN): Workings: Capitalised: only the prototype design/construction/testing costs incurred from the date all six HKAS 38.57 criteria were first met (1 May 20X6) = HK$800,000 . Expensed as incurred: Market research into demand → research phase (obtaining new knowledge/evaluating applications) → expense (HKAS 38.54); Staff training → fails control/identifiability → expense (HKAS 38.13; training costs are not eligible, HKAS 38.29); Advertising/launch campaign → promotional expenditure → expense. Amortisation from date available for use (1 Oct 20X6) to year end: 800,000 / 5 × 3/12 = HK$40,000 (HKAS 38.97). Carrying amount = 800,000 − 40,000 = HK$760,000 . Distractor analysis: B (HK$800,000): capitalised correctly but no amortisation charged (wrongly treated as indefinite life). C (HK$855,000): wrongly capitalises training costs as well (900,000 − 900,000/5 × 3/12 = 900,000 − 45,000). D (HK$1,235,000): wrongly capitalises the research phase market research too ((800,000 + 500,000) − 1,300,000/5 × 3/12 = 1,300,000 − 65,000). 解題思路（繁中）: 呢類 multi item 題目要逐項過篩：market research（研究需求）係 research phase → expense；prototype 喺六條件達成後先 capitalise；training 同 advertising 無論點都係 expense（training 過唔到 control，advertising 係推廣支出）。資本化之後仲要記得由 available for use 日起 pro rate 攤銷 3 個月 。四個選項分別對應：正確、唔攤銷、連 training 都 capitalise、連 research 都 capitalise。 Rule Check: HKAS 38.54, 38.57, 38.13, 38.29, 38.97 Common Trap（繁中）: ①研究階段同開發階段分唔清——「market research into demand」係典型 research；②以為 training/advertising 係「令產品用得返」嘅直接成本——佢哋唔係 directly attributable 嘅 preparation costs，要費用化；③ capitalise 咗就唔記得攤銷。Jun 2025 panel report 特別點名考生對 internally generated brands 同 training costs 處理薄弱，呢啲正係出題熱點。

text: M6 Chapter 9: Intangible Assets — Phase 3 Quiz Rules: Closed book · 15 minutes · 5 questions · Submit as 1. … 2. … 3. … 4. … 5. … — 超時如實申報 Question 1 In accordance with HKAS 38 Intangible Assets , which of the following items of Harbour Ferry Limited, a Hong Kong ferry operator, may be recognised as an intangible asset in Harbour Ferry Limited's own statement of financial position? A. An internally generated list of regular commuters that the marketing team has compiled over ten years B. A ferry operating licence purchased from another ferry company for HK$1,500,000 C. Expenditure on staff training programmes that significantly improved customer service quality D. The reputation for reliability that Harbour Ferry Limited has built up with passengers over two decades Question 2 According to HKAS 38, which of the following activities undertaken by Beacon Biotech Limited in an internal project falls within the development phase ? A. The search for and evaluation of alternative compounds that could be used in a new drug coating B. Activities aimed at obtaining new scientific knowledge about cell behaviour C. The design, construction and testing of a pre production prototype of the new drug delivery device D. The formulation and final selection of possible applications of the research findings Question 3 On 1 October 20X5, Coral Ferry Limited acquired a broadcast licence for an agreed price of HK$1,800,000. It also paid legal fees of HK$120,000 to draw up the acquisition contract and a non refundable purchase tax of HK$80,000. The licence has a legal term of 10 years, but management expects the licence to generate economic benefits for only 8 years. There is no active market for the licence and no third party has committed to purchase it. Coral Ferry Limited adopts the cost model, amortises on a straight line basis (monthly) and has a 31 December year end. In accordance with HKAS 38, what is the carrying amount of the licence in Coral Ferry Limited's statement of financial position as at 31 December 20X5? A. HK$1,743,750 B. HK$1,750,000 C. HK$1,937,500 D. HK$1,950,000 Question 4 During the year ended 31 December 20X5, Kowloon Data Limited incurred HK$480,000 (paid in cash) on the development phase of a new data analytics software, after demonstrating that all six recognition criteria in HKAS 38.57 were met. The software became available for use on 1 July 20X5. It has an estimated useful life of 4 years, a nil residual value, and is amortised on a straight line basis (monthly). Which set of journal entries correctly records these transactions for the year ended 31 December 20X5? A. Dr HK$ Cr HK$ : : Intangible asset — capitalised development costs 480,000     Cash 480,000 Amortisation expense 60,000     Accumulated amortisation 60,000 B. Dr HK$ Cr HK$ : : Intangible asset — capitalised development costs 480,000     Cash 480,000 Amortisation expense 120,000     Accumulated amortisation 120,000 C. Dr HK$ Cr HK$ : : Research and development expense 480,000     Cash 480,000 D. Dr HK$ Cr HK$ : : Intangible asset — capitalised development costs 480,000     Cash 480,000 (No amortisation entry, because the software is treated as having an indefinite useful life.) Question 5 Phoenix MedTech Limited is developing a surgical navigation application. For the year ended 31 December 20X6, it incurred the following expenditure: Item HK$ : Market research into likely demand for the application 500,000 Design, construction and testing of pre production prototypes, incurred from 1 May 20X6, the date on which all six HKAS 38.57 criteria were first demonstrated 800,000 Staff training on how to use the new application 100,000 Advertising campaign for the product launch 150,000 The application became available for use on 1 October 20X6. excerpt: M6 Chapter 10: Financial Assets, Financial Liabilities and Equity Instruments — Phase 1 速查表 + Phase 2 閃卡 Phase 1 速查表 Learning Objectives 1. Define a financial a…
text: M6 Chapter 10: Financial Assets, Financial Liabilities and Equity Instruments — Phase 1 速查表 + Phase 2 閃卡 Phase 1 速查表 Learning Objectives 1. Define a financial asset, a financial liability and an equity instrument in accordance with HKAS 32. 2. Classify financial instruments as financial liabilities or equity instruments from the issuer's perspective. 3. Classify and account for financial assets under the three HKFRS 9 measurement categories (amortised cost, FVOCI, FVTPL) using the business model and SPPI tests. 4. Apply the effective interest method to compute amortised cost and interest revenue/expense, and prepare the related journal entries. 5. Apply the three stage expected credit loss (ECL) model and explain derecognition and offsetting requirements. 必背考點 A. Recognition 確認 考點 Rule Reference 定義 A financial instrument is any contract that gives rise to a financial asset of one entity and a financial liability or equity instrument of another entity (雙方要有「對稱」先算 financial instrument). HKAS 32.11 Financial asset Cash; an equity instrument of another entity; a contractual right to receive cash/another financial asset or to exchange under potentially favourable conditions; certain contracts settled in the entity's own equity instruments (variable number to receive). HKAS 32.11 Financial liability Contractual obligation to deliver cash/another financial asset, or to exchange under potentially unfavourable conditions; or a non derivative settled in a variable number of the entity's own equity instruments. HKAS 32.11 Equity instrument Any contract evidencing a residual interest in assets after deducting all liabilities; must have no contractual obligation to deliver cash , and if settled in own shares, the number must be fixed (variable number → financial liability). HKAS 32.11 Initial recognition Recognise a financial asset/liability when the entity becomes party to the contractual provisions of the instrument（通常即簽約日，不是談判或達成口頭協議時）. HKFRS 9.3.1.1 B. Measurement 計量 Initial measurement (financial assets AND financial liabilities): Initially measured at fair value . HKFRS 9.5.1.1 Amortised cost / FVOCI instruments: initial measurement includes directly attributable transaction costs. FVTPL instruments: transaction costs are expensed to profit or loss immediately （伏位：考生成日加埋交易成本入 FVTPL 資產）. Transaction costs = incremental costs directly attributable to acquisition/issue/disposal（內部固定人工如 funding manager salary 唔算 — 非 incremental）. Subsequent measurement of financial assets — 取決於兩個測試 (HKFRS 9.4.1.1)： 1. Business model test : hold to collect / hold to collect and sell / not held to collect (HKFRS 9.B4.1.1–B4.1.6) 2. SPPI test : contractual cash flows are solely payments of principal and interest on principal outstanding（basic lending arrangement; interest 主要補償 time value of money + credit risk）(HKFRS 9.B4.1.7A) Category Conditions Measurement mechanics Reference Amortised cost Business model = hold to collect AND cash flows pass SPPI Effective interest method; interest revenue = opening gross carrying amount × EIR; gains/losses to P&L on derecognition / impairment HKFRS 9.4.1.2; 9.5.7.2 FVOCI (debt) Business model = hold to collect AND sell AND passes SPPI Carrying amount = fair value ; interest revenue still on amortised cost (EIR) basis via P&L; FV movements to OCI; impairment gains/losses to P&L HKFRS 9.4.1.2A; 9.5.7.10 FVTPL Residual / fall back category: fails SPPI, or business model = hold to sell/trade Fair value; all gains/losses (including interest effect) to P&L; transaction costs expensed day 1 HKFRS 9.4.1.4; 9.5.7.1 FVOCI election (equity) Irrevocable election at initial recognition for equity instruments not held for trading All FV changes to OCI; dividends still to P&L ; no recycling, no ECL impairment HKFRS 9.5.7.5; 9.5.7.1A; 9.B5.7.3 Effective interest method (HKFRS 9.App A): EIR = rate that exactly discounts estimated future cash flows over the expected life back to the gross carrying amount , adjusted for transaction costs, premiums and discounts. Contractual (coupon) rate → 決定實收/實付現金流； EIR → 決定 P&L 入賬嘅 interest revenue/expense。兩者通常唔同。 Amortised cost 公式：Closing = Opening + (Opening × EIR) − Cash received/paid。 Subsequent measurement of financial liabilities: Default = amortised cost (effective interest method) HKFRS 9.4.2.1 Exceptions measured at FVTPL : liabilities designated at FVTPL on initial recognition; liabilities arising when a transfer of a financial asset does not qualify for derecognition; derivatives; financial guarantee contracts; below market loan commitments; contingent consideration under HKFRS 3（後四項超出 module 範圍）. FVTPL designated liabilities: FV change attributable to own credit risk → OCI ；其餘 → P&L HKFRS 9.5.7.7 C. Impairment — Expected Credit Loss Model 預期信貸虧損 ECL provision (loss allowance) required for all financial assets at amortised cost and debt instruments at FVOCI ； equity instruments designated at FVOCI are exempt . HKFRS 9.5.5.1 / 9.5.5.2 Credit loss = difference between contractual cash flows due and cash flows expected, discounted at the original EIR . (HKFRS 9.App A) Impairment loss/gain = amount needed to adjust the loss allowance to the required amount at the reporting date → recognised in profit or loss ；SOFP 對應：amortised cost → loss allowance；FVOCI debt → equity. HKFRS 9.5.5.8 Rebuttable presumption : more than 30 days past due → significant increase in credit risk. HKFRS 9.B5.5.17 Stage Trigger Loss allowance Interest revenue basis Stage 1 No significant increase in credit risk（初始通常入呢度） 12 month ECL Gross carrying amount × EIR (HKFRS 9.5.5.3) Stage 2 Significant increase in credit risk （如 credit rating downgrade、借款人盈利轉差、 30 days past due） Lifetime ECL Gross carrying amount × EIR (HKFRS 9.5.5.5) Stage 3 Credit impaired （如違約、破產 — events with detrimental impact on cash flows） Lifetime ECL Net carrying amount × EIR (HKFRS 9.5.5.11; 9.5.4.1(b)) 考試伏位：Stage 1 即使有 lifetime ECL 估計，都只確認 12 month ECL ；Stage 2 → Stage 3 唯一改變係 interest revenue 由 gross 轉 net basis 。 D. Derecognition & Presentation 終止確認與列報 Derecognition of financial assets (HKFRS 9.3.2.3): Derecognise when (i) contractual rights to cash flows expire , or (ii) the asset is transferred AND substantially all risks and rewards of ownership are transferred. HKFRS 9.3.2.6(a) On derecognition: difference between carrying amount and consideration received → profit or loss . HKFRS 9.3.2.12 Transfer NOT qualifying （e.g. sale with agreement to repurchase at fixed price / with recourse）: keep the asset, recognise a separate financial liability for consideration received, no offsetting ; continue recognising income on asset and expense on liability. HKFRS 9.3.2.6(b); 9.3.2.15 Derecognition of financial liabilities : when obligation is discharged, expires or is cancelled ；difference between carrying amount and consideration paid → P&L. HKFRS 9.3.3.1; 9.3.3.3 Offsetting (Presentation) : HKAS 1 generally prohibits offsetting assets and liabilities. HKAS 1.32 HKAS 32 requires offsetting (net presentation) only when BOTH : (1) a currently legally enforceable right to set off（contingent on future default = 唔算 currently enforceable）; AND (2) intention to settle net , or to realise the asset and settle the liability simultaneously . HKAS 32.42; 32.43 註：本章 LP 冇獨立 disclosure 章節；presentation/offsetting 要求（HKAS 32）即本章嘅列報考點。 E. Key Journal Entries 必背分錄 1. Purchase of bond at amortised cost (with transaction costs) 2. Year end interest — amortised cost bond bought at a PREMIUM (coupon EIR interest) (If bought at a discount: Dr Cash (coupon), Dr Investment in bonds (EIR interest − coupon), Cr Interest revenue (opening × EIR).) 3. Purchase of equity shares at FVTPL Year end FV gain: Dr Investment in shares / Cr Fair value gain (P&L) 4. FVOCI debt — fair value adjustment (after EIR entries) 5. Raising an ECL loss allowance / stage migration 6. Factoring receivables WITHOUT recourse (qualifies for derecognition) 7. Bank loan drawdown (net of origination fee) and annual repayment 易混淆概念對比 表一：Amortised cost vs FVOCI (debt) vs FVTPL — financial assets 比較點 Amortised cost FVOCI (debt) FVTPL Business model Hold to collect Hold to collect and sell Hold to sell / trading（或 fail SPPI 嘅任何 model） SPPI test Pass Pass Fail → 必定 FVTPL （不论 business model） Transaction costs on initial recognition 加入 carrying amount 加入 carrying amount 即時 expense 入 P&L Carrying amount Amortised cost (EIR roll forward) Fair value Fair value Interest revenue EIR × gross carrying amount → P&L EIR × amortised cost basis → P&L（與 FV 無關） 冇分開計；FV 變動已包含 FV movements 唔認（除 derecognition/impairment） OCI P&L ECL impairment Yes — loss allowance Yes（debt；impairment 入 P&L） No （FV 已反映） 點樣分辨（繁中）： 問自己兩條問題——(1) 現金流係咪 SPPI？唔係就直接 FVTPL，唔使再諗 business model。(2) 係 SPPI 嘅話，睇 entity 係「收息持有」(amortised cost) 定「收息＋會賣」(FVOCI)。考試伏位：FVOCI debt 嘅 interest revenue 仍然用 amortised cost 計 ，唔好用 fair value opening balance 乘 EIR；FVTPL 嘅交易成本 唔可以資本化 。 表二：ECL 三階段 vs Equity instrument FVOCI election 比較點 Stage 1 Stage 2 Stage 3 Equity designated at FVOCI Trigger 初始確認 / 冇顯著惡化 Significant increase in credit risk（ 30 days past due 有 rebuttable presumption） Credit impaired（違約、破產） Irrevocable election，non trading equity Loss allowance 12 month ECL Lifetime ECL Lifetime ECL 豁免 — 唔做 ECL Interest revenue basis Gross carrying amount Gross carrying amount Net carrying amount 唔適用（股息照入 P&L） 對 P&L 影響 只認未來 12 個月預期損失 補足至 lifetime，差額入 P&L 再調整至最新 lifetime 估計 FV 變動全入 OCI， 永不 recycle 點樣分辨（繁中）： 記口訣「 12 Gross / Life Gross / Life Net 」。Stage 2 同 Stage 3 嘅 allowance 都係 lifetime ECL，分別只在 interest revenue 計法 （gross vs net）——呢個係 examiner 最鍾意嘅伏位。另外唔好將「 30 days past due」直接當 Stage 3：佢只係 significant increase in credit risk 嘅 rebuttable presumption （Stage 2），除非有證據話已 credit impaired。 Phase 2 閃卡 Card 1 Front: Define a financial instrument under HKAS 32 and state the three elements it can give rise to. Back: Any contract that gives rise to a financial asset of one entity AND a financial liability or equity instrument of another entity (HKAS 32.11). Requires "symmetry" between the two parties; without it, not a financial instrument. Primary instruments (receivables, payables, bonds, shares) vs derivative instruments (derive value from another variable). 💬 白話解：一張合約要「一邊係資產、另一邊係負債或權益」先叫金融工具。只有一邊有嘢（例如单方面承諾）就唔係。 Card 2 Front: From the issuer's perspective, how do you decide whether an instrument settled in the entity's own shares is equity or a financial liability? Back: Fixed number of own shares for fixed consideration → equity instrument (holder bears residual price risk like ordinary shareholders). Variable number of own shares (e.g. to always deliver HK$100 worth of shares) → financial liability (holder faces no residual risk). Also check: any contractual obligation to deliver cash / exchange on potentially unfavourable terms → financial liability (HKAS 32.11). 💬 白話解：關鍵係「股數固定定浮動」。固定股數 = 持有人自己承受股價風險 = equity；浮動股數保證持有人實收金額 = 其實係還錢 = liability。 Card 3 Front: When is a financial asset or financial liability first recognised, and at what amount? Back: Recognised when the entity becomes party to the contractual provisions of the instrument — usually contract execution date, not during negotiations (HKFRS 9.3.1.1). Initial measurement at fair value (HKFRS 9.5.1.1). Add directly attributable transaction costs — except FVTPL instruments, where transaction costs are expensed immediately. 💬 白話解：簽咗約先確認，傾緊偈未算數。初始按公平值計；交易成本只有非 FVTPL 先可以加入去，FVTPL 要即時打落 P&L。 Card 4 Front: State the two tests that determine the subsequent measurement category of a financial asset, and the three resulting categories. Back: Test 1 — Business model : hold to collect / hold to collect and sell / not held to collect (HKFRS 9.B4.1.1–B4.1.6). Test 2 — Contractual cash flow characteristics : SPPI (solely payments of principal and interest) (HKFRS 9.B4.1.7A). Hold to collect + SPPI → amortised cost (HKFRS 9.4.1.2); hold to collect and sell + SPPI → FVOCI (HKFRS 9.4.1.2A); everything else → FVTPL (fall back, HKFRS 9.4.1.4). 💬 白話解：先過 SPPI 關（唔過 = 直接 FVTPL），再問你係咪「坐住收息」。 Equity shares 嘅股息唔係 SPPI，所以預設一定係 FVTPL。 Card 5 Front: Explain the difference between the contractual (coupon) interest rate and the effective interest rate (EIR), and how each is used. Back: Coupon rate → determines the cash flows received/paid. EIR → rate that exactly discounts estimated future cash flows over the expected life to the gross carrying amount ; determines interest revenue/expense in P&L (HKFRS 9.App A). EIR differs from coupon when the instrument is acquired/issued at a premium/discount or with transaction costs — these are amortised over the life via the EIR. Amortised cost roll forward: Closing = Opening + (Opening × EIR) − Cash flow. 💬 白話解：票面息率管「收幾多現金」，EIR 管「P&L 認幾多息」。買債券有折讓/溢價/手續費，兩個率就會唔同，差額靠 EIR 喺年期內慢慢攤。 Card 6 Front: What is the FVOCI election for equity instruments, and what are its consequences? Back: Irrevocable election at initial recognition for investments in equity instruments not held for trading (HKFRS 9.5.7.5). Initial measurement = fair value plus transaction costs; all subsequent FV changes → OCI (HKFRS 9.5.7.1A). Dividends received still recognised in profit or loss (HKFRS 9.B5.7.3). Exempt from ECL impairment ; no recycling of gains/losses. 💬 白話解：想避開 P&L 波動可以揀 FVOCI，但一揀唔准反口，而且只限唔係攞嚟買賣嘅股票。記住：股息照入 P&L，減值唔使做。 Card 7 Front: Summarise the three stages of the HKFRS 9 expected credit loss model (trigger, loss allowance, interest revenue basis). Back: Stage 1 : no significant increase in credit risk → 12 month ECL ; interest on gross carrying amount (HKFRS 9.5.5.3). Stage 2 : significant increase in credit risk (e.g. rating downgrade, deteriorating results, 30 days past due — rebuttable presumption, HKFRS 9.B5.5.17) → lifetime ECL ; interest on gross carrying amount (HKFRS 9.5.5.5). Stage 3 : credit impaired (default, bankruptcy) → lifetime ECL ; interest on net carrying amount (HKFRS 9.5.5.11; 9.5.4.1(b)). Movement in allowance → impairment loss/gain in P&L (HKFRS 9.5.5.8). 💬 白話解：口訣「12 Gross / Life Gross / Life Net」。Stage 轉換時 P&L 只認 allowance 嘅 變動額 ，唔係成個 lifetime ECL。 Card 8 Front: When may a transferred financial asset be derecognised, and what happens if the transfer does not qualify? When must financial assets and liabilities be offset? Back: Derecognise when cash flow rights expire , or the transfer passes the risks and rewards test (substantially all transferred, e.g. factoring without recourse ) — difference between carrying amount and consideration → P&L (HKFRS 9.3.2.3; 9.3.2.6(a); 9.3.2.12). Not qualified (e.g. sale with fixed price repurchase / with recourse): keep the asset , recognise a separate financial liability for consideration received, no offsetting (HKFRS 9.3.2.6(b); 9.3.2.15). Offsetting only when both : (1) currently legally enforceable right of set off; (2) intention to settle net or simultaneously (HKAS 32.42). HKAS 1.32 otherwise prohibits offsetting. 💬 白話解：賣斷（冇追索權）先可以 derecognise；有追索權 = 其實借錢，資產留低、另認負債。Offsetting 要「而家」就有法律權利＋真係打算淨額交收，得其一唔得。 本章急救詞彙 EN Term 繁中白話 English Model Sentence Financial instrument 令一邊有金融資產、另一邊有金融負債或權益嘅合約 A financial instrument is any contract that gives rise to a financial asset of one entity and a financial liability or equity instrument of another entity. SPPI (solely payments of principal and interest) 現金流純粹係本金加利息，即基本借貸安排 The bonds pass the SPPI test because their contractual cash flows are solely payments of principal and interest on the principal amount outstanding. Business model Entity 管理金融資產嘅方式：收息持有、收息兼賣、定純粹買賣 Because the entity holds the bonds to collect contractual cash flows, the business model test supports amortised cost measurement. Effective interest rate (EIR) 將未來現金流折返到賬面值嘅實際利率，用嚟計 P&L 利息 The effective interest rate exactly discounts the estimated future cash flows to the gross carrying amount of the financial asset. Amortised cost 用 EIR 滾存嘅成本：期初＋EIR利息−現金流 The closing amortised cost equals the opening balance plus interest at the effective interest rate less the coupon received. Expected credit loss (ECL) 按違約概率加權嘅預期現金短欠，按原 EIR 折現 The entity recognised a loss allowance equal to 12 month expected credit losses at initial recognition. Credit impaired 已發生對現金流有不利影響嘅事件（如違約、破產），即 Stage 3 When the borrower entered bankruptcy, the loan became credit impaired and was transferred to Stage 3. Derecognition 將已確認嘅資產/負債從財務狀況表移除 The receivables were derecognised because substantially all risks and rewards of ownership were transferred to the factor.
