text: M6 Chapter 13: Accounting Policies, Changes in Accounting Estimates and Errors — Phase 1 速查表 + Phase 2 閃卡 Phase 1 速查表 Learning Objectives 1. Distinguish between accounting policies, accounting estimates and prior period errors in accordance with HKAS 8. 2. Apply the criteria in HKAS 8 for selecting and changing accounting policies, including mandatory and voluntary changes. 3. Account for a change in accounting policy retrospectively, a change in accounting estimate prospectively, and a material prior period error by retrospective restatement. 4. Compute the effect of accounting changes and error corrections on profit or loss, carrying amounts, tax and retained earnings. 5. Prepare the required note disclosures for changes in accounting policies, changes in accounting estimates and corrections of prior period errors. 必背考點 A. Recognition / Classification — 點樣分三類更改 Definitions (HKAS 8 para. 5) Accounting policies : the specific principles, bases, conventions, rules and practices applied by an entity in preparing and presenting financial statements. Example: choosing FIFO or weighted average cost formula under HKAS 2; cost model vs revaluation model under HKAS 16. Accounting estimates : monetary amounts in financial statements that are subject to measurement uncertainty (HKAS 8 para. 32A). Examples: loss allowance for expected credit losses; net realisable value of inventory; warranty provision; fair value of an asset or liability; depreciation expense. Prior period errors : omissions from, and misstatements in, the entity's financial statements for one or more prior periods arising from a failure to use, or misuse of, reliable information that (a) was available when those financial statements were authorised for issue, and (b) could reasonably be expected to have been obtained and taken into account. Examples: mathematical mistakes, mistakes in applying accounting policies, oversights or misinterpretations of facts, fraud. When may an accounting policy be changed? (HKAS 8 para. 14) — Only if the change: is required by a HKFRS (mandatory); or results in the financial statements providing reliable and more relevant information (voluntary). NOT changes in accounting policy (HKAS 8 para. 16): applying a policy for transactions/events/conditions that differ in substance from those previously occurring; and applying a new policy for transactions/events/conditions that did not occur previously or were immaterial (e.g. previously immaterial leases becoming material → apply HKFRS 16 going forward). Special case (HKAS 8 para. 17): first time adoption of the revaluation model under HKAS 16 / HKAS 38 is a change in accounting policy, BUT it is dealt with as a revaluation under HKAS 16 / HKAS 38 — HKAS 8 paras. 19–31 do not apply. Estimate vs policy boundary rules: A change in the measurement basis applied is a change in accounting policy, NOT a change in estimate (HKAS 8 para. 35; e.g. FIFO → weighted average). If it is difficult to distinguish a policy change from an estimate change → treat as a change in accounting estimate (HKAS 8 para. 35). Revising an estimate because of new information / more experience is NOT a correction of an error (HKAS 8 paras. 32–34): an estimate uses information available at the time ; an error is failure to use / misuse of information that was available . Materiality (HKAS 8 paras. 5, 41; HKAS 1 definition): HKFRS accounting policies need not be applied when the effect is immaterial . Financial statements do not comply with HKFRSs if they contain material errors . Material prior period errors must be corrected retrospectively in the first set of financial statements authorised for issue after discovery . B. Measurement / Accounting Treatment — Retrospective vs Prospective Change in accounting policy (HKAS 8 paras. 19–24): Mandatory change with transitional provisions in the HKFRS → follow those transitional provisions (retrospective or prospective as specified) (HKAS 8 para. 19(a)). Mandatory change without transitional provisions → apply retrospectively (HKAS 8 para. 19(b)). Voluntary change → apply retrospectively (HKAS 8 para. 19(b)). Retrospective application (HKAS 8 paras. 5, 22): apply the new policy as if it had always been applied ; adjust (a) the opening balance of each affected component of equity (e.g. retained earnings) for the earliest prior period presented , and (b) the other comparative amounts disclosed for each prior period presented. Limitation: retrospective application only to the extent practicable (HKAS 8 paras. 23–24). Change in accounting estimate (HKAS 8 paras. 36–38): Recognise prospectively — apply from the date of the change; never adjust prior periods. Effect goes to profit or loss in: (a) the period of change only , if it affects only that period (e.g. annual warranty / ECL allowance); or (b) the period of change and future periods , if it affects both (e.g. revised useful life → depreciation for current + remaining years). To the extent the change affects assets/liabilities/equity, adjust the carrying amount of the related item in the period of change (HKAS 8 para. 37). Correction of prior period error (HKAS 8 paras. 42–46): Correct by retrospective restatement in the first set of financial statements issued after discovery: restate the comparative amounts for the prior period(s) presented in which the error occurred; or if the error occurred before the earliest prior period presented → restate the opening balances of assets, liabilities and equity for the earliest prior period presented. Purpose: current period financial statements are presented as if the error never occurred . Remember the tax effect : restate income tax expense/payable at the applicable rate (LP examples use HK profits tax rate 16.5%). Key journal entries (all from LP worked examples, HK$) 1. Warranty claims paid during the year (Dr/Cr balance: 350,000 = 350,000): Account Dr Cr Warranty provision 350,000 Cash 350,000 2. Revised warranty estimate recognised prospectively (540,000 = 540,000): Account Dr Cr Warranty expense 540,000 Warranty provision 540,000 3. Depreciation after revision of useful life & residual value, per year (310,000 = 310,000): Account Dr Cr Depreciation – machinery 310,000 Accumulated depreciation – machinery 310,000 4. Actual credit losses written off against the allowance (500,000 = 500,000): Account Dr Cr Allowance for expected credit losses 500,000 Receivables 500,000 5. Top up of allowance to revised estimate of HK$700,000 (800,000 = 800,000): Account Dr Cr Expected credit losses 800,000 Allowance for expected credit losses 800,000 (Working: 700,000 required closing balance − 400,000 opening balance + 500,000 written off = 800,000 charge to profit or loss.) 6. Prior period adjustment — opening inventory overstated by HK$9,000,000 (sold goods wrongly included in closing inventory); tax rate 16.5%. Net effect on opening retained earnings = 9,000,000 × (1 − 16.5%) = 7,515,000 (Dr total = Cr total = 9,000,000): Account Dr Cr Retained earnings (opening balance) 7,515,000 Income tax payable 1,485,000 Inventories 9,000,000 (Dr 7,515,000 + Dr 1,485,000 = Cr 9,000,000 — balanced.) C. Disclosure Requirements Change in accounting policy — initial application of a HKFRS (HKAS 8 para. 28): the title of the HKFRS; that the change is made in accordance with its transitional provisions (if any); the nature of the change; a description of the transitional provisions and those that might affect future periods (if applicable); for the current period and each prior period presented , to the extent practicable, the amount of the adjustment for each financial statement line item affected and (if HKAS 33 applies) for basic and diluted EPS ; the amount of the adjustment relating to periods before those presented , to the extent practicable. New HKFRS issued but not yet effective (HKAS 8 para. 30): disclose that fact + known or reasonably estimable information relevant to assessing the possible impact on initial application. Change in accounting policy — voluntary (HKAS 8 para. 29): the nature of the change; the reasons why the new policy provides reliable and more relevant information; the same line item / EPS adjustment amounts as above (current + each prior period presented; periods before those presented), to the extent practicable. Change in accounting estimate (HKAS 8 para. 39): disclose the nature and amount of the change that has an effect in the current period or is expected to have an effect in future periods (if practicable to quantify the future effect). Correction of prior period error (HKAS 8 para. 49): the nature of the prior period error; for each prior period presented , to the extent practicable, the amount of the correction for each financial statement line item affected and (if HKAS 33 applies) for basic and diluted EPS ; the amount of the correction at the beginning of the earliest prior period presented . Timing rule for all three: disclosures are given in the period of change / period the error is corrected; subsequent periods need not repeat the disclosures. 易混淆概念對比 Table 1: Change in Accounting Policy vs Change in Accounting Estimate vs Prior Period Error Change in Accounting Policy Change in Accounting Estimate Prior Period Error Nature Change in principles, bases, conventions, rules, practices (e.g. FIFO → weighted average; cost model → fair value model) Revision of a monetary amount subject to measurement uncertainty (e.g. useful life, warranty %, ECL allowance) Omission/misstatement from failure to use or misuse of reliable info available at the time (maths mistakes, fraud, oversight) Trigger Required by HKFRS, or voluntary to give reliable + more relevant info (HKAS 8.14) New information, change in circumstances, more experience (HKAS 8.32–34) Discovered after prior FS authorised for issue Treatment Retrospective application (subject to transitional provisions / practicability) (HKAS 8.19, 22) Prospective recognition in P&L — current period, or current + future periods (HKAS 8.36–38) Retrospective restatement of comparatives / opening balances (HKAS 8.42) Adjust opening retained earnings of earliest prior period presented? Yes (cumulative pre comparative effect) No — never touch prior periods Yes, if error occurred before earliest prior period presented Disclosure HKAS 8.28 / 8.29 (nature, title of HKFRS or reasons, line item amounts) HKAS 8.39 (nature and amount) HKAS 8.49 (nature, line item corrections, opening balance correction) 點樣分辨 / 考試伏位 睇下係咪改「量度基礎/原則」：改 measurement basis = policy change（HKAS 8.35）。唔好見到「depreciation」就以為係 policy Useful life、residual value、warranty %、ECL 呢啲 estimate revision 一律 prospective；考生最常犯錯係 restate 咗 comparatives（Jun 2025 panel report 指考生識計數但唔識講 prospective treatment） 關鍵：資料當時「已經存在兼可合理取得」但冇用到 → error；如果係新資料先令估計改變 → estimate change，唔係 error Table 2: Mandatory Change vs Voluntary Change in Accounting Policy Mandatory (initial application of a HKFRS) Voluntary Condition Required by a HKFRS (HKAS 8.14(a)) Provides reliable and more relevant information (HKAS 8.14(b)) Treatment Follow the HKFRS's transitional provisions if any; if none → retrospective (HKAS 8.19) Retrospective application (HKAS 8.19(b)), to the extent practicable (HKAS 8.23–24) Example HKFRS 16 first adoption for former operating leases (transitional provisions HKFRS 16.C5–C10) FIFO → weighted average; cost model → fair value model for investment property (HKAS 40) Unique disclosure items Title of HKFRS; description of transitional provisions; those affecting future periods (HKAS 8.28) Reasons why the new policy gives reliable and more relevant information (HKAS 8.29) Common disclosure items Line item + EPS adjustment amounts for current and each prior period presented; amounts for periods before those presented Same 考試伏位 MCQ 成日問「all changes in policy 必須披露乜」：答案係 每個受影響 line item 嘅調整金額 （title of HKFRS / reasons 只係各自類型先要）；記住特殊位：首次用 revaluation model 雖然係 policy change，但跟 HKAS 16/38 做 revaluation 處理，HKAS 8 paras. 19–31 唔適用 自願改 policy 一定要講得出點解「more relevant」；答 disclosure 題時 voluntary 冇 transitional provisions 可以寫，唔好照抄 mandatory 嘅 disclosure list Phase 2 閃卡 Card 1 Front: How does HKAS 8 define "accounting policies", and give two examples of policy choices. Back: Specific principles, bases, conventions, rules and practices applied by an entity in preparing and presenting financial statements (HKAS 8 para. 5). Examples: FIFO vs weighted average cost formula (HKAS 2); cost model vs revaluation model (HKAS 16 / HKAS 38); cost model vs fair value model for investment property (HKAS 40). 💬 白話解：Accounting policy 即係公司揀嘅「會計原則同做法」，例如存貨用 FIFO 定 weighted average。呢個係「揀邊把尺」嘅問題，唔係「把尺度出嚟幾多」嘅問題。 Card 2 Front: Under HKAS 8 para. 14, when is an entity permitted to change an accounting policy? Back: Only if the change: is required by a HKFRS; or results in the financial statements providing reliable and more relevant information about the effects of transactions, other events or conditions on the entity's financial position, financial performance or cash flows. 💬 白話解：改 policy 唔可以話改就改——一係準則逼你改，一係你要證明改咗之後資料更相關可靠。隨意改嚟「調節盈利」係唔得嘅。 Card 3 Front: Which two situations are NOT changes in accounting policy under HKAS 8 para. 16? Back: Applying an accounting policy for transactions/events/conditions that differ in substance from those previously occurring. Applying a new accounting policy for transactions/events/conditions that did not occur previously or were immaterial (e.g. previously immaterial leases becoming material → apply HKFRS 16). 💬 白話解：新嘢第一次出現、或者以前唔重要依家先重要，咁樣用新政策唔算「改政策」，所以唔使 retrospective restate。考試鍾意用呢個做 distractor。 Card 4 Front: Explain the mechanics of retrospective application of a change in accounting policy (HKAS 8 paras. 22–24). Back: Apply the new policy as if it had always been applied. Adjust the opening balance of each affected component of equity (e.g. retained earnings) for the earliest prior period presented. Adjust the other comparative amounts disclosed for each prior period presented. Apply retrospectively only to the extent practicable. 💬 白話解：即係「扮成一向都係咁做」——最早呈報嗰年嘅期初 retained earnings 要調整，之後每年 comparative 都要重報。計唔到（impracticable）先可以豁免。 Card 5 Front: How is a change in accounting estimate recognised, and how does the treatment differ between a one period effect and a multi period effect (HKAS 8 paras. 36–38)? Back: Recognised prospectively from the date of the change; prior periods are never adjusted. Affects current period only (e.g. annual warranty or ECL allowance) → include in profit or loss of the period of change. Affects current and future periods (e.g. revised useful life) → include in profit or loss of the period of change and each future period (via revised depreciation). Related asset/liability/equity carrying amounts are adjusted in the period of change. 💬 白話解：估計改咗就「由今日起計」，唔准返轉頭改舊數。Warranty 呢類一年一估嘅只影響今年；useful life 呢類長命估計就影響今年加埋以後每年嘅折舊。 Card 6 Front: A change in the measurement basis applied — policy change or estimate change? What if the two are difficult to distinguish? Back: A change in the measurement basis applied is a change in an accounting policy, NOT a change in an accounting estimate (HKAS 8 para. 35) — e.g. FIFO → weighted average. If it is difficult to distinguish a change in accounting policy from a change in accounting estimate, the change is treated as a change in an accounting estimate. 💬 白話解：換「把尺」（measurement basis）= 改 policy；把尺度嘅「讀數」改咗 = 改 estimate。真係分唔到？HKAS 8 叫你當佢係 estimate change，即 prospective 處理。 Card 7 Front: Define a prior period error and state how a material one is corrected (HKAS 8 paras. 5, 41–42). Back: Omissions/misstatements in prior period financial statements from failure to use, or misuse of, reliable information that was available and could reasonably have been obtained when those statements were authorised for issue (e.g. mathematical mistakes, mistakes in applying policies, oversights, misinterpretation of facts, fraud). Material prior period errors are corrected retrospectively in the first set of financial statements authorised for issue after discovery: restate comparatives for the period(s) in which the error occurred, or restate opening balances of assets, liabilities and equity for the earliest prior period presented if the error occurred earlier. 💬 白話解：Error 同 estimate change 嘅分界在於「資料當時存唔存在」：當時已經有但你冇用/用錯 = error，要 retrospective restate；新資料先至改估計 = estimate change，prospective。 Card 8 Front: List the disclosure requirements when correcting a material prior period error (HKAS 8 para. 49). Back: The nature of the prior period error. For each prior period presented, to the extent practicable, the amount of the correction for each financial statement line item affected, and for basic and diluted EPS if HKAS 33 applies. The amount of the correction at the beginning of the earliest prior period presented. Disclose in the period the error is corrected; subsequent periods need not repeat. 💬 白話解：Error disclosure 三寶：「咩錯」（nature）、「每個受影響項目改咗幾多」（line item amounts）、「最早嗰年期初改咗幾多」。只係發現嗰年披露一次，之後唔使重複。 本章急救詞彙 EN Term 繁中白話 English Model Sentence Accounting policy 公司編製財報時採用嘅具體原則、基準、慣例、規則同做法 Accounting policies are the specific principles, bases, conventions, rules and practices applied by an entity in preparing and presenting financial statements. Accounting estimate 受計量不確定性影響嘅財報金額，例如保養撥備、壞賬準備 Accounting estimates are monetary amounts in financial statements that are subject to measurement uncertainty. Prior period error 因當時已有資料冇用到或用錯而導致嘅前期遺漏或錯報 A material prior period error must be corrected retrospectively in the first set of financial statements authorised for issue after its discovery. Retrospective application 當新政策「一向都係咁用」咁重報以前嘅數 Retrospective application requires adjusting the opening balance of each affected component of equity for the earliest prior period presented. Retrospective restatement 修正錯誤時重報比較期間金額或最早呈報期間嘅期初結餘 The entity corrected the error by retrospective restatement of the comparative amounts for the period in which the error occurred. Prospective recognition 由改變當日起向前應用，絕不調整以前期間 A change in accounting estimate is recognised prospectively in profit or loss of the period of the change and, if affected, future periods. Transitional provisions 新準則首次應用時嘅過渡安排，決定追溯定前瞻 The change in accounting policy was accounted for in accordance with the transitional provisions of the new HKFRS. Impracticable 就算盡咗合理努力都做不到追溯調整，先可以豁免 Retrospective application is required only to the extent that it is practicable to determine the period specific and cumulative effects.

excerpt: M6 Chapter 13: Accounting Policies, Changes in Accounting Estimates and Errors — Phase 3 Answers Q1 — Answer: B Model Answer (EN): B is correct. A change in the…
text: M6 Chapter 13: Accounting Policies, Changes in Accounting Estimates and Errors — Phase 3 Answers Q1 — Answer: B Model Answer (EN): B is correct. A change in the inventory cost formula (FIFO → weighted average) is a change in the measurement basis applied, which is a change in accounting policy under HKAS 8 (HKAS 8 para. 35; the LP's Illustrative Example 2 treats exactly this change as a voluntary change in accounting policy). A is a change in accounting estimate — the warranty percentage is a monetary amount subject to measurement uncertainty, revised due to new information (HKAS 8 paras. 32–34). C is NOT a change in accounting policy — applying a new policy to transactions that did not occur previously or were immaterial is excluded by HKAS 8 para. 16. D is NOT a change in accounting policy — applying a policy to transactions that differ in substance from those previously occurring is excluded by HKAS 8 para. 16. 解題思路（繁中）: 關鍵係分清楚「把尺」（measurement basis / 原則做法）同「讀數」（估計金額）。B 改成本公式＝換把尺＝policy change。A 改保養百分比只係估計修訂，屬 estimate change。C 同 D 係 HKAS 8 para. 16 明文講明「唔算改 policy」嘅兩種情況：以前冇發生/唔重要嘅交易第一次用新政策，同埋實質唔同嘅交易用唔同政策。考試伏位：見到「HKFRS 16 first time application to newly material leases」唔好即刻當係 policy change。 Rule Check: HKAS 8 paras. 5, 16, 35 Common Trap（繁中）: 考生成日將「新交易類型用現行政策」或者「以前 immaterial 依家 material 嘅交易改用新準則」誤當 change in accounting policy，因而錯誤咁要求 retrospective restatement。 Q2 — Answer: B Model Answer (EN): B is correct. A voluntary change in accounting policy must be applied retrospectively: the new policy is applied as if it had always been applied, adjusting the opening balance of each affected component of equity (e.g. retained earnings) for the earliest prior period presented and the other comparative amounts disclosed for each prior period presented, subject to practicability (HKAS 8 paras. 19(b), 22–24). A is wrong — prospective application applies to changes in accounting estimates, not voluntary policy changes. C is wrong — a change in inventory cost formula is a policy change (change in measurement basis), not an estimate change, and the cumulative effect is adjusted against opening equity, not current profit or loss. D is wrong — transitional provisions are relevant only for mandatory changes required by the initial application of a HKFRS (HKAS 8 para. 19(a)); this change is voluntary and HKAS 2 contains no transitional provisions for a voluntary switch of cost formula. 解題思路（繁中）: 第一步判斷 mandatory 定 voluntary——呢度係自願改，所以冇 transitional provisions 可以跟，直接 retrospective。Retrospective 嘅標準操作：最早呈報比較期間嘅期初 retained earnings 調整累計影響，每個呈報嘅前期 comparative 全部重報，以 practicable 為限。A 同 C 係「estimate change」嘅處理方法，係最強 distractor；D 混淆咗 mandatory change 先會用到嘅 transitional provisions 概念。 Rule Check: HKAS 8 paras. 19, 22, 23–24 Common Trap（繁中）: 以為所有改變都係 prospective。記住口訣：Policy change 同 error correction → retrospective（向後改）；Estimate change → prospective（向前行）。 Q3 — Answer: B Model Answer (EN): B is correct. The revision from 2% to 3% of sales is a change in accounting estimate recognised prospectively in profit or loss of the current period (HKAS 8 paras. 36–38). Warranty expense for 20X4 = 3% × HK$5,000,000 = HK$150,000: Account Dr (HK$) Cr (HK$) Warranty expense 150,000 Warranty provision 150,000 A is the entry for warranty claims paid in cash (Dr Warranty provision / Cr Cash), not the expense accrual. C wrongly charges the estimate change to retained earnings — a change in estimate never adjusts prior periods or opening equity; only retrospective items (policy changes, error corrections) touch opening retained earnings. D uses the superseded 2% estimate (HK$100,000) instead of the revised 3%. 解題思路（繁中）: 呢題考兩層：(1) 保養百分比修訂 = estimate change，prospective，所以用新比率 3% 落今年 P&L；(2) 分錄方向——計提保養費用係 Dr Warranty expense / Cr Warranty provision。A 係「賠咗錢」嘅分錄（用撥備找數），唔係計提；C 係 retrospective item 先會用嘅 retained earnings 路徑；D 用舊比率。Balanced check：Dr 150,000 = Cr 150,000 ✓。 Rule Check: HKAS 8 paras. 34, 36–38 Common Trap（繁中）: 誤將 estimate change 當 error 處理而借記 retained earnings。記住：只有 policy change 同 prior period error correction 先會掂 opening retained earnings；estimate change 永遠行 P&L。 Q4 — Answer: C Model Answer (EN): C is correct — HK$390,000. The revision of useful life and residual value is a change in accounting estimate applied prospectively (HKAS 8 paras. 36–38). Workings: Original annual depreciation = (HK$1,800,000 − HK$120,000) ÷ 8 = HK$210,000 Accumulated depreciation at 31 December 20X3 = 3 years × HK$210,000 = HK$630,000 Carrying amount at 1 January 20X4 = HK$1,800,000 − HK$630,000 = HK$1,170,000 Revised depreciation = (HK$1,170,000 − HK$0) ÷ 3 = HK$390,000 per year for 20X4–20X6 Distractor analysis: A (HK$210,000) ignores the revision entirely; B (HK$350,000) wrongly deducts the superseded residual value of HK$120,000 from the carrying amount; D (HK$600,000) wrongly spreads the original cost over 3 years, ignoring accumulated depreciation already charged. 解題思路（繁中）: Prospective 嘅核心做法：用「修訂日嘅 carrying amount」減「新 residual value」，再除以「新剩餘年期」。最常見錯誤：用返 cost（1,800,000）而唔係 carrying amount（1,170,000）做起點——即係 D；或者繼續扣舊 residual value——即係 B；或者根本冇更新——即係 A。Jun 2025 考官報告特別提到考生識計數但唔識解釋呢個係 prospective treatment，所以答題時要講明「change in accounting estimate, applied prospectively」。 Rule Check: HKAS 8 paras. 34, 36–38 Common Trap（繁中）: 忘記 estimate change 唔 restate 以前年度——20X1–20X3 嘅折舊維持每年 HK$210,000，唔准返轉頭改；修訂只影響 20X4 起嘅折舊。 Q5 — Answer: B Model Answer (EN): B is correct — a decrease of HK$668,000. The counting error is a material prior period error corrected by retrospective restatement (HKAS 8 para. 42): the 20X4 comparatives are restated in the 20X5 financial statements as if the error had never occurred. Workings: Closing inventory overstated by HK$800,000 → cost of goods sold understated and profit overstated by HK$800,000 in 20X4. Tax effect = HK$800,000 × 16.5% = HK$132,000 (income tax expense and income tax payable restated downward). Net of tax reduction in retained earnings as at 31 December 20X4 = HK$800,000 − HK$132,000 = HK$668,000 . Correcting journal entry (balanced: Dr total 800,000 = Cr 800,000): Account Dr (HK$) Cr (HK$) Retained earnings 668,000 Income tax payable 132,000 Inventories 800,000 A ignores the tax effect. C deducts only the tax amount. D is wrong — material prior period errors are never corrected prospectively; retrospective restatement is mandatory (HKAS 8 paras. 41–42). 解題思路（繁中）: Prior period error 修正三步：(1) 判斷方向——closing inventory 高估 → 20X4 COGS 低估 → profit 高估 → retained earnings 要 下調 ；(2) 計稅務影響——LP 所有例子都用 16.5%，稅隨利潤跌而跌，所以淨影響 = 800,000 × 83.5% = 668,000；(3) 記住 retained earnings 永遠用 net of tax 金額調整。A 忘記稅；C 本末倒置；D 用錯 prospective——error correction 係 retrospective restatement，冇得揀。 Rule Check: HKAS 8 paras. 41–42, 46 Common Trap（繁中）: (1) 調整 retained earnings 時忘記扣稅效應；(2) 方向搞錯——inventory 高估代表 profit 高估，要 減 唔係加；(3) 以為 error 可以 prospective 處理——material prior period error 必須 retrospective restatement，呢個係 HKAS 8 嘅硬性規定。

text: M6 Chapter 13: Accounting Policies, Changes in Accounting Estimates and Errors — Phase 3 Quiz Rules: Closed book · 15 minutes · 5 questions · Submit as 1. … 2. … 3. … 4. … 5. … — 超時如實申報 Question 1 Pearl Lighting Limited (Pearl), a Hong Kong lighting retailer, is reviewing its accounting treatments for the year ended 31 December 20X5. In accordance with HKAS 8, which of the following constitutes a change in accounting policy ? A. Pearl revises its warranty provision estimate from 2% to 3% of sales following an increase in products returned under warranty during 20X4. B. Pearl changes its inventory cost formula from the first in, first out (FIFO) method to the weighted average cost method because management believes it provides more relevant information. C. Pearl applies HKFRS 16 Leases for the first time to leasing arrangements that were previously immaterial but have become material in the current year. D. Pearl applies its existing revenue recognition policy to a new line of business whose transactions differ in substance from those previously occurring. Question 2 Golden Harvest Trading Limited (Golden Harvest) voluntarily changes its inventory cost formula during the year ended 31 December 20X6 because the new formula provides reliable and more relevant information. In accordance with HKAS 8, how should Golden Harvest account for this change? A. Prospectively, by applying the new cost formula only to purchases made from the date of the change. B. Retrospectively, by adjusting the opening balance of each affected component of equity for the earliest prior period presented and the other comparative amounts disclosed for each prior period presented, to the extent practicable. C. As a change in accounting estimate, by including the cumulative effect in profit or loss of the current period only. D. In accordance with the transitional provisions of HKAS 2 Inventories, since the change relates to inventory measurement. Question 3 Cascade Home Appliances Limited (Cascade) offers a one year warranty on all products sold. For the year ended 31 December 20X3, Cascade estimated warranty expense at 2% of sales. For the year ended 31 December 20X4, based on an analysis showing an increase in products returned under warranty, Cascade revised the estimate to 3% of sales. Sales for 20X4 were HK$5,000,000. Which journal entry correctly records the warranty expense for the year ended 31 December 20X4 in accordance with HKAS 8? A. Dr Warranty provision HK$150,000; Cr Cash HK$150,000 B. Dr Warranty expense HK$150,000; Cr Warranty provision HK$150,000 C. Dr Retained earnings HK$150,000; Cr Warranty provision HK$150,000 D. Dr Warranty expense HK$100,000; Cr Warranty provision HK$100,000 Question 4 On 1 January 20X1, Harbour Logistics Limited (Harbour) acquired machinery at a cost of HK$1,800,000. At acquisition, the estimated useful life was 8 years and the residual value was HK$120,000. Harbour depreciates machinery on a straight line basis. On 1 January 20X4, due to technological obsolescence, Harbour revised the remaining useful life to 3 years and the residual value to nil. In accordance with HKAS 8, what is the depreciation expense for the year ended 31 December 20X4? A. HK$210,000 B. HK$350,000 C. HK$390,000 D. HK$600,000 Question 5 During the year ended 31 December 20X5, Victoria Textiles Limited (Victoria) discovered that, due to a counting error, goods already sold had been incorrectly included in closing inventory as at 31 December 20X4, overstating inventory by HK$800,000. The error is material. The income tax rate is 16.5%, and the error correction has a corresponding effect on accounting and taxable profits. In accordance with HKAS 8, by what amount should Victoria's retained earnings as at 31 December 20X4 be restated in the financial statements for the year ended 31 December 20X5? A. Decrease of HK$800,000 B. Decrease of HK$668,000 C. Decrease of HK$132,000 D. No restatement is required; the error is corrected prospectively in the 20X5 financial statements.

title: M6 Chapter 14: Events after the Reporting Period — Phase 1 速查表 + Phase 2 閃卡
headings: M6 Chapter 14: Events after the Reporting Period — Phase 1 速查表 + Phase 2 閃卡
B. Measurement（點樣計數 / 分錄）

text: M6 Chapter 14: Events after the Reporting Period — Phase 1 速查表 + Phase 2 閃卡 Phase 1 速查表 Learning Objectives 1. Define "events after the reporting period" and identify the time window to which HKAS 10 applies. 2. Distinguish between adjusting and non adjusting events after the reporting period. 3. Apply the correct accounting treatment (adjust vs do not adjust; going concern basis) to events after the reporting period. 4. Prepare the required disclosures in respect of events after the reporting period, including the date of authorisation for issue and material non adjusting events. 必背考點 A. Recognition（認唔認入賬） Scope of HKAS 10 (HKAS 10.3): Events after the reporting period are those favourable or unfavourable events that occur between the end of the reporting period and the date when the financial statements are authorised for issue . Events outside this window are beyond the scope of HKAS 10. "Authorised for issue" is not defined in HKAS 10 — it depends on the entity's authorisation process. If shareholders have the power to amend the financial statements after issue, that fact must be disclosed. The authorisation date is when the board/management authorises issue — not the date the statements are posted on a website, filed with the Companies Registry, or approved by shareholders at the AGM. Adjusting events (HKAS 10.3(a)): Events that provide evidence of conditions that existed at the end of the reporting period . The entity shall adjust the amounts recognised in its financial statements (HKAS 10.8) — either adjusting an existing balance or recognising an amount not previously recognised. Non adjusting events (HKAS 10.3(b)): Events that are indicative of conditions that arose after the end of the reporting period . The entity shall not adjust the amounts recognised (HKAS 10.10); the accounting consequences are recognised in the reporting period in which they occur. If material , disclosure in the notes is required (HKAS 10.21). Going concern override (HKAS 10.14–15): If management determines after the reporting period that it intends to liquidate the entity or cease trading (or has no realistic alternative), the entity shall not prepare its financial statements on a going concern basis . This applies whether the deterioration stems from an adjusting or a non adjusting event. Examples of adjusting events (HKAS 10.9): Settlement after the reporting period of a court case that confirms the entity had a present obligation at the end of the reporting period. Bankruptcy of a customer after the reporting period — usually confirms the customer was credit impaired at the end of the reporting period. Sale of inventories below cost after the reporting period — may give evidence about their net realisable value at the end of the reporting period (HKAS 10.9(b)(ii)). Determination after the reporting period of the cost of assets purchased / proceeds of assets sold before the end of the reporting period. Discovery of fraud or errors showing the financial statements are incorrect. Examples of non adjusting events (HKAS 10.11, 10.22): A decline in the fair value of investments held at the end of the reporting period (HKAS 10.11). Declaration of dividends payable to shareholders — not recognised as a liability at the end of the reporting period (HKAS 10.12–13), because there is no obligation to pay at period end. Major business combination or disposal of a major subsidiary; announcing a plan to discontinue an operation; major purchases/disposals of assets or classification as held for sale under HKFRS 5; destruction of a major production plant by natural disaster; announcement/commencement of a major restructuring; major new share issue; abnormally large changes in asset prices or foreign exchange rates; changes in tax rates/laws enacted or announced after the reporting period (HKAS 12 effect); significant commitments or contingent liabilities (e.g. issuing a significant guarantee); major litigation arising solely out of events that occurred after the reporting period (HKAS 10.22). B. Measurement（點樣計數 / 分錄） Adjusting events: revise the measurement of items as at the end of the reporting period in light of the new evidence (e.g. write receivables down when a customer goes bankrupt; write inventories down to NRV; recognise a liability confirmed by a court settlement). Non adjusting events: measurement consequences fall into the next reporting period — no retrospective measurement change for the period just ended. Going concern (HKAS 10.15): if the inability to continue as a going concern has a pervasive effect , HKAS 10 requires a fundamental change in the basis of accounting (i.e. prepare a new set of financial statements on a non going concern basis) — not merely adjusting amounts within the original basis. Disclosure per HKAS 1 (HKAS 1.25) is required. Key journal entries（來自 LP 例子，全部平衡）: 1. Omitted supplier invoice discovered after year end for goods delivered and on hand at year end (adjusting): Account Dr HK$ Cr HK$ Inventory – raw materials 150,000 Trade payable 150,000 2. Out of court settlement of a pre year end personal injury claim (adjusting): Account Dr HK$ Cr HK$ Compensation expense 2,000,000 Claims payable 2,000,000 3. Customer liquidated after year end — debt existed at year end (adjusting): Account Dr HK$ Cr HK$ Credit loss 20,000,000 Trade receivable 20,000,000 4. Post year end sale below cost evidences NRV at year end — 50% write down of HK$500,000 inventory (adjusting): Account Dr HK$ Cr HK$ Loss on inventory write down 250,000 Finished goods inventory 250,000 5. Goods paid for before year end found defective and returned after year end for a full refund (adjusting): Account Dr HK$ Cr HK$ Receivable (refund) 750,000 Asset (e.g. fishing net / inventory) 750,000 C. Disclosure（要披露乜） Date of authorisation for issue (HKAS 10.17–18): disclose the date the financial statements were authorised for issue and who gave that authorisation ; if the owners have power to amend the financial statements after issue, disclose that fact. Rationale: the financial statements do not reflect events after this date. Updating disclosure about conditions at the end of the reporting period (HKAS 10.19–20): where information received after the reporting period relates to conditions existing at period end (e.g. a contingent liability that was not recognised), the entity must update the related disclosures in light of the new information — even where no recognised amount changes. Material non adjusting events (HKAS 10.21): for each material category of non adjusting event, disclose: the nature of the event ; and an estimate of its financial effect , or a statement that such an estimate cannot be made . Immaterial non adjusting events require no disclosure. Dividends (HKAS 1.137): disclose in the notes the amount of dividends proposed or declared before the financial statements were authorised for issue but not recognised as a distribution to owners during the period, and the related amount per share . 易混淆概念對比 Table 1: Adjusting events vs Non adjusting events Adjusting events Non adjusting events Definition Provide evidence of conditions existing at the end of the reporting period (HKAS 10.3(a)) Indicative of conditions that arose after the end of the reporting period (HKAS 10.3(b)) Accounting treatment Adjust amounts recognised / recognise items not previously recognised (HKAS 10.8) Do not adjust ; recognise in the period the event occurs (HKAS 10.10) Disclosure Update disclosures about conditions existing at period end (HKAS 10.19–20) Disclose nature + estimate of financial effect only if material (HKAS 10.21) Typical examples Court case settlement; customer bankruptcy; inventory sold below cost; fraud/errors discovered Dividends declared; major share issue; plant destroyed by storm; FV decline of investments; major acquisition 點樣分辨：問自己「呢件事反映嘅情況，喺年結日當日存唔存在？」存在 → adjusting；年結後先出現 → non adjusting。考試伏位：件事「幾時被發現」唔重要，重要嘅係「個 condition 幾時存在」—— customer bankruptcy、訴訟和解雖然年結後先知道，但都係 adjusting。Dividends declared 係最常考嘅 non adjusting trap：宣派股息唔可以 confirm 做年結負債。 Table 2: Material non adjusting event vs Going concern failure Material non adjusting event Event indicating entity is no longer a going concern Root cause New condition arising after period end Deterioration from conditions existing at period end or arising after period end (either can trigger it) Effect on the 20X1 financial statements No adjustment; note disclosure of nature + financial effect (HKAS 10.21) Do not prepare on a going concern basis (HKAS 10.14) Scale of change Amounts in the original financial statements untouched Fundamental change in the basis of accounting — a new basis, not adjustments within the old basis (HKAS 10.15) Other disclosure Estimate of financial effect (or statement it cannot be made) HKAS 1 disclosures that the going concern basis is not used (HKAS 1.25) 點樣分辨：non adjusting event 再大件事，只要公司仲係 going concern，都只係「披露」；但一旦管理層決定清盤/停業（或無其他現實選擇），就唔係調幾個數咁簡單，而係成個編製基礎都要改。考試伏位：唔好以為 non adjusting event 永遠只係披露——如果佢令 going concern assumption 失效，HKAS 10 要求 fundamental change in basis。 Phase 2 閃卡 Card 1 Front: According to HKAS 10.3, what are "events after the reporting period"? Back: Favourable or unfavourable events occurring between the end of the reporting period and the date the financial statements are authorised for issue . Two types: adjusting events (evidence of conditions existing at period end) and non adjusting events (conditions arising after period end). 💬 繁中白話解釋：HKAS 10 管嘅時間窗係「年結日之後、財務報表獲授權刊發之前」。記住終點係 authorisation date，唔係 AGM 批准日、唔係交 Companies Registry 嗰日。 Card 2 Front: State the accounting treatment for adjusting events under HKAS 10.8. Back: The entity shall adjust the amounts recognised in its financial statements to reflect adjusting events. This may mean: (1) adjusting an existing balance, or (2) recognising an amount not previously recognised. 💬 繁中白話解釋：Adjusting event 即係話「年結日其實已經係咁，只係我哋遲知」——所以要返轉頭改返份報表嘅數。 Card 3 Front: Give FOUR examples of adjusting events listed in HKAS 10.9. Back: Settlement of a court case confirming a present obligation at period end. Bankruptcy of a customer confirming credit impairment at period end. Sale of inventories below cost giving evidence of NRV at period end. Determination of cost/proceeds of assets bought/sold before period end. Discovery of fraud or errors showing the financial statements are incorrect. (any four) 💬 繁中白話解釋：共通點：件事本身或者背後嘅 condition 喺年結日已經存在，年結後嘅新消息只係「證實」咗佢。 Card 4 Front: State the accounting treatment for non adjusting events under HKAS 10.10 and HKAS 10.21. Back: The entity shall not adjust amounts recognised in the financial statements (HKAS 10.10). Accounting consequences are recognised in the reporting period in which the event occurs. If material , disclose the nature of the event and an estimate of its financial effect (or a statement that an estimate cannot be made) (HKAS 10.21). 💬 繁中白話解釋：Non adjusting = 新年新事。數留返落個新年度先計，但如果夠大單（material），舊年度報表嘅 notes 要講清楚件事同埋財務影響。 Card 5 Front: How should dividends declared after the reporting period be treated? (HKAS 10.12–13, HKAS 1.137) Back: Not recognised as a liability at the end of the reporting period — no obligation existed at period end (non adjusting event). Disclose in the notes: the total amount of dividends proposed/declared before authorisation for issue and the amount per share (HKAS 1.137). 💬 繁中白話解釋：呢個係經典考試陷阱！年結後宣派股息 ≠ 年結負債，因為宣派之前公司無任何義務要派。只可以喺 notes 披露總額同每股金額。 Card 6 Front: What does HKAS 10 require if events after the reporting period indicate the entity is no longer a going concern? (HKAS 10.14–15) Back: The entity shall not prepare its financial statements on a going concern basis (HKAS 10.14). Where the effect is pervasive : a fundamental change in the basis of accounting is required — not mere adjustments within the original basis (HKAS 10.15). HKAS 1 disclosures apply (HKAS 1.25). 💬 繁中白話解釋：Going concern 一冇咗，就唔係「調整」層次，而係成盤賬用另一個 basis 重編。記住關鍵字：fundamental change in the basis of accounting。 Card 7 Front: What must an entity disclose about the date of authorisation for issue? (HKAS 10.17–18) Back: The date when the financial statements were authorised for issue. Who gave that authorisation. If owners have the power to amend the financial statements after issue, disclose that fact. 💬 繁中白話解釋：因為報表唔會反映 authorisation date 之後發生嘅事，所以用家一定要知道呢個日期同埋邊個授權，先至識判斷資料嘅時效。 Card 8 Front: An entity receives post year end information about a contingent liability that existed at year end but was never recognised. What is required? (HKAS 10.19–20) Back: The entity must update the related disclosures about conditions existing at the end of the reporting period in light of the new information. This applies even where the new information does not change any recognised amounts (unless the information now causes a liability to be recognised). 💬 繁中白話解釋：就算個數唔郁（例如 contingent liability 仍然唔 recognise），notes 嘅披露都要跟新資料 update。Adjusting event 唔單止調數，仲要 update 披露。 本章急救詞彙 EN Term 繁中白話 English Model Sentence Events after the reporting period 年結日後、報表授權刊發前發生嘅事 Events after the reporting period occur between the end of the reporting period and the date the financial statements are authorised for issue. Authorised for issue 管理層/董事會正式批准報表對外發放嗰一刻 The board authorised the financial statements for issue on 5 March 20X7. Adjusting event 證實年結日已存在狀況嘅事，要改數 The customer's bankruptcy is an adjusting event because it confirms the receivable was credit impaired at the reporting date. Non adjusting event 年結後先出現嘅新狀況，唔改數但可能要披露 The destruction of the warehouse by fire is a non adjusting event disclosed in the notes. Going concern basis 假設公司會繼續經營落去嘅編製基礎 The financial statements shall not be prepared on a going concern basis if management intends to liquidate the entity. Fundamental change in the basis of accounting 成個會計基礎重編，唔係淨係調整 A pervasive loss of going concern requires a fundamental change in the basis of accounting. Net realisable value (NRV) 存貨估計售價減埋完工同銷售成本 The post year end clearance sale provided evidence of the net realisable value of inventories at the reporting date. Present obligation 年結日已經存在嘅法律或推定義務 The court settlement confirms that the entity had a present obligation at the end of the reporting period.

Q4 — Answer: Write-down of HK$264,000; Dr Loss on inventory write down 264,000 / Cr Finished goods inventory 264,000
excerpt: M6 Chapter 14: Events after the Reporting Period — Phase 3 Answers Q1 — Answer: B Model Answer (EN): Under HKAS 10, events after the reporting period are those …
text: M6 Chapter 14: Events after the Reporting Period — Phase 3 Answers Q1 — Answer: B Model Answer (EN): Under HKAS 10, events after the reporting period are those that occur between the end of the reporting period and the date when the financial statements are authorised for issue . For Harbour Lighting, the window runs from 31 December 20X7 to 12 March 20X8 , the date the board of directors authorises the financial statements for issue. The upload date (20 March), the filing with the Companies Registry (2 April) and shareholder approval at the AGM (28 May) are all irrelevant to fixing the authorisation date. 解題思路（繁中）: 呢題考 HKAS 10 時間窗嘅終點。時間窗 = 年結日 → authorised for issue 嗰日。Board of directors 授權刊發嗰日先係 authorisation date。A 錯：18 Feb 只係完成草稿，報表仍未 ready to be authorised。C 錯：交 Companies Registry 係 administrative filing，同 authorisation 無關。D 錯：shareholders 喺 AGM approve 唔等於 authorisation for issue；除非股東有權喺刊發後修改報表（咁要先披露），否則 AGM 日期完全唔用。考試伏位：題目特登俾晒五個日期，咪俾「最後嗰個日期」或者「最正式嗰個程序」呃到。 Rule Check: HKAS 10.3 Common Trap（繁中）: 以為 shareholder approval 先係終點。HKAS 10 嘅 window 喺 board authorises for issue 嗰刻已經關閉；股東批准日之後發生嘅事完全喺 scope 之外。 Q2 — Answer: B Model Answer (EN): The discovery of fraud (deliberate overstatement of revenue) is an adjusting event under HKAS 10.9 — the discovery of fraud or errors that show the financial statements are incorrect provides evidence of conditions that existed at the end of the reporting period (30 September 20X6). Velvet Curtain must adjust the amounts recognised in its 20X6 financial statements (HKAS 10.8). Options A (major business combination), C (announcing a plan to discontinue an operation) and D (a major share issue) are all examples of non adjusting events listed in HKAS 10.22 — they reflect conditions that arose after the reporting period. 解題思路（繁中）: 分辨關鍵：個 condition 喺年結日存唔存在？B 嘅收入造假係喺 20X6 年度內發生嘅，audit 只係「發現」佢——discovery of fraud or errors 係 HKAS 10.9 明文嘅 adjusting example。A、C、D 全部係 HKAS 10.22 嘅 non adjusting examples：acquisition、discontinuation plan、share issue 都係年結後先出現嘅新情況，再大單都唔可以調整，最多做 disclosure。考試伏位：唔好見到「大件事/影響大」就覺得要 adjust——materiality 只決定 non adjusting event 使唔使披露，唔會將佢變成 adjusting。 Rule Check: HKAS 10.3(a), 10.8, 10.9; HKAS 10.22 Common Trap（繁中）: 將「事件被發現/發生嘅日期」當成分類標準。正確問題係：件事反映嘅 underlying condition 喺年結日存在嗎？Fraud 發生喺年內 → adjusting；announcement 同 issue 先係年後嘅新嘢 → non adjusting。 Q3 — Answer: C Model Answer (EN): A dividend declared after the reporting period is a non adjusting event (HKAS 10.12–13): the entity had no obligation to pay the dividend at 31 December 20X7, so no liability is recognised at the reporting date. Under HKAS 1.137, Marble Fountain must disclose in the notes the amount of dividends proposed or declared before the financial statements were authorised for issue but not recognised as a distribution to owners during the period — here HK$2,400,000 (3,000,000 shares × HK$0.80) — and the related amount per share (HK$0.80) . 解題思路（繁中）: 呢題係 dividends declared 嘅標準考法。A 錯：雖然宣派發生喺 authorisation date 之前，但年結日（31 Dec 20X7）公司根本無 obligation，所以唔可以 confirm 做負債。B 錯：股息唔屬於 20X7 年度嘅 distribution，唔可以喺 20X7 嘅 SOCIE 扣 retained earnings——佢會喺 20X8 先確認。D 錯：雖然唔 adjust，但因為宣派發生喺 authorisation 之前，HKAS 1.137 要求 notes 披露總額同每股金額，唔可以隻字不提。計數：3,000,000 × $0.80 = $2,400,000。 Rule Check: HKAS 10.12–13; HKAS 1.137 Common Trap（繁中）: 見到「declared before authorisation for issue」就以為可以入賬做 liability。「宣派」先係製造 obligation 嘅動作——宣派之前無 obligation，所以永遠唔會係年結負債。 Q4 — Answer: Write down of HK$264,000; Dr Loss on inventory write down 264,000 / Cr Finished goods inventory 264,000 Model Answer (EN): (a) Classification: Adjusting event. The competitor's product launch in May 20X8 (before the reporting date) had already reduced demand for the model at 30 June 20X8; the post year end clearance sale merely provides evidence of the net realisable value of the inventories at the end of the reporting period (HKAS 10.3(a), 10.8, 10.9(b)(ii)). Workings: NRV = (4,000 units × HK$180) − HK$24,000 = HK$720,000 − HK$24,000 = HK$696,000 Write down = Cost − NRV = HK$960,000 − HK$696,000 = HK$264,000 (b) Journal entry as at 30 June 20X8: Account Dr HK$ Cr HK$ Loss on inventory write down 264,000 Finished goods inventory 264,000 解題思路（繁中）: 呢題嘅伏位喺個日期：clearance sale 係 20 July（年結後），所以好多同學會當佢 non adjusting。但題目特登講明 demand decline 係由 May 20X8 （年結前）嘅 competitor launch 引起——即係話 NRV 低於成本呢個 condition 喺 30 June 已經存在，7 月嘅平賣只係提供證據。NRV 記得要扣 selling costs（$180 × 4,000 − $24,000 = $696,000），唔係淨係用售價。分錄要平衡：Dr 損失 / Cr 存貨 $264,000。 Rule Check: HKAS 10.3(a), 10.8, 10.9(b)(ii) Common Trap（繁中）: (1) 見到「年結後先賣」就判 non adjusting——要睇減值嘅原因幾時出現；(2) 計 NRV 唔記得扣 selling costs，變咗 write down $240,000；(3) 分錯方向，將存貨放 Debit。 Q5 — Answer: C Model Answer (EN): After the reporting period, management determined that it must liquidate the entity — the going concern assumption is no longer appropriate. Under HKAS 10.14, Coral Island shall not prepare its financial statements on a going concern basis . Because the inability to continue as a going concern has a pervasive effect on the entity's financial position, HKAS 10.15 requires a fundamental change in the basis of accounting (a new basis of preparation), rather than adjustments to amounts recognised within the original going concern basis. The disclosures required by HKAS 1 (HKAS 1.25) must also be given. Note that this outcome applies even though the typhoon is a non adjusting event (a condition arising after the reporting period). 解題思路（繁中）: 呢題測 going concern override。A 錯：雖然 typhoon 本身係 non adjusting event，但管理層已決定清盤——going concern 一失效就唔可以只係披露。B 錯：HKAS 10.15 講明，影響係 pervasive 嘅話，唔係「調整某幾個數」而係 fundamental change in the basis of accounting，成個 basis 都要換。D 錯：雙重錯誤——（1）繼續用 going concern basis 違反 HKAS 10.14；（2）material non adjusting event 一定要喺 20X8 報表 notes 披露，唔可以無披露。考試伏位：non adjusting event 唔一定「只係披露」——如果佢令 going concern 唔成立，後果係改變編製基礎。 Rule Check: HKAS 10.14, 10.15; HKAS 1.25 Common Trap（繁中）: 以為「事件年結後發生 = non adjusting = 只係披露」呢條公式適用於所有情況。Going concern 係例外：無論觸發原因係 adjusting 定 non adjusting，只要管理層 intend to liquidate / cease trading，就唔可以用 going concern basis。

title: M6 Chapter 14: Events after the Reporting Period — Phase 3 Quiz
headings: M6 Chapter 14: Events after the Reporting Period — Phase 3 Quiz
excerpt: M6 Chapter 14: Events after the Reporting Period — Phase 3 Quiz Rules: Closed book · 15 minutes · 5 questions · Submit as 1. … 2. … 3. … 4. … 5. … — 超時如實申報 Q1. …
text: M6 Chapter 14: Events after the Reporting Period — Phase 3 Quiz Rules: Closed book · 15 minutes · 5 questions · Submit as 1. … 2. … 3. … 4. … 5. … — 超時如實申報 Q1. Harbour Lighting Limited (Harbour Lighting) prepares financial statements for the year ended 31 December 20X7. Management completes the draft financial statements on 18 February 20X8 and circulates them to the audit committee. The board of directors reviews and authorises the financial statements for issue on 12 March 20X8. The financial statements are uploaded to the company's website on 20 March 20X8, filed with the Companies Registry on 2 April 20X8, and approved by shareholders at the annual general meeting on 28 May 20X8. In accordance with HKAS 10, within which period must Harbour Lighting identify events after the reporting period? A. Between 31 December 20X7 and 18 February 20X8 B. Between 31 December 20X7 and 12 March 20X8 C. Between 31 December 20X7 and 2 April 20X8 D. Between 31 December 20X7 and 28 May 20X8 Q2. Velvet Curtain Limited (Velvet Curtain), a retailer of home furnishings, has a reporting period ended 30 September 20X6. Its financial statements were authorised for issue on 15 December 20X6. In accordance with HKAS 10, which of the following events is an adjusting event after the reporting period? A. On 2 November 20X6, Velvet Curtain acquired 100% of a competitor, increasing its market share by 15%. B. On 20 October 20X6, Velvet Curtain's internal audit team discovered that the sales department had deliberately overstated revenue for the year ended 30 September 20X6. C. On 8 November 20X6, Velvet Curtain announced a plan to discontinue its loss making curtain dyeing operation. D. On 25 November 20X6, Velvet Curtain issued 5,000,000 new ordinary shares to the public. Q3. Marble Fountain Limited (Marble Fountain) has a reporting period ended 31 December 20X7, and its financial statements were authorised for issue on 20 March 20X8. On 5 March 20X8, the board declared a final dividend of HK$0.80 per share on the 3,000,000 ordinary shares in issue. In accordance with HKAS 10 and HKAS 1, how should Marble Fountain account for the dividend in its financial statements for the year ended 31 December 20X7? A. Recognise a dividend payable of HK$2,400,000 as a liability at 31 December 20X7, because the declaration occurred before the financial statements were authorised for issue. B. Recognise a dividend payable of HK$2,400,000 as a deduction from retained earnings in the statement of changes in equity for the year ended 31 December 20X7. C. Make no adjustment, but disclose in the notes the total dividend of HK$2,400,000 and the amount per share of HK$0.80. D. Make no adjustment and no disclosure, because the dividend was declared after the end of the reporting period. Q4. Copper Kettle Limited (Copper Kettle), a manufacturer of cookware, has a reporting period ended 30 June 20X8. Its financial statements are expected to be authorised for issue on 25 September 20X8. At 30 June 20X8, Copper Kettle holds 4,000 units of a discontinued saucepan model in finished goods inventory, recorded at a total cost of HK$960,000. On 20 July 20X8, in a clearance sale, Copper Kettle sold the entire batch of 4,000 units for HK$180 per unit, incurring selling costs of HK$24,000 in total. The clearance price was driven by a competitor's product launch in May 20X8, which had already sharply reduced demand for the model before 30 June 20X8. In accordance with HKAS 10: (a) State whether this is an adjusting or non adjusting event, and calculate the amount of any write down required in the financial statements for the year ended 30 June 20X8. Show your workings. (b) Prepare the journal entry (Dr/Cr) as at 30 June 20X8 to record any adjustment. Q5. Coral Island Limited (Coral Island) operates a single food processing plant, its only revenue generating asset, and has a reporting period ended 31 March 20X8. On 10 April 20X8, before the financial statements were authorised for issue, a typhoon completely destroyed the plant. The damage was not covered by insurance. Coral Island was unable to obtain financing to rebuild, and on 30 April 20X8 management resolved to liquidate the company. In accordance with HKAS 10, how should Coral Island prepare its financial statements for the year ended 31 March 20X8? A. Continue to prepare the financial statements on a going concern basis, making no adjustment, and disclose the typhoon as a material non adjusting event with an estimate of its financial effect. B. Adjust the carrying amount of the plant to its recoverable amount of nil within the 31 March 20X8 financial statements, and retain the going concern basis for all other items. C. Not prepare the financial statements on a going concern basis, because the pervasive effect of the loss requires a fundamental change in the basis of accounting rather than adjustments to amounts recognised, with the related disclosures required by HKAS 1. D. Prepare the financial statements on a going concern basis because the typhoon occurred after the end of the reporting period, and recognise the destruction of the plant in the financial statements for the year ending 31 March 20X9 with no disclosure in the 31 March 20X8 financial statements.
