excerpt: M8 Chapter 4: Audit Planning II — Phase 3 Quiz Rules: Closed book · 15 minutes · 5 questions · Submit as 1. … 2. … 3. … 4. … 5. … — 超時如實申報 Question 1 (Calculati…
text: M8 Chapter 4: Audit Planning II — Phase 3 Quiz Rules: Closed book · 15 minutes · 5 questions · Submit as 1. … 2. … 3. … 4. … 5. … — 超時如實申報 Question 1 (Calculation / short answer) The audit engagement partner of Harbour Textiles Ltd has set a firm policy that overall audit risk must not exceed 5%. Following the risk assessment at the planning stage, the engagement team has assessed inherent risk at 80% and control risk at 50% for the revenue cycle. Calculate the maximum acceptable detection risk, and state what this level of detection risk implies for the extent of substantive procedures the auditor should perform over the revenue cycle. Question 2 (Scenario MCQ) You are the audit senior of Bright Logistics Ltd, a warehousing company. At the year end inventory count, you select a sample of inventory items physically located on the warehouse shelves and trace each item into the client's inventory listing records. Which financial statement assertion is this procedure primarily designed to test? A. Existence of recorded inventory B. Completeness of recorded inventory C. Accuracy, valuation and allocation of inventory D. Rights and obligations over inventory Question 3 (Scenario MCQ) During the audit of Pearl Catering Group Ltd, the audit junior discovers that the company lent HK$45,000 interest free to one of its directors during the year. The amount is quantitatively immaterial against all of the firm's materiality benchmarks (0.5% of revenue, 5% of profit before tax, 2% of total assets), and the loan has been correctly recorded in the accounting records. No disclosure of the loan has been made in the draft financial statements. Which of the following best describes how the auditor should treat this matter? A. Ignore the matter, because the amount is quantitatively immaterial and correctly recorded B. Treat the loan as material by nature, because transactions with directors require disclosure as related party transactions C. Increase financial statement materiality so that the loan becomes clearly immaterial D. Request the director to repay the loan before the auditor's report is signed Question 4 (Scenario MCQ) Dragon Manufacturing Ltd has an internal audit function, and the engagement partner of the external auditor is considering using internal auditors to provide direct assistance on the audit. The proposed assignments are: (1) Reperforming the year end bank reconciliations, a routine procedure involving limited judgement (2) Evaluating the reasonableness of a highly subjective provision for a legal claim, which involves significant judgement and a high risk of material misstatement Under HKSA 610 (Revised 2013) Using the Work of Internal Auditors, which of the following is correct? A. Both (1) and (2) may be assigned, provided the internal auditors are supervised B. (1) may be assigned, but (2) must not be assigned to internal auditors C. (2) may be assigned, but (1) must not be assigned because bank reconciliations involve the control system D. Neither (1) nor (2) may be assigned, because direct assistance is prohibited for all external audits in Hong Kong Question 5 (MCQ) The audit manager is designing substantive analytical procedures over the payroll expense of a client. Which of the following statements about the design of substantive analytical procedures is correct? A. The acceptable threshold should be set by reference to materiality for the financial statements as a whole B. The auditor should first calculate the difference between the recorded amount and prior year balances, then develop the expectation C. The threshold must not exceed performance materiality and must be small enough to detect misstatements that could be material in aggregate D. Substantive analytical procedures alone provide sufficient appropriate audit evidence over payroll and require no corroborating procedures End of quiz — do not open the answers file until you have submitted your responses.

title: M8 Chapter 5: Sampling — Phase 1 速查表 + Phase 2 閃卡
headings: M8 Chapter 5: Sampling — Phase 1 速查表 + Phase 2 閃卡
A. Evidence — 抽樣風險與核心定義
B. Evidence — Statistical vs Non-statistical Sampling（HKSA 530）
C. Procedures — Sample Selection Methods（HKSA 530.2–.4, App 1）
D. Procedures — Techniques for Substantive Tests
E. Procedures / Assertions — Tests of Control vs Substantive Procedures（HKSA 315 (Revised 2019)、HKSA 500、HKSA 520）
excerpt: M8 Chapter 5: Sampling — Phase 1 速查表 + Phase 2 閃卡 Phase 1 速查表 Learning Objectives 1. Explain the concept of audit sampling and representative sampling under HKS…
text: M8 Chapter 5: Sampling — Phase 1 速查表 + Phase 2 閃卡 Phase 1 速查表 Learning Objectives 1. Explain the concept of audit sampling and representative sampling under HKSA 530 Audit Sampling. 2. Distinguish between sampling risk and non sampling risk, and between statistical and non statistical sampling. 3. Describe the principal sample selection methods and the factors that influence sample size for tests of control and tests of details. 4. Apply substantive sampling techniques (variable sampling and monetary unit sampling) to an audit plan. 5. Evaluate sample results, including projecting misstatements and dealing with anomalous errors. 必背考點 A. Evidence — 抽樣風險與核心定義 Audit sampling (HKSA 530): The application of audit procedures to less than 100% of items within a population of audit relevance such that all sampling units have a chance of selection , in order to provide the auditor with a reasonable basis on which to draw conclusions about the entire population. Population: the entire set of data from which a sample is selected and about which the auditor wishes to draw conclusions. Representative sample: one in which the properties of interest of the sample are approximately the same as those of the population. A sample may fail to be representative because of both sampling risk and non sampling risk . Sampling risk (HKSA 530): the risk that the auditor's conclusion based on a sample may be different from the conclusion if the entire population were subjected to the same audit procedure. Sampling risk is a component of detection risk — the only risk in the audit risk model under the auditor's control. Two types of erroneous conclusion: (a) Affects audit EFFECTIVENESS (the one the auditor is primarily concerned with — more likely to lead to an inappropriate audit opinion): Tests of control: concluding controls are more effective than they actually are; Tests of details: concluding a material misstatement does not exist when in fact it does . (b) Affects audit EFFICIENCY (leads to additional work to establish initial conclusions were incorrect): Tests of control: concluding controls are less effective than they actually are; Tests of details: concluding a material misstatement exists when in fact it does not . Non sampling risk (HKSA 530): the risk that the auditor reaches an erroneous conclusion for any reason not related to sampling risk — e.g. applying inappropriate audit procedures, failure to recognise a misstatement or deviation, misinterpreting audit evidence. 考試重點：auditor 只提供 reasonable assurance ，永遠唔係 absolute assurance —— 因為根本冇驗證 100% 嘅交易。 B. Evidence — Statistical vs Non statistical Sampling（HKSA 530） Statistical sampling must have BOTH : (i) random selection of sample items; and (ii) the use of probability theory to evaluate sample results, including measurement of sampling risk . Any approach lacking either characteristic = non statistical sampling. Whichever approach is used is a matter of professional judgement ; statistical sampling still requires professional judgement (e.g. defining what constitutes a misstatement, setting performance materiality). Non statistical sampling: sample size based on auditor's judgement of what is desirable; no complex mathematical procedures; results are not statistically valid ; risk of bias; not defensible if selection lacks logic; different auditors may produce different samples. C. Procedures — Sample Selection Methods（HKSA 530.2–.4, App 1） Method Statistical? Key point Random selection Yes Random number generators or tables Systematic selection Yes Population units ÷ sample size = sampling interval (e.g. every 50th invoice); starting point best set by random number generator; ensure no pattern within the population matches the interval Monetary unit sampling (MUS) Yes Value weighted selection; conclusion in monetary amounts; larger balances have a greater chance of selection (protective for the auditor); starting point need NOT be zero Haphazard selection No No structured technique; must avoid conscious bias (e.g. easy to locate items); inappropriate when using statistical sampling Block selection No Block of contiguous items; often used in cut off testing ; rarely appropriate for drawing valid inferences about the entire population Stratification (HKSA 530): breaking a population into sub populations with similar characteristics; objective is to reduce variability within each stratum so sample sizes can be reduced WITHOUT increasing sampling risk . Tests of details often stratified by monetary value (larger items = higher overstatement risk) or by risk characteristic (e.g. receivables by age). Results from a stratum can only be projected to that stratum ; combine stratum projections for the total balance. Three approaches to testing items (only the third is "audit sampling"): 1. 100% selection — NOT sampling; appropriate for small populations of high value items, significant risk, or high expected misstatement in tests of details; 2. Selection of specific items — NOT sampling (not all units stand a chance); high value/unusual/error prone items; subject to non sampling risk; 3. Audit sampling — every sampling unit stands an equal chance of selection. Factors to consider when designing/selecting a sample (4 factors): 1. The purpose of the procedure ; 2. The combination of procedures being performed; 3. The nature of the audit evidence sought; 4. The possible misstatement conditions . Factors influencing sample size — Tests of control (HKSA 530, Appendix 2): ↑ Extent to which risk assessment takes into account relevant controls (more reliance on controls) → Increase ↑ Tolerable rate of deviation → Decrease ↑ Expected rate of deviation of the population → Increase ↑ Assurance required that tolerable rate is not exceeded → Increase ↑ Number of sampling units in population → Negligible effect (large populations) Factors influencing sample size — Tests of details (HKSA 530, Appendix 3): ↑ Assessed risk of material misstatement → Increase (no tests of control ⇒ need low detection risk ⇒ more substantive evidence) ↑ Use of other substantive procedures directed at the same assertion → Decrease ↑ Assurance required that tolerable misstatement is not exceeded → Increase ↑ Tolerable misstatement → Decrease ↑ Expected misstatement in the population → Increase Stratification of the population (when appropriate) → Decrease Number of sampling units in population → Negligible effect (but under MUS, ↑ monetary value of population increases sample size unless offset by a proportional increase in materiality) Sampling process (3 steps): Step 1 Design the sample (objectives, period covered, size, population/sampling unit, assertions, what constitutes a deviation/misstatement) → Step 2 Select the sample and carry out tests (apply alternative procedures if expected evidence unavailable) → Step 3 Evaluate the results . D. Procedures — Techniques for Substantive Tests Variable sampling: predicts the value of a specific variable within a population; each individual item is the sampling unit. Three common types: Mean per unit — sample mean × number of items in population; Ratio estimation — apply the sample ratio to the entire population; Difference estimation — like ratio estimation but also incorporates the records in the population itself. Monetary unit sampling (MUS): uses the currency unit value (not the items) as the sampling population; applied to large variance populations (receivables, inventories); sample size considers population size, tolerable misstatement (related to performance materiality) and assurance level required. Sampling interval = population value ÷ sample size ; select the balance containing each cumulative interval. Attribute sampling: used to test controls ; each item either does or does not possess the attribute ("correct / not correct"); monetary amount is irrelevant — a test of control provides indirect evidence over the financial statements. Upper deviation rate = sample (population) deviation rate + sampling risk ; if upper deviation rate ≤ tolerable rate of deviation, the auditor can place reliance on the control. (Confidence level + sampling risk = 100%.) E. Procedures / Assertions — Tests of Control vs Substantive Procedures（HKSA 315 (Revised 2019)、HKSA 500、HKSA 520） Tests of control: evaluate the operating effectiveness of controls in preventing, or detecting and correcting, material misstatement; focus is on the processes , NOT the monetary amount. Substantive procedures (HKSA 500): = tests of details + substantive analytical procedures ; aim to detect material misstatement at the assertion level ; focus on monetary values. Analytical procedures (HKSA 520.4): evaluations of financial information through analysis of plausible relationships among financial and non financial data; they identify possible sources of misstatement but do not, in themselves, detect misstatements (misstatements may cancel out/contra). Use as the main substantive evidence only where internal controls are assessed as reliable. Mandatory rule: the auditor must perform some substantive testing over ALL material transactions and balances — can never rely wholly on tests of control. Audit risk model: Audit risk = Inherent risk × Control risk × Detection risk . Assertion direction example (completeness of revenue): trace from sales orders → GDNs → sales invoice → sales day book → sales ledger → general ledger (starting point "outside" the accounting system tests for understatement). Example: tracing receivables to post year end cash receipts supports existence and valuation assertions. F. Evidence — Evaluation of Results（HKSA 530.12, .14, .15, .A21–.A23） HKSA 530.12: the auditor shall investigate the nature and cause of any deviations or misstatements identified, and evaluate their possible effect on the purpose of the audit procedure and on other areas of the audit. Anomalous error: a one off misstatement/deviation not representative of the population; the auditor must obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence (via further procedures) that it is genuinely anomalous, and be satisfied it is not indicative of a fraud risk factor . Anomalous misstatements may be excluded from projection (tests of details only — for tests of control the sample deviation rate IS the projected rate). HKSA 530.14: the auditor shall project misstatements found in the sample to the population for tests of details. Projected misstatement = (misstatement in sample ÷ sample value) × population value . HKSA 530.15(a),(b): evaluate (a) the results of the sample; and (b) whether sampling has provided a reasonable basis for conclusions about the population. Evaluation rule (HKSA 530.A21/A22): projected misstatement + anomalous misstatement = best estimate of misstatement in the population ; if this total exceeds tolerable misstatement , the sample does NOT provide a reasonable basis for conclusions. The closer the total is to tolerable misstatement, the more likely actual misstatement exceeds it. Tolerable misstatement (HKSA 530.A22; HKSA 320 para. 9): the application of performance materiality to a particular sampling procedure; may be the same as, or lower than, performance materiality. If sampling does not provide a reasonable basis (HKSA 530.A23): (i) request management to investigate identified misstatements and potential further misstatements and make necessary adjustments; or (ii) tailor the nature, timing and extent of additional procedures (e.g. increase sample size, test an alternative control, modify related substantive procedures). Tolerable rate of deviation: the rate of deviation from prescribed internal control procedures set by the auditor in respect of which the auditor seeks assurance that it is not exceeded by the actual rate in the population. 易混淆概念對比 Table 1: Sampling Risk vs Non sampling Risk 比較點 Sampling Risk Non sampling Risk Definition (HKSA 530) Conclusion based on a sample may differ from the conclusion if the entire population were subjected to the same procedure Erroneous conclusion for any reason NOT related to sampling risk Root cause Sample not representative / sample too small Inappropriate procedures; failure to recognise a misstatement or deviation; misinterpreting evidence Relationship Component of detection risk Opposite of sampling risk How to reduce Increase the sample size Better training/supervision, appropriate procedure design, proper direction & review 點樣分辨 問題出在「抽唔啱」— 樣本本身代表性不足 問題出在「做唔啱」— 就算抽啱樣本，人為判斷/程序都出錯 考試伏位 Panelist 報告（Jun 2024）話考生分唔清兩者："did not put enough effort into studying audit sampling"。記住：misinterpreting audit evidence = non sampling risk ，唔好見到「risk」就亂揀 100% testing 冇 sampling risk，但仍然有 non sampling risk Table 2: Statistical vs Non statistical Sampling 比較點 Statistical Sampling Non statistical Sampling Defining characteristics BOTH (i) random selection AND (ii) probability theory to evaluate results, including measurement of sampling risk Any approach lacking either characteristic; sample size by auditor's judgement Selection methods Random, systematic, monetary unit sampling Haphazard, block selection Measurement of sampling risk Yes — mathematically measured No — results not statistically valid Advantages Defensible/precise probability statements; efficient sample sizes; usable by all staff levels; standard testing programme No complex maths; no specialist knowledge; harnesses auditor's judgement and experience Disadvantages Complex mathematics; principles must be properly applied Bias risk; sample sizes too large (cost) or too small (invalid); not defensible without logic; inconsistent between auditors 點樣分辨 兩個條件缺一不可：random + probability theory。淨係 random selection 而冇 probability evaluation 都唔算 Haphazard selection 喺 statistical sampling 入面係 inappropriate （HKSA 530 明確講） 考試伏位 唔好以為 statistical = 唔使 professional judgement — 兩者都要 judgement Block selection 雖然常用於 cut off testing，但對成個 population 推論「rarely appropriate」 Phase 2 閃卡 Card 1 Front: Define "audit sampling" according to HKSA 530, and state the two key numerical/selection characteristics in the definition. Back: The application of audit procedures to less than 100% of items within a population of audit relevance; Such that all sampling units have a chance of selection ; Purpose: to provide a reasonable basis for conclusions about the entire population . 100% examination and selection of specific items are NOT audit sampling. 💬 白話解：抽樣嘅精髓係「唔驗晒，但每個單位都有機會被抽中」。如果 auditor 淨係揀大額嗰啲嚟驗（specific items），嗰個唔叫 sampling，考試好鐘意用呢個位考你。 Card 2 Front: State the two types of erroneous conclusion caused by sampling risk, and identify which one the auditor is PRIMARILY concerned with and why. Back: Type (a) — effectiveness: controls concluded more effective than they are (ToC); material misstatement concluded not to exist when it does (ToD) → auditor primarily concerned — affects audit effectiveness , more likely to lead to an inappropriate audit opinion . Type (b) — efficiency: controls concluded less effective than they are (ToC); misstatement concluded to exist when it does not (ToD) → affects audit efficiency (extra work). 💬 白話解：記憶口訣 —— 「漏咗」（以為冇錯其實有錯）先係大鑊，會出錯 opinion；「做多了」（以為有錯其實冇錯）只係嘥時間。Effectiveness 永遠係考官首選答案。 Card 3 Front: Give three examples of non sampling risk and explain how it differs from sampling risk. Back: Applying inappropriate audit procedures ; Failure to recognise a misstatement or deviation; Misinterpreting the audit evidence obtained. Difference: non sampling risk arises even if the whole population is tested — it is unrelated to the fact that only a sample was examined. 💬 白話解：凡係「人為失手」—— 用錯程序、睇漏咗、解讀錯 evidence —— 全部歸 non sampling risk。抽樣方法本身冇問題都會中。 Card 4 Front: List the FIVE principal sample selection methods in HKSA 530 and classify each as statistical or non statistical. Back: Random selection — statistical (random number generators/tables); Systematic selection — statistical (sampling interval = population units ÷ sample size); Monetary unit sampling — statistical (value weighted; larger balances more likely selected); Haphazard selection — non statistical (no structured technique; must avoid bias; inappropriate for statistical sampling); Block selection — non statistical (contiguous items; cut off testing; rarely appropriate for inferences about the whole population). 💬 白話解：三統計、兩非統計。記住 haphazard 同 block 係「 judgement 派」；MUS 雖然揀大額嘢，但佢係 statistical 嘅 value weighted selection。 Card 5 Front: For tests of details, state the effect (increase/decrease/negligible) on sample size of: (1) higher assessed risk of material misstatement; (2) higher tolerable misstatement; (3) more expected misstatement; (4) more use of other substantive procedures on the same assertion; (5) stratification; (6) more sampling units in the population. (HKSA 530, Appendix 3) Back: 1. Higher RMM → Increase ; 2. Higher tolerable misstatement → Decrease ; 3. More expected misstatement → Increase ; 4. More other substantive procedures on same assertion → Decrease ; 5. Stratification → Decrease ; 6. More sampling units → Negligible effect (large populations). 💬 白話解：方向邏輯好簡單 —— 「越驚錯就抽越多」（risk↑、expected error↑ → size↑）；「條線越鬆/有其他人幫手 → 抽越少」（tolerable↑、其他 procedures↑、stratify → size↓）。人口數量對大 population 基本上冇影響，呢個係最常見 distractor。 Card 6 Front: Explain how monetary unit sampling (MUS) works, including how the sampling interval is calculated and why it is "protective" for the auditor. Back: Uses the currency unit value (not individual items) as the sampling population; Sampling interval = total population value ÷ sample size ; Starting from a (possibly random) start point, select the balance containing each cumulative interval; Larger balances have a greater chance of selection → automatically directs effort to higher value (higher overstatement risk) items — hence protective; Suited to large variance populations (receivables, inventories). 💬 白話解：想像成條 population 係一條「銀紙長龍」，每隔 interval 插一支旗，旗插喺邊個客戶嘅累計餘額入面就抽邊個。大額客戶「佔地」大，自然易中旗 —— 所以 MUS 天生偏向抽大額，對 auditor 有保護作用。 Card 7 Front: What is attribute sampling, and how does the auditor use the "upper deviation rate" to conclude on a test of control? Back: Technique used to test controls ; result is binary — the item either does or does not possess the attribute (e.g. authorised / not authorised); Monetary amount is irrelevant → tests of control give indirect evidence over the financial statements; Upper deviation rate = sample deviation rate + sampling risk (confidence level + sampling risk = 100%); If upper deviation rate ≤ tolerable rate of deviation → auditor can place reliance on the control ; otherwise increase substantive procedures. 💬 白話解：即使樣本錯誤率低過 tolerable rate 都唔可以即刻落結論 —— 一定要加返 sampling risk 上去先比較。呢個「加返個 risk buffer」嘅動作係 LP Illustrative Example 9 嘅核心。 Card 8 Front: An auditor finds a misstatement in a sample which appears to be a one off "anomalous error". What must the auditor do before excluding it from projection, and how are sample results evaluated overall? (HKSA 530.12, .14, .15) Back: Investigate the nature and cause of the misstatement (HKSA 530.12); Perform further procedures to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence that it is genuinely anomalous and not representative of the population; Be satisfied it is not indicative of a fraud risk factor ; Only then may it be excluded from projection (tests of details); Overall evaluation: projected misstatement + anomalous misstatement = best estimate; if total tolerable misstatement (application of performance materiality per HKSA 320 para. 9), the sample gives no reasonable basis → ask management to investigate/adjust, or extend procedures (increase sample size, test alternative control, modify substantive procedures). 💬 白話解：「一時失手」唔係你話咁算 —— auditor 要攞足證據證明佢真係 isolated，仲要排除 fraud 因素。最後條數好簡單：projected + anomalous 大過 tolerable misstatement = 個 sample 冇用，要做多啲嘢。 本章急救詞彙 EN Term 繁中白話 English Model Sentence Audit sampling 抽唔到100%，但個個單位都有機會被抽中嘅測試方法 Audit sampling involves applying audit procedures to less than 100% of items such that all sampling units have a chance of selection. Population 想落結論嗰成堆數據（成個餘額） The population of trade receivables comprises all individual customer balances at year end. Sampling risk 樣本唔代表性，令結論同驗晒成個 population 唔同嘅風險 Sampling risk increases when the sample size is too small to be representative of the population. Non sampling risk 同抽樣無關嘅人為失手風險（用錯程序、睇漏、解讀錯） Misinterpreting audit evidence is an example of non sampling risk. Tolerable misstatement Auditor 接受得嘅最大錯誤金額（performance materiality 嘅應用） The projected misstatement plus the anomalous misstatement exceeded tolerable misstatement, so the sample provided no reasonable basis for conclusions. Tolerable rate of deviation 控制測試入面接受得嘅最高偏差率 If the upper deviation rate exceeds the tolerable rate of deviation, the auditor cannot place reliance on the control. Stratification 將 population 按特性（例如金額）拆細，抽少啲但唔加風險 Stratifying the receivables population by monetary value reduced the sample size without increasing sampling risk. Monetary unit sampling 用「銀碼」做抽樣單位，大額項目天然易被抽中 Under monetary unit sampling, the sampling interval is calculated by dividing the population value by the sample size.

excerpt: M8 Chapter 5: Sampling — Phase 3 Answers Q1 — Answer: B Model Answer (EN): The test is a test of control — it evaluates the operating effectiveness of the autho…
text: M8 Chapter 5: Sampling — Phase 3 Answers Q1 — Answer: B Model Answer (EN): The test is a test of control — it evaluates the operating effectiveness of the authorisation control (whether the purchasing director authorised invoices as required by policy), not the monetary amount of the transactions. Because each invoice either does or does not possess the attribute of "authorised", it is performed using attribute sampling , and the result is binary (correct / not correct). Since the focus is on the process rather than a figure in the financial statements, the test provides only indirect evidence over the financial statements. 解題思路（繁中）: 關鍵字眼係「inspect for evidence of authorisation」— 測試目標係個 control （批核程序）有冇運作，而唔係張 invoice 嘅金額啱唔啱，所以係 test of control + attribute sampling。 A 錯：佢冇驗證 purchases 嘅 valuation，monetary amount 喺 attribute sampling 入面係 irrelevant。 C 錯：analytical procedures 係分析數據之間嘅 plausible relationships，同逐張 invoice 檢查簽名完全唔同。 D 錯：呢個唔係 test of details of balances，亦同 completeness of trade payables 無關；test of details 會直接驗證財務報表金額。 考試伏位：existence vs completeness 方向感之外，M8 最常見陷阱係將「inspect documents for authorisation」誤當 substantive procedure —— 記住「check 簽名/批核 = test of control」。 Rule Check: HKSA 530 (attribute sampling for tests of control); HKSA 500 (substantive procedures = tests of details + substantive analytical procedures) Common Trap（繁中）: 見到「inspect invoice」就以為係 substantive test。分辨方法：問自己「呢個測試係咪關心張單嘅銀碼？」— 唔關心銀碼、只關心控制有冇執行，就係 test of control，提供嘅係 indirect evidence。 Q2 — Answer: C Model Answer (EN): Non sampling risk is the risk that the auditor reaches an erroneous conclusion for any reason not related to sampling risk — for example, the application of inappropriate audit procedures , the failure to recognise a misstatement or deviation, or the misinterpretation of audit evidence. Applying an inappropriate audit procedure (option C) would produce an erroneous conclusion even if the entire population had been tested, so it is non sampling risk. 解題思路（繁中）: A 錯：sample deviation rate 低過 population 實際率 → 以為 controls 好過實際 —— 呢個係典型 sampling risk （影響 audit effectiveness）。 B 錯：樣本太細、唔具代表性，係 sampling risk 嘅根本成因（解法：增加 sample size）。 D 錯：以為 controls 差過實際 → 做多了 substantive work —— 都係 sampling risk（影響 audit efficiency）。 C 啱：就算抽 100% 嚟驗，用錯程序都會出錯結論，所以同「抽樣」本身無關。 Panelist 報告（Jun 2024）特別提到考生喺 sampling vs non sampling risk 上表現差 —— 呢個係必考伏位。 Rule Check: HKSA 530 (definitions of sampling risk and non sampling risk; two types of erroneous conclusion) Common Trap（繁中）: 「assessing controls as effective when they are ineffective」聽落好似人為判斷錯誤，但其實 LP 明確歸類為 sampling risk（樣本偏差率唔等於人口偏差率所致）。只有「用錯程序／睇漏咗／解讀錯 evidence」先係 non sampling risk。 Q3 — Answer: C Model Answer (EN): Per HKSA 530, Appendix 3, the more the auditor relies on other substantive procedures (tests of details or substantive analytical procedures) directed at the same assertion to reduce detection risk to an acceptable level, the less assurance is required from sampling, and therefore the smaller the sample size can be. The other options all require a LARGER sample: higher assessed risk of material misstatement (A) and higher expected misstatement (B) both increase the sample size; a decrease in tolerable misstatement (D) also increases the sample size (the lower the tolerable misstatement, the larger the sample). 解題思路（繁中）: 呢題考 HKSA 530 Appendix 3 嘅因素方向。記憶邏輯：「越驚有錯 → 抽越多」；「有其他證據幫手 / 條線放鬆 → 抽越少」。 A 錯：RMM 上升 → detection risk 要更低 → sample size 增加 。 B 錯：expected misstatement 越高 → 要更大樣本先估得準實際錯誤 → 增加 。 D 錯：tolerable misstatement 下降 （條線收緊）→ sample size 增加；注意係「decrease tolerable misstatement」，方向同你想要嘅相反。 C 啱：其他 substantive procedures 針對同一 assertion 做多了 → sampling 需要提供嘅 assurance 減少 → sample size 下降。 考試伏位：number of sampling units in the population 對大 population 只有 negligible effect —— 考官好鐘意用呢個做 distractor（本題冇用，但記住）。 Rule Check: HKSA 530, Appendix 3 (factors influencing sample size for tests of details) Common Trap（繁中）: 將「increase in tolerable misstatement」同「decrease in tolerable misstatement」方向調轉。記住：tolerable misstatement 越 高 （越寬鬆），sample size 越 細 。 Q4 — Answer: (a) HK$2,880,000; (b) No — the sample does not provide a reasonable basis Model Answer (EN): (a) Projected misstatement = (misstatement in sample ÷ sample value) × population value = (HK$360,000 ÷ HK$6,000,000) × HK$48,000,000 = 6% × HK$48,000,000 = HK$2,880,000 (overstatement). (b) Under HKSA 530, the auditor's best estimate of misstatement in the population is the projected misstatement plus the anomalous misstatement (here HK$2,880,000 + nil = HK$2,880,000). Since this total exceeds tolerable misstatement of HK$2,500,000 , the sample does NOT provide a reasonable basis for conclusions about the population. Appropriate course of action (any ONE): Request management to investigate the identified misstatements and the potential for further misstatements, and make any necessary adjustments ; or Tailor the nature, timing and extent of additional audit procedures to achieve the required assurance — e.g. increase the sample size, or modify related substantive procedures. 解題思路（繁中）: 投影公式係「sample 錯誤率 × 成個 population 價值」。先計錯誤率：360,000/6,000,000 = 6%，再乘 48,000,000 = 2,880,000。 (b) 嘅比較基準係 tolerable misstatement （唔係 overall materiality）— 記住 tolerable misstatement 係 performance materiality 應用喺個別抽樣程序上（HKSA 320 para. 9）。 因為冇 anomalous error，best estimate 就係 projected misstatement 本身。2.88m 2.5m → 個 sample 唔能提供 reasonable basis。 之後嘅行動有兩大路線：叫管理層查兼改數，或者加做程序（加大 sample / 改 substantive procedures）。答一個已夠，但兩個都識先穩陣。 伏位：唔好攞 HK$360,000 直接同 tolerable misstatement 比 —— 未投影嘅 sample error 唔係結論基礎。 Rule Check: HKSA 530.14 (projection of misstatements); HKSA 530.15(a),(b); HKSA 530.A22 (projected + anomalous vs tolerable misstatement); HKSA 530.A23 (responses when no reasonable basis); HKSA 320 para. 9 (performance materiality) Common Trap（繁中）: 忘記投影，直接話「360,000 < 2,500,000 所以冇問題」— 呢個係 zero mark 級錯誤。另一个伏位：以為有 anomalous error 就可以唔投影 —— 本題講明冇 anomalous error，所以全部要投影。 Q5 — Answer: (a) Sample deviation rate 4%; upper deviation rate 7%; (b) Yes — reliance can be placed on the control Model Answer (EN): (a) Sample deviation rate = 8 ÷ 200 × 100% = 4% . Upper deviation rate = sample deviation rate + sampling risk = 4% + 3% = 7% . (b) The upper deviation rate of 7% is below the tolerable rate of deviation of 8% . Therefore, the auditor can place reliance on the control over the authorisation of purchase invoices over HK$20,000. (Note: the auditor cannot conclude the sample is sufficient merely because the 4% sample deviation rate is below the tolerable rate of 8% — the sampling risk allowance must be added first.) 解題思路（繁中）: Attribute sampling 嘅結果係 binary：authorized / not authorized，所以 8/200 = 4% 就係個 rate。 關鍵一步：一定要將 sampling risk (3%) 加落 sample deviation rate ，得出 upper deviation rate 7%，先可以同 tolerable rate of deviation (8%) 比較。 7% ≤ 8% → 可以 rely 個 control。 伏位 1：直接攞 4% 同 8% 比就落結論 —— LP 明確話「the auditor cannot conclude that the sample is sufficient」除非加埋 sampling risk。 伏位 2：confidence level + sampling risk = 100%，所以 3% sampling risk 即 97% confidence level（本題冇問，但要識）。 伏位 3：如果 upper deviation rate 超過 tolerable rate，唔可以 ignore deviations —— 要增加 sample size、測試 alternative control 或修改 substantive procedures。 Rule Check: HKSA 530 (attribute sampling; tolerable rate of deviation); upper deviation rate per LP Illustrative Example 9 methodology (population/sample error rate + sampling risk) Common Trap（繁中）: 最衰格嘅錯係見 4% < 8% 就即刻寫「rely on the control」。考試一定要寫出 upper deviation rate 嘅計算同埋比較，先攞到 full marks。仲有：tolerable rate of deviation 係 test of control 專用，tolerable misstatement 先係 test of details 用 —— 唔好撈亂。

text: M8 Chapter 5: Sampling — Phase 3 Quiz Rules: Closed book · 15 minutes · 5 questions · Submit as 1. … 2. … 3. … 4. … 5. … — 超時如實申報 Question 1 (MCQ) During the audit of Harbourline Trading Ltd, the audit senior selects a sample of 60 purchase invoices and inspects each one for evidence of authorisation by the purchasing director, as required by the company's internal control policy. Which of the following statements BEST describes this test? A. It is a substantive test of details which provides direct evidence over the valuation of purchases. B. It is a test of control using attribute sampling, which provides indirect evidence over the financial statements. C. It is a substantive analytical procedure performed to identify plausible relationships in the purchases data. D. It is a test of details of balances which provides evidence over the completeness of trade payables. Question 2 (MCQ) Which of the following is an example of NON SAMPLING risk? A. The auditor concludes that controls are more effective than they actually are because the deviation rate in the sample is lower than the actual deviation rate in the population. B. The auditor concludes that a material misstatement does not exist because the sample selected was too small to be representative of the population. C. The auditor fails to detect a misstatement because an inappropriate audit procedure was applied to the items selected for testing. D. The auditor concludes that controls are less effective than they actually are, resulting in unnecessary additional substantive procedures. Question 3 (MCQ) The audit manager of Brightway Electronics Ltd wishes to reduce the sample size for the test of details of trade receivables, while keeping sampling risk at an acceptable level. Which of the following changes would, other things being equal, achieve this? A. Increasing the auditor's assessment of the risk of material misstatement of trade receivables. B. Increasing the amount of misstatement the auditor expects to find in the population. C. Making more use of other substantive procedures directed at the same assertion. D. Decreasing tolerable misstatement for the trade receivables population. Question 4 (Calculation / short answer) You are the audit senior of Manley Garments Ltd. The trade receivables population totals HK$48,000,000, from which you have selected a sample of balances totalling HK$6,000,000 for confirmation testing (a test of details). Your testing identifies overstatement errors totalling HK$360,000 in the sample. None of the errors is anomalous. Tolerable misstatement for trade receivables has been set at HK$2,500,000. Required: (a) Calculate the projected misstatement for the trade receivables population, showing your workings. (b) State, with reasons based on HKSA 530, whether the sample provides a reasonable basis for conclusions about the population, and identify ONE appropriate course of action available to the auditor if it does not. Question 5 (Calculation / short answer) You are testing the operating effectiveness of a control at Kwun Tong Logistics Ltd which requires every purchase invoice over HK$20,000 to be authorised by the finance director. You select a sample of 200 purchase invoices and find that 8 of them were not authorised. Your sampling parameters are: sampling risk 3%, tolerable rate of deviation 8%. Required: (a) Calculate the sample deviation rate and the upper deviation rate, showing your workings. (b) State, with reasons, whether the auditor can place reliance on this control. End of quiz. Do not look at the answers file until you have submitted all five answers.

text: M8 Chapter 6: Auditing IT Systems — Phase 1 速查表 + Phase 2 閃卡 Phase 1 速查表 Learning Objectives Explain how the complexities of computerised systems (including IT security risks) affect the audit of financial statements (HKSA 315 (Revised 2019), para. 25). Distinguish between general IT controls and application controls (input, processing, output, master file controls) and evaluate their impact on evidence accumulation. Distinguish manual controls from automated controls and explain when the auditor may audit only manual controls to assess control risk. Illustrate computer assisted auditing techniques (CAATs): the test data approach, audit software and parallel simulation. Describe the auditor's concerns when processing is outsourced to a service bureau (Type 1 / Type 2 reports) and the auditor's role in cybersecurity. 必背考點 A. Procedures（審計程序） 1. Understanding the IT system — HKSA 315 (Revised 2019), para. 25 The auditor MUST obtain an understanding of the entity's information system and communication relevant to the preparation of the financial statements, through risk assessment procedures : How transactions are initiated, recorded, processed, corrected, incorporated into the general ledger and reported in the financial statements; The accounting records, specific accounts and supporting records relating to information flows; The financial reporting process used to prepare the FS (including disclosures); The entity's resources, including the IT environment ; How the entity communicates significant financial reporting matters (within the entity; management ↔ TCWG; external parties); Evaluate whether the information system and communication appropriately support preparation of the FS per the applicable financial reporting framework. 2. Risk assessment procedures over general controls（防止未授權改動系統） LP Apply & Analyse 3 示範程序： Observe the client's procedures to confirm adequate segregation of duties ; Review the log of amendments for evidence changes were made by an appropriate individual; Attempt to log in using credentials of a non finance staff member (system should reject access); Check anti virus systems are in place and up to date; Review the backup policy for the accounting system; Inspect logs of access into the accounting system. 3. Procedures over backup and recovery（business continuity） Inquire of management / TCWG and inspect backup procedures — key check: backups taken off site ; Inspect disaster recovery procedures ; Inspect insurance contracts and maintenance agreements ; Inspect equipment protection against hazards (fire, flood). 4. Testing manual controls Manual controls = operated by employees (e.g. approvals, reconciliations, follow up of reconciling items, manual data entry controls such as pre numbering source documents). Manual controls are inherently riskier than automated controls (human error / override) → auditor selects a sample of transactions to confirm the control operated as expected; inconsistent operation → deviation/exception . Auditor may choose to audit only manual controls to assess control risk where appropriate (HKSA 315 (Revised 2019), Appendix 5, para. 1 acknowledges the mix of manual and automated elements varies with the entity's use of IT). B. Evidence（審計證據 — CAATs） 1. CAATs 總論 CAATs use computers to perform audit procedures but do NOT change the overall scope or objective of the audit . Two common types: audit software and test data . Uses: tests of details on transactions/balances; analytical review (e.g. gross profit margins vs prior year); designing sample sizes & sampling; reperforming calculations; tests of controls over general and application controls. Advantages: time efficiency; test larger sample sizes ; trace key controls/processes otherwise impossible manually; cost effective long term (if client doesn't change IT system). Disadvantages: initial setup cost & staff training time; possible incompatibility with client's system; risk of data corruption / loss of client's live data . 2. Test data（測試數據） Used for tests of controls (compliance tests) : auditor enters a sample of transactions into the client's system and compares results with pre determined results . Examples: process a sale taking a customer over its credit limit → system should reject; input a non existent customer account number → system should reject; enter an inappropriately large bonus for junior staff → payroll should flag exception; create a dummy employee to test mandatory fields. Inherent problems (6.5.1.1): Risk of corrupting the client's system / difficulty removing test data → use copy files instead of live data (must be satisfied copy files are genuine and virus free); Tests the system only at a specific point in time — processing at other times of the period is not covered. 3. Audit software（審計軟件） Used to carry out substantive procedures to detect material misstatement (general or customised packages). Uses: analytical procedures (AR/AP days, year on year comparisons); designing & extracting samples ; reperforming calculations (e.g. recasting inventory valuation report); checking file data (e.g. invoice prices agree to sales master file); preparing confirmation letters ; scanning files for large/unusual items and completeness of document ranges. Reduces detection risk (gives more resources to analyse data and investigate unusual items). ⚠️ It does NOT reduce inherent risk or control risk — those are not under the auditor's control. Consider requesting client permission before extracting data; may need to reference data extraction in the engagement letter . 4. Parallel simulation（平行模擬） Auditor creates programmed procedures to duplicate part of the client's IT system ; takes live data processed by the client's system and reprocesses it through the auditor's version ; compares outputs. Advantages: facilitates substantive testing of balances; evidence on controls in application programs; tests accuracy of large volumes; focuses attention on differences. Disadvantage: expensive to implement , especially for complex calculations. 5. PCs as an audit tool Speed and accuracy; embedded checks identify inordinate transactions/balances; detect calculation errors. ⚠️ Using PCs does NOT remove the need for normal audit procedures (e.g. verifying receivables valuation, payables completeness still required). C. Ethics（專業道德 — Internal Audit 角色） Internal audit (IA) is part of the entity's system of internal control and may evaluate IT controls. IA CANNOT implement internal controls — doing so creates a self review threat (reviewing their own work) and destroys independence/objectivity. IA can only recommend improvements and test operating effectiveness of controls implemented by management. External auditors may choose to rely on IA's work (see Chapter 4 for the detailed criteria). D. Report modifications（報告修改 — IT 失效嘅後果） Ineffective general controls → application controls unlikely to be effective → auditor places little/no reliance on the IT system → adopt a more substantive approach (risk of material misstatement likely high). 呢個係 extent of testing 嘅問題， 唔係自動 modify opinion 。 Inadequate backup / loss of accounting data → auditor may be unable to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence → if so serious that the auditor cannot form an opinion → disclaimer of opinion (see Chapter 9). Disaster without continuity controls may threaten going concern → disclosure required; if FS prepared on going concern basis but basis inappropriate → modified opinion (see Chapter 9). Cybersecurity breach / unauthorised access may cause material misstatement and is a fraud risk factor — but does NOT automatically lead to a disclaimer; unmodified opinion still possible if reasonable assurance obtained. 易混淆概念對比 Table 1: General IT Controls vs Application Controls General IT Controls Application Controls Definition Controls over the environment within which the computer system is developed, maintained and operated Controls operating within the business application to ensure data is processed completely, accurately, validly and timely Scope Pervasive — affect ALL application systems Specific to individual transaction processing (e.g. sales, payroll, purchases) Examples Program change control; logical access controls (passwords, user ID); backup & recovery; systems development controls; IT operations controls; physical access to data centre Batch total checks; sequence checks; arithmetic checks; range checks; existence checks; authorisation checks; exception reporting; check digit / hash total verification LP reference HKSA 315 (Revised 2019) App. 5 para. 18 (risks from IT); App. 6 para. 2 (examples: access management, change management, IT operations) LP §6.4 (input / processing / output / master file controls) 點樣分辨 問自己：呢個控制係咪「成個 IT 環境」都受影響？係 → general。只係針對某個 application 嘅 data input/processing/output → application 考試伏位：考官審計順序係 先 general 後 application —— general controls ineffective ⇒ application controls generally ineffective ⇒ more substantive approach。Password/user ID 屬 general (logical access) ，唔好當 application control Table 2: Test Data vs Audit Software vs Parallel Simulation Test Data Audit Software Parallel Simulation Purpose Tests of controls (compliance tests) Substantive procedures (detect material misstatement) Both: substantive testing + evidence on application controls Mechanism Auditor inputs fictitious transactions into client's system; compares results with pre determined results Auditor's own software interrogates client's real data files (analyse, sample, recalculate) Auditor reprocesses client's live data through auditor's replica of part of the system; compares outputs Data used Auditor created data (valid + invalid) Client's actual data Client's live data, run through both systems Risk reduced / key issue Does not directly reduce detection risk; tests whether controls operate Reduces detection risk (larger coverage, faster analysis) Expensive to implement; best for complex calculations 點樣分辨 口訣： Test data 測 control，audit software 做 substantive 。見到「input dummy/fictitious data to see if system rejects」= test data；見到「extract / recalculate / scan client's file」= audit software；見到「reprocess live data through auditor's version & compare」= parallel simulation 考試伏位：(1) audit software reduces detection risk only ，唔可以話佢 reduce inherent/control risk；(2) test data 兩大 inherent problems = corrupt client data + point in time only；(3) CAATs 唔會改變 audit scope/objective Phase 2 閃卡 Card 1 Front: According to HKSA 315 (Revised 2019) para. 25, what must the auditor understand about the entity's information system relevant to financial reporting? Back: How transactions are initiated, recorded, processed, corrected, incorporated into the general ledger and reported in the FS The accounting records, specific accounts and supporting records The financial reporting process (including disclosures) The entity's resources, including the IT environment How significant matters are communicated (within entity; management ↔ TCWG; external parties) Evaluate whether the system supports FS preparation per the applicable framework 💬 白話解釋：呢段係 risk assessment 嘅基本功——核數師要由「交易點樣入系統、點樣流到落 FS」成條鏈都要明白，仲要評估個系統撐唔撐到份報表。考試常見伏位係以為淨係要識 IT，其實連 communication 同 evaluation 都係 para. 25 要求。 Card 2 Front: Define "general IT controls" and give FOUR examples. Back: Definition: controls over the environment within which the computer system is developed, maintained and operated, and within which application controls operate Examples: program change control; logical access controls (user ID/password); backup and recovery; systems development controls; IT operations controls; data and program security They have a pervasive effect on all application systems 💬 白話解釋：General controls 係「大環境」嘅控制，唔係針對個別交易。記住審計次序：general controls 差 → application controls 都靠唔住 → 唯有做多啲 substantive procedures。 Card 3 Front: What are the FOUR categories of application controls, and what is each designed to ensure? Back: Input controls — data input is accurate (e.g. check digit verification, hash totals, input verification by second person) Processing controls — data is processed correctly and files updated timely (e.g. re entry verification of rejected data, parallel run of new system) Output controls — output is correct and distributed only to authorised individuals (e.g. batch control totals, exception report review) Controls over master file information — standing data protected from unauthorised changes (passwords, logs of amendments, segregation of duties) 💬 白話解釋：跟住數據流向記：Input → Processing → Output，外加 master file（standing data 如薪金率、客戶 credit limit）。Master file 俾人亂改 = 長期性錯誤，係 auditor 嘅 major concern。 Card 4 Front: Distinguish between manual controls and automated controls. Which is inherently riskier and why? Back: Automated control : built into the IT system (e.g. system rejects customer over credit limit) Manual control : operated by an employee (e.g. sales director overrides a system rejection; approvals; reconciliations) Manual controls are inherently riskier — susceptible to human error, erroneous or fraudulent operation, and override HKSA 315 (Revised 2019) App. 5 para. 2: automated controls may be more reliable because they cannot be as easily bypassed, ignored or overridden, and are less prone to simple errors; more effective for high volume recurring transactions 💬 白話解釋：記住「人會攰、會呃、會撳錯掣；機器唔會」——但機器可以俾人 override，所以兩者都要 test。Manual control 要靠 sample testing 去 confirm 有持續運作。 Card 5 Front: What is the "test data" approach, and what are its TWO inherent problems? Back: Test data: auditor enters a sample of transactions (valid and invalid) into the client's IT system and compares the results with pre determined results — a test of control Example: input a sale taking a customer over its credit limit → system should reject Inherent problems: 1. Risk of corrupting the client's system / live data → use copy files (verified genuine and virus free) 2. Tests the system only at a specific point in time — other periods not covered 💬 白話解釋：Test data = 擺啲假交易落客個系統度，睇佢擋唔擋到。兩個弱點：污糟咗人哋啲 live data 點算（所以用 copy files）；同埋你只係測嗰一刻，唔代表成年都 work。 Card 6 Front: List FIVE procedures an auditor can perform using audit software, and state which component of audit risk it reduces. Back: Analytical procedures (e.g. AR/AP days, current vs prior year comparisons) Designing and extracting samples for substantive testing Reperforming calculations (e.g. recasting the inventory valuation report) Checking data accuracy (e.g. invoice prices agree to sales master file) Preparing confirmation letters ; scanning files for gaps in document sequences and large/unusual items Reduces detection risk only — inherent risk and control risk are not within the auditor's control 💬 白話解釋：Audit software 係幫你「查數」——搵 sample、重計、做 ratio。考試經典伏位：佢 reduce detection risk， 唔係 inherent/control risk（RoMM = IR × CR，呢啲係 client 嘅嘢，auditor 控制唔到）。 Card 7 Front: What are a Type 1 report and a Type 2 report in the context of a service bureau (third party computer processing company)? Back: Type 1 report : focuses on the description and design of controls at the third party Type 2 report : also covers the operating effectiveness of those controls Obtained with the client's permission; auditor may also discuss controls directly with the third party (backups, access rights, cybersecurity, standing data changes) 💬 白話解釋：口訣「 Type 1 = 設計，Type 2 = 設計 + 運作成效 」。Client 外咗包 IT 俾人，auditor 唔可以求其信——要攞 service auditor report 或者直接同 third party 傾。 Card 8 Front: Explain the audit consequences if a client has inadequate backup and recovery procedures and accounting data is irrecoverably lost. Back: Auditor may be unable to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence over areas of the FS If so serious that an opinion cannot be formed → disclaimer of opinion Lack of continuity controls after a disaster may also threaten going concern → disclosure; if going concern basis inappropriate but used → modified opinion Risk assessment must reflect inadequate backup → more substantive approach likely 💬 白話解釋：數據冇咗 = 冇證據 = 出唔到意見 → disclaimer。呢個係 evidence insufficiency 嘅極端例子。但記住：backup 不足本身唔會即刻觸發 disclaimer，要睇實際係咪失去咗證據。 本章急救詞彙 EN Term 繁中白話 English Model Sentence General IT controls 籠統嘅 IT 環境控制，影響晒所有應用系統 "General IT controls include program change control, logical access controls, and backup and recovery controls." Application controls 針對個別應用系統嘅輸入/處理/輸出控制 "Batch total checks are application controls that ensure supplier invoices are input completely and accurately." Logical access control 用 user ID + password 限制邊個可以入邊個範圍 "A logical access control requires user identification, checks authenticity, and restricts access to authorised areas only." CAATs (computer assisted auditing techniques) 用電腦幫手做審計程序嘅技術 "CAATs do not change the overall scope or objective of the audit." Test data 擺假數落客個系統，測 control 擋唔擋到 "The auditor used test data to confirm that the system rejects sales orders exceeding a customer's credit limit." Audit software 用核數師自己嘅軟件查客戶真數據 "Audit software was used to reperform the inventory valuation and extract a sample of trade receivables." Parallel simulation 用核數師版本嘅系統 reprocess 客戶 live data 再對 output "Parallel simulation involves reprocessing the client's live data through the auditor's own program and comparing the outputs." Service bureau 第三方電腦處理公司（外判 IT） "Where a service bureau processes the client's data, the auditor may request a Type 2 report on the operating effectiveness of controls."

title: M8 Chapter 6: Auditing IT Systems — Phase 3 Answers
headings: M8 Chapter 6: Auditing IT Systems — Phase 3 Answers
excerpt: M8 Chapter 6: Auditing IT Systems — Phase 3 Answers Q1 — Answer: B Model Answer (EN): This is audit software used to perform a substantive procedure . The audit…
text: M8 Chapter 6: Auditing IT Systems — Phase 3 Answers Q1 — Answer: B Model Answer (EN): This is audit software used to perform a substantive procedure . The auditor is interrogating the client's actual, complete data file (all 48,000 real invoices) using the firm's own software to reperform a calculation — one of the listed uses of audit software (reperforming calculations such as recasting reports; ensuring information in files is correct). Its purpose is to detect material misstatement in the invoiced amounts, not to test whether a control operates. Because the entire population is tested, detection risk is reduced. 解題思路（繁中）: 關鍵字眼：「extract the client's complete sales invoice file 」+「 recalculate 」→ 用緊客戶真實數據做 re performance = audit software 做 substantive procedure。 A (test data) 錯：test data 係擺「假交易」落個系統測 control 有冇運作（test of controls），呢度冇輸入任何 auditor created data，而係查真數。 C (parallel simulation) 錯：parallel simulation 係核數師建立自己版本嘅系統去 reprocess 客戶 live data 再比較兩個系統嘅 output ；呢度只係重計 discount，冇複製成個處理程序。 D 錯在「risk assessment procedure」：audit software 重計全個 population 係 substantive procedure（detect material misstatement），唔係用嚟 identify/assess risks。 考試伏位：CAATs 大分類 = test data（tests of controls）vs audit software（substantive procedures） ，呢個係 panelist 點名嘅 MCQ 弱項（Jun 2025: key features of different CAATs）。 Rule Check: LP §6.5.2 Audit Software (uses: reperform calculations; substantive procedures; reduces detection risk); §6.5.1 Test Data (tests of control); §6.5.3 Parallel Simulation. Common Trap（繁中）: 見到「用電腦做」就亂揀 CAAT 名。記住口訣： test data 測 control（放假數）；audit software 做 substantive（查真數） 。 Q2 — Answer: C Model Answer (EN): C is a range check — an application control ensuring that data input stays within a reasonable range (here, overtime hours). Application controls operate within the business application to ensure data is processed completely, accurately, validly and in a timely manner. Options A, B and D are all general IT controls : A is program change control (change management process), B is backup and recovery, and D is physical access control — they concern the overall IT environment in which applications operate. 解題思路（繁中）: 分辨口訣：「呢個控制係咪只針對某個 application 嘅 data 輸入/處理/輸出？」C 係 payroll 系統入面嘅 range check （LP §6.4 明列 application controls 例子之一）→ application control。 A = program change control（HKSA 315 (Revised 2019) App. 6 para. 2(b) change management process）→ general。 B = backup and recovery（App. 6 para. 2(c) IT operations；LP §6.3.3）→ general。 D = physical access to data centre（App. 6 para. 2(a) physical access；LP 明言 physical access may be used to override other controls）→ general。 考試伏位：Pilot paper Q2a/2b 同 Q37 都考 general vs application 分類 —— 見到 backup / program change / physical access / network security 呢啲「環境級」字眼就係 general controls。 Rule Check: HKSA 315 (Revised 2019), Appendix 6, para. 2 (examples of general IT controls); LP §6.4 (application controls: range checks, batch totals, sequence checks etc.). Common Trap（繁中）: 以為「電腦自動做嘅」就係 application control。其實 automated ≠ application：logical access（password）係 automated 但屬 general control；而 application controls 亦可以係 manual（例如人手 batch total check）。 Q3 — Answer: B Model Answer (EN): If general controls are ineffective, it is unlikely that application controls will be effective, because general controls have a pervasive effect on all application systems. The auditor will therefore place little (if any) reliance on the IT system and carry out a more substantive approach to auditing the financial statements, since the risk of material misstatement is likely to be high. A disclaimer of opinion is not automatic — it would only arise if the auditor were unable to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence. Internal audit cannot implement controls (self review threat). 解題思路（繁中）: 呢條考 LP Key Learning Point： general controls ineffective ⇒ application controls generally ineffective ⇒ little/no reliance ⇒ more substantive approach 。B 完全跟返呢個邏輯鏈。 A 錯：application controls「睇落設計得好」都冇用，因為佢哋喺一個失效嘅 IT 環境底下運作，auditor 唔可以靠佢哋嚟減 substantive testing。 C 錯：disclaimer 係「攞唔到 sufficient appropriate evidence 兼且影響 pervasive」先出；general controls 差只係推高 RMM，仲可以靠 substantive procedures 補救 —— 唔係自動 disclaimer 。 D 錯：internal audit 唔可以 implement internal controls（self review threat，會變成 review 自己嘅嘢），佢哋只可以 recommend。 考試伏位：呢題同時踩兩個 panelist 弱項 —— control risk 同 substantive procedures 嘅關係（Jun 2023 Q1(e)），同 internal audit 嘅 self review threat。 Rule Check: LP §6.3 Key Learning Point (ineffective general controls → little reliance → more substantive approach); HKSA 315 (Revised 2019), Appendix 5, para. 18 (risks arising from use of IT); LP §6.1.2 (IA self review threat). Common Trap（繁中）: 揀 C —— 以為 control 壞咗就一定要 modify opinion。記住： control weakness 影響 audit approach（做幾多 substantive work），唔直接等於 opinion modification 。Opinion 層面要睇最終攞唔攞到證據。 Q4 — Answer: B Model Answer (EN): A Type 2 report covers both the description and design of controls at the third party and the operating effectiveness of those controls. A Type 1 report focuses only on the description and design of controls, so it would not provide evidence that the payroll controls operated effectively throughout the year. Options C and D are not service auditor reports: an engagement letter references may be needed for the auditor's own data extraction, and a management representation letter does not provide independent evidence over the service bureau's controls. 解題思路（繁中）: 口訣： Type 1 = 設計（design）；Type 2 = 設計 + 運作成效（operating effectiveness） 。題目要求「not only designed but also operated effectively」→ Type 2。 A 錯：Type 1 只講 design，答唔到「成年有冇真係運作」。 C 錯：engagement letter 加 data extraction 條款係 auditor 自己用 audit software 抽客戶數據嘅安排，同 service bureau report 無關。 D 錯：management representation letter 唔係獨立證據，而且 LP 冇提及向 third party 攞 representation letter 嚟評估其 controls；正確做法係攞 Type 1/Type 2 report 或（經 client 同意）直接同 third party 討論。 考試伏位：「Type 1 vs Type 2」係 LP Knowledge Check 都有嘅經典位，見到 operating effectiveness 呢兩個字就揀 Type 2。 Rule Check: LP §6.7 (Type 1 report: description and design of controls; Type 2 report: also covers operating effectiveness; auditor may discuss controls with the third party with client's permission). Common Trap（繁中）: 倒轉咗兩個 report —— 記住數字越大、涵蓋越多：Type 2 包含 Type 1 嘅內容再加 operating effectiveness。 Q5 — Answer: 見 Model Answer Model Answer (EN): (a) Disadvantages of CAATs (any two): High initial setup costs and time spent in the first year of use. Audit staff require training in the use of CAATs (adding to initial costs). The auditor's software may not be compatible with the client's IT system. Risk of data corruption or loss of the client's live data (strong controls needed to prevent this). Cost effectiveness depends on the client not changing its IT system . (b) Inherent problems with test data (any two): Risk that the client's system/live data is corrupted or that test data cannot easily be removed — mitigated by using copy files (which must be genuine and virus free). Test data only tests the system at a specific point in time ; processing errors at other times in the reporting period may not be detected. Clients may be nervous/unwilling to allow the auditor to input data into their live system. 解題思路（繁中）: (a) 同 (b) 唔好撈亂：CAATs disadvantages 係「成本、培訓、兼容性、數據損毀風險」；test data inherent problems 係「污糟 live data（用 copy files 解決）+ point in time 限制」。「point in time」係 test data 獨有 嘅弱點，唔好寫落 CAATs disadvantages 度。 答「do not change audit scope/objective」係 唔啱 嘅 —— 嗰句係 CAATs 嘅特性（中性陳述），唔係 disadvantage。 考試伏位：Jun 2025 panelist report 特別點名考生唔識 CAATs 嘅 key features；呢類「list TWO」題型係 Section B 最常見嘅 command word（List），每點一分，寫短 bullet 就得，唔使長篇。 Rule Check: LP §6.5 (CAATs advantages and disadvantages); §6.5.1.1 (Inherent Problems with Test Data: corruption of client data → copy files; point in time testing only). Common Trap（繁中）: 兩 part 答案交叉寫（例如將「training costs」寫入 test data 嘅 inherent problems）。Test data 嘅 inherent problems 係 技術性限制 （corruption + point in time），成本問題屬 CAATs 整體。

excerpt: M8 Chapter 6: Auditing IT Systems — Phase 3 Quiz Rules: Closed book · 15 minutes · 5 questions · Submit as 1. … 2. … 3. … 4. … 5. … — 超時如實申報 Q1 (MCQ, scenario) …
text: M8 Chapter 6: Auditing IT Systems — Phase 3 Quiz Rules: Closed book · 15 minutes · 5 questions · Submit as 1. … 2. … 3. … 4. … 5. … — 超時如實申報 Q1 (MCQ, scenario) You are the audit senior of Beacon Toys Limited, a toy wholesaler whose sales and receivables are fully computerised. You want to obtain evidence that the invoicing system calculates the early settlement discount correctly on every sales invoice issued during the year . Using your firm's own software, you extract the client's complete sales invoice file and recalculate the discount on each of the 48,000 invoices, comparing your results to the amounts actually charged. Which computer assisted auditing technique are you using, and what type of procedure is it? A. Test data approach — a test of controls B. Audit software — a substantive procedure C. Parallel simulation — a test of controls D. Audit software — a risk assessment procedure Q2 (MCQ) Which of the following is an application control ? A. Requiring all program changes to be logged and authorised by a responsible official before migration to the production environment B. Storing a copy of the daily backup of the accounting system at an off site location C. The payroll system rejecting an overtime hours entry of 320 hours for a single month because it falls outside a pre set acceptable range D. Restricting physical access to the data centre to authorised IT personnel only Q3 (MCQ, scenario) During the audit of Harbour Freight Limited, you conclude that the company's general IT controls are ineffective : ex employees still have active login credentials, there is no log of program changes, and backups have not been tested for over a year. The application controls over the sales cycle (batch totals and sequence checks) appear to be well designed. What is the MOST likely consequence for your audit approach? A. Place full reliance on the application controls because they are well designed, and reduce substantive testing accordingly B. Place little (if any) reliance on the IT system and adopt a more substantive approach to auditing the financial statements C. Immediately issue a disclaimer of opinion because general controls are ineffective D. Ask internal audit to implement new general controls during the audit so that reliance can be placed on them Q4 (MCQ, scenario) Norton Logistics Limited outsources the processing of its entire payroll to CompServe Limited, a third party computer processing company. With Norton's permission, you contact CompServe to assess whether you can rely on the payroll data. You ask CompServe's service auditor for a report that addresses not only how the payroll controls are designed , but also whether those controls operated effectively throughout the year. Which report should you request? A. A Type 1 report B. A Type 2 report C. An engagement letter referencing data extraction D. A management representation letter from CompServe Q5 (Short answer) (a) State TWO disadvantages of using computer assisted auditing techniques (CAATs). (b) State TWO inherent problems with using the test data approach on a client's computerised system. (Answer each part in no more than two short bullet points.)
