text: Exam Lens Briefing — HKICPA QP Module 10: Business & Company Law Purpose: Intelligence briefing for quiz item writers (chapter level OTQ quizzes). Based on the Pilot Paper (2019, CBE), Jun 2024 / Jun 2025 / Jun 2026 question + answer papers, and Panelists' Reports for Jun 2024, Dec 2024, Jun 2025, Dec 2025, Jun 2026. 1. Exam Structure Duration: 3 hours (180 minutes), single section. Format: 100% written questions — no MCQ, no separate case study section . All questions compulsory. Current format (Jun 2024 → Jun 2026): SIX questions, 100 marks , all compulsory. Jun 2024: Q1 15 / Q2 10 / Q3 15 / Q4 20 / Q5 25 / Q6 15. Jun 2025: Q1 10 / Q2 20 / Q3 10 / Q4 20 / Q5 20 / Q6 20. Jun 2026: Q1 15 / Q2 15 / Q3 15 / Q4 25 / Q5 20 / Q6 10. Format change history: The 2019 Pilot Paper had SEVEN compulsory questions (40/10/15/15/10/5/5) with one dominant 40 mark integrated mega case. From at least Jun 2024 onwards the paper standardised to six questions with no single question above 25 marks — flatter mark distribution, broader topic coverage per sitting. Quiz writers should calibrate to the 6 question era, not the pilot. Timing discipline built into the paper: every question states "X marks – approximately Y minutes" at roughly 1.8 minutes per mark (5 marks ≈ 9 min; 15 marks ≈ 27 min; 25 marks ≈ 45 min). Question anatomy (post 2024 papers): each question = short "Case background" scenario (150–350 words) + 1–3 sub requirements (a)/(b)/(c), each worth 2–15 marks. Sub parts routinely mix topics within one scenario (e.g. Jun 2026 Q2 = employment + anti corruption + long service payment; Jun 2024 Q4 = agency + negligence). Verbs used: "Analyse whether…" (application marks), "Explain…" (knowledge marks), "Explain … and analyse whether…" (hybrid). Roughly half the marks on any paper are "analyse" marks tied to the scenario facts. Open book reality: M10 is the only open book paper at Associate Level ; delivered as CBE on a BYOD basis (candidates bring their own laptop). The Jun 2026 paper is structured with an explicit "Answer Area" under each sub question, consistent with typed CBE responses. Practical implications confirmed by the answers/reports: Suggested answers cite precise Ordinance sections (e.g. s.9(3) PBO Cap.201; s.31R EO Cap.57; s.24 SOGO Cap.26; s.177(1) CWUMPO Cap.32; ss.723–727 CO Cap.622) and named cases with year/citation (Roscorla v Thomas [1842], Salomon v Salomon [1897], Gilford Motor v Horne [1933]) — open book means candidates are expected to locate and deploy authority, not memorise it, but the exam still rewards accurate citation. Panelists repeatedly warn that candidates who "write what they know" (i.e. transcribe notes/textbook) instead of applying law to the scenario score poorly — open book is not copy book. Suggested answers carry the standing caveat: "longer than what candidates are expected to give… credit will be awarded for valid answers not fully covered." 2. Question Style Scenario based throughout. Every question embeds the law in a named character fact pattern ("Tommy is an artist…", "Billy was employed as Purchasing Manager…"). Pure bookwork questions do not appear; even "explain" parts are framed as advising a character. IRAC pattern expected answers. Model answers consistently follow: Issue ("This question required candidates to discuss X") → Rule stated with authority → Application to the named facts → Conclusion (e.g. "Therefore, Elegant Goods is not bound to give Tommy the free gift"). Sub conclusions are decisive and one sided when facts are clear. Citation density expected: Statute first: pinpoint sections with chapter numbers — Employment Ordinance (Cap.57), Prevention of Bribery Ordinance (Cap.201), Sale of Goods Ordinance (Cap.26), Companies Ordinance (Cap.622), Companies (Winding Up and Miscellaneous Provisions) Ordinance (Cap.32), Misrepresentation Ordinance (Cap.284), Organized and Serious Crimes Ordinance (Cap.455). A 5 mark answer typically cites 1–2 sections; a 15 mark answer several sections across a statutory scheme. Case law: landmark/common law governed areas (contract, tort, veil piercing, unfair prejudice) expect named cases — often with full citation in model answers (e.g. Hong Kong Fir Shipping [1962], Krell v Henry [1903], Aluminium Industrie Vaassen v Romalpa [1976], Re Taiwa Land Investment [1981] HKLR 297, Wong Man Yin v Ricacorp [2003]). Panelists single out missing case citation as a weakness even when the conclusion was right (Dec 2024 Q2(b); Jun 2026 Q5(a)). Hybrid explain+analyse parts are the norm (e.g. "explain … and analyse whether…"), so a quiz stem that only tests recall under represents exam demand. Issue spotting is the discriminator: the most common failure mode across all five reports is misidentifying the legal issue (e.g. past consideration misread as misrepresentation or promissory estoppel; revocation of offer not spotted; ratification misread as estoppel; negligent misstatement answered as ordinary negligence; deregistration answered as liquidation). Cross topic scenarios are standard — one storyline can span 2–3 LP chapters, and sub parts explicitly signpost the syllabus area ("In relation to agency law…", "In relation to the tort of negligence…"). 3. Topic Frequency Map (marks % of paper, from Panelists' Reports) LP Ch. Topic area Jun 24 Dec 24 Jun 25 Dec 25 Jun 26 Typical 8–11, 13 Company Law (incl. charges, dormant status, deregistration, veil, unfair prejudice, winding up) 30% 30% 30% 30% 35% 30–35% — dominant every sitting 2–3 Law of Contract (+ consumer/misrepresentation where merged) 15% 15% 15% 15% 15% 15% — fixed anchor 12 Law for Public Companies / listed co. regulation (SFO disclosure, insider dealing, listing rules) 10% 10% 10% 10% 10% 10% — appears every sitting 4 Tort & Negligence (elements, negligent misstatement, vicarious liability, novus actus) 10% 10% 10% 15% 10% 10–15% 5 Agency (creation, ratification, apparent authority, fiduciary duties, undisclosed principal) 10% 5% 10% 10% 10% 5–10% 7 Employment (status test, implied duties, summary dismissal, long service payment) 9% 10% 10% 10% 10% ~10% 6 AML (OSCO Cap.455) + Prevention of Bribery (PBO Cap.201) 6% 5% 10% 5% 5% 5–10% 1 HK Legal System & Regulatory Bodies (court jurisdiction, precedent) — 5% 5% 5% — 0–5% (small, periodic) 2–3 Consumer Protection (separately itemised) 10% 10% — — 5% 0–10% (alternates) Specific sub topics actually examined (Jun 24 – Jun 26): Ch.2/3 Contract: discharge of contract & frustration (J24 Q1, D25 Q2), retention of title/Romalpa (J24 Q2), passing of property & nemo dat + s.24 SOGO exception (D24 Q2, J26 Q3(c)), consideration sufficient not adequate (J26 Q1(a)), revocation of offer (J26 Q1(b)), past consideration (D24 Q1(b), J26 Q1(c)), offer vs invitation to treat (D24 Q1(a)), misrepresentation + remedies (J25 Q2). Ch.4 Tort: negligence elements (J24 Q4(b), D24 Q3(b), D25 Q3(c)), negligent misstatement/valuer liability (J25 Q3, J26 Q4(a)), vicarious liability (D24 Q3(c)), novus actus interveniens (D25 Q3(d)). Ch.5 Agency: creation of agency (J24 Q4(a)(i), D25 Q3(a), J26 Q3(a)), ratification (J24 Q4(a)(ii)), apparent authority (D25 Q3(b), J26 Q3(b)), fiduciary duties/secret commission (J25 Q4(a)), undisclosed principal (D24 Q4(a)). Ch.6 AML/PBO: PBO s.9 offences — agent accepting advantage, s.9(3) false documents (J24 Q3(b)(c), J25 Q4(b), D25 Q1(b), J26 Q2(b)); OSCO money laundering (D24 Q3(a)). Ch.7 Employment: implied duties of employee (J24 Q3(a), D25 Q1(a)), employment status employee vs contractor (J25 Q1), summary dismissal s.9 EO (J26 Q2(a)), long service payment s.31R EO (J26 Q2(c)). Ch.8 Incorporation: separate legal entity & veil lifting (J25 Q6), private→public conversion (J25 Q5(a)). Ch.9 Internal Administration: directors' types & fiduciary duties (D24 Q5). Ch.10 Contentious Matters: unfair prejudice ss.723–727 CO (J26 Q5(a)), just & equitable winding up s.177(1) CWUMPO (J26 Q5(b)(c)). Ch.11 Capital & Financing: debentures, fixed & floating charges (J24 Q5(a), J26 Q4(b)), prospectus (Pilot Q6). Ch.12 Listed/Public: SFO disclosure of interests incl. deemed spouse interests (D24 Q6, J26 Q6), insider dealing (J24 Q6(a), D25 Q6), Main Board listing requirements (J25 Q5(b)). Ch.13 Winding up/cessation: dormant status (J24 Q5(b), D25 Q4(a)), deregistration (J24 Q5(c), D25 Q4(b)), voluntary winding up of solvent company (D25 Q4(c)). Ch.1 Legal System: court/tribunal jurisdiction by claim amount (J25 Q2(c), D24 Q4(b), D25 Q1(c)), precedent (Pilot Q2). Partnership (limited partnership status change, joint & several liability) appears periodically (J24 Q6(b), D25 Q5) — note it sits outside the 13 chapter LP list but is examinable. Takeaway for quiz weighting: Company Law (Ch.8–11,13) + Contract (Ch.2–3) ≈ half the paper. Public companies/listed regulation is guaranteed ~10%. Every other area rotates at 5–15%. 4. Panelist Reported Weaknesses (by session) Recurring across ALL five sessions: Candidates write out everything they know on the topic instead of identifying and answering the specific issue ("write what they know" syndrome — fatal in an open book paper). Insufficient application of legal principles to the scenario facts; conclusions without analysis. Missing Ordinance section references and/or case citations even when the conclusion is correct. Shallow syllabus coverage — candidates bank on 2–3 "popular" topics and collapse on anything less common. Some candidates leave parts unanswered (time management at the back of the paper — Q5/Q6 suffer). Jun 2024: Q4(a)(ii): ratification widely misidentified as agency by estoppel. Q6(a)(ii): insider dealing analysis only fair; some blank (time pressure on last question). Q6(b): partnership status change registration requirements poorly known; answers confused with limited partner liability / LP registration. Q5(c): deregistration misidentified as liquidation. Q1(b)(c): frustration issue missed. Q3(c): PBO s.9(3) false documents offence — answers duplicated Q3(b). Dec 2024: Q1(a): online advertisement wrongly treated as an offer (invitation to treat issue missed). Q1(b): past consideration issue missed; irrelevant offer/misrepresentation discussion. Q2(b): correct conclusion but no supporting case law. Q3(c): vicarious liability not understood — generic employment law answers. Q4(a): undisclosed principal unknown — candidates defaulted to creation of agency. Q5(c)(d)(e): directors' fiduciary duties, breach, and remedies discussed only superficially. Q6(b): disclosure of interest breach consequences under explained. Jun 2025: Q2(a)(b): misrepresentation types recited but not applied ; remedies likewise under applied. Q3: negligent misstatement confused with ordinary negligence. Q4(b): PBO criminal offence — very few cited sections or case law. Q6(b)(c): lifting the corporate veil — overall poor; issue not identified; some blanks. Q6(c): separate legal/beneficial ownership of company assets not understood. Dec 2025: Q2(b): frustration — candidates could not deploy case information in argument; disappointing. Q3(b): apparent authority — issue spotted but application weak. Q3(d): novus actus interveniens — poor grasp of the concept. Q4(c): voluntary winding up of a solvent non defunct company — unsatisfactory. Q5(b): joint and several liability of partners not understood. Q1(b): wrong PBO subsection cited (s.9(1) instead of s.9(2)) — precision matters. Jun 2026: Q1(b): revocation of offer — issue missed by many; some merely copied the scenario back. Q1(c): past consideration misidentified as misrepresentation / promissory estoppel. Q2(b): anti corruption misidentified as money laundering. Q2(c): long service payment — incomplete grounds (e.g. "illness" without "certified permanently unfit"). Q3(b): apparent authority wrongly applied to a ratification style fact pattern. Q3(c): nemo dat stated but the s.24 SOGO exception not applied. Q5(a): CO sections and case law for unfair prejudice not cited by all. Q5(c): just and equitable winding up — issue/case law not correctly identified. Q6(a): director/CEO vs shareholder disclosure obligations conflated. 5. Difficulty Calibration Guide (for 5 question chapter OTQ quizzes) What "exam standard" means for M10: The exam is 100% scenario based written answers; there are no MCQs in the real paper. An OTQ quiz is therefore a training proxy — it should test the same issue spotting + rule selection + application skills, not just recall. An "exam standard" item = one where a candidate who merely copied their open book notes would get it wrong , and a candidate who spotted the correct issue and matched the correct rule/exception gets it right. Difficulty tiers observed in the real paper (use as anchor): Easy (candidates "performed well"): straight recall of a popular framework — creation of agency, elements of negligence, summary dismissal grounds, sufficient not adequate consideration, dormant status, disclosure thresholds. ≈ 40–50% of exam marks. Medium ("fair"): application of a known rule to facts with one twist — ratification vs estoppel, PBO s.9(2) vs s.9(3), apparent authority limits, misrepresentation remedies. ≈ 30–40%. Hard ("poor"): less popular sub topic OR multi layer analysis — past consideration exceptions, novus actus interveniens, voluntary winding up of solvent company, veil lifting in family property context, just and equitable winding up, undisclosed principal, vicarious liability. ≈ 15–25%. Recommended mix for a 5 item chapter quiz: 2 × easy (rule recall + one step identification; tests the core framework of the chapter). 2 × medium (mini scenario, 2–4 sentences, requiring selection of the correct rule/exception and the correct conclusion; distractors = the misidentifications panelists actually reported, e.g. estoppel when answer is ratification; s.9(1) when answer is s.9(2)). 1 × hard (longer mini scenario or a less popular sub topic; requires recognising the issue before the rule — mirror the paper's "poor performance" items for that chapter). Item writing rules derived from the exam: Every medium/hard item must be a mini scenario with named parties , matching the paper's voice ("In relation to agency law…"). Distractors should be plausible neighbouring doctrines (the exact confusions in Section 4), not random wrong answers. Where the chapter is statute driven, at least one item should test pinpoint section knowledge (correct Ordinance + section number), reflecting the exam's citation expectations. For case law driven chapters (contract, tort, veil, unfair prejudice), at least one item should test which landmark case establishes which principle . Calibrate time: an exam standard medium OTQ ≈ 2–3 minutes; a 5 item quiz should be completable in ~12–15 minutes (proportional to the paper's 1.8 min/mark pace). Never make "copy from the book" sufficient — if the correct answer is a verbatim LP sentence with no application step, it is below exam standard for medium/hard items. 6. DO NOT CLONE List Past paper questions below are reserved for student self practice in the final 10 days before the exam. Do not copy, paraphrase, or reuse the fact pattern + issue combination in quiz items. (Names, industries, and issue pairings are all distinctive.) Pilot Paper (2019): Pilot Q1 (40m) — Thomas/Golden Cow: restrictive covenant + veil piercing (Gilford Motor), ultra vires objects clause, unfair prejudice buy out, summary dismissal of secretary. Pilot Q2 (10m) — precedent: CFI vs CA authority, House of Lords in HK, obiter on administrative matters. Pilot Q3 (15m) — sausage factory river pollution: negligence/Rylands style claim against upstream chemical factory. Pilot Q4 (15m) — anti virus guarantee advertisement (unilateral offer); piano sale retention of ownership. Pilot Q5 (10m) — bank branch manager OSCO money laundering; civil servant lifestyle beyond means (PBO s.10). Pilot Q6 (5m) — debenture issue and prospectus requirements. Pilot Q7 (5m) — self styled managing director exceeding HK$200k authority limit; binding contract. June 2024: J24 Q1 (15m) — WWL annual dinner: discharge of contract; injured magician = frustration; wrong logo souvenirs = breach of condition; remedies. J24 Q2 (10m) — SIL/UML sheet iron: retention of title (Romalpa) clause enforceability against liquidator. J24 Q3 (15m) — HGL pharmaceutical: employees' implied duties; Ernest selling formula (PBO bribery); Edith forged invoices (PBO s.9(3)). J24 Q4 (20m) — GAL fine art: creation of agency; Susanna's unauthorised painting purchase (ratification); food poisoning negligence claim against café. J24 Q5 (25m) — GDL eco garment: debenture, fixed & floating charges; dormant status; deregistration requirements. J24 Q6 (15m) — solicitor Ricky: inside information & insider dealing in SWL shares; general→limited partner status change. June 2025: J25 Q1 (10m) — FSL platform delivery rider Peter: employee vs independent contractor status. J25 Q2 (20m) — HJL liquidation auction of "rough diamonds" (actually cubic zirconia): misrepresentation, remedies, court jurisdiction for HK$3.2m claim. J25 Q3 (10m) — PVL shopping centre valuation passed to Mrs Rich: negligent misstatement. J25 Q4 (20m) — golf coach Johnathan's secret commission: agent's fiduciary duties + PBO offence. J25 Q5 (20m) — TFL health app: private→public conversion; Main Board listing requirements. J25 Q6 (20m) — Jessica/Jerry divorce: separate legal entity, veil lifting over pre marriage properties vested in HGL; company funded assets. June 2026: J26 Q1 (15m) — Tommy the artist: HK$60,000 sculpture (sufficient not adequate consideration); revoked offer to Millie; Lily's free gift promise (past consideration). J26 Q2 (15m) — GTL restaurant: Billy's forged invoices — summary dismissal + PBO s.9(3); Fanny's long service payment on retirement (dementia). J26 Q3 (15m) — GDL car dealership: creation of agency; Michelle's unauthorised antique racing car purchase; stolen sedan — nemo dat + s.24 SOGO. J26 Q4 (25m) — HFL AI company: TCC valuation report relied on by Mrs Gold (negligent misstatement); fixed/floating charges for debt financing. J26 Q5 (20m) — GWL wine: Venessa's unfair prejudice petition; grounds for winding up; just and equitable petition. J26 Q6 (10m) — VEL listed: CEO vs substantial shareholder disclosure of interests; wife's deemed interest in husband's shares. Also reserved (Dec 2024 / Dec 2025 — identified from panelists' reports; question papers not in the reviewed set): D24 Q1 — online advertisement offer vs invitation to treat; past consideration. D24 Q2 — passing of property; buyer claiming paid for goods from seller's receivers. D24 Q3 — AML; pedestrian negligence; vicarious liability. D24 Q4 — undisclosed principal; CFI jurisdiction. D24 Q5 — BSL: types of directors; directors' fiduciary duties, breach (diverting business to BBL), remedies. D24 Q6 — substantial shareholder disclosure obligations & breach consequences. D25 Q1 — employee fiduciary duties; PBO s.9(2); District Court civil jurisdiction. D25 Q2 — discharge of contract; frustrated tenancy agreement. D25 Q3 — creation of agency; apparent authority; negligence; novus actus interveniens. D25 Q4 — dormant status; deregistration; voluntary winding up of solvent company. D25 Q5 — general partnership duties; joint and several liability. D25 Q6 — insider dealing. text: Exam Lens — HKICPA QP Module 6 Financial Accounting (Associate Level) Purpose: Briefing for quiz item writers (5 item OTQ chapter quizzes). Based on official past papers (Jun 2023, Jun 2024, Jun 2025), the CBE Pilot Examination Paper (published Sep 2025), and Examination Panelists' Reports (Jun 2023–Jun 2025). 1. Exam Structure 1.1 Format change alert — TWO formats in the source set Legacy format (Jun 2023 – Jun 2025 sessions) New CBE format (Pilot Paper, published Sep 2025) Duration 3 hours (Section B timings imply 1.8 min/mark × 100 marks = 180 min) 2 hours 30 minutes (1.5 min/mark stated on cover) Section A 15 MCQs = 20 marks (20%). Q1–Q10 = 1 mark each (straightforward); Q11–Q15 = 2 marks each (more complex concepts/computations) Objective Type Questions (OTQs) = 63 marks (63%). 48 numbered items (Q1–Q48), mix of 1/2/3 mark items Section B Written questions = 80 marks (80%). 4–5 compulsory questions of 10–30 marks each Scenario based / task based questions = 37 marks (37%). 2 scenarios (Q49 consolidation ≈ 20 marks; Q50 cash flows ≈ 17 marks), each split into sub tasks (a)–(e) Delivery Paper based written answers Computer based exam (CBE): radio button MCQs, True/False, select all that apply, drag and drop classification, drop down menus, numeric fill in fields, journal entry construction grids, spreadsheet style statement preparation (typed figures into pre formatted statement templates) Compulsory? All questions compulsory All questions compulsory When the format changed: The three most recent live sessions analysed (Jun 2023, Jun 2024, Jun 2025) all used the legacy 20% MCQ + 80% written format. The Pilot Paper (copyright 2025, published September 2025) introduces the new CBE structure (63% OTQ + 37% task based), i.e. the change takes effect for sessions after June 2025. The Jun 2025 panelists' report explicitly flags "the transition to computer based examinations" and notes consolidation journal entry mechanics "remain a critical area of assessment... especially with the transition to CBE." Practical implication for quiz writers: OTQs now carry the majority of marks (63%). Item writing skill in objective formats (MCQ, multi select, True/False, numeric entry, drag and drop) is now the highest leverage authoring skill for M6. 1.2 Legacy Section B composition (per session) Jun 2023 (80 marks): Q1 Consolidation + associate (25) Q2 SPLOCI + SOCIE from trial balance (20) Q3 Related parties (10) Q4 Impairment (10) Q5 Revenue (15) Jun 2024 (80 marks): Q1 Control + consolidation (30) Q2 PPE revaluation + SOCIE + disclosures (20) Q3 Conceptual Framework + provisions + borrowing costs (20) Q4 Lessor finance lease (10) Jun 2025 (80 marks): Q1 Associate definition + consolidation incl. equity method (28) Q2 Intangibles + statement of cash flows (28) Q3 Conceptual Framework + change in estimate (12) Q4 EPS + related party (12) Mark to time guide is printed per question (e.g., "28 marks – approximately 50 minutes"). Question 1 is always a consolidation question (25–30 marks) — the anchor of Section B in every session reviewed. 2. Question Style 2.1 Command words (legacy Section B) Explain — the dominant command word. Almost always scenario linked: "Explain, based on the information provided, why...", "Explain, with reference to HKAS 33, how...", "Explain, with computations, how...". Pure regurgitation scores poorly; application to case facts is required. Define — short book knowledge items: "Define 'liability'...", "Define 'recoverable amount'", "Define 'qualifying asset'" (2–4 marks). Outline / Describe — lists of criteria or disclosure requirements: "Outline the five steps in HKFRS 15", "Describe the recognition criteria of a provision for restructuring", "Outline FOUR disclosure requirements... You are NOT required to draft the disclosure note." Prepare — full statements: consolidated SFP, SPLOCI, SOCIE, statement of cash flows (indirect method). Always with the note "You have to show your workings, including supporting calculations and/or the consolidation adjustment journal entries." Calculate / Compute — targeted numbers: impairment loss, depreciation, gain/loss on disposal, gross/net investment in lease, profit attributable to NCI, EPS. Identify / Determine — used heavily in new format OTQs. Cross standard hybrids are common: one scenario, two or three standards (e.g., Jun 2025 Q4 = HKAS 33 + HKAS 24; Jun 2024 Q3 = Conceptual Framework + HKAS 37 + HKAS 23). 2.2 Scenario style Fictional Hong Kong companies with animal/themed names (Peacock, Salmon, Alligator, Baboons, Paddlefish, Supreme Gold...), HK$ amounts, 31 March / 30 September / 31 December year ends. Scenario length: ~0.5–1.5 pages per written question, including extracts of SFP / SPLOCI / trial balance tables. Accounting policies are stated explicitly in the scenario (cost model vs revaluation model, straight line, monthly depreciation, NCI at fair value vs proportionate share). Questions are designed so that ignoring a stated policy (e.g., eliminate accumulated depreciation on revaluation; transfer revaluation surplus to retained earnings) loses marks. Numbers are engineered to test specific adjustments: mid period acquisitions/disposals (monthly depreciation), mark up on cost (20%) for unrealised profit, deferred consideration with a stated discount rate, options with exercise price vs average market price. 2.3 OTQ design patterns (from Pilot Paper + panelists' topic lists) Single best answer MCQ with 4 options (A–D) , majority 1 mark; 2 mark items involve multi step computation. Distractor engineering (recurring patterns): Each distractor = the output of a specific error (e.g., omitting transaction costs from initial measurement; adding instead of deducting; grossing up mark up vs margin; using full year instead of pro rated depreciation; ignoring the revaluation surplus ceiling on a downward revaluation). "Definition swap" distractors: e.g., NRV definition vs fair value definition (HKFRS 13 wording) offered as alternatives for an HKAS 2 definition question. Boundary/threshold traps: SME FRF qualifying criteria (banking/insurance licences, size thresholds, shareholder approval); ECL staging (Stage 1/2/3); dilutive vs anti dilutive options (exercise price vs average market price). Reversal of rule traps: impairment reversal capped at depreciated historical cost; revaluation decrease below surplus goes to P&L. NOT questions are common : "Identify which... would NOT give rise to a temporary difference", "which of the following statements is NOT correct", "which is NOT a measurement classification". True/False items — a single statement on a precise rule (e.g., goodwill on associate acquisition is NOT separately recognised; highest and best use land valuation). Select all that apply (2–3 marks): e.g., items qualifying as cash and cash equivalents; factors indicating finance lease classification; HKFRS 10/12 disclosure requirements. Drag and drop classification (up to 3 marks): classify 7 properties as investment property / owner occupied / inventory. Numeric fill in (1–3 marks): calculate FIFO inventory value, impairment write down allocated across a disposal group, revaluation surplus balance. Drop down selection and journal entry grid items: pick Dr/Cr accounts and amounts (e.g., FVTPL designated bond with own credit risk split to OCI). Every OTQ cites the governing standard in the stem ("According to HKAS 16...", "In accordance with HKFRS 9...") — mirror this in quiz items. 2.4 How calculation questions are asked Calculations are embedded in a scenario, rarely standalone: the stem gives cost, dates, useful life, residual value, and requires a specific output (carrying amount, impairment loss, depreciation expense, gain/loss on disposal, EPS, lease investment). Written section calculations must be accompanied by workings / journal entries — markers award method marks via workings. Dates are deliberately mid year (e.g., acquired 1 July, disposed 1 April) to force pro rating — monthly depreciation is the norm ("Depreciation is recorded on a monthly basis"). 3. written 2 of 3 10 Financial Instruments (HKFRS 9) Amortised cost bonds, transaction costs, FVTPL in Q2 – in Q2 (FV change) MCQ every year (2 items 2024/2025) 16 Income Taxes (HKAS 12) Tax base, deferred tax, temporary differences in Q2 (current tax) – – MCQ every year, flagged weak every year 18 FX (HKAS 21) – – – – MCQ every year 6 Investment Property (HKAS 40) – – – – MCQ every year 12 NCA Held for Sale (HKFRS 5) – – – – MCQ 2024/2025, flagged weak both years 2 Fair Value (HKFRS 13) – – – – MCQ every year 4 Inventories (HKAS 2) – – – – MCQ every year 14 Events After Reporting (HKAS 10) – – – – MCQ 2023/2024 25 Joint Arrangements (HKFRS 11) – – – – MCQ 2024 – SME FRF/SME FRS – – – – MCQ 2024 + Pilot 3.2 Takeaways for quiz coverage prioritisation Tier 1 (must have quiz coverage): Consolidation + associates + business combinations (Ch 22–24); PPE (Ch 5); Intangibles (Ch 9); Cash flows (Ch 21); FS presentation (Ch 20); Revenue (Ch 3); Financial instruments (Ch 10); Income taxes (Ch 16). Tier 2 (tested every year in OTQs): Inventories (4), Investment property (6), Leases (7), Impairment (11), FV measurement (2), Provisions (15), FX (18), EPS (17), Conceptual Framework (1). Tier 3 (rotating): HKAS 8 (13), HKAS 10 (14), HKFRS 5 (12), HKAS 24 (19), HKFRS 11 (25), HKAS 23 (8), SME FRF. Under the new CBE format (63% OTQ), every chapter is realistically examinable every session — Tier 3 topics can no longer be skipped in quiz banks. 4. Panelist Reported Weaknesses (by session) 4.1 Jun 2023 MCQ weak spots: HKAS 40 classification (PPE vs investment property); HKAS 8 (estimate vs policy change); HKFRS 16 (purchase option impact on ROU asset and depreciation); HKAS 12 (tax base of an asset; deductible vs taxable temporary differences). Q1 Consolidation: basic computations (goodwill, FV differential) fine; profit allocation to NCI was the main failure point . Equity method for associates (HKAS 28) "lower than expected — most candidates appear to not have been aware of the application of the equity method". Q2 HKAS 1: many unaware of OCI statement presentation; SOCIE format unknown ("performance unsatisfactory"). Bond transaction costs — confusion whether to add or deduct from initial bond carrying amount. Q4 HKAS 36: recoverable amount wrongly defined as the lower (not higher) of FVLCD and VIU; no awareness of the ceiling on impairment reversal . Q5 HKFRS 15: most could not adequately outline the five step model — "standard textbook material" not learned; weak use of HKFRS 15 terminology in journal entries (contract liability etc.). General: wildly variable preparation; blank answers; inability to produce sensible calculations/journal entries; candidates must explain rationale, not state conclusions. 4.2 Jun 2024 MCQ weak spots: HKFRS 9 subsequent measurement of financial liabilities and assets; HKFRS 5 measurement requirements; HKAS 1 materiality concepts; HKAS 12 tax base of an asset / deferred tax recognition (repeat weakness). Q1 Control (HKFRS 10): weak awareness — ownership % alone is not control. Consolidation: difficulty with deferred consideration , upstream intra group equipment transfer , unrealised profit on equipment and its realisation through excess depreciation adjustment, NCI profit allocation (repeat weakness). Q2 HKAS 16: revaluation journal entries wrong when candidates ignored the stated policy to eliminate accumulated depreciation against gross carrying amount, and ignored the transfer of revaluation surplus to retained earnings as the asset is used . SOCIE left blank or wrong format again (same complaint as Jun 2023). PPE disclosure requirements left blank by many. Q3 HKAS 37/23: candidates wrongly concluded a restructuring provision should be recognised merely because the board approved the plan — no grasp of constructive obligation . HKAS 23 flagged as a consistently weak area across multiple reports (commencement of capitalisation; treatment of interest income on specific borrowings). Q4 HKFRS 16 lessor: some left blank; confusion between gross vs net investment in the lease . General: "common sense" approaches fail; technical accuracy and standard references essential; disclosure note awareness expected at company level. 4.3 Jun 2025 MCQ weak spots: HKFRS 16 lease payment concepts (lessee); HKFRS 13 principal market; HKFRS 5 measurement (third consecutive year flagged); HKFRS 15 refund liabilities; HKAS 12 tax base of a liability / deferred tax (third consecutive year flagged). Q1: candidates could identify facts for significant influence but could not link facts to accounting requirements . Consolidation: unrealised profit on downstream inventory sale poorly handled — some attributed the unrealised profit adjustment to NCI incorrectly (downstream = parent side, no NCI impact). Equity method: most capitalised associate profits, but many failed to eliminate dividend income recorded by the parent and did not know investment in associate must be presented as a separate line in consolidated SFP. Q2: conceptual HKAS 38 answers "disappointing" — could not differentiate definition vs recognition criteria ; weak on internally generated brands and training costs. Cash flow statement: average; strong on operating activity working capital, weak on computing cash paid for PPE/intangibles , dividends paid , and wrongly treating FVTPL fair value changes as cash flows . Q3: Conceptual Framework performance "unsatisfactory" — vague "true and fair view" answers instead of the objective of GPFR and the two fundamental qualitative characteristics. HKAS 8: computations fine but no discussion of the change in estimate treatment (prospective application). Q4 EPS: unsatisfactory — weighted average shares for mid year issue poorly done; belief that options only matter when exercised (rather than when potentially dilutive); failure to compare exercise price with average market price to test dilution. HKAS 24 part often not attempted. General: consolidation mechanics via adjustment journal entries remain "a critical area of assessment... especially with the transition to computer based examinations". 4.4 Cross session patterns (mark losing habits to design quizzes against) 1. HKAS 12 deferred tax weak in all three years (tax base of asset/liability, deductible vs taxable temporary differences). 2. HKFRS 5 measurement weak in all sessions it appeared (2024, 2025 + flagged in pilot era design). 3. NCI profit allocation and intra group unrealised profit (both upstream and downstream, inventory and depreciable assets) — the perennial consolidation failure point. 4. Ignoring stated accounting policies in the scenario (revaluation surplus transfer, accumulated depreciation elimination). 5. Statement formats unknown — SOCIE, OCI section, and (newer) cash flow statement mechanics for non cash items. 6. Conceptual/knowledge questions score worse than calculations — definitions, recognition criteria, Conceptual Framework content, disclosure requirements are systematically under prepared. 7. Vague answers without standard references — panelists repeatedly demand rationale + HKAS/HKFRS citation, not conclusions. 8. Blank short questions (disclosure outlines, related party parts) — candidates skip what they cannot compute. 5. Difficulty Calibration Guide (for a 5 item OTQ chapter quiz) 5.1 What "exam standard" means for M6 OTQs Anchor to the real paper's structure: legacy Section A = 10 easy (1 mark) + 5 harder (2 mark) items. A 5 item quiz should replicate this gradient: Items 1–3 (Foundational / 1 mark equivalent): single concept recall or one step application — a definition, a classification, a recognition criterion, a simple one step computation (e.g., depreciation for one year, FIFO closing inventory, basic EPS). Item 4 (Intermediate / 1–2 mark equivalent): two step application — requires selecting the correct rule AND executing a short computation or multi factor classification (e.g., carrying amount after revaluation decrease below surplus; tax base of a liability; NRV vs cost decision). Item 5 (Exam standard challenge / 2 mark equivalent): multi step computation or a NOT judgement across four plausible statements — mirrors legacy Q11–Q15 and pilot 2–3 mark items. Must include distractors generated from documented candidate errors (Section 4). Target facility: an exam standard 5 item set should be answerable in ~7–8 minutes (1.5 min/mark under CBE pacing). If a prepared student cannot finish in that time, the items are over engineered. Cognitive mix: roughly 40% knowledge/definition, 60% application/computation — matching the exam's stated aim of "core foundational technical knowledge... and skills in applying the knowledge to tackle routine professional problems, including computations". 5.2 Item writing rules to match exam style Always cite the standard in the stem ("In accordance with HKAS 16...", "According to HKFRS 15..."). Use mini scenarios with named HK companies and HK$ amounts, even for 1 mark items (the exam almost never asks a bare definition without a wrapper — but bare definition True/False items do occur in the pilot). Numbers must be clean but require work: mid period dates (pro rating), mark up vs margin conversions, stated discount rates, stated useful lives. Every distractor must correspond to a real, documented error (use Section 4: e.g., lower of instead of higher of for recoverable amount; adding transaction costs to bond instead of deducting; recognising restructuring provision on board approval alone; treating FV change as cash flow; attributing downstream unrealised profit to NCI). Include at least one "NOT"/"except" item or multi select per quiz occasionally to match pilot formats; vary correct answer positions. Provide answer explanations that name the standard and the precise paragraph level rule — the panelists' core complaint is candidates asserting conclusions without rationale. Difficulty ceiling: do not exceed the complexity of pilot 2–3 mark items (e.g., CGU impairment with headquarters allocation, disposal group write down allocation, deferred tax on multiple items). M6 is an associate level module — no professional level judgement scenarios. 5.3 Chapter emphasis guidance for quiz quotas Heaviest drill weight: consolidation mechanics (Ch 22–24) even in OTQ form (pilot shows consolidation OTQs: goodwill computation, adjustment JE selection, NCI effects); HKAS 12; HKFRS 9; HKFRS 15; HKAS 16/38/40 property family; HKFRS 16; HKAS 36; HKFRS 5. Include Conceptual Framework and disclosure type OTQs in every rotation — these are where candidates actually lose marks. 6. text: Exam Lens — HKICPA QP Module 8: Principles of Auditing Purpose: Briefing for quiz item writers. Built from official past papers (Pilot CBE paper, Jun 2023 / Jun 2024 / Jun 2025) and the corresponding Examination Panelists' Reports. 1. Exam Structure Current format (Jun 2023 – Jun 2025 sessions — confirmed by papers + panelists' reports) Duration: 3 hours (implied by paper: ~1.8 minutes per mark; Section B's 80 marks ≈ 144–148 minutes + Section A ≈ 36 minutes). Total: 100 marks, all questions compulsory. Section A — Multiple Choice Questions: 20 marks (20%). MCQs are NOT released in the published past papers; their coverage is only known from panelists' reports (see §3 and §4). Section B — Written Questions: 80 marks (80%), exactly 4 compulsory scenario/discussion questions. Mark splits per session: Jun 2023: Q1 22 / Q2 17 / Q3 17 / Q4 24 Jun 2024: Q1 27 / Q2 17 / Q3 23 / Q4 13 Jun 2025: Q1 17 / Q2 19 / Q3 19 / Q4 25 Each question broken into 4–6 sub requirements of 2–10 marks each. Suggested time is printed per question (e.g., "17 marks – approximately 30 minutes"). New CBE format (per Pilot Examination Paper, published Oct 2025 — FORMAT CHANGE) Duration reduced to 2 hours 30 minutes; 100 marks; all compulsory. Section A — Objective Type Questions (OTQ): 74 marks (74%) , 37 questions (Q1–37), 2 marks each. OTQ types observed: True/False statements (including paired sub statements, e.g., Q1a/1b, 2a/2b, 3a/3b). Drop down / fill in the blank ("Please Select" menus, e.g., "Substantive procedures are designed to ___ material misstatements"). Single best answer MCQ (A–D). "Pick the correct combination" items using roman numeral lists (e.g., "(1), (2) and (3) only"). Multiple response ("Identify THREE…", e.g., answers "B, D, E"). Section B — Scenario Based Questions: 26 marks (26%) , 13 questions (Q38–50), 2 marks each, organised into 4 scenario groups (3+5+3+2 questions), each preceded by a scenario of ~150–300 words. Answers are still objective type (MCQ / multi select), NOT free text. Implication: the Institute is shifting M8 from long form written answers to fully objective, scenario anchored testing. Quiz writers should design for BOTH: written style practice (current reality for recent sessions) and OTQ style (direction of travel per pilot). CBE features (from pilot paper) Computer based; answer areas embedded per question; drop down selection controls. Every item is 2 marks; no partial credit indicated. Scenario blocks displayed once, then 2–5 linked questions. 2. Question Style Command words (Section B written, ranked by frequency across Jun 23–25) List — the dominant command word ("List FOUR key matters…", "List FIVE factors…", "List THREE types…"). Pure recall; usually 2–6 marks. Describe — recall + slight elaboration ("Describe FOUR audit procedures…"). Explain — must show why/how, applied to the scenario ("Explain the relationship between an overall audit strategy and an audit plan"). Define — precise definitions ("Define Key Audit Matters", "Define the audit risk model"). Identify — selection/recognition. Contrast — direct comparison ("Contrast an emphasis of matter paragraph with an other matter paragraph"). Analyse / Determine — highest cognitive level, reserved for opinion determination and risk analysis requirements ("Determine the type of auditor's opinion… with detailed explanation", "Analyse the inherent risk of accounts receivable"). Scenario style (Section B) Short Hong Kong flavoured scenarios: 80–250 words, private HK companies ("Asia Pacific Limited", "Felix Limited", "Sunshine Limited") in familiar trades (F&B, computer hardware wholesale, manufacturing, dried seafood, property investment). Candidate role played as audit manager / senior in charge / training manager. Typically a light scenario wrapper around largely knowledge based requirements; only 1–2 sub parts per question genuinely require application to case facts. One "big" question per paper (24–27 marks) usually on audit completion/reporting (going concern, subsequent events, opinion types). MCQ / OTQ design patterns (from pilot paper + panelist reports) Assertion↔procedure matching is the single most repeated mechanic ("Which procedure tests completeness of trade payables?", "Which assertion is NOT relevant to receivables confirmation?"). Negation stems are common: "NOT relevant", "NOT appropriate", "would NOT be", "NOT explicitly stated". Combination items (roman numeral lists) test lists from the LP (assertions, profitability ratios, elements of analytical procedures, general IT controls). Distractors are plausible but wrong swaps: existence vs completeness direction of testing; observation vs inspection; qualified vs adverse vs disclaimer. Scenario based OTQs chain 2–5 items off one mini case: ethics threats → opinion type → cooling off period (pilot Q38–40); e commerce risks → IT controls → inventory valuation procedures → opinion (pilot Q41–45). Topics flagged by panelists as MCQ tested: professional ethics (every session), control activities, inherent risk, tests of control vs substantive procedures, audit risk model, CAATs, legal/regulatory framework, communication with TCWG. 3. Difficulty Calibration Guide (for 5 question OTQ chapter quizzes) What "exam standard" means in M8 Baselines: panelists repeatedly call most M8 items "straightforward" — the exam is primarily a knowledge recall + light application test, NOT a deep case analysis exam. Exam standard = a competent student who studied the LP can answer in ~1.5–2 minutes per mark. Cognitive mix to replicate (per 5 question quiz): ~2 questions: pure recall / definition (List/Define/Identify level) — e.g., "Which of the following is NOT an element of an assurance engagement?" ~2 questions: discrimination between easily confused concepts — the Institute's favourite trap zone (rights vs duties; EoM vs OM; observation vs inspection; existence vs completeness testing direction; qualified vs adverse vs disclaimer). ~1 question: application to a 2–4 sentence mini scenario (e.g., "Given control risk is assessed as low and inherent risk is not significant, what happens to the extent of substantive procedures?"). Difficulty ceiling: do NOT exceed the hardest observed exam behaviour — opinion determination with justification (Jun 23 Q4(f) type) or multi factor case analysis (Jun 24 Q4(c) type). Anything requiring synthesis of 3+ standards or open ended judgement beyond the LP is above exam standard. Difficulty floor: single fact trivia with no distractor plausibility (e.g., "What does HKSA stand for?") is below standard — every distractor must be a documented student confusion from §4. Scenario length for OTQs: max 3–5 sentences, one entity, one issue — mirroring pilot Section B items; full page scenarios belong to written question practice, not chapter quizzes. Mark/time pacing cue: 2 mark OTQs are the new standard unit; design quizzes as 5 × 2 mark items ≈ 5 minutes. Answer key rigour: model answers must be traceable to the LP/HKSA wording (the Institute's suggested answers quote standards nearly verbatim — e.g., HKSA 200 overall objectives). Avoid ambiguity: negation stems ("NOT") must have exactly one defensible answer. Chapter quiz emphasis: weight item difficulty toward the cross session failure list in §4 — an exam standard quiz should make students trip on the same traps the panelists keep reporting (assertion procedure matching, concept adjacency, requirement precision). 6.
